3-0014-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, le dernier Conseil européen a été l’occasion d’aboutir – enfin! – sur le sujet fondamental travaillé ici pendant de nombreux mois: celui du règlement «retour», dernière pièce de la stratégie européenne en matière d’immigration et plus spécifiquement de lutte contre l’immigration illégale.

Les médias se sont fait l’écho des débats qui ont eu lieu autour de la table du Conseil entre les chefs d’État. Sur ce sujet essentiel, nous avons travaillé, nous avons négocié, nous avons voté: maintenant, il faut agir. Et sur ce sujet clé, l’essentiel sera désormais dans la mise en œuvre concrète des mesures qui ont été validées. Dix-neuf États membres sur vingt-sept ont signé une lettre commune: 19 États membres de groupes politiques différents, certains issus du PPE, d’autres d’autres groupes de la droite, certains issus du groupe Renew, d’autres du groupe socialiste, qui ont dit ensemble l’urgence d’agir pour ouvrir des centres de retour.

Après que nous aurons subi pendant si longtemps des procès en inefficacité, des procès en illégitimité, nous voyons aujourd’hui des États prêts à se saisir de cet outil fondamental pour pouvoir garantir que, demain, plus personne ne pourra s’établir durablement en Europe sans y avoir été légalement autorisé. Quelle tristesse de voir que certains États choisissent de rompre avec cette logique, et de voir en particulier le président français déclarer que ce n’est pas son Europe.

Bien sûr, ce n’est peut-être pas son Europe. Il voudrait aujourd’hui contester ces centres de retour parce qu’ils ne seraient pas efficaces. Mais qu’est-ce qui est moins efficace que la situation actuelle quand, en France, moins d’une OQTF sur dix est effectivement mise en œuvre? Ce n’est peut être pas «son» Europe, mais c’est la nôtre, c’est celle que nous construisons ensemble: une Europe qui retrouvera la maîtrise de ses frontières et la maîtrise de son destin, une Europe qui rendra à nos démocraties le pouvoir de décider qui rentre sur leur sol et qui ne peut pas s’y établir, une Europe qui mettra fin à l’immigration illégale et à toutes les tragédies qui l’entourent. Nous sommes fiers de construire cette Europe-là! C’est l’Europe de l’avenir!
3-0014-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the last European Council was an opportunity to achieve something – finally! – on the fundamental subject worked here for many months: that of the “return” regulation, the last piece of the European strategy on immigration and more specifically the fight against illegal immigration.

The media echoed the debates that took place around the Council table between heads of state. On this essential subject, we worked, we negotiated, we voted: now we must act. And on this key subject, the main thing will now be in the concrete implementation of the measures which have been validated. Nineteen out of twenty-seven Member States signed a joint letter: 19 Member States from different political groups, some from the EPP, others from other right-wing groups, some from the Renew group, others from the Socialist group, who together said the urgency of action to open return centers.

After having suffered for so long from trials of ineffectiveness, trials of illegitimacy, today we see States ready to seize this fundamental tool to be able to guarantee that, tomorrow, no one will be able to establish themselves permanently in Europe without having been legally authorized to do so. How sad to see that certain States choose to break with this logic, and to see in particular the French president declaring that this is not his Europe.

Of course, this may not be his Europe. Today he would like to challenge these return centers because they would not be effective. But what is less effective than the current situation when, in France, less than one OQTF in ten is actually implemented? It may not be “his” Europe, but it is ours, it is the one that we are building together: a Europe that will regain control of its borders and control of its destiny, a Europe that will give back to our democracies the power to decide who returns to their soil and who cannot settle there, a Europe that will put an end to illegal immigration and all the tragedies that surround it. We are proud to build this Europe! This is the Europe of the future!

3-0016-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Az elmúlt években, amikor megrendezték a szokásos vitákat a csúcstalálkozókról, mindig külön kitértek a magyar kormány álláspontjára, és folyamatosan aggódtak a demokrácia állapotáért. De most, hogy az új TISZA-kormány tényleg elkezdi rombolni a jogállamot, síri csend van. Hahó! Van itt valaki? Egy egyetlen soros alkotmánymódosítással eltávolítanák a köztársasági elnököt, és még csak indoklás sincs. Megakadályozzák, hogy az ellenzék vezetője még egyszer miniszterelnök-jelölt lehessen. Visszamenőleg 12 évben korlátozzák a képviselői mandátumot, így az ellenzéki képviselők nagy részét egész egyszerűen kizárják a politikai életből.

Ha itt az Európai Parlamentben lenne ilyen szabály, akkor 164 képviselő nem indulhatna újra 29-ben, nem indulhatna Manfred Weber, de a Zöldek és a szocialisták frakcióvezetője sem, mint ahogy az Európai Parlament elnöke sem. Szóval kíváncsian várjuk az ír elnökség, de leginkább a jogállamiságra különösen érzékeny Európai Bizottság álláspontját. A hallgatás annak bizonyítéka lenne, hogy valójában eddig sem a demokrácia állapota érdekelte a Bizottságot, csak az, hogy engedelmes kormányok legyenek a tagállamokban. Ellen fogunk állni.
3-0016-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President! In recent years, when they held the usual discussions about the summits, they always addressed the Hungarian government's position separately and were constantly worried about the state of democracy. But now that the new TISZA government is really starting to destroy the rule of law, there is grave silence. Haha! Is there anyone here? They would remove the president of the republic with a single constitutional amendment, and there is not even a justification. They prevent the leader of the opposition from being a candidate for prime minister again. They retroactively restrict the mandate of representatives to 12 years, so most of the opposition representatives are quite simply excluded from political life.

If there were such a rule here in the European Parliament, then 164 representatives would not be able to run again in 29, Manfred Weber would not be able to run, nor would the leader of the Greens and the Socialists, nor the President of the European Parliament. So we eagerly await the position of the Irish presidency, but especially the European Commission, which is particularly sensitive to the rule of law. The silence would be proof that the Commission has not really been interested in the state of democracy so far, only that there are obedient governments in the member states. We will resist.

3-0017-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, c'è stato un tempo in cui le tesi dei Conservatori sulla protezione dei confini e sul realismo industriale venivano derise o liquidate come provocazioni.

Le conclusioni dell'ultimo Consiglio europeo dimostrano che quel tempo è finito: oggi, l'Unione comincia a muoversi lungo il percorso che noi abbiamo indicato per anni, a partire dalla gestione dei flussi migratori.

Purtroppo non potremo cancellare gli errori del passato, quando le sinistre imposero la tragica politica delle frontiere aperte a chiunque, ma siamo consci di aver cambiato paradigma per il futuro.

L'Unione guarda finalmente alla dimensione esterna, alla gestione ferma dei flussi, al rimpatrio veloce di chi non ha diritto alla protezione internazionale: in questo modo, contrasteremo i trafficanti di esseri umani, salveremo la vita dei migranti più di quanto sia mai accaduto in passato e lavoreremo per garantire loro il diritto a non emigrare.

È il buon senso che vince e che ora deve trovare un adeguato sostegno finanziario nel prossimo bilancio pluriennale.

Lo stesso realismo serve sulla competitività strategica. La prossima settimana la Commissione presenterà la revisione del sistema ETS e noi Conservatori saremo molto attenti a ciò che verrà presentato.

Non accetteremo norme cieche, incapaci di vedere la deindustrializzazione dell'Europa e la consegna del nostro destino economico nelle mani del fanatismo ambientalista e del regime cinese. Difenderemo il principio della neutralità tecnologica e la competitività del nostro tessuto produttivo.

Dalla nostra salute economica dipende la nostra possibilità di investire sulla sicurezza interna e sulla difesa esterna, sulla ricerca scientifica, sul sistema sanitario e scolastico e sulla conservazione della natura, che, paradossalmente, sembra interessare sempre di meno agli pseudoambientalisti da salotto.

A noi Conservatori interessa proteggere la terra dei nostri padri e proteggere la vita delle persone che vi abitano. È il motivo per cui noi siamo qui.
3-0017-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, there was a time when the Conservative theses on border protection and industrial realism were derided or dismissed as provocations.

The conclusions of the last European Council demonstrate that that time is over: today, the Union begins to move along the path that we have indicated for years, starting with the management of migratory flows.

Unfortunately we will not be able to erase the mistakes of the past, when the left imposed the tragic policy of borders open to anyone, but we are aware that we have changed the paradigm for the future.

The Union is finally looking at the external dimension, at the firm management of flows, at the rapid repatriation of those who are not entitled to international protection: in this way, we will fight human traffickers, we will save the lives of migrants more than has ever happened in the past and we will work to guarantee them the right not to emigrate.

It is common sense that wins and must now find adequate financial support in the next multi-year budget.

The same realism is needed for strategic competitiveness. Next week the Commission will present the review of the ETS system and we Conservatives will be very attentive to what is presented.

We will not accept blind regulations, unable to see the deindustrialization of Europe and the handing over of our economic destiny into the hands of environmental fanaticism and the Chinese regime. We will defend the principle of technological neutrality and the competitiveness of our production fabric.

Our ability to invest in internal security and external defense, in scientific research, in the health and education system and in nature conservation depends on our economic health, which, paradoxically, seems to be of less and less interest to armchair pseudo-environmentalists.

We Conservatives are interested in protecting the land of our fathers and protecting the lives of the people who live there. It's why we are here.

3-0020-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, l’Europe brûle littéralement. Les personnes âgées suffoquent dans les EHPAD, les enfants étouffent à l’école, les hôpitaux surchauffent au sens propre comme au sens figuré, les morgues débordent, les récoltes sont menacées, les forêts partent en fumée… Et quelle est votre réponse, à la Commission européenne? Mettre la lutte contre le changement climatique en pause.

Il fallait oser, car la canicule, quoi qu’on en dise, n’est pas juste un incident météo: la canicule est politique, et les morts de cette canicule sont le résultat de votre politique. N’est-ce pas vous, à la Commission européenne, qui avez détruit méthodiquement plus d’une vingtaine de réglementations environnementales depuis le début de votre nouveau mandat? N’est-ce pas vous, Monsieur le Commissaire, personnellement, qui signez à tour de bras des accords de libre-échange pour aller chercher à l’autre bout du monde ce que l’on sait que l’on peut produire ici?

Alors oui, vous n’êtes pas seul. Il y a les États membres, qui manifestement se cachent aujourd’hui. Mais vous vous êtes aussi embarqué dans le sillage de l’extrême droite, désormais votre complice favorite, pionnière du déni du réchauffement climatique et toujours prête à défendre les privilégiés.

Mais descendez de votre bureau climatisé et ouvrez les yeux: vous verrez que tout le monde n’est pas logé à la même enseigne. Pendant que les puissants se barricadent au frais, les plus pauvres morflent. Plus vous êtes exploité, plus vous brûlez. Ce massacre climatique est en réalité un massacre de classe. Ce sont les riches qui tuent les pauvres. Le 1 % le plus riche pollue autant que les deux tiers de l’humanité, 100 entreprises sont responsables de 70 % des émissions mondiales, Bernard Arnault émet 1 200 fois plus de CO2 qu’un Français moyen, mais, surtout, ne leur demandons aucun effort! Continuons comme avant, ne les mettons pas à contribution! Ne touchons surtout pas à leur mode de vie!

Les trois épisodes caniculaires que nous venons de vivre ne sont pourtant que la bande-annonce de ce qui nous attend dans les années à venir. Face à la canicule, adoptons les bons gestes barrières: taxons les riches et sortons de l’idéologie néolibérale! Car, à force de recul, de renoncement et d’inaction, vous nous condamnez à brûler.
3-0020-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Europe is literally burning. The elderly are suffocating in nursing homes, children are suffocating at school, hospitals are literally and figuratively overheating, morgues are overflowing, harvests are threatened, forests are going up in smoke... And what is your response, to the European Commission? Putting the fight against climate change on pause.

You had to dare, because the heatwave, whatever people say about it, is not just a weather incident: the heatwave is political, and the deaths from this heatwave are the result of your politics. Isn't it you, at the European Commission, who have methodically destroyed more than twenty environmental regulations since the start of your new mandate? Is it not you, Mr Commissioner, personally, who is signing free trade agreements with all your might to go and find on the other side of the world what we know we can produce here?

So yes, you are not alone. There are the Member States, which are clearly in hiding today. But you have also embarked in the wake of the extreme right, now your favorite accomplice, pioneer of the denial of global warming and always ready to defend the privileged.

But come down from your air-conditioned office and open your eyes: you will see that not everyone is in the same boat. While the powerful barricade themselves in the cold, the poorest are languishing. The more you are exploited, the more you burn. This climate massacre is in reality a class massacre. It is the rich who kill the poor. The richest 1% pollute as much as two thirds of humanity, 100 companies are responsible for 70% of global emissions, Bernard Arnault emits 1,200 times more CO2 than an average French person, but, above all, let's not ask them for any effort! Let's continue as before, let's not put them to work! Let's not touch their way of life!

The three heatwave episodes that we have just experienced are, however, only the trailer of what awaits us in the years to come. Faced with the heatwave, let's adopt the right barrier gestures: let's tax the rich and get away from neoliberal ideology! Because, by dint of retreat, renunciation and inaction, you condemn us to burn.

3-0021-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Einige Tausend Hitzetote haben Europa und Deutschland bereits zu beklagen, und währenddessen möchte man durch den CO2-Emissionshandel die Preise für Energie noch teurer machen, um das Klima weltweit zu beeinflussen. Genau das ist der Unterschied zwischen Theorie und Praxis; das ist der Unterschied zwischen denen auf der linken Seite und den patriotischen Kräften in Europa.

Wir glauben nicht daran, dass höhere Steuern und Mehrbelastung für die Bürger irgendetwas am Weltklima verändern würden – und dieser Ansatz ist ja auch bereits in der Realität gescheitert. Stattdessen möchten wir den Menschen ganz praktisch helfen, beispielsweise indem Altenheime, Pflegeheime, Krankenhäuser, Schulen ganz konkret und systematisch mit Klimaanlagen ausgestattet werden. Wir wollen praktische Politik statt Wolkenkuckucksheim.

Etwas anderes, was auf der Tagesordnung stand, ist die Frage nach dem Erweiterungsprozess. Der Balkan ist eine unglaublich wichtige Region für uns; sie ist strategisch wichtig für Europa. Deswegen möchten auch wir, dass der Balkan und die Europäische Union sehr viel enger zusammenarbeiten, beispielsweise durch privilegierte Handelsbeziehungen – dass diese noch weiter ausgebaut werden.

Was wir aber nicht wollen, ist, dass diese Länder bei dem aktuellen Stand in die Europäische Union aufgenommen werden. Wir wollen nicht, dass weitere Empfängerländer aufgenommen werden, die am Ende des Tages den deutschen Steuerzahler weiter und noch mehr belasten.

Schon die letzten Erweiterungsrunden sind nicht voll verarbeitet worden von der Europäischen Union. Nach wie vor gibt es große Konflikte; nach wie vor sind die institutionellen Regeln nicht auf diese Größe ausgelegt. Wir müssen erst einmal daran arbeiten, dass diese Europäische Union und die europäische Kooperation wieder arbeitsfähig werden, indem man sich auf das Wesentliche konzentriert und indem man eben nicht immer neue Aufgaben und Länder hinzunimmt.

Wir wollen, dass der Balkan näher an uns herangeführt wird, aber eben ohne den deutschen Steuerzahler zu belasten.
3-0021-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Europe and Germany have already suffered several thousand heat deaths, and in the meantime they want to make energy prices even more expensive through CO2 emissions trading in order to influence the climate worldwide. That is exactly the difference between theory and practice; that is the difference between those on the left and the patriotic forces in Europe.

We do not believe that higher taxes and additional burdens for citizens would change anything about the global climate - and this approach has already failed in reality. Instead, we want to help people in a very practical way, for example by specifically and systematically equipping old people's homes, nursing homes, hospitals and schools with air conditioning systems. We want practical politics instead of cloud cuckoo land.

Something else that was on the agenda is the question of the enlargement process. The Balkans is an incredibly important region for us; it is strategically important for Europe. That's why we also want the Balkans and the European Union to work much more closely together, for example through privileged trade relations - and to expand these even further.

But what we don't want is for these countries to be admitted to the European Union as things stand. We do not want additional recipient countries to be accepted, which at the end of the day will place even greater burdens on German taxpayers.

Even the last rounds of enlargement have not been fully processed by the European Union. There are still major conflicts; The institutional rules are still not designed for this size. We first have to work on making this European Union and European cooperation operational again by concentrating on the essentials and by not always adding new tasks and countries.

We want the Balkans to be brought closer to us, but without putting a burden on the German taxpayer.

3-0022-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Dzięki państwom wschodniej flanki i polskiej prezydencji Europa wreszcie uznała, że wschodnia granica Unii jest pierwszą linią naszego wspólnego bezpieczeństwa. Dlatego program Eastern Flank Watch nie może oznaczać samego monitorowania zagrożeń. Samo obserwowanie drona czy rakiety to za mało. Konieczne są realne zdolności obronne: systemy antydronowe wczesnego ostrzegania, zintegrowana obrona powietrzna i nowoczesne technologie.

Polska daje przykład, jak działać skutecznie. Jesteśmy największym beneficjentem programu SAFE i wykorzystujemy te środki na realne wzmocnienie bezpieczeństwa Polski, wschodniej flanki i całej Europy.

Pomimo weta prezydenta i sabotażu opozycji w Polsce wojna Wschodu z Zachodem to nie jest teoria. Jesteśmy w stanie wojny hybrydowej w Europie i w Polsce, na którą spadały ruskie drony. Zamykane były lotniska, prowadzona była dywersja na torach kolejowych, a Putin wykorzystywał migrantów jako żywą tarczę. Putin nie testuje tylko Polski, Rumunii czy państw bałtyckich. On testuje całą Unię Europejską. Dlatego wschodnia flanka musi być dziś najtrwalszą i najtwardszą linią obrony całej Unii Europejskiej.
3-0022-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Thanks to the countries of the eastern flank and the Polish Presidency, Europe has finally recognized that the Union's eastern border is the first line of our common security. Therefore, the Eastern Flank Watch program cannot mean merely monitoring threats. Just observing a drone or rocket is not enough. Real defense capabilities are necessary: ​​early warning anti-drone systems, integrated air defense and modern technologies.

Poland sets an example of how to act effectively. We are the largest beneficiary of the SAFE program and we use these funds to really strengthen the security of Poland, the eastern flank and the whole of Europe.

Despite the president's veto and the sabotage of the opposition in Poland, the war between the East and the West is not a theory. We are in a state of hybrid war in Europe and Poland, which has been hit by Russian drones. Airports were closed, sabotage was carried out on railway tracks, and Putin used migrants as a human shield. Putin is not just testing Poland, Romania or the Baltic states. He is testing the entire European Union. Therefore, the eastern flank must be the most durable and toughest line of defense of the entire European Union today.

3-0023-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, le conclusioni del Consiglio europeo dedicano spazio alla Palestina, mentre in quest'Aula ogni proposta di dibattito o risoluzione sul tema viene sistematicamente bloccata dalla destra e dal centro‑destra.

Questo mese è stata bocciata anche la proposta di dibattito sul dottor Abu Safiya, pediatra palestinese imprigionato da 18 mesi senza processo, che sta rischiando la vita.

A giugno, i leader europei hanno scritto nero su bianco che: Israele deve ritirarsi da Gaza; la linea gialla è inaccettabile; i ministri israeliani promuovono violazioni dei diritti umani; la nuova legge sulla pena di morte è discriminatoria e inumana e va abrogata; la colonizzazione della Cisgiordania è una grave violazione del diritto internazionale.

Lo sapevamo già: caro Consiglio, oltre alle parole, però, servono i fatti. Perché non spingete i vostri ministri ad adottare delle sanzioni efficaci, come fu fatto con la Russia nel 2022?

Invece, il Parlamento deve ritrovare la voce. Il Parlamento sta in silenzio davanti a un genocidio: è un silenzio colpevole, è un silenzio pesante, è un disonore per questa istituzione.
3-0023-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, the conclusions of the European Council dedicate space to Palestine, while in this House every proposal for debate or resolution on the topic is systematically blocked by the right and centre-right.

This month, the proposal for a debate on Dr. Abu Safiya, a Palestinian pediatrician imprisoned for 18 months without trial, who is risking his life, was also rejected.

In June, European leaders wrote in black and white that: Israel must withdraw from Gaza; the yellow line is unacceptable; Israeli ministers promote human rights violations; the new law on the death penalty is discriminatory and inhumane and must be repealed; The colonization of the West Bank is a serious violation of international law.

We already knew it: dear Council, in addition to words, however, we need facts. Why don't you push your ministers to adopt effective sanctions, as was done with Russia in 2022?

Instead, Parliament must find its voice again. Parliament remains silent in the face of genocide: it is a guilty silence, it is a heavy silence, it is a disgrace for this institution.

3-0025-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, nel Suo intervento, analizzando il tema del bilancio, Lei ha parlato di risorse proprie, ma io ho un messaggio chiaro da mandarle: basta tasse, perché prima si razionalizzano le spese, si tagliano i costi – spesso inutili, che anche questo Parlamento avalla – e poi si ragiona, e si tagliano gli sprechi e le inefficienze.

Perché dobbiamo essere realisti: l'industria europea è in difficoltà, ci sono tante sacche di povertà, sempre più europei non arrivano a fine mese. Parlare di risorse proprie – quindi, di nuove tasse – è totalmente fuori luogo e scollegato dalla realtà.

A livello globale ci sono dei modelli di economia, tipo l'economia argentina, che stanno basando il rilancio dell'economia sulla riduzione delle tasse. In quest'Aula, invece, si parla di aumentarle. Siamo fuori dal mondo, Commissario. Serve un'inversione di tendenza, altro che nuove tasse.
3-0025-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Commissioner, in your speech, analyzing the topic of the budget, you spoke about own resources, but I have a clear message to send you: no more taxes, because first we rationalize expenses, cut costs - often useless, which this Parliament also endorses - and then we think, and cut waste and inefficiencies.

Because we have to be realistic: European industry is in difficulty, there are many pockets of poverty, more and more Europeans don't make ends meet. Talking about own resources - therefore, about new taxes - is totally out of place and disconnected from reality.

At a global level there are economic models, such as the Argentine economy, which are basing the revival of the economy on tax reductions. In this House, however, there is talk of increasing them. We are out of this world, Commissioner. We need a reversal of the trend, rather than new taxes.

3-0029-0000.sourceText: (ECR), “blauwe kaart”-vraag. – Meneer Gerbrandy, u spreekt hier over Europees, over de Green Deal. Hoe reflecteert u op het feit dat de Europese Commissie in de nieuwe veehouderijstrategie heeft gezegd dat er geen verdere krimp van de veestapel mocht komen, terwijl uw kabinet nu werkt aan de liquidatie van duizenden familiebedrijven in Nederland en daarmee de voedselzekerheid op het spel zet. U spreekt over de Straat van Hormuz en afhankelijkheden, maar wat vindt u ervan als we voor dierlijke productie en andere landbouwproductie afhankelijk worden van derde landen? Heeft u daar wel eens op gereflecteerd? En wat u doet met agrarische families en gezinsbedrijven en mensen aan de keukentafel?
3-0029-0000.englishText: (ECR), “blue card” question. – Mr Gerbrandy, you are talking about European here, about the Green Deal. How do you reflect on the fact that the European Commission stated in the new livestock farming strategy that there should be no further decline in the livestock herd, while your government is now working on the liquidation of thousands of family businesses in the Netherlands, thereby endangering food security? You talk about the Strait of Hormuz and dependencies, but what do you think if we become dependent on third countries for animal production and other agricultural production? Have you ever reflected on that? And what do you do with agricultural families and family businesses and people at the kitchen table?

3-0030-0000.sourceText: (Renew), “blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Heerlijk altijd die nationale politiek in het Europees Parlement. Voedselzekerheid: wellicht heeft u onlangs ook het rapport gelezen waarin staat dat Nederland een importeur is van voedsel. Niet vanwege menselijke consumptie, maar vanwege de enorme hoeveelheid diervoeding die wij moeten importeren om ons waterhoofd aan dierlijke productie overeind te houden. Als u echt, echt betrokken bent bij de voedselzekerheid van Europa, dan weet u dat ons dieet plantaardiger moet worden en dat de toekomst niet ligt in het nog verder uitbreiden van de veestapel, wat volgens mij het beleid is van uw partij, waarmee niet alleen onze economie, maar zeker ook onze wereld helemaal kapot gaat.
3-0030-0000.englishText: (Renew), “blue card” response. – Always wonderful to see national politics in the European Parliament. Food security: you may have also recently read the report stating that the Netherlands is an importer of food. Not because of human consumption, but because of the enormous amount of animal feed that we have to import to maintain our hydrocephalus in animal production. If you are really, really concerned about Europe's food security, then you know that our diet must become more plant-based and that the future does not lie in further expanding livestock, which I believe is the policy of your party, which is destroying not only our economy, but certainly also our world.

3-0031-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Ein Thema ist beim letzten Europäischen Rat irgendwie erstaunlicherweise zu kurz gekommen – der zukünftige EU‑Haushalt. Dabei ist es doch das Thema, das die Grundlage bildet für alles, was wir hier an Programmen diskutieren.

Die Verhandlungen für den Haushalt ab 2028 laufen, und gleichzeitig stehen viele nationale Budgets unter Druck; das müssen wir natürlich anerkennen, und das tun wir auch. Deswegen hätte ich mir mehr Ambitionen von den Mitgliedstaaten erwartet, denn wenn es ernst wird, dann schauen alle nach Brüssel. Aber wenn es darum geht, den gemeinsamen Haushalt zu finanzieren, dann wird es plötzlich ganz still.

Dabei hat dieses Haus gute Vorschläge gemacht, wie wir aus dem Deadlock herausrauskommen, wie wir aus dieser Sackgasse der Verhandlungen herauskommen: Wir brauchen mehr und bessere Eigenmittel für den künftigen EU‑Haushalt, eine Digitalabgabe, eine Besteuerung von Kryptowährungen oder von Online‑Glücksspiel, das europaweit zunimmt.

Das sind gute Vorschläge, und ich erwarte von den Mitgliedstaaten, dass sie sich endlich zusammenreißen und diese Sachen für den künftigen Haushalt genau prüfen.
3-0031-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! One topic was somehow surprisingly neglected at the last European Council - the future EU budget. It is the topic that forms the basis for everything we discuss here in terms of programs.

Negotiations for the budget from 2028 are ongoing, and at the same time many national budgets are under pressure; Of course we have to recognize that, and that's what we do. That's why I would have expected more ambition from the member states, because when things get serious, everyone looks to Brussels. But when it comes to financing the common household, everything suddenly becomes very quiet.

This House has made good suggestions on how we can get out of the deadlock, how we can get out of this impasse in negotiations: We need more and better own resources for the future EU budget, a digital levy, a tax on cryptocurrencies or on online gambling, which is increasing across Europe.

These are good proposals and I expect the Member States to finally get their act together and examine these things carefully for the future budget.

3-0032-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, Colegas, o mercado único é um desígnio europeu e o 28.º regime é a melhor ferramenta para o concretizar.

Falo-vos de um regime que oferece uma via pragmática para ultrapassar a fragmentação jurídica que continua a limitar o crescimento das empresas europeias, em particular das PME e das start‑ups. Ao permitir um quadro jurídico opcional, uniforme e diretamente aplicável em toda a União, reduz a complexidade administrativa, os custos de conformidade e a incerteza jurídica, que hoje travam a expansão além‑fronteiras. Num contexto de transição verde e digital, e de crescente concorrência internacional, a União não pode dar-se ao luxo de desperdiçar ferramentas que podem aumentar a sua eficiência económica e a sua autonomia estratégica.

O dossiê do 28.º regime deve ser rapidamente retomado pelas instituições europeias. Não sendo uma bala de prata, representa um sério passo em frente que deve ser dado por uma União que demasiadas vezes teima em ficar exatamente como está.
3-0032-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Colleagues, the single market is a European goal and the 28th regime is the best tool to achieve it.

I am talking to you about a regime that offers a pragmatic way to overcome the legal fragmentation that continues to limit the growth of European companies, in particular SMEs and start-ups. By allowing for an optional, uniform and directly applicable legal framework across the Union, it reduces administrative complexity, compliance costs and legal uncertainty, which currently hold back cross-border expansion. In a context of green and digital transition, and growing international competition, the Union cannot afford to waste tools that can increase its economic efficiency and strategic autonomy.

The 28th regime dossier must be quickly taken up by the European institutions. Not being a silver bullet, it represents a serious step forward that must be taken by a Union that too often insists on staying exactly as it is.

3-0033-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, het MFK staat eindelijk, zou ik zeggen, ook op de agenda van de Raad. We staan aan het begin van dit proces rond deze nieuwe meerjarenbegroting en de klassieke tegenstellingen en rode lijnen tekenen zich al af binnen de Raad, in de Commissie en ook in dit Parlement. We zouden echter best het klassieke debat overstijgen en de oefening niet beperken tot een droge discussie over meer of minder middelen.

Europa heeft in de eerste plaats nood aan bijkomende hervormingen die de efficiëntie verhogen, onze concurrentiekracht vergroten en de broodnodige investeringen aanmoedigen. De focus moet daarbij onder meer, maar zeker niet in het minst, liggen op de versterking van de interne markt, de volwaardige kapitaalmarktenunie en ook deregulering. Dit zijn, als je er even over nadenkt, hervormingen die weinig of geen geld kosten, maar die wel een hoog rendement hebben. Het debat overstijgt of zou het boekhoudkundig perspectief moeten overstijgen. Europa staat voor grote uitdagingen op het vlak van concurrentievermogen, veiligheid, defensie en geopolitiek. We pleiten voor een welomschreven prioriteitengeheel en hervormingen die toelaten een toekomstgerichte Europese begroting uit te bouwen.
3-0033-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the MFF is finally, I would say, also on the Council's agenda. We are at the beginning of this process surrounding this new multi-annual budget and the classic contradictions and red lines are already emerging within the Council, in the Commission and also in this Parliament. However, we would best go beyond the classic debate and not limit the exercise to a dry discussion about more or fewer resources.

Europe first and foremost needs additional reforms that increase efficiency, increase our competitiveness and encourage much-needed investment. The focus must be, among other things, but certainly not least, on strengthening the internal market, the fully-fledged capital markets union and also deregulation. If you think about it, these are reforms that cost little or no money, but have a high return. The debate transcends or should transcend the accounting perspective. Europe faces major challenges in the areas of competitiveness, security, defense and geopolitics. We argue for a well-defined set of priorities and reforms that allow the development of a future-oriented European budget.

3-0035-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjednice, povjereniče, zaključci Europskog vijeća jasno pokazuje da se Europa nalazi u odlučujućem trenutku.

Rasprava o novom proračunu nije samo rasprava o brojkama, već i rasprava o tome kakvu Europu želimo graditi u narednim godinama. Stoga pozdravljam snažniji fokus na konkurentnost, na inovacije, na otpornost europskoga gospodarstva. Međutim, moramo osigurati da novi Europski fond za konkurentnost mora biti otvoren za sve i da ne smije produbiti razlike između država članica koje već danas imaju snažne inovacijske kapacitete i onih koje ih tek razvijaju. Ne smijemo ponoviti situaciju koju danas imamo u programu Obzor Europa, gdje svega šest država članica koristi 70 % sredstava.

A danas govorimo o Europi koja može biti konkurentna i mora biti globalno konkurentna samo ako raste zajedno: sjever i jug, istok i zapad.
3-0035-0000.englishText:
Dear President, Commissioner, the conclusions of the European Council clearly show that Europe is at a decisive moment.

The discussion on the new budget is not only a discussion about numbers, but also a discussion about what kind of Europe we want to build in the coming years. Therefore, I welcome a stronger focus on competitiveness, on innovation, on the resilience of the European economy. However, we must ensure that the new European Competitiveness Fund must be open to everyone and must not deepen the differences between member states that already have strong innovation capacities today and those that are still developing them. We must not repeat the situation we have today in the Horizon Europe program, where only six member states use 70% of the funds.

And today we are talking about a Europe that can be competitive and must be globally competitive only if it grows together: north and south, east and west.

3-0036-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, un debate sobre las conclusiones del Consejo Europeo sin el Consejo es absolutamente inaceptable. Dígaselo y trasládele tres mensajes.

En primer lugar: apoyo a Ucrania, por supuesto. Pero cuando llegue el momento de la negociación de la paz, Europa tiene que asegurarse de estar en la mesa y no en el menú.

En segundo lugar: responsabilidades de Rusia. Para eso hace falta apoyar la activación del estatuto de bloqueo para proteger a los jueces de la Corte Penal Internacional que están siendo unilateralmente sancionados por el Gobierno de Trump de los Estados Unidos.

Y en tercer lugar, un mensaje muy claro: hemos aprobado en este Pleno del Parlamento Europeo una nueva extensión de la derogación temporal de la ePrivacy. ¿Por qué lo hemos hecho? Porque el Consejo no ha hecho todavía su trabajo de aprobar de una vez el Reglamento que el Parlamento Europeo aprobó la pasada legislatura contra los delitos sexuales contra los menores en línea. Es el momento de hacerlo. Trasládele ese mensaje, comisario Šefčovič.
3-0036-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, a debate on the conclusions of the European Council without the Council is absolutely unacceptable. Tell him and send him three messages.

First of all: support for Ukraine, of course. But when the time comes for peace negotiations, Europe has to make sure it is at the table and not on the menu.

Secondly: Russia's responsibilities. For this, it is necessary to support the activation of the blocking statute to protect the judges of the International Criminal Court who are being unilaterally sanctioned by the Trump Government of the United States.

And thirdly, a very clear message: we have approved in this plenary session of the European Parliament a new extension of the temporary repeal of ePrivacy. Why have we done it? Because the Council has not yet done its job of approving once and for all the Regulation that the European Parliament approved last term against sexual crimes against minors online. It's time to do it. Pass that message on to him, Commissioner Šefčovič.

3-0037-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, waar is het Ierse voorzitterschap hier? We hebben gesproken over nieuwe aanvallen op schepen in de Straat van Hormuz. De meststoffencrisis kan weer verergeren. Onze voedselzekerheid komt in gevaar, maar de Commissie en de Raad weigeren en talmen met het herzien van de nitraatrichtlijn. Wanneer kunnen we die tegemoetzien? Dit huis heeft dat geëist.

Op het gebied van het MFK komt de Raad maar niet tot overeenstemming. De voedselveiligheid en voedselzekerheid zijn in gevaar. Herstel landbouw en visserijsteun. Geef meer ruimte aan dierlijke mest. Stop de natuurherstelverordening: ons platteland en onze regio's dragen de last. Zet vaart achter de terugkeerhubs. Versterk Frontex en onze buitengrensbewaking: de instroom is te groot. De regio's en het platteland dragen de lasten van de Europese Spreidingswet en de nationale Nederlandse Spreidingswet. Commissie en Raad, kom in beweging, kom in actie. Bescherm onze buitengrenzen, bescherm ons platteland, bescherm onze voedselzekerheid.
3-0037-0000.englishText:
Mr President, where is the Irish Presidency here? We talked about new attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The fertilizer crisis could worsen again. Our food security is at risk, but the Commission and the Council refuse and delay in revising the Nitrates Directive. When can we expect that? This house has demanded that.

The Council is unable to reach agreement on the MFF. Food safety and food security are at risk. Restore agriculture and fisheries support. Give more space to animal manure. Stop the nature restoration ordinance: our countryside and our regions bear the burden. Speed ​​up the return hubs. Strengthen Frontex and our external border control: the influx is too great. The regions and the countryside bear the burden of the European Distribution Act and the national Dutch Distribution Act. Commission and Council, get moving, take action. Protect our external borders, protect our countryside, protect our food security.

3-0038-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, el Consejo Europeo cree en el derecho y en las reglas tanto como la FIFA.

Vivimos en un mundo de impunidad: Trump hace una llamada y se anula una tarjeta roja. Pero nosotros hacemos algo peor: no solo desobedecemos las resoluciones de los tribunales internacionales de justicia y de la ONU sobre nuestra obligación de frenar el genocidio, de dejar de vender armas, sino que hacemos lo contrario. Y todavía hay algo peor: permitimos que se persiga a esos funcionarios públicos, cooperamos con los Estados Unidos, sin ni tan siquiera haber recibido una llamada de Trump —o quizá nos ha llamado Trump—. La cuestión es que hay unas sanciones contra esos funcionarios públicos, hay una norma que se debe aplicar y no la estamos aplicando.

Trump es un cínico, pero nos dice la verdad. Nosotros somos unos hipócritas: decimos una cosa y hacemos la contraria.
3-0038-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the European Council believes in law and rules as much as FIFA.

We live in a world of impunity: Trump makes a call and a red card is annulled. But we do something worse: not only do we disobey the resolutions of the international courts of justice and the UN on our obligation to stop genocide, to stop selling weapons, but we do the opposite. And there is something even worse: we allow these public officials to be persecuted, we cooperate with the United States, without even having received a call from Trump — or perhaps Trump has called us. The point is that there are sanctions against these public officials, there is a rule that must be applied and we are not applying it.

Trump is a cynic, but he tells us the truth. We are hypocrites: we say one thing and do the opposite.

3-0039-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, la posición que ha adoptado el Consejo Europeo con respecto al marco financiero plurianual es sencillamente decepcionante.

Mientras Europa se enfrenta a enormes desafíos como la transición climática, la competitividad, la soberanía digital o el acceso a la vivienda, la respuesta que ha dado el Consejo ha sido recortar el presupuesto; es decir, una Europa más pequeña y sin capacidad de respuesta.

No podemos hacer más con menos. No podemos hablar de autonomía estratégica y, al mismo tiempo, renunciar al Fondo Social Europeo, a la PAC o a las políticas de cohesión. Y todo por una falta de valentía a la hora de aprobar y desbloquear un paquete de recursos propios que precisamente nos dé la capacidad de tener una posición política propia en un mundo cada vez más incierto, más violento y, sobre todo, más competitivo.

Por eso, desde el Parlamento le decimos al Consejo que Europa no se fortalece desde la renuncia, los recortes y la falta de ambición, sino que se construye con la solidaridad y con recursos suficientes para dar respuesta a lo que nos reclama la ciudadanía.
3-0039-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the position that the European Council has taken with regard to the multiannual financial framework is simply disappointing.

While Europe faces enormous challenges such as climate transition, competitiveness, digital sovereignty or access to housing, the Council's response has been to cut the budget; that is, a smaller Europe without the capacity to respond.

We cannot do more with less. We cannot talk about strategic autonomy and, at the same time, renounce the European Social Fund, the CAP or cohesion policies. And all because of a lack of courage when it comes to approving and unlocking a package of our own resources that precisely gives us the ability to have our own political position in an increasingly uncertain, more violent and, above all, more competitive world.

For this reason, from Parliament we tell the Council that Europe is not strengthened by resignation, cuts and lack of ambition, but rather it is built with solidarity and with sufficient resources to respond to what citizens demand of us.

3-0040-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, vă mulțumim pentru informațiile pe care ni le-ați adus, dar vreau să mă refer la câteva puncte.

În primul rând: CFM-ul. Domnule comisar, ați spus că sunt două niveluri. Nu este clar ce facem cu resursele proprii, pentru că noi, Parlamentul, am propus de foarte multe ori de unde pot veni aceste resurse noi pentru a nu avea un CFM mai mic, pentru a nu avea un buget mai mic - nici măcar cu inflația.

Apoi, competitivitatea: o Europă și o piață. Ați spus decalajul comercial cu China, dar ce facem pentru competitivitate? Pentru că dacă vrem să susținem industria, așa cum ați spus, atunci trebuie o revizuire a ETS și trebuie cu adevărat politici de susținere - nu numai a industriei siderurgice, dar a industriei și, bineînțeles, a agriculturii, pentru că securitatea alimentară este foarte importantă.

Practici comerciale neloiale. Păi da, dar avem acorduri în care puneți taxe vamale la materii prime mai mici decât la produsul finit, ceea ce este ilogic, pentru că producătorul din Europa nu o să poată să fie atunci competitiv. Așadar, eu cred că trebuie, domnule comisar - sigur, vine concediu - dar haideți să gândim cu adevărat un CFM care să ducă la competitivitate și la reindustrializarea Uniunii Europene.
3-0040-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, thank you for the information you have brought us, but I want to address a few points.

First: the CFM. Commissioner, you said there are two levels. It is not clear what we are doing with our own resources, because we, the Parliament, have proposed many times where these new resources can come from in order not to have a lower CFM, in order not to have a lower budget - not even with inflation.

Then, competitiveness: one Europe and one market. You mentioned the trade gap with China, but what are we doing for competitiveness? Because if we want to support industry, as you said, then we need a review of the ETS and we really need policies to support - not only the steel industry, but the industry and, of course, agriculture, because food security is very important.

Unfair commercial practices. Well, yes, but we have agreements where you put customs duties on raw materials lower than on the finished product, which is illogical, because the producer in Europe will then not be able to be competitive. So, I think we have to, Commissioner - sure, leave is coming - but let's really think about an MFF that will lead to competitiveness and the re-industrialisation of the European Union.

3-0041-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Bildung, Kultur, Wettbewerb, Sozialarbeit, Forschung, Verteidigung, Infrastruktur, Entwicklungszusammenarbeit. Aufgaben erfüllen – das wollen wir gut, aber wir kriegen dafür nicht mehr Mittel. Wenn wir uns einmal anschauen – der EU‑Haushalt, der jetzt angestrebt ist, ist nicht mal halb so groß wie der deutsche Bundeshaushalt.

Wenn wir eine handlungsfähige Europäische Union wollen, dann brauchen wir auch eine ordentliche Mittelausstattung. Horizontale Kürzungen anzustreben und die Kohäsionsmittel weiter runter zu kürzen, ist dabei das völlig falsche Signal. Es ist EU‑vertragsrechtlich geregelt, dass die Europäische Union in den Zusammenhalt der Mitgliedstaaten investiert. Mit diesen Kürzungen sorgen wir dafür, dass genau dieser Zusammenhalt in solchen herausfordernden Zeiten auseinanderdriftet; das können wir uns nicht leisten.

Wir wollen die Aufgaben gut erfüllen. Wir wollen eine handlungsfähige Union. Das bedeutet auch, dass die Mitgliedstaaten dazu angehalten werden müssen, diese Europäische Union mit ordentlichen finanziellen Mitteln auszustatten. Mitgliedstaaten müssen dafür sorgen, dass wir dieser Verantwortung gerecht werden und nicht weiter Kürzungen vorgenommen werden.
3-0041-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Education, culture, competition, social work, research, defense, infrastructure, development cooperation. Completing tasks is something we want to do well, but we don’t get more funding for it. If we look at it - the EU budget that is now being targeted is not even half as big as the German federal budget.

If we want a European Union that is capable of acting, then we also need proper funding. Aiming for horizontal cuts and further reducing the cohesion funds sends completely the wrong signal. It is regulated by EU treaty law that the European Union invests in the cohesion of the member states. With these cuts we are ensuring that precisely this solidarity is drifting apart in such challenging times; we can't afford that.

We want to complete the tasks well. We want a Union that is able to act. This also means that the Member States must be encouraged to provide this European Union with proper financial resources. Member States must ensure that we live up to this responsibility and that no further cuts are made.

3-0042-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je n’ai pas grand-chose à dire – il y aurait trop de choses à dire, à vrai dire – sur les sujets abordés. Je voudrais simplement dire à mes collègues que je suis choquée par le peu de députés présents dans notre hémicycle.

Je veux le redire: Mme la Présidente a essayé de mettre en place un certain nombre de mesures. C’est extrêmement préoccupant, y compris pour nos concitoyens. Les sujets abordés sont décisifs. Hier, nous parlions de la cybersécurité, de l’intelligence artificielle, et puis il y a tant de domaines qui sont importants, donc, s’il vous plaît, demandez à vos collègues d’être présents.

Ça a une importance, y compris pour l’image du Parlement vis-à-vis de la Commission européenne et du Conseil. Ensemble, soyons plus forts, mes chers collègues!
3-0042-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I do not have much to say – there would be too much to say, in fact – on the topics discussed. I would simply like to say to my colleagues that I am shocked by the few deputies present in our hemicycle.

I want to say it again: Madam President tried to put in place a certain number of measures. This is extremely worrying, including for our fellow citizens. The topics covered are decisive. Yesterday we were talking about cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and there are so many areas that are important, so please ask your colleagues to be present.

This is important, including for the image of Parliament vis-à-vis the European Commission and the Council. Together, let's be stronger, my dear colleagues!

3-0045-5000.sourceText:
Rada Europejska po raz kolejny próbuje pogodzić rzeczy, których pogodzić się nie da. Z jednej strony mówi o potrzebie obniżania cen energii, odbudowie europejskiego przemysłu, konkurencyjności i zmniejszaniu zależności. Z drugiej strony wzywa do przyspieszenia dekarbonizacji i podtrzymuje zasadniczą rolę systemu ETS.

To jest właśnie źródło problemu.

Nie można jednocześnie żądać tańszej energii i przyspieszać polityki, która sztucznie podnosi jej cenę. Nie można mówić o reindustrializacji Europy i nakładać na europejskie przedsiębiorstwa kolejne koszty emisji. Nie można mówić o konkurencji ze Stanami Zjednoczonymi i Chinami, gdy sami świadomie pogarszamy warunki działania własnego przemysłu.

ETS stał się dodatkowym podatkiem od europejskiej produkcji, energii i inwestycji.

Przegląd wskaźników czy korekta zasad bezpłatnych uprawnień nie rozwiążą problemu, jeżeli sam mechanizm nadal będzie windował koszty działalności w Europie. W efekcie produkcja przenosi się tam, gdzie energię i emisje reguluje się rozsądniej. A razem z nią znikają miejsca pracy, inwestycje i potencjał rozwojowy naszych państw.

Europa musi wreszcie zatrzymać tę gospodarczą autodestrukcję.

Potrzebujemy taniej energii, neutralności technologicznej i realnej odbudowy przemysłu. Najpierw konkurencyjność, inwestycje i bezpieczeństwo gospodarcze.

Dekarbonizacja nie może odbywać się za cenę likwidacji miejsc pracy i wyprowadzania produkcji poza Unię.”
3-0045-5000.englishText:
The European Council is once again trying to reconcile the irreconcilable. On the one hand, it talks about the need to reduce energy prices, rebuild European industry, competitiveness and reduce dependencies. On the other hand, it calls for the acceleration of decarbonization and maintains the essential role of the ETS.

This is the source of the problem.

You cannot simultaneously demand cheaper energy and accelerate policies that artificially raise its price. We cannot talk about the reindustrialization of Europe and impose further emission costs on European companies. We cannot talk about competition with the United States and China when we consciously worsen the operating conditions of our own industry.

The ETS has become an additional tax on European production, energy and investment.

A review of indicators or a correction of the rules for free allowances will not solve the problem if the mechanism itself continues to increase the costs of operating in Europe. As a result, production is moved to where energy and emissions are regulated more sensibly. And with it, jobs, investments and the development potential of our countries disappear.

Europe must finally stop this economic self-destruction.

We need cheap energy, technological neutrality and real industrial reconstruction. First, competitiveness, investment and economic security.

Decarbonization cannot take place at the price of eliminating jobs and moving production outside the EU.

3-0048-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: JAVI LÓPEZ

Vice-President
3-0048-0000.englishText:
IN THE CHAIR: JAVI LÓPEZ

Vice-President

3-0055-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, señor presidente en ejercicio del Consejo, en primer lugar, me gustaría decir que estamos encantados en este Parlamento de pertenecer al Intergrupo sobre Resiliencia, Gestión de Catástrofes y Protección Civil, que está dando lugar a muchas cuestiones importantes sobre nuevas tecnologías y posibilidades para el futuro.

Por tanto, en estos momentos, este Parlamento está trabajando —y seguiremos trabajando con ahínco— en un momento difícil para los países, en el que el cambio climático está produciendo olas de calor muy dificultosas, tanto en mi país, donde hay 57 focos de incendio activos en estos momentos —en Cataluña, Andalucía—, así como en otros países de la Unión Europea de forma importante. Se trata de una crisis humanitaria y de protección civil muy importante y de un golpe al mundo rural en un momento muy crítico.

Por eso, tenemos que trabajar con seriedad y sin dogmatismo ideológico, es decir, trabajar en la prevención y trabajar también en las medidas. La Comisión Europea ha puesto a disposición el mayor dispositivo de la historia con 777 bomberos en 14 Estados y el refuerzo del rescEU y de la protección civil y los fondos que tienen que ver con ello.

Pero, en la prevención, ¿cómo lo tenemos que hacer? Hemos perdido una oportunidad única con NextGenerationEU y el Mecanismo de Recuperación y Resiliencia, porque son fondos fundamentales que deberían haberse destinado a la prevención. En cambio, países como el nuestro no han aprovechado lo suficiente estos fondos en este caso. Se renunció incluso a la compra de diez aviones de extinción de incendios en 2023. Esto es un error mayúsculo que luego se paga. Por tanto, por un lado, hay que aprovechar los fondos para los medios, pero también hay que simplificar.

Y termino con esto: flexibilizar directivas que impidan labores tradicionales como la silvicultura, el pastoreo conducido, la caza sostenible o la agricultura sostenible en algunas zonas es esencial para prevenir. Echar del campo a la gente o a la vida —como antaño— que respetaba la cuestión de la naturaleza es un error, porque sobreprotege y, al final, tarde o temprano, son pasto de las llamas.
3-0055-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, Mr President-in-Office of the Council, first of all, I would like to say that we are delighted in this Parliament to belong to the Intergroup on Resilience, Disaster Management and Civil Protection, which is raising many important questions about new technologies and possibilities for the future.

Therefore, at the moment, this Parliament is working - and we will continue to work hard - at a difficult time for countries, in which climate change is producing very difficult heat waves, both in my country, where there are 57 active fire outbreaks at the moment - in Catalonia, Andalusia - as well as in other countries of the European Union to a significant extent. This is a very important humanitarian and civil protection crisis and a blow to the rural world at a very critical moment.

Therefore, we have to work seriously and without ideological dogmatism, that is, work on prevention and also work on measures. The European Commission has made available the largest device in history with 777 firefighters in 14 States and the reinforcement of rescEU and civil protection and the funds that have to do with it.

But, in prevention, how should we do it? We have missed a unique opportunity with NextGenerationEU and the Recovery and Resilience Facility, because they are vital funds that should have been allocated to prevention. On the other hand, countries like ours have not taken sufficient advantage of these funds in this case. The purchase of ten firefighting aircraft in 2023 was even renounced. This is a major mistake that will later be paid for. Therefore, on the one hand, we must take advantage of media funds, but we must also simplify.

And I end with this: relaxing directives that prevent traditional tasks such as forestry, managed grazing, sustainable hunting or sustainable agriculture in some areas is essential to prevent. Throwing people or life out of the countryside—as in the past—that respected the issue of nature is a mistake, because it overprotects and, in the end, sooner or later, they become food for the flames.

3-0056-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, quiero comenzar con un agradecimiento a su persona por su compromiso en esta materia. Me consta el gran trabajo que está llevando a cabo y el trabajo que, durante el pasado verano, llevó a cabo para responder con solidaridad —que es como Europa tiene que hacerlo ante las desgracias—, en muchos países, como en mi propio país, España, donde usted estuvo en primera línea, apostando y apoyando todas las necesidades.

La realidad hoy es que hay más de 2 000 muertos en Francia, más de 1 200 en Bélgica, más de 1 000 en España y cerca de 500 en los Países Bajos. Miles de hectáreas calcinadas en Francia, Portugal y España. Carreteras que se derriten. Vías ferroviarias deformadas. Infraestructuras que dejan de funcionar.

Esto no son eslóganes, son los hechos: la realidad letal del cambio climático. Y mientras Europa enterraba a sus muertos, un ministro de la extrema derecha, aquí en Europa, se permitía bromear en las redes sociales sobre el calor, presumiendo —desde su piscina— con una cervecita bien fresca. Ese mensaje fue infame, porque cuando se frivoliza con la emergencia climática se alimenta la inacción y la inacción mata.

Por eso, hoy quiero preguntar al Partido Popular y a los falsos patriotas de la extrema derecha: ¿qué informes manejan ustedes para seguir negando el cambio climático? ¿Qué evidencia científica les permite justificar que hay que desmantelar, precisamente, las políticas que salvan vidas? Porque cada vez que atacan el Pacto Verde Europeo, cada vez que intentan acabar con el principio de «no causar un perjuicio significativo» y cada vez que debilitan la lucha contra la deforestación, ponen vidas en riesgo.

El Pacto Verde Europeo no es una carga, es nuestro escudo, es el mejor seguro de vida de los europeos, porque proteger su salud, proteger su poder adquisitivo, su empleo y su soberanía es lo que consigue el Pacto Verde Europeo. Necesitamos acelerar las energías renovables, porque es la energía más limpia y también la más barata que se puede producir.

Mitigar ya no basta, tenemos que adaptarnos. Y por eso exigimos una ley vinculante para proteger a los trabajadores expuestos al calor extremo dentro de la futura Ley de Empleo de Calidad. Y exigimos también un auténtico plan europeo de adaptación al cambio climático.

Europa no puede seguir esperando. Estamos negociando el próximo presupuesto europeo y en esa negociación se está decidiendo quién quiere invertir para proteger a las personas y quién prefiere recortar los instrumentos que las protegen, quién quiere reforzar la acción climática y quién sigue empeñado en debilitarla.

He comenzado esta intervención hablando de miles de ciudadanos que han perdido la vida y, precisamente por ellos, nuestro deber es conseguir que el próximo verano no tengamos que comenzar con este debate.

Defender el Pacto Verde Europeo es defender vidas, defender las renovables es defender la libertad en Europa y defender la transición justa es, sencillamente, defender a los europeos.
3-0056-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Madam Commissioner, I would like to begin by thanking you for your commitment to this matter. I am aware of the great work you are carrying out and the work that, last summer, you carried out to respond with solidarity - which is how Europe has to do in the face of misfortunes - in many countries, such as in my own country, Spain, where you were on the front line, supporting and supporting all needs.

The reality today is that there are more than 2,000 dead in France, more than 1,200 in Belgium, more than 1,000 in Spain and close to 500 in the Netherlands. Thousands of hectares burned in France, Portugal and Spain. Melting roads. Deformed railway tracks. Infrastructures that stop working.

These are not slogans, these are the facts: the lethal reality of climate change. And while Europe was burying its dead, a far-right minister, here in Europe, allowed himself to joke on social media about the heat, showing off—from his pool—with a very cool beer. That message was infamous, because when the climate emergency is trivialized, inaction is fueled and inaction kills.

Therefore, today I want to ask the Popular Party and the false patriots of the extreme right: what reports do you use to continue denying climate change? What scientific evidence allows them to justify that precisely the policies that save lives must be dismantled? Because every time they attack the European Green Deal, every time they try to end the principle of “do no significant harm” and every time they weaken the fight against deforestation, they put lives at risk.

The European Green Deal is not a burden, it is our shield, it is the best life insurance for Europeans, because protecting their health, protecting their purchasing power, their employment and their sovereignty is what the European Green Deal achieves. We need to accelerate renewable energy, because it is the cleanest and also the cheapest energy that can be produced.

Mitigating is no longer enough, we have to adapt. And that is why we demand a binding law to protect workers exposed to extreme heat within the future Quality Employment Law. And we also demand an authentic European plan for adaptation to climate change.

Europe cannot continue waiting. We are negotiating the next European budget and in that negotiation it is being decided who wants to invest to protect people and who prefers to cut the instruments that protect them, who wants to strengthen climate action and who remains committed to weakening it.

I began this intervention by talking about thousands of citizens who have lost their lives and, precisely because of them, our duty is to ensure that next summer we do not have to start this debate.

Defending the European Green Deal is defending lives, defending renewables is defending freedom in Europe and defending the just transition is, simply, defending Europeans.

3-0058-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signor Presidente del Consiglio, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, io ritengo che non possiamo perdere l'occasione di questo dibattito scendendo in questioni di ordine ideologico, perché la prevenzione – e la strategia per la prevenzione che si è data anche l'Unione europea – è la prima risposta che si deve dare a fenomeni come quello che abbiamo vissuto nelle settimane scorse e che assai verosimilmente vivremo nel corso di tutta l'estate.

Prevenzione anzitutto sotto il profilo sanitario, e bene hanno fatto quegli Stati membri – penso all'Italia – che hanno saputo dare sul fronte sanitario delle direttive chiare a tutte le Regioni per occuparsi in primo luogo degli anziani e della solitudine.

In secondo luogo, prevenzione significa adattare al cambiamento del clima le nostre infrastrutture, sia quelle energetiche sia quelle che si occupano della socialità. Ma prevenzione significa mettere in primo luogo la necessità che ogni investimento venga diretto per evitare che si possano verificare fenomeni che hanno un impatto sulla vita di ogni cittadino.

Vedete, Presidente e colleghi che siete intervenuti anche prima di me, l'adattamento al cambiamento climatico non vuol dire che l'uomo è una presenza non gradita nel sistema dell'ambiente. Adattamento al clima vuol dire che gli Stati – ciascun governo – devono saper adottare delle politiche e mettere a frutto gli investimenti che sono disponibili.

Allora il nostro dibattito anche su questo tema diventerà un dibattito seriamente sensato: abbandonare ogni approccio ideologico, concentrarsi – io apprezzo molto il lavoro che sta svolgendo la Commissaria – su temi pragmatici e pratici, che partono da regole che devono essere condivise.
3-0058-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr President of the Council, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, I believe that we cannot miss the opportunity for this debate by descending into questions of an ideological nature, because prevention - and the strategy for prevention which the European Union has also adopted - is the first response that must be given to phenomena such as what we have experienced in recent weeks and which we will very likely experience throughout the summer.

Prevention first and foremost from a health perspective, and those Member States - I am thinking of Italy - have done well by being able to give clear directives to all the Regions on the health front to deal primarily with the elderly and loneliness.

Secondly, prevention means adapting our infrastructures to climate change, both energy ones and those dealing with social issues. But prevention means putting first and foremost the need for every investment to be directed to prevent phenomena from occurring that have an impact on the life of every citizen.

You see, President and colleagues who spoke before me, adaptation to climate change does not mean that man is an unwelcome presence in the environmental system. Climate adaptation means that states - each government - must be able to adopt policies and make the most of the investments that are available.

Then our debate on this issue too will become a seriously sensible debate: abandon any ideological approach, concentrate - I greatly appreciate the work that the Commissioner is carrying out - on pragmatic and practical issues, which start from rules that must be shared.

3-0059-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, je voulais tout d’abord m’adresser à vous: merci pour l’engagement que vous avez dans cette politique de protection civile et la défense d’un monde qui se mobilise en ce moment.

Dans mon pays, plus de 15 000 hectares sont partis en fumée: c’est trois fois plus que l’an dernier à la même période. Je voulais remercier l’ensemble des députés qui sont engagés également dans l’intergroupe de protection civile. Ces éléments-là font l’actualité, mais vous êtes toujours là, également, à nos côtés, pour défendre cette politique aux côtés de Hadja Lahbib.

Le climat accélère, mais notre réponse, elle, reste trop lente. Nous ne pouvons pas davantage choisir entre atténuation et adaptation. Il faut combiner les deux politiques, c’est certain. Les feux de forêt ne sont plus seulement une conséquence du dérèglement climatique: ils en deviennent un accélérateur, parce que, lorsqu’une forêt brûle, elle rejette du carbone, et en plus elle ne peut plus en absorber.

Les fumées tuent, la canicule aussi. En 2003, il y a plus de vingt ans, nous disions: «Plus jamais cela!» Pour autant, depuis quarante ans ou presque sapeur-pompier, je suis sûr qu’à l’automne la plupart des décideurs politiques auront oublié l’émotion que suscite finalement cette situation.

La préparation ne peut plus être une politique d’urgence. Ce doit être un élément porté chaque jour, une politique d’anticipation portée par chaque citoyen, chaque entreprise, chacun d’entre nous.

Monsieur le Président, laissez-moi encore quelques secondes. Je viens d’apprendre, il y a quelques minutes, le décès d’un jeune sapeur-pompier volontaire, en France, qui luttait contre un feu. Nous ne sommes que début juillet. L’été sera compliqué…

(Le Président retire la parole à l’orateur)
3-0059-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I wanted first of all to address you: thank you for the commitment you have to this civil protection policy and the defense of a world which is mobilizing at the moment.

In my country, more than 15,000 hectares went up in smoke: that’s three times more than last year at the same period. I wanted to thank all the deputies who are also involved in the civil protection intergroup. These elements make the news, but you are also still there, alongside us, to defend this policy alongside Hadja Lahbib.

The climate is accelerating, but our response remains too slow. Nor can we choose between mitigation and adaptation. We need to combine the two policies, that’s for sure. Forest fires are no longer just a consequence of climate change: they become an accelerator of it, because when a forest burns, it releases carbon, and what's more, it can no longer absorb it.

The smoke kills, and so does the heatwave. In 2003, more than twenty years ago, we said: “Never again!” However, for almost forty years as a firefighter, I am sure that by the fall most political decision-makers will have forgotten the emotion that this situation ultimately arouses.

Preparedness can no longer be an emergency policy. It must be an element carried out every day, a policy of anticipation carried by each citizen, each company, each of us.

Mr. President, give me a few more seconds. I just learned, a few minutes ago, of the death of a young volunteer firefighter, in France, who was fighting a fire. It's only the beginning of July. Summer will be complicated...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

3-0062-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, en Europe, moins d’un foyer sur cinq est équipé d’un climatiseur. Aux États-Unis et au Japon, neuf foyers sur dix en possèdent. Et pourtant, avec l’argent du contribuable, nous sommes tellement riches que nous climatisons le monde entier. L’Agence française de développement prête 20 millions d’euros pour rénover la climatisation d’une banque en Thaïlande, elle verse 7 millions pour équiper des bâtiments administratifs à Djibouti, elle installe des climatiseurs à technologie Inverter dans les dispensaires du Sénégal. Quant à l’Europe, elle offre 11 climatiseurs à un service de pédiatrie du Monténégro, elle prête 40 millions d’euros pour climatiser un hôpital neuf de 250 lits en Turquie, elle cofinance la climatisation des hôpitaux tunisiens de Gafsa et de Sidi Bouzid.

Vous financez le confort thermique à l’autre bout du monde pendant que vous expliquez aux Européens qu’ils doivent souffrir en silence et sans clim parce que ça pollue. Alors, assez de vos leçons de morale! Assez de vos gabegies! Ce n’est pas votre argent, c’est celui des Européens.
3-0062-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, in Europe, less than one in five homes is equipped with an air conditioner. In the United States and Japan, nine out of ten households have them. And yet, with taxpayers' money, we are so rich that we air-condition the entire world. The French Development Agency lends 20 million euros to renovate the air conditioning of a bank in Thailand, it pays 7 million to equip administrative buildings in Djibouti, it installs inverter technology air conditioners in dispensaries in Senegal. As for Europe, it offers 11 air conditioners to a pediatric department in Montenegro, it lends 40 million euros to air condition a new 250-bed hospital in Turkey, it co-finances the air conditioning of the Tunisian hospitals of Gafsa and Sidi Bouzid.

You finance thermal comfort on the other side of the world while you explain to Europeans that they must suffer in silence and without air conditioning because it pollutes. So, enough of your moral lessons! Enough of your mismanagement! It’s not your money, it’s the Europeans’.

3-0063-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, first of all, I would like to thank you all for your constructive and positive contribution to this debate so far. What I've heard is really encouraging. I think that we are all on the same page that we need to work without ideology. And what I've heard so far nearly goes far beyond ideology.

Because indeed, as you rightly say, Ms García Pérez, this is the lethal reality of climate change that we are facing today. And we cannot deny this reality. That's why also I count on your support for the negotiation of the next MFF. We propose, on behalf of the Commission, a very ambitious budget, to have a EU CPM here – a comprehensive manner to respond to the climate change and to the risks we are facing today.

You've raised the importance of helping the people who live in rural areas. Yes, people and local communities play a major role in wildfire risk prevention and management. The share of wildfire ignition caused by human activity in the EU by far exceeds those from natural causes and could be as high as 96 % – 96 % caused by human activity.

Complementing the preparedness union strategy, the Commission today proposes to promote and disseminate good practices in wildfire risk assessment and awareness and community involvement, for example through the EU CPM Knowledge Network, develop a toolkit for supporting resilience-building and promote volunteering and exchange opportunities in the field of preparedness.

We are working also with Member States on guidelines to increase awareness about risks and threats, with particular attention to ensuring that information is accessible, inclusive and adapted to the needs of groups at risk.

I totally agree that EU CPM, our mechanism of civil protection, is European solidarity at its best, and we need to develop it further. That is why we presented one year ago our new preparedness strategy. We will present also, as requested by Mr Knotek, a climate adaptation plan that will be presented by Commissioner Hoekstra in autumn.

Yes, I totally agree that the first responders are always Member States. They are the ones who need to spend the money and the budget we allocate on the right funds. That is why also we need to adapt our cities with the RFF, for instance, or the solidarity funds, because we must protect our citizens and particularly those living also in urban areas by making our cities, buildings and public spaces more resilient.

Finally, I will respond to Mr Allione.

Si nous avons aujourd’hui le cœur lourd en raison du nombre de morts qui ne cesse d’augmenter – je regardais hier encore dans le journal tous ces citoyens qui refusent de quitter leur village dans le sud de la France parce qu’ils y sont attachés, parce qu’ils y sont nés, parce qu’ils veulent y voir grandir leurs enfants et aussi parce qu’ils veulent contribuer, même avec parfois des bouteilles d’eau simplement, à réduire l’ampleur des feux –, nous ne sommes pas à un moment où il faut pleurer, où il faut présenter nos condoléances. Même si nous avons le cœur lourd, nous devons absolument agir!

Et nous ne cessons d’agir, vous le savez: nous avons activé le mécanisme déjà de nombreuses fois depuis le début de la saison, qui a commencé fin avril. Jamais la «saison des feux», comme on l’appelle malheureusement maintenant, n’a commencé aussi tôt. Et oui, quand il s’agit de reconnaître le statut des volontaires et des pompiers, nous y travaillons, même si cela ressort plutôt de la compétence de la commissaire Mînzatu.

Nous avons aujourd’hui, pour la première fois, des échanges de jeunes sapeurs-pompiers, de jeunes volontaires qui ont lieu à Varsovie. Ce n’est jamais arrivé avant. Nous voulons aussi contribuer à créer de la prise de conscience, à avoir une nouvelle génération, qui est plus à même de répondre à ces dangers et à ce réchauffement climatique.

3-0066-0000.sourceText:
Ana Miguel Pedro (PPE). – Senhor Presidente, a União Europeia já conta este ano com mais de 118 000 hectares ardidos até ao início de julho, acima da média dos últimos 20 anos.

Portugal sabe que estes números não são abstrações. Sabe o que significa ver aldeias cercadas pelas chamas, sabe o que significa retirar populações à pressa, o que significa perder casas, empresas, explorações agrícolas, floresta, solo fértil e memória coletiva.

Pela primeira vez em Portugal, a participação das Forças Armadas na prevenção e combate direto aos incêndios é um sinal de compromisso e prontidão. Mostra que Portugal mobiliza todos os instrumentos do Estado quando as populações estão em risco.

Mas se um Estado-Membro precisa de mobilizar todos os seus meios nacionais tão cedo no verão, então a União Europeia tem de responder com outra escala. É justo reconhecer que a União Europeia avançou. Mas sejamos claros, já não basta. A Europa tem de deixar de chegar quando o país já está exausto, tem de chegar antes.

Por isso, desafio a Comissão Europeia a ir mais longe. Precisamos de transformar o RescEU numa verdadeira força permanente europeia de combate a incêndios, com meios aéreos próprios, com brigadas multinacionais e com pré-posicionamento automático nas regiões de maior risco.

Desafio também a Comissão a mudar a lógica do financiamento europeu. A prevenção tem de ser uma prioridade central do próximo orçamento europeu: gestão de combustível, cadastro, caminhos florestais, pontos de água, apoio ao mundo rural e tecnologia de deteção precoce.
