E precisamos de justiça mais firme: a resposta penal não pode ser simbólica.

Temos verões cada vez mais longos, mais secos e mais extremos. A escala da ameaça mudou, a resposta europeia tem de mudar também.

(A oradora recusa uma pergunta «cartão azul» de João Oliveira)
3-0066-0000.englishText:
Ana Miguel Pedro (PPE). – Mr President, the European Union already has more than 118,000 hectares burnt this year by the beginning of July, above the average of the last 20 years.

Portugal knows that these numbers are not abstractions. You know what it means to see villages surrounded by flames, you know what it means to hurriedly remove populations, what it means to lose homes, businesses, farms, forests, fertile soil and collective memory.

For the first time in Portugal, the participation of the Armed Forces in preventing and directly fighting fires is a sign of commitment and readiness. It shows that Portugal mobilizes all State instruments when populations are at risk.

But if a Member State needs to mobilize all its national resources so early in the summer, then the European Union must respond on a different scale. It is fair to recognize that the European Union has moved forward. But let's be clear, it's not enough anymore. Europe must stop arriving when the country is already exhausted, it must arrive sooner.

Therefore, I challenge the European Commission to go further. We need to transform RescEU into a true permanent European firefighting force, with its own air assets, with multinational brigades and with automatic pre-positioning in the highest risk regions.

I also challenge the Commission to change the logic of European financing. Prevention must be a central priority of the next European budget: fuel management, registration, forestry paths, water points, support for rural areas and early detection technology.

And we need firmer justice: the criminal response cannot be symbolic.

We have increasingly longer, drier and more extreme summers. The scale of the threat has changed, the European response must change too.

(The speaker refuses a “blue card” question from João Oliveira)

3-0067-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, tijdens de laatste hittegolf werd het voetbaltoernooi van mijn zoontje afgelast. Een enorme teleurstelling voor mijn zoon, maar het was simpelweg te warm om nog veilig te kunnen spelen. En met een knuffel kom je dan al heel ver om die teleurstelling weg te nemen. Maar dat is natuurlijk klein leed, want op andere plekken in Europa gingen tijdens diezelfde hittegolf mensenlevens verloren en bosbranden verwoestten complete gebieden.

En toch blijven rechtse partijen in dit huis, in het Parlement stemmen tegen verduurzaming, tegen vergroening, en klimaatmaatregelen vertragen en fossiele belangen beschermen. Ik vraag me echt af: wanneer houdt het op? Bij tienduizend doden, bij honderdduizend doden? Wanneer stoppen we met die cognitieve dissonantie? Wanneer erkennen klimaatontkenners en partijen die hen napraten dat dit een probleem is van vandaag en niet pas van morgen? We weten wat er moet gebeuren. We moeten stoppen met fossiele subsidies. We moeten die energietransitie versnellen. Ik vraag maar één ding: bescherm onze mensen tegen hitte.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
3-0067-0000.englishText:
Mr President, during the last heat wave, my son's football tournament was cancelled. A huge disappointment for my son, but it was simply too hot to play safely. And a hug goes a long way to take away that disappointment. But that is of course a small matter, because in other places in Europe lives were lost during the same heat wave and forest fires destroyed entire areas.

And yet right-wing parties in this house, in Parliament, continue to vote against sustainability, against greening, and delay climate measures and protect fossil interests. I really wonder: when will it end? With ten thousand deaths, with a hundred thousand deaths? When do we stop with this cognitive dissonance? When will climate deniers and parties that parrot them recognize that this is a problem of today and not just tomorrow? We know what needs to be done. We must stop fossil subsidies. We must accelerate that energy transition. I ask only one thing: protect our people from heat.

(The speaker agrees to answer a “blue card” question)

3-0068-0000.sourceText: Taip, gerbiamas pranešėjau. Jūs, socialdemokratai, labai kovojate su klimato kaita, su CO2, kad būtų nulinis CO2 išmetimas. Ir čia Europa tikrai padarė didelę pažangą. Pramonė, faktiškai, galima sakyti, stagnuoja, CO2 mažiau išmetama, bet Europa labiausiai kenčia nuo karščių. Ką jūs ne taip darote?
3-0068-0000.englishText: Yes, dear reporter. You social democrats fight hard against climate change, against CO2, to zero CO2 emissions. And here Europe has really made great progress. The industry, in fact, one can say, is stagnating, CO2 emissions are lower, but Europe suffers the most from the heat. What are you doing wrong?

3-0070-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Rendkívüli aszállyal nézünk szembe. A Copernicus aszálymegfigyelő adatai szerint júniusban tovább romlott a helyzet, ami azt is jelenti, hogy riasztási szintű aszály alakult ki többek között Németországban, Franciaországban, de Magyarországon is. Az én hazámban áprilisban a szokásos csapadékmennyiségnek csak a tizede hullott, 4 mm. 2021. óta akkora csapadékhiány halmozódott fel, mint a teljes évnyi csapadékmennyiség. Ennyinek felel meg. Jelentős beruházásokra van szükség a vízvisszatartás és az öntözött területek növelése érdekében, de ehhez uniós forrásokra is szükség van. Ehhez képest az Európai Bizottság 20%-kal megvágná az agrárkasszát a hétéves költségvetésben.

Sokan kérjük arra az Európai Bizottságot, hogy változtasson ezen, biztosítson külön forrásokat, ne csak a vízvisszatartásra, létesítményfejlesztésre, hanem az öntözésfejlesztésre is. Utóbbi ugyanis nagyon kis hangsúlyt kap a Bizottság terveiben. Ha nem lesz elég víz, akkor nem lesz élelmiszerbiztonság sem, pláne nem megfizethető áron.

(A felszólaló hajlandó válaszolni egy kékkártyás kérdésre)
3-0070-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr. President! We are facing an extraordinary crisis. According to the data of the Copernicus drought monitor, the situation worsened in June, which also means that an alarm-level drought has developed in Germany, France, and Hungary as well. In my country, only a tenth of the usual amount of precipitation fell in April, 4 mm. Since 2021, as much precipitation deficit as the entire year's precipitation has accumulated. That's what it amounts to. Significant investments are needed to increase water retention and irrigated areas, but this also requires EU funds. In comparison, the European Commission would cut the agricultural fund by 20% in the seven-year budget.

Many of us are asking the European Commission to change this, to provide separate resources, not only for water retention and facility development, but also for irrigation development. The latter receives very little emphasis in the Commission's plans. If there is not enough water, there will be no food security, especially not at an affordable price.

(The speaker is willing to answer a blue card question)

3-0072-0000.sourceText: Köszönöm a kérdését. Azt hiszem, hogy a célban egyetértünk: abban, hogy a klímaváltozás következményei ellen fel kell lépni, de az, hogy hogyan kezeljük ezt, abban már eltérő megközelítéseink vannak. Önök, és mondhatom azt, hogy a baloldali nagykoalíció egy tervgazdasági megközelítéssel dolgoznak, ami azt jelenti, hogy olyan terveket tesznek kötelezővé, amelyekről nagyon hamar kiderül, hogy nem teljesülnek, és mindeközben nincsenek tekintettel arra, hogy milyen következményei vannak ezeknek a terveknek. Gondoljanak csak az autóiparra! Beletolták az európai autóipart kötelező tervekbe, kötelező átállásba, következésképp tönkremennek. A Volkswagen ennek is következményeként jelentette be, hogy százezer embertől válik meg, százezer munkahely szűnik meg, ez a következménye az Önök politikájának.
3-0072-0000.englishText: Thank you for your question. I think that we agree on the goal: that the consequences of climate change must be combated, but we already have different approaches to how to deal with it. You, and I can say that the left-wing grand coalition, work with a planned economy approach, which means that they make plans mandatory, which very quickly turn out not to be fulfilled, and meanwhile they do not take into account the consequences of these plans. Just think of the automotive industry! They pushed the European car industry into mandatory plans, mandatory transition, and as a result they are going to ruin. As a consequence of this, Volkswagen also announced that it will lose 100,000 people, 100,000 jobs, this is a consequence of your policy.

3-0073-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, în ultimele săptămâni, Europa a ars și s-a inundat în același timp. Franța, Spania și Italia au înregistrat temperaturi de peste 38 de grade. România a fost lovită de furtuni violente, inundații și distrugeri. Răspunsul Uniunii Europene rămâne însă prea des unul birocratic. Vorbim despre obiective pentru anul 2050, în timp ce oamenii au nevoie de soluții astăzi.

Pactul verde a rămas un exercițiu birocratic construit pe reguli multe și costuri mari pentru cetățeni și industrie - contrazis de știință. Un raport recent arată că reducerea aerosolilor proveniți din arderea cărbunelui a contribuit la creșterea încălzirii globale cu 1 grad Celsius în orașele europene. Asta în condițiile în care Uniunea Europeană a împovărat industria europeană, a crescut costul vieții, a diminuat competitivitatea economiei noastre.

Cetățenii Europei nu mai au nevoie de promisiuni pentru 2050. Și încă un lucru: încercarea de a introduce „cu ligheanul lumină în casa fără ferestre” nu e știință - este prostie în stare pură.
3-0073-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, in the last few weeks, Europe has burned and flooded at the same time. France, Spain and Italy recorded temperatures above 38 degrees. Romania was hit by violent storms, floods and destruction. However, the European Union's response too often remains a bureaucratic one. We are talking about goals for the year 2050, while people need solutions today.

The Green Deal remained a bureaucratic exercise built on many rules and high costs for citizens and industry - contradicted by science. A recent report shows that reducing aerosols from burning coal contributed to a 1 degree Celsius increase in global warming in European cities. This in the conditions in which the European Union burdened the European industry, increased the cost of living, decreased the competitiveness of our economy.

The citizens of Europe no longer need promises for 2050. And one more thing: trying to "bring light into the house without windows" is not science - it is pure stupidity.

3-0074-0000.sourceText:
Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem. Ako je možné, že v roku 2026 sú v Európe krajiny, kde nemocnice nemajú klimatizáciu, kde je počas horúčav 42 stupňov na izbe? Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré ani nerátajú, nerátajú úmrtia kvôli horúčavám? Čiže ani nevieme, koľko ľudí vlastne zomrelo. Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré majú ministrov, ktorí sa zrazu zobudili do toho, že existuje zmena klímy, a nepočúvali o tom posledných 30 rokov? A potom, potom budeme počúvať o tom, že za všetko zlé môže Brusel. Ten zlý magický Brusel. A pritom v mnohých členských krajinách stále stovkami miliónov, miliardami, dotujeme fosílnu ideológiu, dotujeme fosílnu loby. Namiesto toho, aby sme presne tieto peniaze, ale aj európske peniaze, použili na pomoc poľnohospodárom, na pomoc mestám udržať si zeleň, na modernizáciu nemocníc tak, aby pacienti neležali pri horúčavách na izbách a sestričky neodpadávali pri operáciách. Ďakujem.

(Rečník súhlasil, že odpovie na otázku položenú zdvihnutím modrej karty)
3-0074-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, thank you. How is it possible that in 2026 there are countries in Europe where hospitals do not have air conditioning, where it is 42 degrees in the room during the heat? How is it possible that there are countries in Europe that do not even count deaths due to heat? So we don't even know how many people actually died. How is it possible that there are countries in Europe that have ministers who have suddenly woken up to the fact that climate change exists and have not listened to it for the last 30 years? And then, then we will hear that Brussels is to blame for everything bad. That evil magical Brussels. And at the same time, in many member countries, we still subsidize the fossil ideology, we subsidize the fossil lobby with hundreds of millions, billions. Instead of using exactly this money, as well as European money, to help farmers, to help cities to keep green, to modernize hospitals so that patients do not lie in the heat in the rooms and nurses do not drop out during operations. Thank you.

(The speaker agreed to answer the question posed by holding up the blue card)

3-0077-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, señor presidente en ejercicio del Consejo, (la oradora se expresa en una lengua no oficial), así reaccionaba Núria, una pagesa catalana al ver cómo las llamas de los incendios que estos días afectan a Cataluña convertían el territorio en cenizas. Eventos climáticos extremos como las olas de calor o los incendios de sexta generación, que ya forman parte de los veranos en el sur de Europa, son cada vez más frecuentes en el centro y en el norte del continente.

(La oradora se expresa en una lengua no oficial), decía Núria, y hemos dejado de escucharla. El ritmo del sistema bajo el que vivimos es incompatible con la sostenibilidad del mundo en el cual residimos. Frente a un mundo complejo, rápido y expansivo, la solución pasa por potenciar las formas de vida arraigadas al territorio y en armonía con el entorno.

Ni la tierra es plana ni el callo solar funciona. O apostamos por la ciencia, la evidencia y la gestión regional y local del territorio o el negacionismo climático conseguirá que Europa se convierta en un cenicero gigante.

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0077-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Madam Commissioner, Mr. President-in-Office of the Council, (the speaker speaks in an unofficial language), this is how Núria, a Catalan countrywoman, reacted when she saw how the flames of the fires that are affecting Catalonia these days turned the territory into ashes. Extreme climatic events such as heat waves or sixth generation fires, which are already part of summers in southern Europe, are increasingly frequent in the center and north of the continent.

(The speaker expresses herself in an unofficial language), Núria said, and we have stopped listening to her. The rhythm of the system under which we live is incompatible with the sustainability of the world in which we reside. Faced with a complex, fast and expansive world, the solution is to promote ways of life rooted in the territory and in harmony with the environment.

Neither the earth is flat nor does the solar callus work. Either we bet on science, evidence and regional and local management of the territory or climate denialism will cause Europe to become a giant ashtray.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question asked under the “blue card” procedure)

3-0078-0000.sourceText: Señor presidente, este año se calculan ya 20 000 muertes en Europa, la mitad de ellas de personas mayores, y seguimos sin hacer nada. La falta de inversiones para adaptar sus viviendas no está siendo una prioridad para esta comisión. Muchas residencias de mayores tampoco cumplen con la adaptación climática. En Europa los mayores sufren un edadismo que les hace vivir peor y morir antes. Pregúntense, señorías, porque todos llegaremos a mayores, ¿por qué dejamos de ser sujetos con derechos a partir de cierta edad y pasamos a convertirnos en objetos que hay que esconder o apartar y cuya vida ya no vale nada? ¿Es esto lo que queremos? Yo, sinceramente, no.
3-0078-0000.englishText: Mr. President, this year there are already an estimated 20,000 deaths in Europe, half of them elderly people, and we continue to do nothing. The lack of investments to adapt their homes is not being a priority for this commission. Many nursing homes also do not comply with climate adaptation. In Europe, the elderly suffer from ageism that makes them live worse and die earlier. Ask yourselves, ladies and gentlemen, because we will all grow up, why do we stop being subjects with rights after a certain age and begin to become objects that must be hidden or set aside and whose life is no longer worth anything? Is this what we want? I, honestly, don't.

3-0079-0000.sourceText: Creo que es verdad que estamos hablando a grandes rasgos, pero, cuando vemos la cifra de miles de muertos que también han expuesto nuestros compañeros, dentro de estas cifras hay una mayoría que son los mayores de edad. Creo que tenemos que prestar más atención a estos grupos vulnerables —la gente mayor y los menores—. Hemos visto que en Alemania no hay ni un hospital que esté climatizado, no hay residencias climatizadas, tampoco hay escuelas bien climatizadas en toda Europa. Tenemos que adaptarnos urgentemente a esta situación, porque el cambio climático creo que nos pone dos objetivos por delante: la descarbonización —de la que hemos hablado—, el Pacto Verde, pero también la adaptación, que ya hoy es una realidad de esta subida de las temperaturas.
3-0079-0000.englishText: I think it is true that we are speaking in broad strokes, but, when we see the number of thousands of deaths that our colleagues have also exposed, within these figures there is a majority who are of legal age. I think we have to pay more attention to these vulnerable groups—the elderly and the children. We have seen that in Germany there is not a single hospital that is air-conditioned, there are no air-conditioned residences, nor are there well-air-conditioned schools in all of Europe. We have to urgently adapt to this situation, because I think climate change puts two objectives before us: decarbonization - which we have talked about -, the Green Deal, but also adaptation, which is already a reality today of this rise in temperatures.

3-0080-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η κλιματική κρίση είναι εδώ, κι ας μην την αναγνωρίζουν οι συντηρητικοί μιμητές του Τραμπ, κι ας την υποτιμά ακόμα και η κυρία von der Leyen. Ο καύσωνας σκοτώνει, οι πυρκαγιές καταστρέφουν, οι χώρες του ευρωπαϊκού Νότου δοκιμάζονται. Στην πρώτη γραμμή βρίσκεται η Κύπρος. Ακραίες θερμοκρασίες, παρατεταμένη ξηρασία, καμένα δάση, χαμένες περιουσίες, ανθρώπινες ζωές σε κίνδυνο.

Δεν αρκεί να μετράμε τις καταστροφές. Χρειαζόμαστε περισσότερη πρόληψη, όχι με κριτήριο το κόστος. Περισσότερη ανθεκτικότητα. Περισσότερη ευρωπαϊκή αλληλεγγύη. Η Κύπρος, λόγω της στρατηγικής γεωγραφικής της θέσης, μπορεί και πρέπει να γίνει πρότυπο ευρωπαϊκό περιφερειακό κέντρο δασοπυρόσβεσης και πολιτικής προστασίας για την Ανατολική Μεσόγειο, με μόνιμα εναέρια μέσα, με εξειδικευμένο προσωπικό, με επαρκή ευρωπαϊκή χρηματοδότηση. Η κλιματική κρίση δεν γνωρίζει σύνορα ούτε η ευρωπαϊκή αλληλεγγύη πρέπει να προσφέρεται με το σταγονόμετρο.
3-0080-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, the climate crisis is here, even if Trump's conservative imitators don't recognize it, even if Mrs. von der Leyen downplays it. The heat is killing, the fires are destroying, the countries of the European South are being tested. Cyprus is at the forefront. Extreme temperatures, prolonged drought, burnt forests, lost properties, human lives in danger.

It is not enough to count the disasters. We need more prevention, not based on cost. More durability. More European solidarity. Cyprus, due to its strategic geographical location, can and must become a model European regional center for forest firefighting and civil protection for the Eastern Mediterranean, with permanent aerial means, with specialized personnel, with sufficient European funding. The climate crisis knows no borders, nor should European solidarity be offered with a dropper.

3-0081-0000.sourceText:
Milan Uhrík (ESN). – Vážený pán predsedajúci. Tie vlny horúčav sú skutočne niekedy naozaj neznesiteľné, ale teda hovoríte, že musíme znižovať emisie, že musíme obmedzovať dopravu a obmedzovať priemysel, aby sme zastavili to otepľovanie. A ja mám na vás, kolegovia, jednu možno trošku konšpiračnú, ale – podľa mňa – úplne legitímnu otázku. Čo ak sa to otepľovanie napriek tomu drastickému znižovaniu emisií jednoducho nezastaví? V roku 1990 sme mali nejakú úroveň emisií, teraz sa tá úroveň emisií znížila údajne o 40 % oproti roku 1990. Teplo je napriek tomu stále. Kde máte garanciu, že keď znížime tie emisie o 90 %, že to otepľovanie jednoducho nebude? Čo keď bude jediným výsledkom vašej zelenej politiky, vášho Green Dealu, to, že si zničíme naše hospodárstvo, náš priemysel a aj tak bude v Európe teplo? Podľa mňa treba viac peňazí investovať práve na tú adaptáciu, investovať ich do klimatizácií, do vodozádržných opatrení, na boj proti suchám alebo do budovania viac zelených miest, aby tam nebol len samý žeravý betón. Jednoducho pripravovať sa na to, že to teplo v Európe bude.

(Rečník odmietol otázku, ktorú zdvihnutím modrej karty položil Martin Hojsík)
3-0081-0000.englishText:
Milan Uhrík (ESN). – Dear Mr. President. Those heat waves are really really unbearable sometimes, but then you say that we have to cut emissions, that we have to cut back on traffic and cut back on industry to stop the warming. And I have one perhaps a little conspiratorial, but - in my opinion - completely legitimate question for you, colleagues. What if the warming simply doesn't stop despite the drastic reductions in emissions? In 1990 we had some level of emissions, now that level of emissions has been reduced by allegedly 40% compared to 1990. However, the heat is still there. Where do you have the guarantee that when we reduce those emissions by 90%, that warming simply won't happen? What if the only result of your green policy, your Green Deal, is that we destroy our economy, our industry, and it will still be warm in Europe? In my opinion, more money should be invested in exactly that adaptation, invested in air conditioners, in water retention measures, in the fight against droughts or in building more green cities, so that there is not only hot concrete. Simply preparing for the fact that it will be warm in Europe.

(The speaker rejected the question raised by Martin Hojsík by holding up the blue card)

3-0082-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κάθε καλοκαίρι ίδια συζήτηση, ίδια λάθη. Η φύση δεν μας αιφνιδίασε. Η επιστήμη προειδοποιεί εδώ και δεκαετίες. Εσείς όμως κάθε φορά που έπρεπε να διαλέξετε ανάμεσα στο περιβάλλον και το κέρδος, διαλέγατε το κέρδος. Δώσατε γη και ύδωρ —δάση, ακτές, φυσικούς πόρους—, στο όνομα μιας δήθεν ανάπτυξης. Σήμερα τον λογαριασμό δεν τον πληρώνουν όσοι κέρδισαν· τον πληρώνουν οι λαοί.

Δεν υπάρχουν πλέον φυσικές καταστροφές χωρίς πολιτικές ευθύνες. Η κλιματική αλλαγή δεν είναι άλλοθι της πολιτικής αδράνειας. Και όχι, δεν μπορούμε να μιλάμε για ετοιμότητα, όταν απέναντι σε μόνιμους κινδύνους εξακολουθείτε να στέλνετε εποχικούς εργαζόμενους. Δεν μπορούμε να μιλάμε για προστασία των πολιτών, όταν ζητάμε από οικοδόμους, αγρότες, διανομείς, εργαζόμενους στην ύπαιθρο και διασώστες να εργάζονται κάτω από ακραίες θερμοκρασίες και χωρίς επαρκή προστασία.

Σας ζητώ να χρηματοδοτήσει η Ευρώπη την πρόληψη, τη διαχείριση των δασών, τις αντιπυρικές ζώνες, την προστασία των οικισμών και την προστασία των ανθρώπων που βρίσκονται στην πρώτη γραμμή.
3-0082-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, every summer the same discussion, the same mistakes. Nature did not surprise us. Science has been warning for decades. But every time you had to choose between the environment and profit, you chose profit. You gave away land and water—forests, coasts, natural resources—in the name of so-called development. Today the bill is not paid by those who won; it is paid by the people.

There are no more natural disasters without political responsibilities. Climate change is not an excuse for political inaction. And no, we can't talk about preparedness when, in the face of permanent risks, you're still sending seasonal workers. We cannot talk about protecting citizens when we ask builders, farmers, distributors, field workers and rescuers to work under extreme temperatures and without adequate protection.

I am asking you for Europe to fund prevention, forest management, fire zones, the protection of settlements and the protection of people on the front line.

3-0084-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin! Europa brennt mal wieder, und das ist längst keine Ausnahme mehr; es ist zur neuen Realität geworden, und das hat sehr viel mit Klimaveränderung zu tun. Allein in diesem Jahr wurden bereits 1000 Waldbrände registriert, fast doppelt so viele wie im Durchschnitt der vergangenen Jahrzehnte. 2025 war das zerstörerischste Waldbrandjahr in der Geschichte der EU – mehr als 1 Mio. Hektar wurden verwüstet. Frankreich und Portugal haben den Katastrophenschutzmechanismus erst vor wenigen Tagen erneut aktivieren müssen.

Wir reden nicht über ein Zukunftsszenario, wir reden über die traurige Gegenwart. Die Kommission hat bereits über 800 Feuerwehrkräfte aus 14 Ländern in den Hochrisikogebieten Südeuropas vorpositioniert; das ist richtig, das ist notwendig, aber es wird leider nicht reichen, denn wir haben es längst nicht mehr mit einzelnen Extremereignissen zu tun.

Wir arbeiten gerade auch mit Hochdruck daran, den sogenannten Europäischen Katastrophenschutzmechanismus weiterzuentwickeln, wir brauchen aber weitere Investitionen in Prävention, moderne Frühwarnsysteme, klimaresistente Wälder und den Schutz unserer Einsatzkräfte. Unser Leitgedanke muss sein, Krisen antizipieren statt improvisieren, vorbereiten statt hinterherlaufen, handeln, bevor eine Lage eskaliert.

Ich möchte diese Rede hier auch nutzen, um diejenigen in den Fokus unserer Aufmerksamkeit zu stellen, die das verdienen: Wer löscht den Brand, wenn es brennt? Es sind natürlich die Feuerwehrmänner und -frauen. In Europa gibt es ungefähr 2 Mio., 2,5 Mio. freiwillige Feuerwehrleute – die müssen wir in den Fokus stellen. Die müssen wir nicht nur schützen, wir müssen sogar diese Freiwilligkeit fördern. Dazu gehört auch, dass wir unsere Systeme der sozialen Sicherheit an diese Freiwilligkeit anpassen. Europa brennt, und wir müssen dem helfen, der den Brand löscht.
3-0084-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner! Europe is burning again, and this is no longer an exception; it has become the new reality, and that has a lot to do with climate change. This year alone, 1,000 forest fires have been registered, almost twice as many as the average in previous decades. 2025 was the most destructive forest fire year in EU history - more than 1 million hectares were devastated. France and Portugal had to reactivate the civil protection mechanism just a few days ago.

We're not talking about a future scenario, we're talking about the sad present. The Commission has already prepositioned over 800 firefighters from 14 countries in high-risk areas of southern Europe; That's right, that's necessary, but unfortunately it won't be enough because we're no longer dealing with individual extreme events.

We are currently working hard to further develop the so-called European Civil Protection Mechanism, but we need further investments in prevention, modern early warning systems, climate-resilient forests and the protection of our emergency services. Our guiding principle must be to anticipate crises instead of improvising, to prepare instead of running after them, and to act before a situation escalates.

I would also like to use this speech to focus our attention on those who deserve it: Who will put out the fire when there is a fire? Of course they are the firefighters. There are about 2 million, 2.5 million volunteer firefighters in Europe - we need to focus on them. Not only do we have to protect them, we even have to promote this voluntariness. This also includes adapting our social security systems to this voluntary nature. Europe is burning and we must help whoever puts out the fire.

3-0085-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, in Europa siamo già alla terza ondata di super caldo e siamo solo all'inizio di luglio, quindi i dati sul cambiamento climatico sono indiscutibili e chi oggi si esercita nel negazionismo è semplicemente pazzo.

Quindi, devono stare fuori dalla politica quelli che negano il cambiamento climatico, perché il nostro dovere è rispondere ai bisogni dei cittadini. E vedo, comunque, che i banchi vuoti dell'estrema destra vanno in questa direzione.

Il punto, oggi, è quello delle nuove diseguaglianze che si stanno creando: diseguaglianze nell'accesso al raffreddamento, diseguaglianze nelle fasce di età, diseguaglianze anche sul piano dei migranti – stanno aumentando i migranti climatici – quindi, c'è un forte nesso tra giustizia ambientale e giustizia sociale.

Serve un approccio di ecologia integrale – quello che già Papa Francesco indicava – dove si danno risposte integrate soprattutto a chi è più vulnerabile.

L'Europa ha fatto molto: prenda in mano il timone e soprattutto si porti dietro tutti, e non solo alcuni.
3-0085-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, in Europe we are already in the third wave of super heat and we are only at the beginning of July, so the data on climate change are indisputable and those who practice denialism today are simply crazy.

Therefore, those who deny climate change must stay out of politics, because our duty is to respond to the needs of citizens. And I see, however, that the empty benches of the far right are going in this direction.

The point today is that of the new inequalities that are being created:  inequalities in access to cooling, inequalities in age groups, inequalities also in terms of migrants - climate migrants are increasing - therefore, there is a strong connection between environmental justice and social justice.

We need an integral ecology approach - what Pope Francis already indicated - where integrated responses are given especially to those who are most vulnerable.

Europe has done a lot: take the helm and above all take everyone with you, and not just some.

3-0086-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, ce week-end, un incendie d’une virulence rare est parti du village de ma famille, Lédenon, dans le Gard. Il a dévasté 500 hectares de garrigue en quelques heures. Des familles ont été confinées, des habitants évacués. D’autres incendies ravagent en ce moment la France et d’autres pays en Europe.

Ces feux arrivent avec un mois d’avance, ils sont plus intenses, plus incontrôlables du fait de la canicule et de la sécheresse des sols. Nous savons que tout cela n’est qu’un début; les scientifiques le répètent depuis des décennies. Pourtant, dans cet hémicycle, certains font toujours le choix d’affaiblir ce qui peut nous protéger en détricotant le pacte vert.

Je pose la question au groupe de Jordan Bardella: allez-vous installer la clim contre les incendies dans le champ des agriculteurs? Vous avez choisi de désarmer l’Union européenne face au changement climatique en votant mois après mois contre la restauration des forêts, contre les énergies renouvelables, contre l’obligation de transparence climatique des entreprises. Vous avez choisi l’inaction alors que les canicules et les incendies ont fait 200 000 morts en Europe sur les quatre dernières années.

Soyons clairs: seule une politique de lutte contre le réchauffement climatique pourra nous sauver. Sortir des énergies fossiles, adapter le logement, nos villes, protéger les forêts, renforcer la sécurité civile: nous avons tous les atouts. La maison brûle, ne regardons pas ailleurs!
3-0086-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, this weekend, a fire of rare virulence started in my family's village, Lédenon, in Gard. It devastated 500 hectares of scrubland in a few hours. Families were confined, residents evacuated. Other fires are currently ravaging France and other countries in Europe.

These fires arrive a month in advance, they are more intense, more uncontrollable due to the heatwave and the dryness of the soil. We know that this is all just the beginning; scientists have been saying this for decades. However, in this chamber, some still choose to weaken what can protect us by unraveling the green pact.

I ask Jordan Bardella's group: will you install air conditioning against fires in the farmers' field? You have chosen to disarm the European Union in the face of climate change by voting month after month against the restoration of forests, against renewable energies, against the obligation of climate transparency for companies. You have chosen inaction when heatwaves and fires have caused 200,000 deaths in Europe over the last four years.

Let's be clear: only a policy to combat global warming can save us. Getting away from fossil fuels, adapting housing, our cities, protecting forests, strengthening civil security: we have all the assets. The house is burning, let's not look elsewhere!

3-0087-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, οι καύσωνες και οι πυρκαγιές δεν είναι απειλές του μέλλοντος αλλά η νέα σκληρή πραγματικότητα. Οι αριθμοί μιλούν από μόνοι τους: Το 2025 αποτέλεσε τη χειρότερη περίοδο δασικών πυρκαγιών, αφού πάνω από 1.000.000 εκτάρια καταστράφηκαν στην Ευρώπη, ενώ ο Ιούνιος του 2026 ήταν ο θερμότερος που έχει καταγραφεί ποτέ σε αρκετές χώρες της Ευρώπης. Πρόκειται για μια πραγματικότητα την οποία η Ελλάδα αλλά και γενικότερα η Μεσόγειος βιώνουν με αυξανόμενη ένταση και η οποία κάνει τη λήψη μέτρων για τη βελτίωση της ανθεκτικότητας των πόλεων απολύτως αναγκαία.

Πρέπει όμως να αναπροσαρμόσουμε το μοντέλο αντιμετώπισης των φυσικών καταστροφών, με έμφαση στην πρόληψη και την έγκαιρη προειδοποίηση αλλά και με δραστική αύξηση των ευρωπαϊκών μέσων. Η Ένωση Ετοιμότητας θα πρέπει να πάρει σάρκα και οστά —με καλύτερο συντονισμό μεταξύ ευρωπαϊκού και εθνικού επιπέδου, ενίσχυση του Ευρωπαϊκού Ταμείου Αλληλεγγύης και του μηχανισμού rescEU, περαιτέρω ανάπτυξη του Ευρωπαϊκού Συστήματος Πληροφοριών για τις δασικές πυρκαγιές, δημιουργία ευρωπαϊκής πλατφόρμας έγκαιρης προειδοποίησης με αξιοποίηση της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και, φυσικά, ενισχυμένη χρηματοδότηση στο πλαίσιο του επόμενου επταετούς προϋπολογισμού της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, ώστε τα κράτη μέλη να είναι επαρκώς εξοπλισμένα.

Η κλιματική κρίση απαιτεί συντονισμένη δράση, αυξημένα μέσα και αλλαγή του τρόπου που ενεργούσαμε στο παρελθόν, και αυτή η αλλαγή πρέπει να γίνει τώρα.
3-0087-0000.englishText:
Madam President, heatwaves and fires are not threats of the future but the new harsh reality. The numbers speak for themselves: 2025 was the worst season for forest fires, after more than 1,000,000 hectares were destroyed in Europe, while June 2026 was the warmest ever recorded in several European countries. This is a reality that Greece and the Mediterranean in general are experiencing with increasing intensity and which makes taking measures to improve the resilience of cities absolutely necessary.

However, we must readjust the model for dealing with natural disasters, with an emphasis on prevention and early warning, but also with a drastic increase in European means. The Preparedness Union should take shape — with better coordination between the European and national levels, strengthening of the European Solidarity Fund and the rescEU mechanism, further development of the European Forest Fire Information System, creation of a European early warning platform using artificial intelligence and, of course, increased funding under the next seven-year budget of the European Union so that Member States are adequately equipped.

The climate crisis requires concerted action, increased means and a change in the way we have acted in the past, and that change must be made now.

3-0088-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, cada verano escuchamos en este hemiciclo la misma excusa: que los incendios son inevitables, que todo es culpa del cambio climático y que debemos resignarnos.

Y mientras unos utilizan cada incendio para hacer su propaganda climática, otros sabemos cómo se evita el fuego. Los incendios en verano se apagan en invierno, señorías, con pastoreo, con cortafuegos, con desbroces, con una gestión forestal inteligente, con esa España rural que ustedes han expulsado con su amado y querido y alabado Pacto Verde Europeo; con esa misma España rural es como se apagan los incendios.

Qué informes utilizamos, preguntaban los socialistas. Señora García Pérez, pregunte a los ganaderos, a los que han impedido pastorear; pregunte a los agricultores, a los silvicultores y a todos los que han sido expulsados del campo por décadas de políticas del bipartidismo y de su Pacto Verde Europeo que ha dado la espalda al mundo rural. Esos son nuestros informes: el mundo real, ese que ustedes solamente pisan cuando hay cámaras.

El clima cambia, señorías, efectivamente, pero el cambio climático no limpia los montes, no abre cortafuegos, no desbroza, no retrasa las ayudas y no explica por qué España concentra el 40 % de los incendios de toda la superficie de la Unión Europea cuando Portugal comparte el mismo clima y no...

(la presidenta retira la palabra a la oradora)

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0088-0000.englishText:
Madam President, every summer in this chamber we hear the same excuse: that fires are inevitable, that everything is the fault of climate change and that we must resign ourselves.

And while some use each fire to make their climate propaganda, others know how to avoid fire. The fires in summer are put out in winter, ladies and gentlemen, with grazing, with firebreaks, with clearing, with intelligent forest management, with that rural Spain that you have expelled with your beloved and praised European Green Deal; With that same rural Spain is how the fires are put out.

What reports do we use, the socialists asked. Mrs. García Pérez, ask the ranchers, those who have been prevented from grazing; ask the farmers, the foresters and all those who have been expelled from the countryside by decades of two-party policies and its European Green Deal that has turned its back on the rural world. Those are our reports: the real world, the one you only step into when there are cameras.

The climate changes, ladies and gentlemen, indeed, but climate change does not clear the mountains, it does not open firebreaks, it does not clear brush, it does not delay aid and it does not explain why Spain concentrates 40% of the fires in the entire surface of the European Union when Portugal shares the same climate and does not...

(the president removes the speaker from speaking)

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question asked under the “blue card” procedure)

3-0089-0000.sourceText: (S&D), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ja, vielen Dank! Ich fände noch mal spannend zu hören, weil Sie ja wieder Klimaideologie als Begriff benutzt haben – könnten Sie uns vielleicht noch mal erklären, was Ihre Definition von „ideologisch“ ist? Denn ich habe das Gefühl, dass Ihre Besessenheit davon, Autokraten dieser Welt eine Importgarantie für fossile Energien zu geben, eine ganz schön ideologische Herangehensweise ist, anstatt EU‑Bürgerinnen und ‑bürgern in Spanien und überall anders tatsächlich die Chance zu geben, auch günstige erneuerbare Energien zu beziehen. Ist das nicht eher die Ideologie? Vielleicht könnten Sie noch mal unsere Definition klären.
3-0089-0000.englishText: (S&D), question about the “blue card” procedure. – Yes, thank you very much! I think it would be interesting to hear it again, because you used climate ideology as a term again - could you perhaps explain to us again what your definition of "ideological" is? Because I have the feeling that your obsession with giving the autocrats of the world an import guarantee for fossil fuels is a very ideological approach, instead of actually giving EU citizens in Spain and everywhere else the chance to purchase cheap renewable energy. Isn't that more the ideology? Maybe you could clarify our definition again.

3-0090-0000.sourceText:
Vamos a ver... lo primero, estamos hablando aquí de incendios, no de energías renovables, pero ¿qué concibo yo como ideología? Su ideología, su fanatismo climático, es simplemente hacer un uso político e ideológico de un hecho fáctico que es el cambio climático, que aquí nadie niega que el clima es cambiante. El clima lleva cambiando desde los orígenes del planeta Tierra.

Ustedes utilizan ese hecho fáctico de que el clima es cambiante para establecer una ideología y establecer sus propios intereses ideológicos, su fanatismo climático, para inventarse cuestiones como esta: que los incendios son culpa del cambio climático, cuando ha quedado más que demostrado que los incendios son culpa de su nefasta gestión y como son incapaces de asumir responsabilidades, ustedes se escudan en su fanatismo climático...

(la presidenta retira la palabra a la oradora)
3-0090-0000.englishText:
Let's see... first of all, we are talking here about fires, not renewable energies, but what do I conceive as an ideology? Their ideology, their climate fanaticism, is simply making political and ideological use of a factual fact that is climate change, and no one here denies that the climate is changing. The climate has been changing since the origins of planet Earth.

You use this factual fact that the climate is changing to establish an ideology and establish your own ideological interests, your climate fanaticism, to invent questions like this: that the fires are the fault of climate change, when it has been more than proven that the fires are the fault of your disastrous management and since you are incapable of assuming responsibilities, you hide behind your climate fanaticism...

(the president removes the speaker from speaking)

3-0091-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, nous vivons l’été le plus frais du reste de notre vie. La canicule, ce n’est plus une anomalie, c’est notre nouvelle normalité, et cette canicule tue: 200 000 personnes en Europe en quatre ans!

Sue Ellen Demestre lance un cri d’alarme au nom des gens du voyage: «Nous cherchons un refuge climatique. Nous ne pouvons plus respirer!» Sarah, sans-abri, mère de quatre enfants, raconte qu’en été tous les abris sont fermés: «On dort dans les parcs, parfois sur le béton. Il n’y a pas d’eau.» Et pendant que nous débattons ici, ouvriers, agricultrices, éboueurs continuent de travailler sous 40 °C, sans protection européenne.

Parce que oui, la canicule ne touche pas tout le monde de la même façon. La Commission le sait; elle la connaît, cette injustice, elle qui a allumé la climatisation pour les commissaires dans les étages supérieurs et l’a éteinte pour les fonctionnaires dans les étages inférieurs. Elle a aussi brillé par son absence de réaction: pas un communiqué, pas un plan d’action, pas un tweet lorsque la haute chaleur a touché notre continent. Cette inaction doit cesser!

Les canicules ne tombent pas du ciel. Elles portent le nom des multinationales des fossiles, et notre plan d’action doit être clair: reprendre en main les firmes qui ont provoqué le dérèglement climatique, adopter une grande loi pour protéger les travailleurs exposés aux chaleurs extrêmes, dégager les moyens urgents pour adapter nos hôpitaux, nos écoles et les logements aux grandes chaleurs. N’attendons plus!

(L’oratrice refuse des questions carton bleu de Jaak Madison et de Kateřina Konečná)
3-0091-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, we are experiencing the coolest summer of our lives. The heatwave is no longer an anomaly, it is our new normal, and this heatwave kills: 200,000 people in Europe in four years!

Sue Ellen Demestre sounds the alarm on behalf of Travelers: “We are looking for climate refuge. We can't breathe anymore!” Sarah, a homeless mother of four, says that in summer all the shelters are closed: “We sleep in parks, sometimes on concrete. There is no water.” And while we debate here, workers, farmers and garbage collectors continue to work under 40°C, without European protection.

Because yes, the heatwave does not affect everyone in the same way. The Commission knows this; she knows this injustice, she who turned on the air conditioning for the commissioners on the upper floors and turned it off for the civil servants on the lower floors. It was also notable for its lack of reaction: not a press release, not an action plan, not a tweet when the high heat hit our continent. This inaction must stop!

Heatwaves don't fall from the sky. They bear the name of fossil multinationals, and our action plan must be clear: take back control of the companies that caused climate change, adopt a major law to protect workers exposed to extreme heat, provide urgent means to adapt our hospitals, our schools and homes to extreme heat. Let's not wait any longer!

(The speaker refuses blue card questions from Jaak Madison and Kateřina Konečná)

3-0092-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κυρία Επίτροπε, προέρχομαι από μία χώρα όπου ο καύσωνας το καλοκαίρι είναι σχεδόν καθημερινό φαινόμενο. Στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση πέρυσι είχαμε ρεκόρ πυρκαγιών με πάνω από 10 εκατομμύρια στρέμματα καμένης γης. Για την Κύπρο, την πατρίδα μου, τα δεδομένα του Ευρωπαϊκού Συστήματος Πληροφόρησης για τις Δασικές Πυρκαγιές καταγράφουν μια ακραία κορύφωση των καμένων εκτάσεων. Χαιρετίζω λοιπόν την απόφαση-σταθμό, καθώς θα υπάρχει ένας αριθμός-ρεκόρ για την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση: 777 πυροσβέστες, 22 αεροσκάφη και 5 ελικόπτερα σε διάφορα σημεία της ευρωπαϊκής επικράτειας, ώστε να συνδράμουν ανά πάσα στιγμή εκεί όπου χρειάζεται.

Θέλω όμως να μάθω αν υπάρχει προγραμματισμός για το πού θα πάνε και πότε —αν μπορείτε να μας πείτε. Ήμουν και παραμένω ένας εξ αυτών που υποστήριξαν σθεναρά την απόλυτη ανάγκη μόνιμης και ενισχυμένης παρουσίας του rescEU στην Κύπρο, καθώς η γεωγραφική απομόνωσή της την καθιστούσε ευάλωτη. Νομίζω πως είμαστε τώρα σε μια σωστή κατεύθυνση και επιβάλλεται η συνεχής ενίσχυση. Οποιεσδήποτε καθυστερήσεις είναι επικίνδυνες, με ανυπολόγιστες συνέπειες για το φυσικό περιβάλλον και την ανθρώπινη ζωή.
3-0092-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I come from a country where summer heat is almost a daily occurrence. In the European Union last year we had record fires with over 10 million hectares of land burned. For Cyprus, my home country, the data of the European Forest Fire Information System records an extreme peak of burned areas. I therefore welcome the landmark decision, as there will be a record number for the European Union: 777 firefighters, 22 aircraft and 5 helicopters in various parts of the European territory, so that they can help at any time where it is needed.

But I want to know if there is any planning as to where they will go and when—if you can tell us. I was and remain one of those who strongly supported the absolute need for a permanent and reinforced rescEU presence in Cyprus, as its geographical isolation made it vulnerable. I think we are now in the right direction and continuous reinforcement is required. Any delays are dangerous, with incalculable consequences for the natural environment and human life.

3-0093-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, justice sociale et justice climatique: même combat. Aujourd’hui déjà et demain plus encore, ce sont les plus vulnérables, au nord comme au sud de la planète, qui paient le prix du dérèglement climatique. En Europe, on estime que le décompte morbide sera chaque été de 80 000 morts. Rien qu’en Belgique, pour la canicule de ce mois de juin, on déplore plus de 1 200 décès supplémentaires liés aux fortes chaleurs, et à nouveau les plus fragiles sont touchés: les personnes âgées, les malades chroniques ou les bébés. Les travailleurs aussi sont en première ligne.

Mais, pendant ce temps, notre gouvernement, par la voix de notre ministre de la défense, nous invite à ne pas dramatiser et à profiter d’une bonne bière au bord de la piscine. Monsieur Francken, je vous invite à vous mettre dans la peau des 130 millions de travailleurs exposés à des températures infernales qui mettent leur santé et leur vie en danger. C’est pourquoi il est urgent d’adopter une directive qui protège les travailleurs et les travailleuses afin de prévenir les risques pour leur santé, pas pour prendre acte ou pour subir.
3-0093-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, social justice and climate justice: same fight. Already today and even more tomorrow, it is the most vulnerable, in the north and south of the planet, who are paying the price of climate change. In Europe, it is estimated that the death toll will be 80,000 each summer. In Belgium alone, during the heatwave this June, there were more than 1,200 additional deaths linked to extreme heat, and once again the most vulnerable were affected: the elderly, the chronically ill and babies. Workers are also on the front line.

But, during this time, our government, through our Minister of Defense, invites us not to dramatize and to enjoy a good beer by the swimming pool. Mr. Francken, I invite you to put yourself in the shoes of the 130 million workers exposed to hellish temperatures that put their health and their lives at risk. This is why it is urgent to adopt a directive that protects workers in order to prevent risks to their health, not to take note or to suffer.

3-0094-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, lejos de remitir la incidencia de los incendios en Europa, como todos desearíamos, cada año se inician antes y son más virulentos.

La Unión es consciente del problema y trata de coordinar mejor los medios efectivos que hay contra los incendios, pero tenemos una causa pendiente: la prevención, no lo hacemos bien. Hemos avanzado algo, como, por ejemplo, con la nueva aprobación de las nuevas técnicas de edición genómica para hacer más resiliente el mundo vegetal o el reconocimiento de anteayer, por parte de la Comisión Europea, de la ganadería extensiva del ovino y del caprino y su importante papel medioambiental y en la lucha contra incendios. Pero aún quedan decisiones políticas y presupuestarias necesarias que evidencien, de manera incontestable, la apuesta por el entorno poblacional del mundo rural y su papel.

Hay que modificar legislación como la Red Natura 2000, reglamentos como el Reglamento de Restauración de la Naturaleza, la Nueva Estrategia de la UE en favor de los Bosques para 2030, reglamentos como los relacionados con la biodiversidad o los hábitats para volver a permitir, sin polémicas, que la población rural europea vuelva a practicar medidas eficaces para prevenir los desastres naturales que son los incendios. ¿Y cómo? Permitiéndoles volver a prácticas que durante siglos y siglos han funcionado, como las talas, los clareos, las limpiezas, las veredas, los cortafuegos.

No sé a qué estamos esperando, pero, mientras discutimos si son galgos o podencos, Europa sigue ardiendo.

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0094-0000.englishText:
Madam President, far from reducing the incidence of fires in Europe, as we would all like, they start earlier and are more virulent each year.

The Union is aware of the problem and is trying to better coordinate the effective means available against fires, but we have a pending cause: prevention, we are not doing it well. We have made some progress, such as, for example, with the new approval of new genomic editing techniques to make the plant world more resilient or the recognition the day before yesterday, by the European Commission, of extensive sheep and goat farming and its important environmental role and in fighting fires. But there are still necessary political and budgetary decisions that demonstrate, in an incontestable way, the commitment to the population environment of the rural world and its role.

Legislation such as the Natura 2000 Network, regulations such as the Nature Restoration Regulation, the New EU Forest Strategy for 2030, regulations such as those related to biodiversity or habitats must be modified to once again allow, without controversy, the European rural population to once again practice effective measures to prevent natural disasters such as fires. And how? Allowing them to return to practices that have worked for centuries and centuries, such as logging, clearing, cleaning, sidewalks, firebreaks.

I don't know what we're waiting for, but, while we discuss whether they are greyhounds or hounds, Europe continues to burn.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question asked under the “blue card” procedure)

3-0095-0000.sourceText: (The Left), “blauwe kaart”-vraag. – Ik heb al een aantal tussenkomsten gehoord van, laten we zeggen, beschaafd rechts, centrumrechts. En ik hoor telkens maar pleidooien voor preventie en voor investeringen en weet ik veel. Nu, wat ik vaststel, is dat overal in Europa, waar het overgrote deel rechtse of centrumrechtse regeringen zijn, er overal net wordt bespaard op preventie, dat er overal wordt bespaard op hulpdiensten en dergelijke. Dus ik zou willen vragen: is dat wel consequent wat u komt vertellen en hoe ziet u dat?
3-0095-0000.englishText: (The Left), “blue card” question. – I have already heard a number of interventions from, let's say, the civilized right, the centre-right. And I keep hearing pleas for prevention and investments and I know a lot. Now, what I notice is that everywhere in Europe, where the vast majority are right-wing or centre-right governments, there are savings everywhere on prevention, everywhere on emergency services and the like. So I would like to ask: is what you are saying consistent and how do you see it?

3-0096-0000.sourceText:
La visión es muy clara, caballero. Y gracias por su pregunta.

Mire, tenemos que ser conscientes de que hay una prevención muy importante, que es la práctica que siempre se ha llevado a cabo en el mundo rural.

Los que mejor conocen el mundo rural son aquellos que por herencia, por tradición, por familia, por conocimientos, lo hacen bien desde hace siglos y, durante yo diría que más de una década, hemos empezado a prohibir sistemáticamente un montón de medidas por las que ellos apostaban. Han desaparecido los cortafuegos, por eso ahora no podemos limitar el alcance del fuego. No les dejamos, cuando entran en Red Natura 2000, utilizar los recursos naturales como lo han hecho siempre. No limpiamos. Hemos acabado con la ganadería extensiva del ovino y del caprino, con lo que representa para la lucha contra incendios.

Oiga, es tan sencillo como aplicar lo que sabemos —el conocimiento— y no prohibirlo.
3-0096-0000.englishText:
The vision is very clear, gentleman. And thanks for your question.

Look, we have to be aware that there is a very important prevention, which is the practice that has always been carried out in the rural world.

Those who know the rural world best are those who, by inheritance, by tradition, by family, by knowledge, have done it well for centuries and, for more than a decade, I would say, we have begun to systematically prohibit a lot of measures that they supported. The firewalls have disappeared, so now we cannot limit the range of the fire. We do not allow them, when they enter the Natura 2000 Network, to use natural resources as they have always done. We don't clean. We have put an end to extensive sheep and goat farming, with what it represents for fighting fires.

Hey, it's as simple as applying what we know—knowledge—and not prohibiting it.

3-0097-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Jedes Jahr sterben in Europa mehr als 175 000 Menschen an den Folgen extremer Hitze. Die Temperaturen in Europa steigen doppelt so schnell wie im globalen Durchschnitt. Doch anstatt dies als den Notfall zu behandeln, der es ist, baut die EU Klimaschutzmaßnahmen ab. Während die reichsten 1 % so viel CO2 ausstoßen wie die ärmsten zwei Drittel der Bevölkerung zusammen, sind es die Arbeiterinnen, Rentnerinnen und einkommensschwachen Familien, die am meisten leiden.

Klimaschutz bedeutet: Besteuerung von extremen Vermögen und Emissionen, Abbau von Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe, Investitionen in öffentliche Dienstleistungen und die größten Umweltverschmutzer zur Kasse zu bitten. Doch während Europa brennt, stecken Konservative und extrem Rechte gemeinsam unter der Decke: Sie schwächen den Green Deal, und die EU steckt weiterhin Milliarden in Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe.

Menschen statt Verschmutzer, Leben statt Gewinne aus fossilen Brennstoffen schützen!

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
3-0097-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Every year more than 175,000 people die in Europe as a result of extreme heat. Temperatures in Europe are rising twice as fast as the global average. But instead of treating this as the emergency it is, the EU is dismantling climate action. While the richest 1% emit as much CO2 as the poorest two-thirds of the population combined, it is workers, retirees and low-income families who suffer the most.

Climate protection means: taxing extreme wealth and emissions, reducing fossil fuel subsidies, investing in public services and making the biggest polluters pay. But while Europe burns, conservatives and the far right are in this together: they are weakening the Green Deal, and the EU continues to pour billions into fossil fuel subsidies.

Protect people instead of polluters, lives instead of profits from fossil fuels!

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question about the “blue card” procedure.)

3-0098-0000.sourceText: Jaa. Kuna räägite saksa keeles, ma räägin eesti keeles. Teie kõne oli ääretult entusiastlik ja ja positiivne, seega kõnepidamine oli väga hea. Kuid kui te räägite fossiilkütustest ja et Euroopa põlemises on süüdi fossiilkütused, meil pole kliimakokkulepet, rohepööret, kõike seda, siis lihtsalt väikene küsimus, et minu teada kliima on alati muutunud. Alati läbi ajaloo. Aastal 1685 oli Thamesi jõgi nii jäätunud, et seal hobused jooksid. Mis teie arvate, miks muutus kliima umbes kakssada aastat tagasi, kui ta nüüd muutub ainult sellepärast, et meil on bensiiniautod? Et kui varem muutus kliima tänu päikesele ja kogu loodusele, siis nüüd ta muutub hoopis sellepärast, et meil on olemas teaduslik areng ja võimalik majandust arendada ka loodusressurssidele. Mis juhtus vahepeal? Miks varem kliima muutus?
3-0098-0000.englishText: Yes. Since you speak in German, I speak in Estonian. Your speech was extremely enthusiastic and positive, so the speech was very good. But when you talk about fossil fuels and that fossil fuels are to blame for the burning of Europe, we don't have a climate agreement, green turn, all that, just a small question that as far as I know the climate has always changed. Always throughout history. In 1685, the River Thames was so frozen over that horses could run. Why do you think the climate changed about two hundred years ago when it is only changing now because we have gas cars? That if before the climate changed thanks to the sun and all of nature, now it changes because we have scientific progress and it is possible to develop the economy on natural resources. What happened in the meantime? Why did the climate change in the past?

3-0099-0000.sourceText:
(The Left), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Ja, es gab Klimawandel auch vor dem menschengemachten Klimawandel. Den menschengemachten Klimawandel zu ignorieren, der wissenschaftlich eindeutig festgestellt ist, das ist klimaterroristische Ideologie, die Sie zusammen verfolgen, unter der Arbeiterinnen, Rentnerinnen und ärmere Familien in dieser EU leiden.

Ich fordere Sie auf, endlich Verantwortung dafür zu übernehmen – für Ihre Politik – und den Leuten ehrlich zu sagen, was auf sie zukommt. Das tun Sie nicht; Sie belügen die Menschen.
3-0099-0000.englishText:
(The Left), answer to a question about the “blue card” procedure. – Yes, climate change existed before man-made climate change. Ignoring man-made climate change, which is clearly scientifically established, is a climate terrorist ideology that you are pursuing together, from which workers, pensioners and poorer families in this EU suffer.

I call on you to finally take responsibility for this - for your policies - and to tell people honestly what's coming. You don't do that; They lie to people.

3-0100-0000.sourceText: Jaa, kui te räägite, et keegi peab võtma vastutuse, siis miks te arvate, et Euroopa peab võtma vastutuse? Kui te räägite kliimamuutustest ja kliimasoojemisest, siis ainult Euroopas on vaid märkimisväärselt vähe tõusnud kliimamuutused. Samas ülejäänud maailmas, Aafrikas, Aasias ei ole seda juhtunud. Miks peab Euroopa inimene teie poliitika tõttu hakkama rohkem kinni maksma rohelepet, kõrgemat kütuse hinda, kõrgemat toasooja hinda, et teha mingit ideoloogilist projekti, nagu tegid kommunistid? Noh, te olete ka ju natukene kommunist. Et miks meie peame kinni maksma Euroopa inimestena teie ideoloogia, kui me teame, et tegelikult inimmõju kliimamuutustele on marginaalne, väga väikene või olematu? Miks te tahate, et Euroopa [cut off]
3-0100-0000.englishText: Yes, if you say that someone has to take responsibility, why do you think Europe has to take responsibility? If you talk about climate change and global warming, only in Europe there is only a significant increase in climate change. However, this has not happened in the rest of the world, in Africa, in Asia. Why does the European person have to start paying more for the green deal, higher fuel prices, higher room heating prices because of your policy, in order to do some ideological project, like the communists did? Well, you're a bit of a communist too. So why do we as European people have to pay for your ideology when we know that the actual human impact on climate change is marginal, very small or non-existent? Why do you want Europe [cut off]

3-0101-0000.sourceText:
Erstens: Es sind 57 Konzerne, die 80 % aller weltweiten Emissionen produzieren. Es sind nicht die Menschen, die es zahlen sollten, es sind diese Konzerne, die zahlen sollten, endlich ihrer Verantwortung gerecht werden sollten. Und ja, das sind auch viele europäische Konzerne.

Ich bin sehr dafür, dass es nicht die Menschen sind, die am meisten darunter leiden – was sie heutzutage schon tun. 175 000 Tote durch extreme Hitze in Europa, und Konzerne wie Exxon sagen für das erste Vierteljahr bereits, dass sie 5 Milliarden mehr Profit gemacht haben. Wo bleibt da eigentlich Ihre Initiative? Wo ist da der Aufschrei zu sagen: Stoppt diese Profite!
3-0101-0000.englishText:
First, there are 57 corporations that produce 80% of all global emissions. It's not the people who should pay, it's these corporations that should pay and finally live up to their responsibility. And yes, that includes many European corporations.

I'm all for ensuring that it's not the people who suffer the most - which they already do these days. 175,000 deaths from extreme heat in Europe, and companies like Exxon already say they made 5 billion more in profit for the first quarter. Where is your initiative? Where is the outcry to say: Stop these profits!

3-0102-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en los últimos días hemos vivido récords de temperatura en toda Europa. Y mucho me temo que este va a ser el verano más fresco de los próximos años. Las olas de calor han dejado miles de víctimas y han multiplicado los incendios. El estrés térmico amenaza a más de 130 millones de trabajadores y la superficie quemada ya supera las 130 000 hectáreas. En nuestra tierra, en Castellón, en Soneja, pero también repetitivamente en León, en Cataluña, de forma simultánea, están luchando contra el fuego. Damos todo nuestro apoyo.

Nuestro nuevo mecanismo de protección civil debe reforzar las capacidades de la Unión para responder. Estamos en ello. Pero, sobre todo, tiene que fomentar una cultura de la preparación, de la planificación, de la prevención, con la participación de actores locales y rurales. Tenemos que entender su dimensión, su frecuencia y su virulencia en emergencia climática. No podremos hacerlo si no desmantelamos las leyes que protegen y monitorean nuestros bosques como aquí se está intentando. Y no lo haremos si no entendemos sus causas: el cambio climático, la despoblación, si no tenemos en cuenta a los actores locales y rurales.

Señorías, este no es un debate sobre más aire acondicionado. Hay que climatizar, sí, pero sobre todo hay que prevenir. Hay que anticiparse y evitar más incendios y, también, más muertes por el calor.
3-0102-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in recent days we have experienced temperature records throughout Europe. And I very much fear that this is going to be the coolest summer in the coming years. The heat waves have left thousands of victims and have multiplied fires. Heat stress threatens more than 130 million workers and the burned area already exceeds 130,000 hectares. In our land, in Castellón, in Soneja, but also repetitively in León, in Catalonia, simultaneously, they are fighting against the fire. We give all our support.

Our new civil protection mechanism must strengthen the Union's capabilities to respond. We are in it. But, above all, it must promote a culture of preparation, planning, and prevention, with the participation of local and rural actors. We have to understand its dimension, its frequency and its virulence in the climate emergency. We will not be able to do this if we do not dismantle the laws that protect and monitor our forests as is being attempted here. And we will not do it if we do not understand its causes: climate change, depopulation, if we do not take into account local and rural actors.

Ladies and gentlemen, this is not a debate about more air conditioning. You have to air condition, yes, but above all you have to prevent. We must anticipate and avoid more fires and, also, more deaths due to heat.

3-0103-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, komission jäsen, meillä on vain yksi planeetta. Tällä hetkellä se palaa monin paikoin, ja sään ääri-ilmiöt yleistyvät. Ilmastonmuutos on täällä. Me näemme sen omin silmin joka päivä, ja tuhannet ihmiset Euroopassa ovat menettäneet henkensä helteen vuoksi. Se on järkyttävää.

Suomessa lapsemme ja lastenlapsemme eivät sinilevän vuoksi voi enää uida meressä samalla tavoin kuin ennen. Myrskyt ja rajut ukkosilmat seuraavat toisiaan. Arktisella alueella asuvat saamelaiset kärsivät ilmastonmuutoksesta erityisen paljon.

On vastuutonta, että vielä tänäkin päivänä on päättäjiä, jotka kieltävät ilmastonmuutoksen. Euroopan kansalaisilla on oikeus odottaa meiltä toimia. Meidän on luovuttava fossiilisista polttoaineista, öljystä ja kivihiilestä. Meidän on rakennettava EU:n varautumisunioni, ja on aika toteuttaa presidentti Niinistön raportti EU:n kokonaisvaltaisen varautumisen vahvistamisesta.

(Puhuja suostui vastaamaan sinisen kortin kysymykseen)
3-0103-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, we only have one planet. Currently, it is burning in many places, and extreme weather events are becoming more common. Climate change is here. We see it with our own eyes every day, and thousands of people in Europe have lost their lives due to the heat. It's shocking.

In Finland, our children and grandchildren can no longer swim in the sea in the same way as before because of blue-green algae. Storms and violent thunderstorms follow each other. The Sámi people who live in the Arctic region are particularly affected by climate change.

It is irresponsible that even today there are decision-makers who deny climate change. European citizens have the right to expect us to act. We need to get rid of fossil fuels, oil and coal. We have to build an EU preparedness union, and it's time to implement President Niinistö's report on strengthening the EU's overall preparedness.

(The speaker agreed to answer the blue card question)

3-0104-0000.sourceText: Ta otázka je vlastně na vás, kolegové ze skupin socialistů, Zelených i Renew. Bavíte se o tom, že máme opustit fosilní paliva. Bavíte se o tom, že nám Evropu a svět oteplují fosilní paliva. Proč se nebavíte o válce? Kolik emisí způsobují vaše války, které začínáte? Vy podporujete nákupy zbraní, které zabíjí lidi a ničí klima. A o tom nikdo z vás neřekl ani slovo. Pojďme to tedy vzít komplexně. Pojďme se podívat na to, jak vaše válečné štvaní, které vy podporujete a do kterého investujete peníze, ničí tuto planetu.
3-0104-0000.englishText: That question is actually up to you, colleagues from the Socialist, Green and Renew groups. You talk about getting off fossil fuels. You are talking about the fact that Europe and the world are being warmed by fossil fuels. Why don't you talk about the war? How much emissions do your wars you start cause? You support weapons purchases that kill people and destroy the climate. And none of you said a word about it. So let's take it comprehensively. Let's look at how your warmongering, which you support and invest money in, is destroying this planet.

3-0105-0000.sourceText:
Det verkar som att parlamentarikern har missat någonting elementärt. Det är Ryssland och Putin som har startat ett krig mot Ukraina, och det är tragiskt. Det kriget pågår varje dag, och vi ska se till att vi gör allt för att stödja Ukraina, för att vi i Europa inte ska köpa rysk gas och olja.

Vi kan på vårt eget sätt stödja Ukraina genom våra egna åtgärder i våra länder, och det är vår uppgift att se till att Ukraina också en dag kan bli medlem i Europeiska unionen.
3-0105-0000.englishText:
It seems that the parliamentarian has missed something elementary. It is Russia and Putin who have started a war against Ukraine, and it is tragic. That war is going on every day, and we must make sure that we do everything to support Ukraine, so that we in Europe will not buy Russian gas and oil.

We can in our own way support Ukraine through our own actions in our countries, and it is our task to ensure that Ukraine can also one day become a member of the European Union.

3-0106-0000.sourceText: Tady přece vůbec nejde o Ukrajinu. Vy jste nebyli schopni odhlasovat, že nesouhlasíte s tím, jak agresivně postupuje Donald Trump v Íránu. A tam se také používají zbraně. Tam se také ničí klima. Vy jste nebyli schopni odhlasovat, že nesouhlasíte s genocidou v Palestině. Také se tam používají zbraně. Prostě dokud nepřistoupíte na to, že mírová politika je ta environmentálně nejčistější politika, a bude to svádět jenom na jednu část ekonomiky nebo sektoru, tak je to „papalášství“ a jenom si na něco hrajete.
3-0106-0000.englishText: This is not about Ukraine at all. You have not been able to vote that you do not agree with how aggressively Donald Trump is proceeding in Iran. And guns are used there too. The climate there is also being destroyed. You were not able to vote that you do not agree with the genocide in Palestine. Weapons are also used there. Simply until you come to the conclusion that the peace policy is the most environmentally clean policy, and it only targets one part of the economy or sector, then it is "bullshit" and you are just playing something.

3-0107-0000.sourceText:
Det är förstås på det sättet att det skulle vara väldigt bra om vi skulle ha fred i världen. Men det betyder inte att vi kan stänga våra ögon för den miljökatastrof som håller på att hända i världen nu, den klimatkatastrof som vi har.

Vi måste jobba på många plan varje dag. Vi måste bekämpa klimatförändringen. Vi måste göra oss av med fossila bränslen. Vi ska satsa på den gröna omställningen, och vi ska jobba för en värld där människor respekteras – demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter – och att varje land har rätt till sin suveränitet.
3-0107-0000.englishText:
It is of course in that way that it would be very good if we had peace in the world. But that does not mean that we can close our eyes to the environmental disaster that is happening in the world now, the climate disaster that we have.

We have to work on many levels every day. We must fight climate change. We must get rid of fossil fuels. We must invest in the green transition, and we must work for a world where people are respected - democracy, human rights - and that every country has the right to its sovereignty.

3-0108-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, face aux vagues de chaleur, la climatisation n’est pas un luxe, c’est un enjeu de santé publique. Depuis 2017, près de 40 000 Français sont morts des conséquences de la chaleur. Pourtant, seuls 24 % des logements sont climatisés, contre plus de 50 % en Italie. Lorsque les températures s’affolent, il faut pouvoir protéger efficacement les écoles, les hôpitaux et les maisons de retraite.

À Nice, nous avons choisi un grand plan d’action, un plan d’action de climatisation de notre ville. S’adapter au changement climatique, ce n’est pas renoncer à le combattre. S’adapter, c’est investir dans le nucléaire pour produire une électricité décarbonée. S’adapter, c’est rendre nos bâtiments vivables été comme hiver. C’est avant tout protéger la vie des plus fragiles.

La véritable écologie, ce n’est pas celle qui culpabilise, c’est celle qui protège. La véritable écologie ne choisit jamais entre la planète et les personnes, elle protège les deux.
3-0108-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, faced with heat waves, air conditioning is not a luxury, it is a public health issue. Since 2017, nearly 40,000 French people have died from the consequences of heat. Yet only 24% of homes are air-conditioned, compared to more than 50% in Italy. When temperatures soar, we must be able to effectively protect schools, hospitals and retirement homes.

In Nice, we have chosen a major action plan, an air conditioning action plan for our city. Adapting to climate change does not mean giving up fighting it. Adapting means investing in nuclear power to produce carbon-free electricity. Adapting means making our buildings livable in both summer and winter. Above all, it is about protecting the lives of the most vulnerable.

The true ecology is not the one that makes people feel guilty, it is the one that protects. True ecology never chooses between the planet and people, it protects both.

3-0109-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, «as ondas de calor extremo são uma emergência de saúde pública», disse ontem o diretor regional da OMS Europa.

Nós já o sabíamos. As temperaturas elevadas têm um impacto direto no aumento da morbilidade e também da mortalidade. O excesso de mortalidade devido ao calor foi de mais de 7 000 mortos, apenas no mês de junho, em três países da Europa.

Mas, para além dos meios de combate a incêndios que a União Europeia tem disponíveis para apoiar todos os países, nós precisamos de fazer mais. O recuo nas políticas de redução do aquecimento global, de desregulação ambiental, tem um custo pesado. Mede-se em doenças evitáveis, mede-se em mortes evitáveis, e as medidas de adaptação e mitigação climática são a chave de longo prazo.

Para muitos neste hemiciclo, basta olhar para ele, os incêndios são uma coisa que acontece porque as ganadarias foram terminadas, as doenças transmitidas por vetores acontecem porque vêm nuns aviões, de uns sítios estranhos, que trazem uns mosquitos a bordo. E as alterações climáticas são ideologia.

Enquanto não nos entendermos sobre os factos, não vamos não correr atrás do prejuízo.
3-0109-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, “extreme heat waves are a public health emergency”, said the regional director of WHO Europe yesterday.

We already knew it. High temperatures have a direct impact on increasing morbidity and mortality. Excess mortality due to heat was more than 7,000 deaths, in the month of June alone, in three European countries.

But beyond the firefighting resources that the European Union has available to support all countries, we need to do more. The retreat in policies to reduce global warming and environmental deregulation has a heavy cost. It is measured in preventable diseases, it is measured in preventable deaths, and climate adaptation and mitigation measures are the long-term key.

For many in this Chamber, just look at it, fires are something that happens because the livestock farms were finished, vector-borne diseases happen because they come on planes, from strange places, that bring mosquitoes on board. And climate change is ideology.

Until we understand the facts, we will not pursue the loss.

3-0110-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, six jours de canicule en juin en France, 2 025 morts. Et pendant que certains discutent encore, d’autres agissent. À Madrid, le métro est climatisé. À Barcelone, des refuges climatiques sont accessibles en quelques minutes à pied. En Grèce, les employeurs doivent prévoir des espaces rafraîchis pour leurs salariés. Ces pays ont compris une chose simple: protéger la population face à la chaleur, ce n’est pas un luxe, c’est une politique publique.

En France, nous sommes en retard. Trop d’écoles, d’EHPAD, trop d’hôpitaux, trop de logements restent inadaptés, et pourtant la chaleur tue. Elle frappe les enfants, les personnes âgées, les malades, les travailleurs. Face à cela, nous proposons un «Plan Clim’»: le droit à la fraîcheur pour tous. Rafraîchir des bâtiments publics prioritaires et aider les familles à adapter leur logement, développer l’isolation et les pompes à chaleur réversibles et, aussi, produire ces équipements chez nous. Chaque euro investi doit protéger les Français, relancer notre industrie et créer des emplois européens non délocalisables.

Voilà notre ligne. Ni déni climatique ni écologie punitive: une écologie de protection qui s’adapte et, surtout – surtout! –, qui sauve des vies.
3-0110-0000.englishText:
Madam President, six days of heatwave in June in France, 2,025 deaths. And while some are still talking, others are taking action. In Madrid, the metro is air-conditioned. In Barcelona, ​​climate shelters can be reached within a few minutes on foot. In Greece, employers must provide cooled spaces for their employees. These countries have understood one simple thing: protecting the population from the heat is not a luxury, it is a public policy.

In France, we are late. Too many schools, nursing homes, too many hospitals, too much housing remains unsuitable, and yet the heat kills. It affects children, the elderly, the sick, and workers. Faced with this, we are proposing an “Air Conditioning Plan”: the right to freshness for everyone. Refresh priority public buildings and help families adapt their homes, develop insulation and reversible heat pumps and, also, produce this equipment here. Each euro invested must protect the French, revive our industry and create European jobs that cannot be relocated.

This is our line. Neither climate denial nor punitive ecology: an ecology of protection that adapts and, above all – above all! –, which saves lives.

3-0111-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Caros Colegas, há uma relação inevitável entre alterações climáticas, ondas de calor e incêndios. Esta circunstância é cada vez menos conjuntural e mais estrutural, o que explica a permanência desta mesma sequência.

A questão que se coloca é: o que fazer?
