Há dois níveis de ação muito relevantes. Primeiro, a mitigação: continuar a apostar na redução das causas, combater as alterações climáticas; mas o segundo é o nível da adaptação. Não podemos ser inocentes ao ponto de pensarmos que a mitigação vai acontecer num ápice e temos de nos preparar para essa circunstância.

O que fazer? Preparar as comunidades mais expostas, reforçar a resiliência dos territórios, modernizar e capacitar as autoridades de proteção civil. Investigar ou investir cada vez mais em investigação contra os fogos.

Mas também é preciso reforçar a atuação de nível europeu, nomeadamente o Mecanismo de Proteção Civil da União Europeia e o RescEU, assim como a partilha de meios e a cooperação operacional.

Só com um nível europeu ativo e preparado podemos ser bem‑sucedidos no combate ao flagelo dos fogos.

(O orador aceita responder a várias perguntas «cartão azul»)
3-0111-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Dear Colleagues, there is an inevitable relationship between climate change, heat waves and fires. This circumstance is less and less cyclical and more structural, which explains the permanence of this same sequence.

The question that arises is: what to do?

There are two very relevant levels of action. First, mitigation: continue to focus on reducing the causes, combating climate change; but the second is the level of adaptation. We cannot be so innocent as to think that mitigation will happen quickly and we must prepare for that circumstance.

What to do? Prepare the most exposed communities, strengthen the resilience of territories, modernize and train civil protection authorities. Investigate or invest more and more in research against fires.

But it is also necessary to reinforce action at European level, namely the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism and RescEU, as well as the sharing of resources and operational cooperation.

Only with an active and prepared European level can we be successful in combating the scourge of fires.

(The speaker agrees to answer several “blue card” questions)

3-0112-0000.sourceText:
Nós estamos a discutir o mecanismo de proteção civil na Europa e tenho defendido que precisamos de incluir num mecanismo de solidariedade a recuperação precoce.

Em Portugal, estamos a ter fogos em florestas onde ainda está deitada a madeira das tempestades e temos populações ainda sem eletricidade e mesmo dificuldades em comunicações.

Os grupos aqui do Parlamento Europeu têm tido um consenso sobre a necessidade da recuperação precoce, exceto o seu grupo, o PPE. E, por isso, pergunto-lhe, quando defende aqui mais solidariedade europeia, se não acha que devíamos fazer tudo e assegurar esta recuperação precoce para limparmos o território e repormos eletricidade e comunicações com solidariedade e rapidamente?
3-0112-0000.englishText:
We are discussing the civil protection mechanism in Europe and I have argued that we need to include early recovery in a solidarity mechanism.

In Portugal, we are having fires in forests where wood from the storms is still lying and we have populations still without electricity and even having difficulties with communications.

The groups here in the European Parliament have had a consensus on the need for early recovery, except for your group, the EPP. And therefore, I ask you, when you advocate for more European solidarity here, if you don't think we should do everything and ensure this early recovery to clean up the territory and restore electricity and communications with solidarity and quickly?

3-0113-0000.sourceText:
Reitero que a aposta na mitigação é crucial, mas isso não significa que não nos devamos preparar para as circunstâncias que são inevitáveis.

Infelizmente, as alterações climáticas são uma realidade e a sua afetação ao nível dos incêndios, particularmente dos incêndios florestais, é também uma realidade. E, para isso, a adaptação e a preparação das comunidades são fulcrais.

O que o meu grupo político defende, e a Comissão Europeia tem-no feito, é apostar em fundos como o preparedness, que ajudam as comunidades a ficarem mais resilientes, mais bem preparadas para melhor vencerem estas circunstâncias.
3-0113-0000.englishText:
I reiterate that focusing on mitigation is crucial, but that does not mean that we should not prepare for unavoidable circumstances.

Unfortunately, climate change is a reality and its impact on fires, particularly forest fires, is also a reality. And, for this, the adaptation and preparation of communities are crucial.

What my political group defends, and the European Commission has done, is to invest in funds such as preparedness, which help communities to become more resilient, better prepared to better overcome these circumstances.

3-0114-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Deputado, não vou aqui nacionalizar a questão, como no passado fez, aliás, o PSD com eurodeputados do PS, vou mesmo europeizá-la. Falou do mecanismo de proteção civil e estamos juntos, não apenas nessa ação, nessa ativação e naquilo em que há ajuda aos Estados-Membros, mas é que aqui nesta casa, em 2023, foi aprovada legislação europeia contra a desflorestação.

No último ano, essa legislação aqui voltou para ser ratificada ou para ser adiada. Ao contrário deste grupo que votou a favor da ratificação, o seu grupo votou a favor do adiamento.

Portanto, a pergunta que lhe deixo é: em vez de um mecanismo de proteção civil, não era melhor ter um mecanismo de proteção dos deputados, que seja a favor da prevenção, e evitar aquilo que hoje acontece em Portugal?
3-0114-0000.englishText:
Mr Deputy, I am not going to nationalize the issue here, as the PSD did in the past with PS MEPs, I am actually going to Europeanize it. He spoke about the civil protection mechanism and we are together, not only in this action, in this activation and in what there is help for Member States, but here in this house, in 2023, European legislation against deforestation was approved.

Last year, this legislation came back to be ratified or postponed. Unlike this group that voted in favor of ratification, your group voted in favor of postponement.

Therefore, the question I leave you with is: instead of a civil protection mechanism, wouldn't it be better to have a mechanism to protect deputies, which is in favor of prevention, and avoid what is happening in Portugal today?

3-0115-0000.sourceText:
O grupo político, a que orgulhosamente pertenço, tem tido uma posição muito consistente nessa como noutras matérias. O que nós não podemos defender é um regime de desflorestação que não seja compatível com outras dimensões que importa acautelar.

Tenho defendido, em muitas circunstâncias, que o conceito de sustentabilidade pressupõe não só avaliar os impactos ambientais das medidas económicas, mas também os impactos económicos das medidas ambientais.

Foi disso que falámos quando tratámos de um tema como aquele que aqui sugere e, portanto, consistência, sentido de responsabilidade e, acima de tudo, uma dimensão de sustentabilidade que seja mais adequada às circunstâncias em que nós vivemos.
3-0115-0000.englishText:
The political group, to which I proudly belong, has had a very consistent position on this as on other matters. What we cannot defend is a deforestation regime that is not compatible with other dimensions that must be taken into account.

I have argued, in many circumstances, that the concept of sustainability presupposes not only evaluating the environmental impacts of economic measures, but also the economic impacts of environmental measures.

This is what we talked about when we discussed a topic like the one you suggest here and, therefore, consistency, a sense of responsibility and, above all, a dimension of sustainability that is more appropriate to the circumstances in which we live.

3-0116-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je voudrais dire aux députés d’extrême droite de cet hémicycle qu’ils portent une très lourde part de responsabilité dans la situation actuelle. Vous avez voté contre tous les textes – tous les textes! – qui nous permettent de réduire les pires effets du dérèglement climatique. Vous avez voté contre le principe même qu’il y ait une politique climatique européenne pour réduire les émissions, et donc pour réduire le choc climatique. Vous avez donc une part de responsabilité très claire dans le fait qu’il y ait, par exemple, en France, 12 millions de personnes – 12 millions de personnes! – dont les maisons sont en train de se fissurer, de se craquer et de perdre toute leur valeur à cause de l’impact du dérèglement climatique.

Vous portez une lourde responsabilité dans le fait que des milliers d’agriculteurs sont en train de perdre toutes leurs récoltes, dans le sud de la France, à cause de la multiplication des feux de forêt, à cause du changement climatique. Assumez, au moins! Assumez au moins cette responsabilité! Dites-le devant l’ensemble des Français et des Européens! Et s’il vous plaît, arrêtez, arrêtez cette politique climatosceptique, qui est insupportable aujourd’hui en Europe!

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0116-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I would like to say to the far-right Members of this Chamber that they bear a very heavy share of responsibility for the current situation. You voted against all the texts – all the texts! – which allow us to reduce the worst effects of climate change. You voted against the very principle of there being a European climate policy to reduce emissions, and therefore to reduce the climate shock. You therefore have a very clear share of responsibility in the fact that there are, for example, in France, 12 million people – 12 million people! – whose homes are cracking, crumbling and losing all their value due to the impact of climate change.

You bear a heavy responsibility for the fact that thousands of farmers are losing all their crops in the south of France due to the increase in forest fires due to climate change. Take responsibility, at least! At least assume this responsibility! Say it in front of all French people and Europeans! And please, stop, stop this climate skeptic policy, which is unbearable today in Europe!

(The speaker accepts a blue card question)

3-0117-0000.sourceText: (ESN), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank, Herr Kollege, dass Sie die Zwischenfrage zulassen. Sie haben gerade gesagt, dass die Verantwortung dafür, dass es zu Umweltkatastrophen und Waldbränden gekommen ist, bei der Rechten liegt. Ich habe mal die Frage: Welches Gesetz kennen Sie ganz konkret, wo Sie glauben, dass es nicht zustande gekommen ist wegen einer Abstimmung der Rechten? Ich würde nämlich behaupten, es sind alle Gesetze zustande gekommen, und am Ende ist doch dann die Feststellung, dass Ihre Gesetze einfach wirkungslos sind.
3-0117-0000.englishText: (ESN), question about the “blue card” procedure. – Thank you, Mr. Colleague, for allowing the question. You just said that the responsibility for causing environmental disasters and forest fires lies with the right. I have a question: What specific law do you know that you believe was not passed because of a right-wing vote? I would claim that all the laws have come into being, and in the end it is the conclusion that your laws are simply ineffective.

3-0118-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur, votre groupe politique et l'ensemble des groupes politiques d'extrême droite ont voté contre la loi sur la restauration de la nature, qui permet justement d'avoir des zones humides qui permettent de limiter les impacts du changement climatique sur le stress hydrique ou sur les feux de forêt. Vous avez voté contre le principe même qu'il y ait une loi climat européenne qui respecte l'accord de Paris. Vous avez voté absolument contre tous les textes sur l'industrie, sur l'automobile, sur tout, sur l'agriculture, qui permettraient de limiter les conséquences absolument dramatiques pour les Européens du changement climatique.

Assumez, ayez au moins l'honneur d'assumer cette responsabilité!
3-0118-0000.englishText:
Sir, your political group and all far-right political groups voted against the law on the restoration of nature, which allows us to have wetlands which make it possible to limit the impacts of climate change on water stress or on forest fires. You voted against the very principle of there being a European climate law that respects the Paris agreement. You voted absolutely against all texts on industry, on automobiles, on everything, on agriculture, which would make it possible to limit the absolutely dramatic consequences for Europeans of climate change.

Take responsibility, at least have the honor of taking on this responsibility!

3-0119-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Viele von uns haben in ihrer Heimat in den letzten Jahren die Erfahrung gemacht, dass wir mit Extremwetterereignissen zurechtkommen müssen. Auch in meiner Heimat Sachsen erleben wir diese Entwicklung unmittelbar: Der Großbrand in der Gohrischheide im vergangenen Jahr war der größte Waldbrand Deutschlands. Deshalb geht an dieser Stelle auch ein großer Dank an die vielen tausend Einsatzkräfte, Feuerwehrleute, Katastrophenhelfer, die uns in diesen Situationen zur Seite stehen und helfen.

Aber gerade deshalb ist es richtig, dass Europa seine Katastrophenvorsorge und den preparedness-Gedanken weiter stärkt. Mit dem Europäischen Katastrophenschutzmechanismus, gemeinsamen Löschflugzeugen und Satellitendaten aus dem Copernicus‑Programm schafft die Europäische Union einen echten Mehrwert. Europa hilft, Gefahren früher zu erkennen und im Ernstfall schneller gemeinsam zu handeln.

Mindestens genauso wichtig ist aber die Vorsorge. Wir brauchen widerstandsfähigere Wälder, neue Konzepte der Wasserversorgung, moderne Frühwarnsysteme und Investitionen in den Bevölkerungsschutz. Europa kann hier unterstützen, die Verantwortung beginnt aber vor Ort mit einer preparedness-Strategie, die Menschen schützt, Infrastruktur sichert und unsere Regionen widerstandsfähiger macht – und genau darauf werden wir auch in den Verhandlungen über einen neuen EU‑Haushalt als Hohes Haus achten müssen.
3-0119-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! Many of us have had the experience of having to cope with extreme weather events in our home countries in recent years. We are also experiencing this development directly in my home country of Saxony: the major fire in Gohrischheide last year was the largest forest fire in Germany. That's why a big thank you goes out to the many thousands of emergency services, firefighters and disaster relief workers who stand by us and help us in these situations.

But that is precisely why it is right for Europe to further strengthen its disaster preparedness and the preparedness idea. With the European Civil Protection Mechanism, shared firefighting aircraft and satellite data from the Copernicus program, the European Union is creating real added value. Europe helps to identify dangers earlier and to act together more quickly in an emergency.

But precaution is at least as important. We need more resilient forests, new water supply concepts, modern early warning systems and investments in civil protection. Europe can provide support here, but responsibility begins locally with a preparedness strategy that protects people, secures infrastructure and makes our regions more resilient - and that is exactly what we will have to pay attention to in the negotiations on a new EU budget as a House.

3-0120-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Då var det dags igen – ny värmebölja här i Strasbourg. Den förra vi hade för två veckor sedan ungefär är faktiskt en av de värsta som vi någonsin haft i flera av EU:s länder.

Men EU och medlemsländerna kan göra mycket för att klimatkrisen i alla fall ska bli mindre katastrofal. I dag har vi från Gröna gruppen skickat ett brev till er i kommissionen med våra krav för att skydda oss i Europa från följderna av extremväder.

Vi måste satsa mer på naturbaserade lösningar, se till att klimatresiliens finns med i all lagstiftning, ta fullt ansvar för hela klimatanpassningsarbetet i alla samhällssektorer, sätta tydliga mål för de 36 största utpekade riskerna, och sist men absolut inte minst skydda de arbetare som riskerar att drabbas av den extrema värmen.

Kort sagt, vi behöver en väldigt stark klimatanpassningslag för EU.
3-0120-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! Then it was time again - new heat wave here in Strasbourg. The last one we had about two weeks ago is actually one of the worst we've ever had in several EU countries.

But the EU and its member states can do a lot to make the climate crisis less catastrophic in any case. Today we from the Green Group have sent a letter to you in the Commission with our demands to protect us in Europe from the consequences of extreme weather.

We must invest more in nature-based solutions, ensure that climate resilience is included in all legislation, take full responsibility for the entire climate adaptation work in all sectors of society, set clear goals for the 36 largest identified risks, and last but certainly not least protect the workers who are at risk of being affected by the extreme heat.

In short, we need a very strong climate adaptation law for the EU.

3-0121-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de hittegolf van eind juni was niet de eerste die we tegenkwamen en zal ook niet de laatste zijn. Net daarom moet onze focus liggen op klimaatadaptatie. Maak huizen, kantoren, ziekenhuizen, rusthuizen, scholen en crèches beter bestand tegen die extreme hitte. En daarom moeten we in de eerste plaats stoppen met het demoniseren van airco's. Een airco is geen symbool van klimaatonverschilligheid. Integendeel, het is een noodzakelijk hulpmiddel om ouderen, zieken, jonge kinderen en zorgverleners te beschermen wanneer de temperaturen hoog oplopen. Airco's redden levens. Ze zijn dus levensnoodzakelijk.

Wat we zeker niet moeten doen, is het voorbeeld van de Commissie volgen, want tijdens de hittegolf in juni moesten medewerkers op de lagere verdiepingen van het commissiegebouw namelijk zonder airco werken, terwijl de kantoren van de commissievoorzitter en de andere commissarissen op de bovenste verdiepingen wel gekoeld werden. Orwell zou zeggen: “All floors are equal, but some floors are more equal than others.” Zoiets heet hypocrisie en vat het beleid van de Commissie heel goed samen.
3-0121-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the heat wave at the end of June was not the first we encountered and will not be the last. That is precisely why our focus must be on climate adaptation. Make houses, offices, hospitals, nursing homes, schools and daycare centers more resistant to extreme heat. And that's why we need to stop demonizing air conditioners in the first place. An air conditioner is not a symbol of climate indifference. On the contrary, it is a necessary tool to protect the elderly, the sick, young children and caregivers when temperatures soar. Air conditioners save lives. So they are essential.

What we should certainly not do is follow the example of the Commission, because during the heat wave in June, employees on the lower floors of the committee building had to work without air conditioning, while the offices of the committee chairman and the other Commissioners on the upper floors were cooled. Orwell would say: “All floors are equal, but some floors are more equal than others.” That's called hypocrisy and it summarizes the Commission's policy very well.

3-0122-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Klimaapokalypse abgesagt – so hat sich die AfD im Mai noch gefreut. Ich würde sagen, das ist gealtert wie frische Milch in der Hitzewelle. Keine zwei Monate später, und wir haben europaweit Temperaturen von über 40 Grad, Waldbrände, Stromausfälle, Hitzetote, Plünderungen. Und die Wissenschaft ist sich einig: Diese extreme Hitzewelle wäre ohne den menschengemachten Klimawandel, ohne die Klimakrise undenkbar, und die Europäische Union trifft es unmittelbar.

Was fällt Ihnen am rechten Rand dazu ein? Klimaanlagen. Wow! Haben Sie schon mal in dieser Hitzewelle auf einer Baustelle gearbeitet? Pakete verteilt? Kranke gepflegt? Nein, haben Sie nicht, Sie sitzen hier im klimatisierten Plenarsaal.

Wir brauchen Investitionen in unsere Krankenhäuser, in Pflegeeinrichtungen, in Produktionshallen – ja, aber wir brauchen auch Katastrophenschutz; wir brauchen mehr erneuerbare Energien; wir brauchen eine resiliente Infrastruktur. Und gleichzeitig – und ich weiß, an zwei Dinge gleichzeitig zu denken, fällt Ihnen schwer –, wir haben es in der Hand, dafür zu sorgen, dass dieser Hitzesommer eine Ausnahme bleibt und nicht der Anfang der Klimakrise ist. Der Green Deal muss konsequent weiterverfolgt werden, Emissionen müssen runter. Anpassung alleine wird uns nicht retten. Wann begreifen Sie das endlich?
3-0122-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, dear colleagues! Climate apocalypse canceled - the AfD was happy in May. I'd say this has aged like fresh milk in a heat wave. Less than two months later and we have temperatures over 40 degrees across Europe, forest fires, power outages, heat deaths, looting. And science agrees: This extreme heat wave would be unthinkable without man-made climate change, without the climate crisis, and the European Union is directly affected.

What comes to mind on the right-hand side? Air conditioning systems. Wow! Have you ever worked on a construction site during this heat wave? Packages distributed? Cared for the sick? No, you haven't, you're sitting here in the air-conditioned plenary hall.

We need investments in our hospitals, in care facilities, in production halls - yes, but we also need disaster protection; we need more renewable energy; we need a resilient infrastructure. And at the same time - and I know it's hard for you to think of two things at the same time - it is up to us to ensure that this hot summer remains an exception and is not the beginning of the climate crisis. The Green Deal must be consistently pursued and emissions must be reduced. Adaptation alone will not save us. When will you finally understand this?

3-0123-0000.sourceText:
President, Commissioner, Colleagues, I will address you in Portuguese.

Mais de 1 300 europeus perderam a vida, acima do que é habitual, entre 21 e 29 de junho, devido à onda de calor. Estima-se que se perdem cerca de 44 000 vidas por ano devido às altas temperaturas na Europa.

A prevenção de incêndios e a resiliência climática são uma das agendas mais importantes deste mandato e quero focar-me numa medida de adaptação climática em particular: ar condicionado acessível a todos os europeus de norte a sul. Não é um luxo, é uma necessidade.

Apenas uma em cada cinco casas na UE tem ar condicionado. Nos Estados Unidos e no Japão, nações que enfrentam verões semelhantes aos nossos, são nove em cada dez. Em vários países europeus, instalar um aparelho de ar condicionado em casa pode exigir licenças, aprovações municipais e consentimento da maioria do condomínio.

Uma União que considera urgente a adaptação às alterações climáticas não pode considerar tecnologias como o ar condicionado um luxo dispensável porque gasta muita energia. Deve e tem de tratá-la já como uma medida de adaptação climática.

(A oradora aceita responder a uma pergunta «cartão azul»)
3-0123-0000.englishText:
President, Commissioner, Colleagues, I will address you in Portuguese.

More than 1,300 Europeans lost their lives, more than usual, between 21 and 29 June, due to the heat wave. It is estimated that around 44,000 lives are lost each year due to high temperatures in Europe.

Fire prevention and climate resilience are one of the most important agendas of this mandate and I want to focus on one climate adaptation measure in particular: affordable air conditioning for all Europeans from north to south. It's not a luxury, it's a necessity.

Only one in five homes in the EU has air conditioning. In the United States and Japan, nations that face summers similar to ours, it is nine out of ten. In several European countries, installing an air conditioning unit at home may require licenses, municipal approvals and the consent of the majority of the condominium.

A Union that considers adaptation to climate change urgent cannot consider technologies such as air conditioning a dispensable luxury because it uses a lot of energy. It should and must now be treated as a climate adaptation measure.

(The speaker agrees to answer a “blue card” question)

3-0124-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Deputada Ana Vasconcelos, falou-nos de ar condicionado a propósito da mitigação do calor, mas queria fazer-lhe uma pergunta sobre gestão de recursos hídricos e acesso a fundos europeus para a melhoria das redes de água e de abastecimento de água e de saneamento que, em muitas circunstâncias, se veem limitadas na possibilidade de utilização de fundos europeus para terem melhor eficiência na gestão dos recursos hídricos, questões tão absolutamente essenciais para fazer face às situações de seca e de calor excessivo que temos.

A Senhora Deputada acha que devemos continuar a lidar com este tipo de restrições no acesso aos fundos europeus, por parte das entidades públicas que têm essa responsabilidade da gestão da água e saneamento?
3-0124-0000.englishText:
Madam Ana Vasconcelos, you spoke to us about air conditioning in terms of heat mitigation, but I wanted to ask you a question about water resources management and access to European funds for the improvement of water and water supply and sanitation networks which, in many circumstances, are limited in the possibility of using European funds to have better efficiency in the management of water resources, issues that are so absolutely essential to face the situations of drought and excessive heat that we have.

Does the Honorable Member think that we should continue to deal with this type of restrictions on access to European funds, by public entities that have this responsibility for water and sanitation management?

3-0125-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Deputado, o Sul da Europa, Portugal incluído, tem sido dos maiores beneficiários de fundos europeus para gerir os recursos hídricos. Aliás, é graças à má gestão desses fundos que não temos tido um bom desempenho na gestão desses recursos e na disponibilidade de água aos nossos cidadãos.

Portanto, sim, devemos gerir melhor os nossos recursos, os recursos europeus e os recursos nacionais, para disponibilização de água de qualidade e para evitar perdas de água por causa de infraestruturas mal mantidas.
3-0125-0000.englishText:
Mr Deputy Speaker, Southern Europe, Portugal included, has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of European funds to manage water resources. In fact, it is thanks to the poor management of these funds that we have not performed well in managing these resources and making water available to our citizens.

Therefore, yes, we must better manage our resources, European resources and national resources, to provide quality water and to avoid water losses due to poorly maintained infrastructure.

3-0126-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, nella più recente ondata di calore abbiamo contato in Europa più di 1 300 vittime, chi per malori causati dal lavoro in condizioni insostenibili, chi per fragilità pregresse o malori improvvisi, che hanno intasato i nostri pronto soccorso, chi per essersi tuffato in bacini o corsi d'acqua pericolosi.

Le città che hanno preso sul serio questa questione – guarda caso nessuna guidata da negazionisti di estrema destra – stanno salvando vite, creando rifugi climatici, potenziando il verde urbano, rimuovendo l'asfalto, desigillando il suolo, si salvano vite, soprattutto quelle dei più fragili e dei più soli.

E pensiamo anche ai detenuti, a chi non ha una casa o che ne ha una che è un frigo d'inverno e un forno d'estate. Ed è qui che le strategie per combattere la crisi climatica, la crisi sociale e i loro effetti si saldano. Investire sull'abitare sostenibile taglia emissioni, crea coesione sociale, crea lavoro stabile, potenzia le filiere industriali europee, come quella delle pompe di calore, salva vite e la loro dignità.

Abbiamo gli strumenti, ci vuole il coraggio della politica.
3-0126-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in the most recent heat wave we counted more than 1 300 victims in Europe, some due to illnesses caused by working in unsustainable conditions, some due to previous frailties or sudden illnesses, which clogged up our emergency rooms, some due to having dived into dangerous basins or waterways.

The cities that have taken this issue seriously - coincidentally none led by far-right deniers - are saving lives, creating climate shelters, enhancing urban greenery, removing asphalt, unsealing the soil, lives are being saved, especially those of the most fragile and loneliest.

And we also think of the prisoners, of those who don't have a home or who have one that is a fridge in the winter and an oven in the summer. And this is where the strategies to fight the climate crisis, the social crisis and their effects come together. Investing in sustainable living cuts emissions, creates social cohesion, creates stable jobs, strengthens European industrial supply chains, such as that of heat pumps, and saves lives and their dignity.

We have the tools, we need political courage.

3-0127-0000.sourceText:
Tiago Moreira de Sá (PfE). – Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Gaston Bachelard escreveu que o fogo é a maior ambiguidade da experiência humana. Desde que o primeiro homem contemplou uma chama, percebemos porquê.

O fogo aquece e destrói; ilumina e consome; brilha no Paraíso e queima no Inferno. Mas, acima de tudo, o fogo foi sempre o símbolo da prova.

Em todas as culturas, a prova de fogo representa o teste decisivo, aquele que revela o verdadeiro valor. Foi assim que, durante séculos, se aferiu a autenticidade do ouro. Só o ouro verdadeiro resiste ao fogo.

O ouro e o bombeiro partilham a mesma verdade essencial: não é o fogo que faz o ouro. Nem o bombeiro. O fogo apenas revela aquilo de que um e o outro são feitos. Sempre que entram nas chamas para proteger os outros, as casas dos outros, as vidas dos outros, os bombeiros portugueses passam, uma vez mais, pela prova de fogo. É aí, face a face com as chamas, que se prova que aqueles homens e mulheres são autenticamente feitos de ouro.

Portugal está a ferro e fogo. O Mecanismo de Proteção Civil da União Europeia pode ajudar, mas só os bombeiros portugueses podem impedir que ardam 900 anos de existência.

(O orador recusa uma pergunta «cartão azul» de Marta Temido)
3-0127-0000.englishText:
Tiago Moreira de Sá (PfE). – Madam President, Commissioner, Gaston Bachelard wrote that fire is the greatest ambiguity in the human experience. Since the first man contemplated a flame, we have understood why.

Fire heats and destroys; illuminates and consumes; shines in Paradise and burns in Hell. But, above all, fire has always been the symbol of proof.

In all cultures, the acid test represents the litmus test, the one that reveals true value. This is how, for centuries, the authenticity of gold was measured. Only real gold resists fire.

Gold and the firefighter share the same essential truth: it is not the fire that makes the gold. Neither did the fireman. Fire only reveals what one and the other are made of. Whenever they enter the flames to protect others, other people's homes, other people's lives, Portuguese firefighters go, once again, through the test of fire. It is there, face to face with the flames, that it is proven that those men and women are authentically made of gold.

Portugal is under fire. The European Union's Civil Protection Mechanism can help, but only Portuguese firefighters can stop 900 years of existence from burning down.

(The speaker refuses a “blue card” question from Marta Temido)

3-0128-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, quest'estate ancora milioni di europei vivono giornate soffocanti. Anziani che non riescono a uscire di casa, bambini che devono rinunciare ai giochi nei parchi, famiglie evacuate per gli incendi, vigili del fuoco che rischiano la vita.

Questa non è più un'emergenza, è una realtà.

L'Europa deve continuare a combattere il cambiamento climatico con la mitigazione, basandosi più su incentivi che sulla penalizzazione, ma deve – accanto alla riduzione delle emissioni – pensare a una grande strategia di adattamento.

Dobbiamo continuare a prevenire i cambiamenti climatici, ma accanto a questo dobbiamo proteggere le persone dagli effetti dei cambiamenti climatici.

I tre miliardi di alberi previsti entro il 2030 sono un segnale importante. L'Europa deve rafforzare la propria strategia di riforestazione: un miliardo di alberi in più nelle città per abbassare le temperature da 2 fino a 8 °C in meno, più foreste dove il fuoco ha distrutto interi territori, più verde nelle aree minacciate dalla desertificazione.

Adattarsi al cambiamento climatico non significa arrendersi, significa difendere la salute, difendere la sicurezza, difendere il futuro dei nostri figli. È una responsabilità che oggi l'Europa deve assumersi.
3-0128-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, millions of Europeans are still experiencing stifling days this summer. Elderly people who cannot leave their homes, children who have to give up playing in parks, families evacuated due to fires, firefighters who risk their lives.

This is no longer an emergency, it's a reality.

Europe must continue to fight climate change with mitigation, based more on incentives than on penalties, but it must - alongside the reduction of emissions - think about a major adaptation strategy.

We must continue to prevent climate change, but alongside this we must protect people from the effects of climate change.

The three billion trees expected by 2030 are an important signal. Europe must strengthen its reforestation strategy: one billion more trees in cities to lower temperatures from 2 to 8 °C less, more forests where fire has destroyed entire territories, more greenery in areas threatened by desertification.

Adapting to climate change does not mean giving up, it means defending health, defending safety, defending the future of our children. It is a responsibility that Europe must assume today.

3-0130-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, el año pasado el sur de Europa sufrió una temporada de incendios sin precedentes marcada por los llamados incendios de sexta generación. Los datos de este año tampoco son buenos, más bien lo contrario.

Yo celebro que la Unión Europea esté reaccionando. La Comisión presentó el pasado mes de marzo la primera Comunicación sobre la gestión integrada de los incendios forestales y también ha aumentado el despliegue de medios. Es un paso en la buena dirección y las demás administraciones públicas debían seguir esta línea.

En este sentido, yo quiero celebrar la importancia que la Xunta de Galicia está dando en estos años a la prevención y a la extinción de los incendios. Está reforzando todavía más, en este año 2026, un dispositivo que es una auténtico referente no solo a nivel nacional, sino internacional. Para este año 2026, la Xunta ha mejorado los sistemas a todos los niveles —prevención, vigilancia, extinción—, se han aumentado los medios materiales y humanos disponibles y se ha aprobado el mayor presupuesto de la historia: más de 213 millones de euros, un 18 % más que el año pasado.
3-0130-0000.englishText:
Madam President, last year southern Europe suffered an unprecedented fire season marked by the so-called sixth generation fires. This year's data is not good either, quite the opposite.

I welcome the fact that the European Union is reacting. Last March, the Commission presented the first Communication on the integrated management of forest fires and has also increased the deployment of resources. It is a step in the right direction and other public administrations should follow this line.

In this sense, I want to celebrate the importance that the Xunta de Galicia is giving in recent years to the prevention and extinction of fires. It is further strengthening, in this year 2026, a device that is a true reference not only at a national level, but also internationally. For this year 2026, the Xunta has improved systems at all levels - prevention, surveillance, extinction -, the material and human resources available have been increased and the largest budget in history has been approved: more than 213 million euros, 18% more than last year.

3-0131-0000.sourceText: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, de la intensidad de este debate y de la controversia suscitada es evidente que la Unión Europea es la región del mundo más afectada por el calentamiento global y tiene un balance trágico en mortalidad este mismo verano, pero rebajar los estándares en la ambición europea en la agenda digital y en la agenda migratoria sin duda ninguna es dañino y, a mi juicio, suicida. Pero nada es más injusto que rebajar los estándares en la transición verde justa, y eso no puede pasar, bajo ningún concepto, por rebajar la partida financiera necesaria en el marco financiero plurianual para que la Unión Europea pueda mantener su ambición en la incorporación de energías renovables, en el combate a la carbonización de la economía europea que ha coadyuvado al calentamiento global. Es imprescindible que haya recursos para proteger a la ciudadanía y, especialmente, a la clase trabajadora que no puede soportar este calor.
3-0131-0000.englishText: Madam President, Madam Commissioner, from the intensity of this debate and the controversy raised, it is evident that the European Union is the region of the world most affected by global warming and has a tragic balance in mortality this summer, but lowering the standards of European ambition in the digital agenda and in the migration agenda is undoubtedly harmful and, in my opinion, suicidal. But nothing is more unfair than lowering the standards in the fair green transition, and that cannot happen, under any circumstances, by lowering the necessary financial item in the multiannual financial framework so that the European Union can maintain its ambition in the incorporation of renewable energies, in the fight against the carbonization of the European economy that has contributed to global warming. It is essential that there are resources to protect citizens and, especially, the working class who cannot withstand this heat.

3-0133-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, seuraa EU-uutisia: helleaallot koettelivat Brysseliä ja muuta Eurooppaa, ja komission rakennuksesta sammutettiin osittain ilmastointi. Nyt vaaditaan hiki hatussa EU:n hellestrategioita ja EU:n tason vastauksia. Mutta mitä yhteistä on Suomen hellepäivällä ja Espanjan yli 40 asteen lämpöaallolla? Eipä juuri mitään, ja siksi ratkaisujenkin on oltava erilaisia.

Pelastuspalvelut, terveydenhuolto, rakentaminen ja varautuminen kuuluvat jäsenmaille. Ne tuntevat omat olosuhteensa paremmin kuin yksikään Brysselissä hikoileva virkamies. Mutta kun lämpömittari nousee, näyttää Brysselissä nousevan valtakuume. Jos puhutaan ilmastotoimista, me kyllä voimme käydä keskustelua Kiinasta ja muista riistolaisista, mutta kun puhutaan varautumisratkaisuista tähän hetkeen, niin ratkaisujen on pysyttävä kansallisissa käsissä.
3-0133-0000.englishText:
Dear President, follow the EU news: heat waves hit Brussels and the rest of Europe, and the air conditioning in the Commission building was partially turned off. What is required now is sweat in the hat, EU heat strategies and answers at the EU level. But what do Finland's hot day and Spain's heat wave of more than 40 degrees have in common? Nothing at all, and that's why the solutions have to be different.

Rescue services, health care, construction and preparedness belong to the member countries. They know their own circumstances better than any civil servant sweating in Brussels. But when the thermometer goes up, it seems that the fever is rising in Brussels. If we are talking about climate action, we can have a discussion about China and other exploiters, but when we are talking about contingency solutions for this moment, the solutions must remain in national hands.

3-0135-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, écoutez, cela a été dit, mais 1 222 personnes sont mortes, en Belgique, à cause de la chaleur. Si cela avait été une attaque militaire, comment est-ce que vous auriez réagi ici? S’il y avait eu 1 200 personnes mortes en Belgique à cause d’une attaque militaire? Cela aurait été l’état d’urgence. Vous auriez mobilisé toutes les troupes, toutes les forces, tous les fonds pour réagir à cela. Et ici, aujourd’hui, qu’est-ce que j’entends de la Commission? «Ne vous inquiétez pas, dans quelques mois, on viendra avec un nouveau plan d’action.»

Mais entre-temps, les fonds pour la militarisation, pour la guerre, s’élèvent à des centaines de milliards pour les avions de chasse. Où sont les centaines de milliards pour nos maisons de repos? Pour les hôpitaux? On doit mettre maintenant des couvertures de survie en Europe – des couvertures de survie! – sur les fenêtres de nos hôpitaux pour que les patients ne crèvent pas de chaleur! Les travailleurs qui doivent travailler à 40 degrés. Où est le plan d’urgence? Comment est-ce qu’on va les sauver?

Et là, l’extrême droite qui nie même l’évidence, c’est une honte! Mais la coalition au gouvernement, la coalition au pouvoir ici, a aussi des questions et des responsabilités auxquelles elle doit répondre.
3-0135-0000.englishText:
Madam President, listen, it has been said, but 1,222 people died in Belgium because of the heat. If this had been a military attack, how would you have reacted here? What if there had been 1,200 people dead in Belgium due to a military attack? It would have been a state of emergency. You would have mobilized all the troops, all the forces, all the funds to react to this. And here, today, what am I hearing from the Commission? “Don’t worry, in a few months, we will come with a new action plan.”

But in the meantime, the funds for militarization, for war, amount to hundreds of billions for fighter planes. Where are the hundreds of billions for our nursing homes? For hospitals? We must now put survival blankets in Europe – survival blankets! – on the windows of our hospitals so that patients do not die of heat! Workers who have to work at 40 degrees. Where is the emergency plan? How are we going to save them?

And there, the extreme right which even denies the obvious, it’s a shame! But the coalition in government, the coalition in power here, also has questions and responsibilities that it must answer.

3-0136-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, čestitam povjerenice za povećanje Fonda za EU Rescue mehanizam za 11 milijardi eura.

Kao izvjestiteljica za mišljenje Odbora za razvoj mislim da je to ključno. Godine 2019. ova kuća uopće nije imala interes da išta učinimo na tom pogledu, ali mi još uvijek ne ulažemo ono što je osnovno, a to su vatrogasci. Nitko ne pomaže vatrogascima da nabave opremu, protekli tjedan u Mostaru, znači, mi koristimo ovu opremu i za prekogranično gašenje požara i u Bosni i Hercegovini. Očajan, vatrogasac je došao i rekao: „Mi ne možemo dalje. Mi ne možemo više, mi nemamo opremu”. Znači, požari dolaze i u Hrvatsku, iz Bosne i Hercegovine, 11 milijardi, ovdje se raspravlja, mi za prevenciju još ništa ne radimo.

Ništa ne koristimo, a 1956. u Mostaru je bilo 46 stupnjeva zabilježeno, vrućine je bilo i bit će, ali našeg nerada još uvijek ovdje postoji.
3-0136-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairperson, I congratulate the Commissioner for increasing the Fund for the EU Rescue Mechanism by 11 billion euros.

As the rapporteur for the opinion of the Development Committee, I think this is crucial. In 2019, this house had absolutely no interest in us doing anything in this regard, but we are still not investing in what is basic, which is firefighters. No one is helping the firefighters to get equipment, last week in Mostar, so we use this equipment for cross-border firefighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina as well. Desperate, the fireman came and said: "We can't go on. We can't do it anymore, we don't have the equipment." So, fires are also coming to Croatia, from Bosnia and Herzegovina, 11 billion, it is being discussed here, we are not doing anything for prevention yet.

We don't use anything, and in 1956 it was 46 degrees in Mostar, there was and will be heat, but our inaction still exists here.

3-0137-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, proteger a las personas frente a las olas de calor implica también proteger a los trabajadores y trabajadoras; porque la preparación frente a las olas de calor empieza por no obligar a nadie a elegir entre su salario y su salud.

Por eso, resulta incomprensible que el Partido Popular en España proponga precisamente recortar prestaciones a quienes están de baja, como si los médicos no tuvieran criterio o como si, por ejemplo, sufrir un golpe de calor no fuera lo suficientemente grave. ¿Esa es su receta para proteger a las personas trabajadoras cuando las temperaturas extremas ya están poniendo en riesgo su salud? Porque el cambio climático no entiende de ideologías, pero sí de consecuencias.

Un trabajo de calidad tiene que ser un trabajo seguro, saludable y adaptado a la realidad del siglo XXI. Y eso, en 2026, pasa por proteger a quienes trabajan frente al calor extremo, por establecer normas mínimas comunes de prevención y protección, y pasa por garantizar los ingresos cuando no sea seguro trabajar. Esa es la diferencia entre quienes entienden la adaptación como un recorte y quienes la entendemos como una ampliación de derechos.
3-0137-0000.englishText:
Madam President, protecting people from heat waves also means protecting workers; because preparation for heat waves begins by not forcing anyone to choose between their salary and their health.

Therefore, it is incomprehensible that the Popular Party in Spain precisely proposes cutting benefits to those who are on sick leave, as if doctors had no judgment or as if, for example, suffering from heat stroke was not serious enough. Is that your recipe for protecting working people when extreme temperatures are already putting their health at risk? Because climate change does not understand ideologies, but it does understand consequences.

A quality job has to be safe, healthy and adapted to the reality of the 21st century. And that, in 2026, involves protecting those who work against extreme heat, establishing common minimum standards for prevention and protection, and guaranteeing income when it is not safe to work. That is the difference between those who understand adaptation as a cut and those of us who understand it as an expansion of rights.

3-0139-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, požari su i sigurnosni i gospodarski i klimatski izazov.

Dolazim iz Hrvatske, iz zemlje koja je bila razarana požarima proteklih godina i dobro znamo što znači štititi živote, domove i prirodu. Zahvaljujući snažnom sustavu civilne zaštite, profesionalnim i dobrovoljnim vatrogascima te protupožarnoj zračnoj floti, pokazali smo da dobra organizacija ipak spašava živote i imovinu. To je ono što zovemo prevencija.

Sada tu razinu spremnosti moramo podići na europsku razinu. Potrebni su i veći zajednički kapaciteti kroz RescuEU, brža prekogranična pomoć i više ulaganja u prevenciju i upravljanje šumama i moderni sustavi ranog upozoravanja. Ulaganje u otpornost nije samo klimatska politika. To je politika sigurnosti europskih građana i zato moramo razgovarati o tome prije nego što dođe sljedeća sezona, jer opet ćemo reći, došli su požari, došlo je toplo vrijeme.

Ne, o tome moramo razmišljati danas.
3-0139-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairperson, colleagues, fires are a safety, economic and climate challenge.

I come from Croatia, from a country that has been devastated by fires in recent years, and we know very well what it means to protect lives, homes and nature. Thanks to a strong civil protection system, professional and volunteer firefighters and a firefighting air fleet, we have shown that good organization saves lives and property. This is what we call prevention.

Now we have to raise that level of readiness to the European level. Greater joint capacities through RescuEU, faster cross-border aid and more investment in forest prevention and management and modern early warning systems are also needed. Investing in resilience is not just climate policy. This is the policy of the safety of European citizens and that is why we have to talk about it before the next season comes, because we will say again, the fires have come, the warm weather has come.

No, we have to think about that today.

3-0140-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária Lahbib, a prevenção e o combate aos incêndios exigem a valorização do mundo rural, exigem o investimento nos serviços públicos e nas estruturas de proteção civil.

Quando se defende a competitividade, esmagam-se as pequenas empresas e os pequenos produtores. Quando se defende a militarização, desviando os recursos da PAC e de outros fundos europeus que deviam apoiar os setores produtivos, arruína-se a agricultura familiar, e tudo isto contribui para a desertificação do mundo rural, transformando o território num barril de pólvora.

Quando se impõem limitações orçamentais ao investimento dos Estados nos serviços públicos, condiciona-se a capacidade de ação dos serviços de saúde, condiciona-se a resposta da proteção civil.

Tudo isso é absolutamente essencial ser revertido. Precisamos de melhor planeamento, precisamos de melhor abordagem às questões da prevenção dos incêndios.

Mas nada disto se consegue fazer se não houver da parte dos Estados a capacidade e os meios para fazerem face às suas responsabilidades, incluindo nestas áreas que sublinhei.
3-0140-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner Lahbib, preventing and fighting fires requires the valorization of the rural world, it requires investment in public services and civil protection structures.

When competitiveness is defended, small companies and small producers are crushed. When militarization is defended, diverting resources from the CAP and other European funds that should support the productive sectors, family farming is ruined, and all of this contributes to the desertification of the rural world, transforming the territory into a powder keg.

When budgetary limitations are imposed on States' investment in public services, the capacity of health services to act is conditioned and the response of civil protection is conditioned.

All of this is absolutely essential to reverse. We need better planning, we need a better approach to fire prevention issues.

But none of this can be done if States do not have the capacity and means to face their responsibilities, including in these areas that I highlighted.

3-0141-0000.sourceText: Sinjura President, imma aħna verament ippreparati? Għadna qed nitkellmu fuq il-heatwaves bħallikieku huma l-problema ta' għada. Imma mhumiex. In-nies qegħdin ibatu biex jorqdu, it-tfal ma jistgħux imorru l-iskola bħas-soltu, ħaddiema qed jaħdmu f'temperaturi perikolużi u b'hekk din hija emerġenza soċjali. In-nies m'għandhomx bżonn iktar dibattiti għandhom bżonn protezzjoni u azzjoni llum. Ninsolaw lid-djar tagħna, nipproteġu l-iskejjel u l-isptarijiet, aktar spazji bid-dell fil-bliet tagħna u dan l-istess Parlament, sena ilu, sejjaħ għall-aċċess għall-ilma tax-xorb fl-ispazji pubbliċi. Dawn huma miżuri prattiċi illi jsalvaw il-ħajjiet u eluf ta' persuni diġà tilfu ħajjithom. Għażiża Kummissjoni, daqshekk strateġiji, in-nies iridu azzjoni tanġibbli. Qed nistenna qafas għar-reżiljenza klimatika illi jaħdem, mhux għaxar snin oħra, mhux is-sajf li ġej, imma issa.
3-0141-0000.englishText: Madam President, but are we really prepared? We are still talking about heatwaves as if they are tomorrow's problem. But they are not. People are struggling to sleep, children cannot go to school as usual, workers are working in dangerous temperatures and thus this is a social emergency. People don't need more debates they need protection and action today. We insulate our homes, protect schools and hospitals, more shaded spaces in our cities and this same Parliament, a year ago, called for access to drinking water in public spaces. These are practical measures that save lives and thousands of people have already lost their lives. Dear Commission, so many strategies, people want tangible action. I am waiting for a framework for climate resilience that works, not another ten years, not next summer, but now.

3-0142-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, χιλιάδες νεκροί από το κύμα καύσωνα στην Ευρώπη. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση και οι κυβερνήσεις, αφού αφαίμαξαν δισ. ευρώ από τους λαούς για να ταΐσουν τα αρπακτικά των πράσινων ομίλων με την επίκληση αλλαγών στο κλίμα, τώρα εμφανίζονται προκλητικά αιφνιδιασμένες και απροετοίμαστες. Την ίδια ώρα, προϋπολογίζουν ήδη εκατοντάδες δισ. πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, καταπνίγοντας και τις πιο στοιχειώδεις ανάγκες που αφορούν βεβαίως τους λαούς, όπως στις υποδομές.

Στην εποχή της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης, οι λαοί και οι εργαζόμενοι στους χώρους δουλειάς λιώνουν στα απάνθρωπα ωράρια και τις υψηλές θερμοκρασίες. Θρηνούν απώλειες και καταστροφές από φυσικά φαινόμενα για τα οποία πάντα προβάλλεται ως άλλοθι η κλιματική αλλαγή, ενώ δασικές υπηρεσίες και πυρόσβεση —όπως στην Ελλάδα— είναι γυμνές από υποδομές και προσωπικό. Ισχυριζόσασταν ότι η καπιταλιστική αγορά και ο ανταγωνισμός θα έλυναν ακρίβεια, ενεργειακή φτώχεια, χαμηλούς μισθούς —και τελικά ο λαός ζει σε αδιανόητες στερήσεις για τον 21ο αιώνα. Από παντού φωνάζει η ανάγκη του νέου κόσμου του σοσιαλισμού, ανατρέποντας το σάπιο, ξεπερασμένο καπιταλιστικό σύστημα του πολέμου, των κερδών και της εκμετάλλευσης.
3-0142-0000.englishText:
Madam President, thousands of dead from the heat wave in Europe. The European Union and governments, after bleeding billions of euros from the people to feed the predators of the green groups by invoking climate change, now appear defiantly caught off guard and unprepared. At the same time, they are already budgeting hundreds of billions of war preparations, suppressing even the most basic needs that of course concern the people, such as infrastructure.

In the age of artificial intelligence, people and workers in the workplace are melting in the inhuman hours and high temperatures. They mourn losses and disasters from natural phenomena for which climate change is always presented as an alibi, while forestry services and firefighting - as in Greece - are bare of infrastructure and personnel. You claimed that the capitalist market and competition would solve precision, energy poverty, low wages—and ultimately the people living in unimaginable deprivation for the 21st century. Everywhere cries out the need for the new world of socialism, overthrowing the rotten, outdated capitalist system of war, profit and exploitation.

3-0143-0000.sourceText: Señora presidenta, señorías, Europa necesita un presupuesto a la altura de la emergencia climática. Acaba de empezar el verano y España ya está en llamas. Y frente a los Gobiernos autonómicos que pactan con los negacionistas del cambio climático y recortan los recursos destinados a afrontar esta crisis, estamos los socialistas, que defendemos invertir donde realmente importa: en prevención, en servicios de emergencia, en adaptación y en una solidaridad europea efectiva, especialmente en las zonas rurales y despobladas donde nuestros agricultores, nuestras familias, nuestros vecinos —como los míos de Leciñena y Robres— arriesgan sus vidas cuando intentan acotar las llamas con sus propios medios. Demos prioridad a la agenda de la adaptación y la prevención climática. Actuemos ahora. Salvemos vidas y salvemos también el patrimonio europeo.
3-0143-0000.englishText: Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Europe needs a budget commensurate with the climate emergency. Summer has just begun and Spain is already on fire. And facing the regional governments that agree with climate change deniers and cut the resources intended to confront this crisis, we are the socialists, who defend investing where it really matters: in prevention, in emergency services, in adaptation and in effective European solidarity, especially in rural and depopulated areas where our farmers, our families, our neighbors - like mine in Leciñena and Robres - risk their lives when they try to contain the flames with their own means. Let's prioritize the climate adaptation and prevention agenda. Let's act now. Let's save lives and let's also save European heritage.

3-0147-5000.sourceText:
(PPE), γραπτώς – Κάθε καλοκαίρι η Ευρώπη δοκιμάζεται όλο και περισσότερο από ακραίους καύσωνες και καταστροφικές δασικές πυρκαγιές. Από την Ελλάδα μέχρι την Πορτογαλία και από την Ισπανία μέχρι τη Γαλλία, οι πολίτες μας περιμένουν από την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση να είναι καλύτερα προετοιμασμένη.

Η αλληλεγγύη μέσω του rescEU είναι πολύτιμη, αλλά από μόνη της δεν αρκεί. Χρειαζόμαστε μια πιο φιλόδοξη ευρωπαϊκή προσέγγιση που θα ενισχύει την πρόληψη και την ετοιμότητα.

Γι’ αυτό καλώ την Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή να δημιουργήσει έναν ευρωπαϊκό μηχανισμό κοινών προμηθειών για την πολιτική προστασία, στα πρότυπα των κοινών προμηθειών που αναπτύσσουμε στον τομέα της άμυνας.

Με κοινές ευρωπαϊκές παραγγελίες, τα κράτη μέλη θα μπορούν να προμηθεύονται πυροσβεστικά οχήματα, αεροσκάφη, εξοπλισμό για τους πυροσβέστες και σύγχρονα μέσα αντιμετώπισης φυσικών καταστροφών με χαμηλότερο κόστος, ταχύτερα και με μεγαλύτερη διαλειτουργικότητα.

Οι φυσικές καταστροφές δεν γνωρίζουν σύνορα. Η απάντησή μας δεν μπορεί να περιορίζεται στα εθνικά σύνορα. Μια ισχυρότερη Ευρώπη στην πολιτική προστασία σημαίνει ισχυρότερη επιχειρησιακή ικανότητα για τις Εθνικές Αρχές και μεγαλύτερη ασφάλεια για τους πολίτες και τις περιουσίες τους.
3-0147-5000.englishText:
(PPE), in writing – Every summer Europe is increasingly tested by extreme heat and devastating forest fires. From Greece to Portugal and from Spain to France, our citizens expect the European Union to be better prepared.

Solidarity through rescEU is valuable, but it is not enough on its own. We need a more ambitious European approach that will strengthen prevention and preparedness.

That is why I call on the European Commission to create a European joint procurement mechanism for civilian protection, along the lines of the joint procurement we are developing in the defense sector.

With joint European procurement, Member States will be able to procure fire engines, aircraft, firefighting equipment and modern disaster response equipment at lower costs, faster and with greater interoperability.

Natural disasters know no borders. Our response cannot be limited to national borders. A stronger Europe in civil protection means stronger operational capacity for National Authorities and greater security for citizens and their assets.

3-0147-7500.sourceText:
Európa-szerte rekordmelegek tombolnak, hőhullámok pusztítanak, és több mint 1300 ember vesztette életét a hőség miatt az elmúlt hetekben. Magyarországon is emberek ezrei szenvedtek az extrém hőségtől. Az Európai Bizottság mégis egy új végrehajtási határozattal szigorítja egyes klímagázok kvótáit a következő évekre, ezzel tovább drágítva a hűtőberendezéseket és a légkondicionálókat.

Ahelyett, hogy segítené az embereket az alkalmazkodásban – például megfizethetőbb légkondicionáló berendezésekkel –, a Bizottság olyan döntéseket hoz, amelyek emberek egészségét és biztonságát sodorják veszélybe elvont zöld ideológiai célok érdekében.

Ez nem klímavédelem, hanem zöld fundamentalizmus. A környezet védelme nem történhet az emberek biztonságának és egészségének rovására. Ésszerű, megfizethető alkalmazkodási megoldásokra van szükség, amelyek egyszerre szolgálják a környezet és az emberek védelmét.
3-0147-7500.englishText:
Across Europe, record temperatures are raging, heat waves are wreaking havoc, and more than 1,300 people have lost their lives due to the heat in recent weeks. Thousands of people in Hungary also suffered from the extreme heat. However, with a new executive decision, the European Commission is tightening the quotas of certain climate gases for the following years, thereby further increasing the price of refrigerators and air conditioners.

Instead of helping people adapt – for example with more affordable air conditioning – the Commission is making decisions that put people's health and safety at risk for abstract green ideological goals.

This is not climate protection, but green fundamentalism. Protecting the environment cannot be at the expense of people's safety and health. Reasonable, affordable adaptation solutions are needed that protect both the environment and people.

3-0147-8125.sourceText:
Los incendios y las olas de calor se han convertido en dos de las amenazas más destructivas y letales a las que se enfrenta Europa. Agravadas de manera directa por la emergencia climática, las olas de calor son cada vez más frecuentes, intensas y prolongadas, lo que provoca miles de muertes y crea las condiciones perfectas para que los incendios forestales se propaguen con una virulencia sin precedentes. Nuestra solidaridad está con las víctimas y con los afectados por estos fenómenos.

Prepararse ante estas amenazas implica anticipar, conocer y prevenir los riesgos, comprender las alertas tempranas y saber cómo actuar antes de una emergencia y durante esta. Las autoridades regionales y locales desempeñan un papel insustituible en este ámbito, pues son las que mejor conocen el territorio, la vegetación, las condiciones climáticas locales y las necesidades específicas de sus comunidades. Del mismo modo, la activación de sistemas de alerta temprana y la educación ciudadana sobre evacuación y autoprotección son competencias que solo pueden ejercerse de manera efectiva desde la proximidad. Cada euro invertido en prevención ahorra hasta seis en respuesta y recuperación.

Desde el Gobierno de España y la Unión, se seguirán reforzando los medios, incluido RescEU, en aplicación de los nuevos planes de preparación ante incendios.
3-0147-8125.englishText:
Fires and heat waves have become two of the most destructive and lethal threats facing Europe. Directly aggravated by the climate emergency, heat waves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged, causing thousands of deaths and creating the perfect conditions for forest fires to spread with unprecedented virulence. Our solidarity is with the victims and those affected by these phenomena.

Preparing for these threats involves anticipating, knowing and preventing the risks, understanding early warnings and knowing how to act before and during an emergency. Regional and local authorities play an irreplaceable role in this area, as they are the ones who best know the territory, the vegetation, the local climatic conditions and the specific needs of their communities. Likewise, the activation of early warning systems and citizen education on evacuation and self-protection are skills that can only be exercised effectively from proximity. Every euro invested in prevention saves up to six in response and recovery.

From the Government of Spain and the Union, the means, including RescEU, will continue to be reinforced in application of the new fire preparedness plans.

3-0147-8750.sourceText:
Danes v Sloveniji zaradi ekstremne vročine velja velika požarna ogroženost. V Franciji in Grčiji se medtem že spopadajo z obsežnimi gozdnimi požari – na skrajnem jugu Francije je moralo domove zapustiti okoli 10.000 ljudi, medtem ko požar zahodno od Aten sili prebivalce, da ostanejo v zaprtih prostorih. To ni izjema, ampak nova evropska realnost.

Evropa je to pomlad podrla temperaturne rekorde. Samo junijski vročinski val je v Evropi zahteval že več kot 1.300 smrtnih žrtev. To je grozljiva statistika.

Znanost nam je to napovedala. Zdaj je čas za ukrepanje, ne za popuščanje podnebnim ambicijam.

Slovenija to razume, predvsem zaradi največjega požara iż leta 2022 ter zgodovinskih poplav iż leta 2023. V zadnjih petih letih smo temeljito reformirali sistem zaščite in reševanja. Z novo opremo, infrastrukturo in izobraženim kadrom. Toda enak temeljit preobrat potrebuje celotna Evropska unija. Brez evropske solidarnosti takrat nam v Sloveniji ne bi uspelo, in brez nje danes ne bo uspelo nikomur.

Zato pozivamo: za spopadanje z vročinskimi valovi potrebujemo celovito ukrepanje – od podnebno prilagojene gradnje in prenove stavb, okrepitve evropskega mehanizma civilne zaščite in RescEU do zavezujoče zaščite delavcev pred vročino ter predvsem odločnega zmanjšanja emisij, da omejimo nadaljnjo rast temperatur.

Solidarnost deluje. Zdaj jo moramo okrepiti.
3-0147-8750.englishText:
Today in Slovenia there is a high risk of fire due to the extreme heat. In France and Greece, meanwhile, they are already dealing with large-scale forest fires - in the far south of France, around 10,000 people had to leave their homes, while a fire west of Athens is forcing residents to stay indoors. This is not an exception, but a new European reality.

Europe broke temperature records this spring. The June heat wave alone claimed more than 1,300 lives in Europe. This is a terrifying statistic.

Science predicted it for us. Now is the time to act, not to compromise on climate ambitions.

Slovenia understands this, especially because of the biggest fire in 2022 and historic floods in 2023. In the last five years, we have thoroughly reformed the protection and rescue system. With new equipment, infrastructure and educated staff. But the entire European Union needs the same thorough turnaround. Without European solidarity, we in Slovenia would not have succeeded then, and without it no one will succeed today.

That is why we urge: to deal with heat waves, we need comprehensive action - from climate-adapted construction and renovation of buildings, strengthening of the European Civil Protection Mechanism and RescEU to binding protection of workers from heat and, above all, a decisive reduction of emissions to limit the further rise in temperatures.

Solidarity works. Now we need to strengthen it.

3-0147-9375.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, WHO:n arvioiden mukaan yli 200 000 ihmistä on kuollut Euroopassa viimeisen neljän vuoden aikana lämmöstä johtuvista syistä. Kesäkuun helleaalto oli ennätyksellisen raju. Vain yhden viikon aikana tuhansia ihmisiä menehtyi Euroopassa. Käynnissä oleva El Niño -ilmiö nostaa hetkellisesti maapallon keskilämpötilaa pahentaen tilannetta entisestään, ja vuodesta 2026 odotetaankin ennätyksellisen kuumaa. Voimme pitää kesän ennätyshelteitä esimakuna tulevaan.

Ilmastonmuutos kiihtyy, minkä seurauksena helleaallot ja maastopalot yleistyvät ja voimistuvat. Meidän on tehtävä kaikkemme, jotta välttäisimme ilmastonmuutoksen pahimmat seuraukset. On täysin eri asia, lämpeneekö maapallo kaksi astetta vai neljä. Paras ja kestävin vaihtoehto helleaaltoihin ja maastopaloihin varautumisessa on ilmastonmuutoksen hillitseminen. Mitä vähemmän meillä on helleaaltoja ja maastopaloja tulevaisuudessa, sitä harvemmin niihin tarvitsee reagoida. Siksi myös ilmasto- ja ympäristöpolitiikkamme kunnianhimon tasoa tulisi nostaa vastaamaan tieteellisiä tosiasioita. Nykyiset toimemme eivät yksiselitteisesti riitä.
3-0147-9375.englishText:
Dear President, according to WHO estimates, more than 200,000 people have died in Europe in the last four years from heat-related causes. The June heat wave was record-breaking. In just one week, thousands of people died in Europe. The ongoing El Niño phenomenon temporarily raises the average temperature of the Earth, worsening the situation even more, and from 2026 it is expected to be record hot. We can consider the summer's record heat as a foretaste of what's to come.

Climate change is accelerating, as a result of which heat waves and wildfires are becoming more common and stronger. We must do everything we can to avoid the worst consequences of climate change. It is a completely different matter whether the earth warms two degrees or four. The best and most sustainable option for preparing for heat waves and wildfires is to curb climate change. The fewer heat waves and wildfires we have in the future, the less often we need to react to them. Therefore, the level of ambition in our climate and environmental policy should also be raised to match the scientific facts. Our current actions are clearly not enough.

3-0147-9687.sourceText:
Cada verano se repiten las mismas imágenes: columnas de humo, carreteras cortadas, vecinos pendientes del viento y bomberos al límite. Pero los incendios no empiezan cuando aparecen las llamas; empiezan mucho antes, cuando se abandona el monte, se cierran caminos, se acumula maleza y desaparecen el pastoreo y la actividad rural.

Asturias, mi región, lo sabe bien. El pasado verano ardieron más de 6 000 hectáreas. No perdimos solo vegetación: perdimos paisaje, explotaciones, memoria y futuro para nuestros pueblos.

Europa ha reforzado sus medios de emergencia, su coordinación y su capacidad de respuesta. Esa solidaridad es imprescindible, pero no podemos limitarnos a actuar cuando todo está ardiendo. La Unión debe seguir apoyando la vigilancia, la gestión forestal, los caminos, los puntos de agua y la cooperación entre administraciones.

Pero Europa no puede sustituir la responsabilidad de los Estados miembros, quienes deben convertir los fondos europeos en actuaciones concretas sobre el terreno. Y España no ha aprovechado suficientemente estos recursos.

La prevención quizá no ofrezca grandes fotografías, pero salva viviendas, empleos, hectáreas y vidas. Los recursos existen; lo que falta es voluntad política y capacidad de gestión para actuar durante el invierno y la primavera, antes de volver a lamentar en verano lo que no se hizo a tiempo.
3-0147-9687.englishText:
Every summer the same images are repeated: columns of smoke, blocked roads, neighbors waiting for the wind and firefighters at their limit. But fires don't start when flames appear; They begin much earlier, when the forest is abandoned, roads are closed, undergrowth accumulates and grazing and rural activity disappear.

Asturias, my region, knows this well. Last summer, more than 6,000 hectares burned. We didn't just lose vegetation: we lost landscape, farms, memory and future for our people.

Europe has strengthened its emergency resources, its coordination and its response capacity. That solidarity is essential, but we cannot limit ourselves to acting when everything is burning. The Union must continue to support surveillance, forest management, roads, water points and cooperation between administrations.

But Europe cannot replace the responsibility of the Member States, who must convert European funds into concrete actions on the ground. And Spain has not taken sufficient advantage of these resources.

Prevention may not provide great pictures, but it saves homes, jobs, acres and lives. The resources exist; What is missing is the political will and management capacity to act during the winter and spring, before regretting again in the summer what was not done in time.
