El Gobierno de Sánchez liquidó a las mejores unidades de policía antidrogas y las otras, sin medios, son impotentes. De ahí los muertos por las ventajas de los narcos que ha provocado el propio Gobierno español.

España es hoy el paraíso de los narcos gracias al Gobierno amigo. Primero, porque están abiertas todas las costas y, después, porque campan a sus anchas y porque invierten y blanquean su dinero en España.

La única forma de frenar el narcotráfico es acabar con los Gobiernos que trabajan para él; es decir, acabar con el socialismo —con el narcosocialismo— es la clave para acabar con esta plaga.
3-0286-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, drug trafficking is not only a terrible enemy for the health of individuals and societies, today drug trafficking is also a weapon of hybrid war and a colossal political power.

Organized crime has entered politics. Decades ago, drug cartels allied themselves with the Ibero-American left. Today, that narcosocialism of the São Paulo Forum is already in Europe and entered through Spain. The Sánchez Government liquidated the best anti-drug police units and the others, without means, are powerless. Hence the deaths due to the advantages of drug traffickers that the Spanish Government itself has caused.

Spain is today the paradise of drug traffickers thanks to the friendly Government. First, because all the coasts are open and, second, because they roam freely and because they invest and launder their money in Spain.

The only way to stop drug trafficking is to put an end to the governments that work for it; That is to say, ending socialism—with narcosocialism—is the key to ending this plague.

3-0287-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, per troppo tempo le istituzioni hanno trattato il narcotraffico, lo spaccio e il consumo di droga come un male endemico, ormai non più estirpabile, quasi invincibile, a volte da arginare, se non, nelle peggiori delle ipotesi, addirittura da ignorare o favorire.

Se vogliamo, invece, essere responsabili come persone impegnate in politica, dobbiamo dimostrare di avere un cuore aperto alla coscienza e al bene comune. Dobbiamo crederci, crederci fermamente, dobbiamo credere nel fatto che queste reti criminali possono essere sconfitte e possono essere sconfitti coloro che guadagnano sulla pelle dei più giovani e sulla morte delle persone.

E se è così, allora abbiamo il compito, il dovere, di dare gli strumenti adeguati alle nostre forze dell'ordine e di investire maggiori risorse. Dobbiamo imporre ai porti maggiori e costanti controlli, difendere i confini e usare il pugno di ferro.

Questo è l'unico modo per vincere contro i trafficanti di morte. Non possiamo infatti lasciare soli coloro che combattono, da soli, in prima linea.
3-0287-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, for too long the institutions have treated drug trafficking, drug dealing and drug consumption as an endemic evil, no longer eradicatable, almost invincible, sometimes to be curbed, if not, in the worst cases, even ignored or encouraged.

If, however, we want to be responsible as people involved in politics, we must demonstrate that we have a heart open to conscience and the common good. We must believe in it, believe in it firmly, we must believe in the fact that these criminal networks can be defeated and those who profit from the skin of the youngest and from the death of people can be defeated.

And if this is the case, then we have the task, the duty, to give our law enforcement agencies the appropriate tools and to invest more resources. We must impose greater and constant controls on ports, defend the borders and use an iron fist.

This is the only way to win against the death dealers. In fact, we cannot leave alone those who fight, alone, on the front line.

3-0289-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa attrae e consuma enormi quantità di sostanze stupefacenti in un mercato di droghe miliardario.

L'Europa è diventata luogo di incontro tra narcotraffico colombiano, narcomafie europee e italiane e organizzazioni criminali belghe, olandesi, francesi e altre.

Questo criminale mercato si alimenta anche di produzione di droga in paesi dell'Asia – dal Laos al Myanmar, dall'Afghanistan al Pakistan – con il recente allarme dell'ONU sulla provenienza di droghe sintetiche da est.

Una rete di complicità rende possibile eludere i controlli di polizia nei maggiori porti europei. Non basta accertare l'identità di quanti attraversano il Mediterraneo e l'Atlantico, è urgente intervenire e intercettare all'origine gli accordi criminali tra cartelli nello smercio verso l'Europa.

Urge, in sede di loro prevista riforma, signor Commissario, rafforzare Europol ed Eurojust nella loro lotta alla criminalità organizzata, per offrire una risposta europea forte. C'è inoltre bisogno di maggiore coordinamento per contrastare il riciclaggio dei profitti del narcotraffico tramite sistemi bancari e finanziari europei.

Considerando gli effetti che questo riciclaggio di denaro ha nella vita...

(Il Presidente toglie la parola all'oratore)
3-0289-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, Europe attracts and consumes enormous quantities of narcotics in a billion-dollar drug market.

Europe has become a meeting place between Colombian drug trafficking, European and Italian drug mafias and Belgian, Dutch, French and other criminal organizations.

This criminal market is also fueled by drug production in Asian countries - from Laos to Myanmar, from Afghanistan to Pakistan - with the recent UN warning about the origin of synthetic drugs from the East.

A network of complicity makes it possible to evade police checks in major European ports. It is not enough to ascertain the identity of those crossing the Mediterranean and the Atlantic, it is urgent to intervene and intercept at the source the criminal agreements between cartels in the sale to Europe.

It is urgent, in the context of their planned reform, Commissioner, to strengthen Europol and Eurojust in their fight against organized crime, to offer a strong European response. There is also a need for greater coordination to combat the laundering of drug trafficking profits through European banking and financial systems.

Considering the effects this money laundering has on life...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

3-0290-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Europa steht vor einer Explosion der Drogenkriminalität, und wir erleben eine Rekordverfügbarkeit illegaler Drogen. Die EU hat die USA inzwischen als größten Kokainmarkt überholt, und bei Eurojust sind die Fallzahlen in nur fünf Jahren – nur fünf Jahren – um 60 % gestiegen; Drogen im Wert von 20 Mrd. EUR wurden festgestellt. Mehr als die Hälfte der gefährlichsten kriminellen Netzwerke Europas sind im Drogenschmuggel tätig, zwei Drittel setzen Gewalt ein, über 70 % nutzen Korruption, um Behörden und Hafenpersonal zu beeinflussen.

Das ist keine Randerscheinung mehr; das ist ein sicherheitspolitisches Totalversagen. Selbst Europol stellt fest: Die Netzwerke, die Drogen nach Europa schmuggeln, sind häufig dieselben kriminellen Strukturen, die auch illegale Migration und Menschenhandel organisieren. Die Kartelle haben längst verstanden: Europas offene Grenzen und politische Kuschelkurse sind ihr Geschäftsmodell.

Unsere Häfen dürfen nicht länger Einfallstore für Drogenkartelle sein, und unsere Grenzen dürfen nicht länger Geschäftsmodelle für Schleuser sein. Die Lösung ist so simpel und heißt: Außengrenzen sichern, Schleusernetzwerke zerschlagen und illegale Migration stoppen.
3-0290-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Europe is facing an explosion in drug crime and we are experiencing record availability of illegal drugs. The EU has now overtaken the US as the largest cocaine market, and Eurojust has seen case numbers rise by 60% in just five years – just five years; Drugs worth €20 billion were discovered. More than half of Europe's most dangerous criminal networks are involved in drug smuggling, two-thirds use violence, and over 70% use corruption to influence authorities and port staff.

This is no longer a fringe phenomenon; This is a total security policy failure. Even Europol notes: The networks that smuggle drugs into Europe are often the same criminal structures that also organize illegal migration and human trafficking. The cartels have long understood: Europe's open borders and political cuddly courses are their business model.

Our ports must no longer be gateways for drug cartels, and our borders must no longer be business models for smugglers. The solution is so simple and means securing external borders, dismantling smuggling networks and stopping illegal migration.

3-0291-0000.sourceText:
Dolors Montserrat (PPE). – Señor presidente, señorías, el narcotráfico mata: mata a quienes consumen, mata el futuro de los jóvenes, mata el Estado de Derecho y mata a los agentes que lo combaten.

Los guardias civiles asesinados en Huelva y Barbate arrollados por narcolanchas no son una tragedia aislada, son la consecuencia de años de impunidad, de falta de recursos de un Gobierno como el de Sánchez, que desprotege a las fuerzas de seguridad, que liquida OCON-Sur —la unidad clave en la lucha contra el narco—.

Europol lo ha advertido: los narcotraficantes ya no solo introducen la droga desde fuera de la Unión Europea, sino que están infiltrados en Europa. Operan desde nuestros puertos, blanquean capitales con empresas pantalla y usan armas de guerra y tecnología punta para corromper, intimidar y matar.

Europa, comisario, acierta con la Alianza Europea de Puertos, persiguiendo el dinero y cortando el oxígeno financiero de las bandas, pero el nuevo marco estratégico solo funcionará si protegemos a quienes nos protegen, tipificamos el eurodelito a cada ataque a cada policía, reconocemos la profesión de riesgo de nuestros policías.

El narcotráfico es la mayor amenaza para la seguridad de Europa y debemos estrechar la cooperación entre Europol, Eurojust, Frontex, Aduanas y las policías nacionales. Debemos exigir a cada Estado más compromiso, más agentes, más medios, más seguridad jurídica y una legislación más dura, porque solo así derrotaremos el narcotráfico. Pero no con Gobiernos que abandonen a sus policías, sino con una Europa que les reconozca, les respalde y les proteja.

(La oradora se niega a que Petras Gražulis le formule una pregunta con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0291-0000.englishText:
Dolors Montserrat (PPE). – Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, drug trafficking kills: it kills those who consume it, it kills the future of young people, it kills the rule of law and it kills the agents who fight it.

The civil guards murdered in Huelva and Barbate run over by drug boats are not an isolated tragedy, they are the consequence of years of impunity, of lack of resources of a Government like Sánchez's, which fails to protect the security forces, which liquidates OCON-Sur - the key unit in the fight against drug trafficking.

Europol has warned: drug traffickers no longer only introduce drugs from outside the European Union, but they are infiltrated into Europe. They operate from our ports, launder money with front companies and use weapons of war and cutting-edge technology to corrupt, intimidate and kill.

Europe, Commissioner, is right with the European Ports Alliance, chasing money and cutting off the financial oxygen of the gangs, but the new strategic framework will only work if we protect those who protect us, we classify each attack on each police officer as a Eurocrime, we recognize the risky profession of our police officers.

Drug trafficking is the greatest threat to Europe's security and we must strengthen cooperation between Europol, Eurojust, Frontex, Customs and national police. We must demand from each State more commitment, more agents, more means, more legal security and tougher legislation, because only then will we defeat drug trafficking. But not with governments that abandon their police officers, but with a Europe that recognizes them, supports them and protects them.

(The speaker refused to allow Petras Gražulis to ask her a question under the “blue card” procedure)

3-0292-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le narcotrafic est une menace majeure pour nos sociétés. Il alimente les violences, corrompt nos économies et fragilise l’état de droit. Face à des organisations criminelles qui opèrent à l’échelle mondiale, notre réponse doit être européenne.

Mais ne nous trompons pas de combat. Le narcotrafic ne se combattra pas en entretenant la confusion entre migration et criminalité organisée. Les réseaux qui acheminent la drogue vers les ports européens n’ont rien à voir avec celles et ceux qui fuient les conflits et les persécutions. Penser qu’une politique migratoire toujours plus restrictive répondra à nos défis sécuritaires est une impasse politique et une erreur stratégique. La lutte contre le narcotrafic exige autre chose, notamment davantage de coopération entre les États membres et une action déterminée contre le blanchiment d’argent.

Soyons fermes contre les trafiquants. Soyons lucides sur les réponses à apporter. Refusons les raccourcis qui affaiblissent à la fois notre sécurité et nos valeurs.
3-0292-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Mr Commissioner, dear colleagues, drug trafficking is a major threat to our societies. It fuels violence, corrupts our economies and weakens the rule of law. Faced with criminal organizations that operate on a global scale, our response must be European.

But let’s not get the fight wrong. Drug trafficking cannot be fought by maintaining confusion between migration and organized crime. The networks that transport drugs to European ports have nothing to do with those fleeing conflict and persecution. Thinking that an ever more restrictive migration policy will respond to our security challenges is a political impasse and a strategic error. The fight against drug trafficking requires something else, notably more cooperation between Member States and determined action against money laundering.

Let's be firm against traffickers. Let's be clear about the answers to be given. Let us refuse shortcuts that weaken both our security and our values.

3-0293-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Mesdames et Messieurs, chers collègues, face au narcotrafic, il ne faut plus des mots mais des actes, car, derrière chaque cargaison interceptée, il y a désormais du sang versé dans nos villes européennes.

L’Union européenne semble enfin prendre conscience de l’ampleur de la menace. Nous avons applaudi des deux mains un accord important avec l’Équateur – dont j’ai été le rapporteur –, pays devenu un point stratégique dans le trafic de cocaïne vers l’Europe. Nous avons également tout fait pour renforcer l’agence de police européenne Europol, afin de mieux coordonner la lutte contre les réseaux criminels transnationaux.

Autant de vraies avancées contre des narcomafias qui désormais kidnappent, corrompent, intimident et, bien souvent, tuent en plein jour. Je pense au jeune Mehdi Kessaci, au père de famille et chauffeur Uber Nessim Ramdane, à Marseille, ou encore à l’étudiante Socayna Jean, victimes des balles, des kalashnikovs, des narcotrafiquants, et tous morts à Marseille, devenue capitale française du narcotrafic. Derrière Marseille, d’autres villes suivront si rien n’est fait: Anvers, Hambourg, Rotterdam. De par mon métier de policier, j’ai vu l’organisation de ces groupes et leur force de frappe sans foi ni loi. Notre faiblesse depuis des décennies est leur principal carburant.

Pour tous ceux qui l’ont payé de leur vie: reprenons le contrôle de nos frontières maritimes, protégeons nos ports stratégiques et donnons des moyens réels à nos douaniers, policiers, gendarmes, magistrats et services de renseignement!

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0293-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, dear colleagues, in the face of drug trafficking, we no longer need words but actions, because, behind each intercepted shipment, there is now blood shed in our European cities.

The European Union finally seems to realize the extent of the threat. We applauded with both hands an important agreement with Ecuador – for which I was rapporteur – a country that has become a strategic point in cocaine trafficking to Europe. We have also done everything to strengthen the European police agency Europol, in order to better coordinate the fight against transnational criminal networks.

So many real advances against drug addicts who now kidnap, corrupt, intimidate and, very often, kill in broad daylight. I think of the young Mehdi Kessaci, the father and Uber driver Nessim Ramdane, in Marseille, or the student Socayna Jean, victims of bullets, Kalashnikovs, drug traffickers, and all dead in Marseille, which has become the French capital of drug trafficking. Behind Marseille, other cities will follow if nothing is done: Antwerp, Hamburg, Rotterdam. Through my job as a police officer, I saw the organization of these groups and their lawless strike force. Our weakness for decades is their main fuel.

For all those who paid for it with their lives: let's regain control of our maritime borders, protect our strategic ports and give real resources to our customs officers, police, gendarmes, magistrates and intelligence services!

(The speaker accepts a blue card question)

3-0294-0000.sourceText: Aš manau, kad mes visi sutiksime, kad čia nėra nei ideologijų, nei kairės, nei dešinės. Visi matome didžiulę problemą, kad tas narkotikų biznis ar nusikaltėliai klesti tiesiog Europoje. Ir viena tendencija – ar jūs nemanote, kad čia persipina jėgos struktūros su nusikalstamu pasauliu, tie, kurie turi kontroliuoti? Pavyzdžiui, Lietuvoje sulaikyta dvylika pareigūnų ir savivaldybės darbuotojai, kurie dalyvavo kontrabandoje. Ar tai yra tik Lietuvos problema? Ar čia yra visuotinė problema?
3-0294-0000.englishText: I think we will all agree that there are no ideologies here, neither left nor right. We all see a huge problem that the drug business or criminals are thriving right in Europe. And one trend - don't you think that there is an intertwining of power structures with the criminal world, those who have to control? For example, twelve officials and municipal employees were arrested in Lithuania for their involvement in smuggling. Is this only a problem in Lithuania? Is this a global problem?

3-0295-0000.sourceText:
Écoutez, cher collègue, la corruption est un combat que nous devons tous mener, mais la majorité de nos policiers, gendarmes, agents pénitentiaires, services de renseignement et militaires font un travail exceptionnel.

Je veux le redire ici: le problème, ce n’est pas majoritairement la corruption dans nos démocraties, ce sont des voyous qu’on a laissés que trop faire et qui ont bénéficié d’un laxisme judiciaire, d’un laxisme politique, d’une lâcheté… Et en France, l’extrême gauche et la gauche sont membres des partis qui défendent des voyous, des criminels, plutôt que nos policiers, nos gendarmes.

Donc, il faut changer de logiciel et il faut une vraie révolution, avec une volonté transpartisane de lutter contre ce narcotrafic, qui peut mettre à bas nos démocraties.
3-0295-0000.englishText:
Listen, dear colleague, corruption is a fight that we all must fight, but the majority of our police, gendarmes, prison officers, intelligence services and military do an exceptional job.

I want to say it again here: the problem is not mainly corruption in our democracies, it is thugs who have been allowed to do too much and who have benefited from judicial laxity, political laxity, cowardice... And in France, the extreme left and the left are members of the parties which defend thugs, criminals, rather than our police, our gendarmes.

So, we need to change the software and we need a real revolution, with a transpartisan desire to fight against this drug trafficking, which can bring down our democracies.

3-0296-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Mam przekonanie, że Unia Europejska przez długi czas nie doceniała problemu ochrony granic, pozostawiając państwa na zewnętrznych granicach Unii bez dostatecznego wsparcia. Aby sprawić, że granice Unii będą bezpieczne, należy spełnić kilka warunków. Kraje graniczne muszą uzyskać znaczące wsparcie finansowe związane z zadaniami ochrony morskiej i lądowej granicy zewnętrznej. Służby krajowe muszą zostać wzmocnione i mieć stosowne narzędzia techniczne – także te, które były tu, w Parlamencie Europejskim, poddawane powszechnej krytyce. Frontex musi wszechstronnie wspierać służby krajowe, a nie prowadzić postępowania wobec funkcjonariuszy. Dość z polityczną poprawnością – państwa muszą zliberalizować przepisy dotyczące używania środków przymusu bezpośredniego, a funkcjonariuszom zapewnić bezpieczeństwo prawne.

Nie sposób nie wiązać przestępczości narkotykowej z grupami przestępczymi rekrutującymi się z obywateli państw trzecich, nielegalnych imigrantów i oszustów azylowych. Aplikujący o pobyt w Unii muszą mieć świadomość, że nieprzestrzeganie prawa wiąże się z szybką karą i skuteczną readmisją. Skuteczna ochrona granic jest pierwszym krokiem przywrócenia porządku i bezpieczeństwa w wielu miastach europejskich.
3-0296-0000.englishText:
Mr President! I believe that the European Union has for a long time underestimated the problem of border protection, leaving states on the external borders of the Union without sufficient support. To make the EU's borders secure, several conditions must be met. Border countries must obtain significant financial support related to the tasks of maritime and land protection of the external border. National services must be strengthened and have appropriate technical tools - including those that have been widely criticized here in the European Parliament. Frontex must comprehensively support national services and not conduct proceedings against officers. Enough with political correctness - states must liberalize the regulations on the use of direct coercive measures and ensure legal security for officers.

It is impossible not to associate drug crime with criminal groups recruited from third-country nationals, illegal immigrants and asylum fraudsters. Applicants for residence in the EU must be aware that failure to comply with the law is associated with a quick penalty and effective readmission. Effective border protection is the first step in restoring order and security in many European cities.

3-0297-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, iedere dag weer gaan onze mensen van de politie en de douane de strijd aan tegen internationale drugsbendes. Door kleine ruimtes kruipend op zoek naar drugs, verstopt op de meest onwaarschijnlijke plekken, geïntimideerd door georganiseerde criminelen die ze proberen te corrumperen. Het gevecht tegen deze onterechte criminaliteit dwingt ons allemaal harder en slimmer te gaan lopen. Een paar heilige huisjes zullen omver moeten: minder nationaal denken, meer Europees.

Ten eerste, meer middelen, meer bevoegdheden en meer mogelijkheden voor Europol, onze unieke Europese politie, met meer operationele aanwezigheid in het veld en meer investeringen in innovaties zoals artificiële intelligentie en drones. Ten tweede, een ambitieuze Europese anti-corruptiestrategie. Zonder corruptie is er geen drugshandel. Ten derde, durven blijven investeren in preventie in onze wijken om te voorkomen dat kwetsbare kinderen gerekruteerd worden door drugscriminelen. Narcos is meer dan een Netflixtitel en cosmetische oplossingen krijgen van mij een duimpje omlaag.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
3-0297-0000.englishText:
Mr President, every day our police and customs people fight international drug gangs. Crawling through small spaces looking for drugs, hiding in the most unlikely places, intimidated by organized criminals trying to corrupt them. The fight against this unjust crime forces us all to run faster and smarter. A few sacred cows will have to be knocked down: less national thinking, more European.

First, more resources, more powers and more opportunities for Europol, our unique European police force, with more operational presence in the field and more investment in innovations such as artificial intelligence and drones. Second, an ambitious European anti-corruption strategy. Without corruption there is no drug trade. Thirdly, dare to continue investing in prevention in our neighborhoods to prevent vulnerable children from being recruited by drug criminals. Narcos is more than a Netflix title and cosmetic solutions get a thumbs down from me.

(The speaker agrees to answer a “blue card” question)

3-0298-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Deputada García Hermida-Van Der Walle, ouvimos neste debate um deputado da extrema-direita espanhola, Hermann Tertsch, fazer uma diferença entre o tráfico de droga, que é mau se vier de alguns países, mas que já pode não ser tão mau se vier de outros.

A mim parece-me que isto é um aproveitamento político verdadeiramente indecente do tráfico de droga e é particularmente difícil de compreender como é que é possível fazer este tipo de aproveitamento quando estão em causa, por exemplo, as vidas de profissionais das forças e serviços de segurança, como aqueles que foram, infelizmente, assassinados em operações de combate à droga.

O que lhe pergunto é se não acha que este é um aproveitamento que não devia ser feito?
3-0298-0000.englishText:
Mrs García Hermida-Van Der Walle, in this debate we heard a deputy from the Spanish extreme right, Hermann Tertsch, making a difference between drug trafficking, which is bad if it comes from some countries, but which may not be so bad if it comes from others.

It seems to me that this is a truly indecent political exploitation of drug trafficking and it is particularly difficult to understand how this type of exploitation is possible when, for example, the lives of professionals in the security forces and services are at stake, such as those who were, unfortunately, murdered in anti-drug operations.

What I'm asking you is, don't you think this is a use that shouldn't be done?

3-0302-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, la recente perdita di due agenti della Guardia civile spagnola per lo speronamento da parte di una barca di narcotrafficanti è l'ennesima dimostrazione di quanto il traffico di stupefacenti costituisca una seria minaccia per le nostre società.

Come mamma di due appartenenti alle forze dell'ordine voglio esprimere la mia solidarietà alle loro famiglie.

Enormi profitti per le organizzazioni criminali, perdita di vite umane, corruzione, riciclaggio, violenza dilagante, minori reclutati, insicurezza ed enormi costi sanitari e sociali: tutto questo è ed è sempre stato il traffico di droga.

E l'impatto sull'Europa – mercato di consumo, hub di transito e luogo di produzione – è davvero enorme. Dobbiamo quindi proseguire con decisione nell'attuazione della strategia ProtectEU e soprattutto nel piano d'azione per individuare e contrastare le rotte di traffico marittime, terrestri e aeree, rafforzare la cooperazione tra Frontex, Europol, l'MAOC-N e le forze di polizia nazionali, migliorare lo scambio di informazioni tra autorità doganali di contrasto e giudiziarie e rafforzare la cooperazione con i paesi terzi di origine degli stupefacenti.

Per questo occorre dotare di risorse e di mezzi le nostre forze di polizia, ma occorre anche investire in prevenzione e recupero per contrastare non solo l'offerta, ma anche la domanda di stupefacenti.

È questa, contro la droga, una battaglia non facile, è vero, ma che l'Unione europea intera non può permettersi di perdere.
3-0302-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the recent loss of two agents of the Spanish Civil Guard when they were rammed by a drug traffickers' boat is yet another demonstration of how drug trafficking constitutes a serious threat to our societies.

As the mother of two members of the police force, I want to express my solidarity with their families.

Huge profits for criminal organizations, loss of life, corruption, money laundering, rampant violence, recruited minors, insecurity and enormous health and social costs: all this is and always has been drug trafficking.

And the impact on Europe – consumer market, transit hub and place of production – is truly enormous. We must therefore continue resolutely in the implementation of the ProtectEU strategy and especially in the action plan to identify and combat maritime, land and air trafficking routes, strengthen cooperation between Frontex, Europol, the MAOC-N and national police forces, improve the exchange of information between customs law enforcement and judicial authorities and strengthen cooperation with third countries of origin of drugs.

This is why we need to equip our police forces with resources and means, but we also need to invest in prevention and recovery to counter not only the supply but also the demand for drugs.

This is not an easy battle against drugs, it is true, but one that the entire European Union cannot afford to lose.

3-0304-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, hoy no voy a hablar de lo peligrosas que son las mafias del Estrecho. Eso ya lo sabemos todos: sabemos que tienen más dinero, sabemos que, sorprendentemente, tienen más medios y sabemos que son cada vez más violentas.

Lo que no entiendo es por qué seguimos tratando a quien nos defiende como si el problema no fuera sangrante. En la frontera del sur de España, los guardias civiles mueren, señorías, mueren y no tienen reconocida la tan peleada profesión de riesgo. Todavía seguimos sin considerar eurodelito las agresiones a las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad europeos que se juegan la vida, cada día, frente a criminales con armas de guerra, sin seguridad física y sin seguridad jurídica.

Y todavía hay Gobiernos en los que se toman decisiones incomprensibles, como el de España, al desmantelar la unidad OCON‑Sur, una unidad que había logrado miles de detenciones y algunos de los mayores golpes al narcotráfico en el Campo de Gibraltar.

Este es el mensaje que reciben las mafias. Ellas se organizan, ellas se arman, avanzan y nosotros desmantelamos herramientas que funcionan. Señorías, despierten: la violencia extrema se combate con medios, con contundencia y con autoridad.
3-0304-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Mr. Commissioner, today I am not going to talk about how dangerous the Strait mafias are. We all already know that: we know that they have more money, we know that, surprisingly, they have more means and we know that they are increasingly violent.

What I don't understand is why we continue treating those who defend us as if the problem were not serious. On the southern border of Spain, the civil guards die, ladies and gentlemen, they die and the much-disputed profession of risk is not recognized. We still do not consider attacks on European security forces and bodies who risk their lives, every day, against criminals with weapons of war, without physical security and without legal security, as a Eurocrime.

And there are still Governments in which incomprehensible decisions are made, such as that of Spain, when dismantling the OCON-Sur unit, a unit that had achieved thousands of arrests and some of the biggest blows to drug trafficking in the Campo de Gibraltar.

This is the message that the mafias receive. They organize, they arm themselves, they advance and we dismantle tools that work. Ladies and gentlemen, wake up: extreme violence is fought with means, with forcefulness and with authority.

3-0305-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, σήμερα βρισκόμαστε εδώ όχι μόνο για να συζητήσουμε αλλά κυρίως για να εκφράσουμε την ευγνωμοσύνη και τον σεβασμό μας στους αφανείς ήρωες, στις γυναίκες και στους άνδρες του Πολεμικού Ναυτικού, των εθνικών ακτοφυλακών, των σωμάτων ασφαλείας, της Frontex και όλων των ευρωπαϊκών υπηρεσιών που αγωνίζονται για την καταπολέμηση της μάστιγας των ναρκωτικών· σε όλους εκείνους που με αυταπάρνηση και υψηλό αίσθημα καθήκοντος φυλάσσουν τα εθνικά και ευρωπαϊκά μας σύνορα.

Η απειλή των ναρκωτικών μπορεί πολλές φορές να μοιάζει μακρινή και αθέατη, στην πραγματικότητα όμως είναι διαρκής, οργανωμένη και αδυσώπητη. Γνωρίζουμε καλά το βαρύ αποτύπωμα στις γειτονιές, στους δρόμους και στις πόλεις μας. Γνωρίζουμε όμως εξίσου καλά ότι η καταπολέμηση των ναρκωτικών απαιτεί συνεχή επαγρύπνηση, άριστο συντονισμό και διεθνή συνεργασία. Γι' αυτό οφείλουμε από αυτή την αίθουσα να ενισχύουμε διαρκώς το έργο όσων επιχειρούν καθημερινά στις θάλασσες και στα λιμάνια της Ευρώπης, στην πρώτη γραμμή της μάχης απέναντι στο οργανωμένο έγκλημα. Κάθε φορτίο ναρκωτικών που αναχαιτίζεται δεν θα φτάσει ποτέ στις κοινωνίες μας. Και κάθε εγκληματικό δίκτυο που εξαρθρώνεται είναι μια νίκη για την ασφάλεια, την ανθρώπινη αξιοπρέπεια και τη συνοχή των κοινωνιών της Ευρώπης.
3-0305-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, today we are here not only to discuss but above all to express our gratitude and respect to the unsung heroes, the women and men of the Navy, the national coast guards, the security forces, Frontex and all the European agencies fighting to fight the scourge of drugs; to all those who selflessly and with a high sense of duty guard the national and our European borders.

The drug threat can often seem distant and invisible, but in reality it is persistent, organized and relentless. We are well aware of the heavy footprint in our neighbourhoods, streets and cities. But we know equally well that the fight against drugs requires constant vigilance, excellent coordination and international cooperation. That is why we must from this room constantly strengthen the work of those who operate every day in the seas and ports of Europe, on the front line of the battle against organized crime. Every drug shipment that is intercepted will never reach our societies. And every criminal network dismantled is a victory for security, human dignity and the cohesion of Europe's societies.

3-0307-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, si le narcotrafic prospère, c’est parce que – disons-le – nos frontières sont devenues des passoires et que l’Union européenne continue de multiplier les obstacles à ceux qui sont chargés de les protéger. Nos policiers, nos douaniers et nos magistrats ont besoin d’une coopération renforcée, pas d’une bureaucratie supplémentaire. Il faut faciliter la collecte et l’échange des données entre les autorités nationales, Europol, Frontex et Eurojust. Les cartels, eux, n’attendent pas les autorisations de Bruxelles pour partager leurs informations.

Pourtant, le Contrôleur européen de la protection des données a suspendu la coopération entre Europol et Frontex. C’est une décision totalement déconnectée de la réalité du terrain. À force de privilégier les contraintes administratives sur l’efficacité opérationnelle, ce sont les criminels qui en sortent gagnants.

Nous devons également clarifier le rôle de la future Agence européenne des douanes. Il n’est pas question de créer une nouvelle couche institutionnelle qui viendrait brouiller les missions d’Europol et de Frontex.

Enfin, donnons à l’Alliance des ports européens les moyens d’échanger librement leurs renseignements avec les autorités de police et de justice. Face à des mafias toujours plus puissantes, notre réponse doit être simple: plus de coopération, plus de renseignement, plus d’efficacité et moins d’idéologie.
3-0307-0000.englishText:
Madam President, if drug trafficking prospers, it is because – let’s say it – our borders have become sieves and the European Union continues to increase obstacles to those responsible for protecting them. Our police, customs officers and magistrates need greater cooperation, not additional bureaucracy. We must facilitate the collection and exchange of data between national authorities, Europol, Frontex and Eurojust. The cartels do not wait for authorization from Brussels to share their information.

However, the European Data Protection Supervisor has suspended cooperation between Europol and Frontex. It is a decision totally disconnected from the reality on the ground. By prioritizing administrative constraints over operational efficiency, it is the criminals who come out on top.

We also need to clarify the role of the future European Customs Agency. There is no question of creating a new institutional layer which would confuse the missions of Europol and Frontex.

Finally, let us give the Alliance of European Ports the means to freely exchange their information with the police and justice authorities. Faced with ever more powerful mafias, our response must be simple: more cooperation, more intelligence, more efficiency and less ideology.

3-0308-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, un vas pleacă încărcat cu 10 tone de cocaină dintr-o țară sud-americană către Europa; fiul de 16 ani al unui doctor din Bruxelles - sau din Paris, sau din Berlin, sau din Roma, sau din București - încearcă primul său gram la o petrecere. Este un copil bun, cu rezultate extraordinare la școală, bine educat de părinți și cu un viitor luminos în față - sau cel puțin așa trebuia să-i fie viitorul până la acel prim gram. Știe că nu este bun, dar prietenii râd de el că nu are curaj să încerce și își spune că este puternic și că va fi o singură dată, apoi se va opri.

În timp ce băiatul trage prima sa linie de „zăpadă” sau „pudra morții”, alt vas încărcat ajunge într-un port european și reușește să descarce marfa. Zecile de tone înseamnă sute de mii, chiar milioane de victime, de dependenți, de tineri care își anulează viitorul, de copii buni precum al meu sau ai voștri.

Și fix în timp ce se întâmplă toate astea, în Parlamentul European, unii colegi de-ai noștri votează să nu întărească structurile de forță competente în combaterea traficului de droguri. Adică fix acele structuri care ar fi putut opri cele două vase venite de pe mare și ne-ar fi putut salva copiii.
3-0308-0000.englishText:
Madam President, a vessel leaves loaded with 10 tons of cocaine from a South American country to Europe; the 16-year-old son of a doctor from Brussels - or from Paris, or from Berlin, or from Rome, or from Bucharest - tries his first gram at a party. He's a good kid with great school results, well-educated by his parents, and a bright future ahead of him - or at least that's what his future was supposed to be until that first gram. He knows he's no good, but his friends laugh at him for not having the guts to try, and he tells himself that he's strong and it'll only be one time, then it'll stop.

While the boy draws his first line of "snow" or "death powder", another loaded ship arrives at a European port and manages to unload its cargo. Tens of tons mean hundreds of thousands, even millions of victims, addicts, young people who cancel their future, good children like mine or yours.

And right while all this is happening, in the European Parliament, some of our colleagues are voting not to strengthen the force structures competent in combating drug trafficking. I mean exactly those structures that could have stopped the two ships coming from the sea and could have saved our children.

3-0309-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, les cartels entrent en Europe par nos failles. La ligne portée en France par Bruno Retailleau doit trouver son prolongement européen. Le narcotrafic n’est plus l’écume de faits divers dispersés, c’est une puissance criminelle, maritime, financière, territoriale. Elle défie nos États, elle jauge nos frontières, elle appelle des moyens d’exception.

Cette puissance transforme nos scrupules en couloir de circulation. Quand il faut empêcher un trafiquant identifié de revenir sur son point de deal, une partie de la gauche trouve l’État trop ferme. Quand les habitants réclament de l’air, elle rouvre le débat sur la dépénalisation. C’est une étrange boussole: moins de contraintes pour les dealers, plus d’abandon pour nos populations.

Lorsque la drogue entre par la mer, c’est l’Europe qui prend l’eau, emportée par une vague qui gagne nos campagnes, qui finit par recruter, par abîmer et par tuer nos enfants. Alors, passons aux actes! Faisons de nos ports des zones de riposte douanière, avec coordination inter-services, commandements clairs, contrôles ciblés vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre, protection des agents menacés. Faisons payer les cartels pour la sécurité: chaque euro doit équiper les services répressifs. Il ne suffit plus d’écoper, il faut définitivement reprendre le gouvernail!

(L'oratrice accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0309-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, cartels enter Europe through our loopholes. The line carried in France by Bruno Retailleau must find its European extension. Drug trafficking is no longer the foam of scattered news items, it is a criminal, maritime, financial, territorial power. It challenges our States, it measures our borders, it calls for exceptional means.

This power transforms our scruples into a traffic corridor. When it is necessary to prevent an identified trafficker from reconsidering his point of deal, part of the left finds the State too firm. When residents demand air, it reopens the debate on decriminalization. It’s a strange compass: fewer constraints for dealers, more abandonment for our populations.

When drugs enter by sea, it is Europe that takes on the water, carried away by a wave that reaches our countryside, which ends up recruiting, damaging and killing our children. So, let’s take action! Let's make our ports customs response zones, with inter-service coordination, clear commands, targeted controls twenty-four hours a day, protection of threatened agents. Let's make the cartels pay for security: every euro must equip the law enforcement services. It is no longer enough to bail out, we must definitely take back the rudder!

(The speaker accepts a blue card question)

3-0310-0000.sourceText:
Céline Imart, vous parlez de Bruno Retailleau et du narcotrafic en France: hier, la présomption de légitime défense a été adoptée à l’Assemblée nationale. On va enfin croire nos policiers avant les voyous.

Mais, pendant un an, Monsieur Retailleau était à Beauvau: réforme de la police judiciaire, recrutement des OPJ, paiement des heures supplémentaires, simplification de la procédure pénale, mais aussi peines planchers, peines minimales pour lutter contre les récidivistes et les délinquants qui s’en prennent à l’uniforme de la République.

Vous ne l’avez pas fait pendant un an: du courage, Céline Imart, rejoignez Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella! Le redressement, c’est maintenant! Ce que vous n’avez pas pu ou voulu faire, faites-le à nos côtés! Le pronostic vital de notre pays est engagé.
3-0310-0000.englishText:
Céline Imart, you are talking about Bruno Retailleau and drug trafficking in France: yesterday, the presumption of self-defense was adopted in the National Assembly. We will finally believe our police before the thugs.

But, for a year, Mr. Retailleau was in Beauvau: reform of the judicial police, recruitment of OPJs, payment of overtime, simplification of the criminal procedure, but also minimum sentences, minimum sentences to fight against repeat offenders and delinquents who attack the uniform of the Republic.

You haven't done it for a year: courage, Céline Imart, join Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella! The recovery is now! What you couldn't or didn't want to do, do it alongside us! The vital prognosis of our country is in jeopardy.

3-0311-0000.sourceText:
Merci, Monsieur Valet, pour votre très aimable invitation. Je tiens à vous rappeler que Bruno Retailleau n’était pas ministre de la justice, mais ministre de l’intérieur. Donc, il a agi sur les compétences qu’il avait à l’intérieur de son portefeuille, qui malheureusement ne concernent pas notamment la justice pour les mineurs.

Mais il a agi sur ce qui, dans son portefeuille, pouvait être fait, c’est-à-dire avoir une loi d’urgence narcotrafic, qui va aller taper les trafiquants au portefeuille, qui va mobiliser les forces de l’ordre et les rendre plus efficaces sur ces points de deal.

Je crois que nous avons des convictions assez similaires sur ce sujet, et en tout cas le combat continue à l’échelle française, mais aussi à l’échelle européenne, parce que ce combat-là, il est vital pour nos enfants.
3-0311-0000.englishText:
Thank you, Mr. Valet, for your very kind invitation. I would like to remind you that Bruno Retailleau was not Minister of Justice, but Minister of the Interior. So, he acted on the skills he had within his portfolio, which unfortunately do not concern justice for minors in particular.

But he acted on what, in his portfolio, could be done, that is to say have an emergency drug trafficking law, which will hit the traffickers in the wallet, which will mobilize the police and make them more effective on these points of dealing.

I believe that we have quite similar convictions on this subject, and in any case the fight continues on a French scale, but also on a European scale, because this fight is vital for our children.

3-0312-0000.sourceText:
Fru formand! Kære kollegaer. Jeg har været politibetjent i 19 år, og jeg ved, hvad narkotika i virkeligheden er. Det er at banke på en dør klokken to om natten. En far og en mor åbner, og deres ansigter krakelerer, når de forstår, hvorfor. Deres barn er død af en overdosis. Det glemmer man aldrig.

Imens så strømmer kokainen ind gennem Europas havne og grænser. Og hvad gør EU? De skriver strategier, mens narkobagmændene tjener milliarder. Strategier alene stopper ikke forbryderne. Det gør betjentene, tolderne og effektiv kontrol. Så løsningen, det er ikke mere EU. Løsningen er permanent grænse- og havnekontrol, stærke nationale politistyrker og hårdere straffe. Giv landene magten tilbage og politiet de redskaber, der skal til for at stoppe forbryderne.

Mine gamle kollegaer knokler hver evig eneste dag, så svigt dem ikke. Det skylder vi både dem og vores unge mennesker.

(Taleren accepterede at besvare et blåt kort-spørgsmål)
3-0312-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Dear colleagues. I have been a police officer for 19 years and I know what drugs really are. It's knocking on a door at two in the morning. A father and a mother open up and their faces crack when they understand why. Your child has died of an overdose. You never forget that.

Meanwhile, the cocaine flows in through Europe's ports and borders. And what does the EU do? They write strategies while the drug lords make billions. Strategies alone will not stop the criminals. This is done by the officers, the customs officers and effective control. So the solution, it is no more EU. The solution is permanent border and port controls, strong national police forces and tougher penalties. Give the states back the power and the police the tools they need to stop the criminals.

My old colleagues are struggling every single day, so don't let them down. We owe that to both them and our young people.

(The speaker agreed to answer a blue card question)

3-0314-0000.sourceText:
Jeg er rigtig stolt af, at vi i Danmark har vores retsforbehold, for jeg har selv arbejdet med international og grænseoverskridende kriminalitet igennem 10 år. Og vores retsforbehold i Danmark beskytter både politiet og vores lovgivning. Det beskytter således, at vi faktisk kan implementere nye efterforskningsmetoder uden at skulle spørge EU om lov. Og det gør, at man kan tilpasse efterforskningsmetoderne inden for det land, man nu kommer fra.

Så jeg er stolt af, at vi i Danmark har et retsforbehold, som beskytter os på lige præcis det her område. Og til det skal jeg også sige, at i og med at jeg selv har arbejdet inden for det her område, så har vi en lang række parallelaftaler i Danmark. Og Danmark er måske en af dem, der er mest førende og bedst til at opklare international organiseret kriminalitet. Så derfor har vi parallelaftaler, som gør, at vi kan få alle de samme oplysninger, som man sidder og forhandler om i den nye aftale.
3-0314-0000.englishText:
I am really proud that in Denmark we have our reservation of rights, because I myself have worked with international and cross-border crime for 10 years. And our reservation of rights in Denmark protects both the police and our legislation. It thus protects that we can actually implement new investigative methods without having to ask the EU for permission. And this means that you can adapt the investigation methods within the country you are now from.

So I'm proud that in Denmark we have a legal reservation that protects us in exactly this area. And to that I must also say that since I myself have worked in this area, we have a large number of parallel agreements in Denmark. And Denmark is perhaps one of the most leading and best at solving international organized crime. So that's why we have parallel agreements, which means that we can get all the same information that you sit and negotiate about in the new agreement.

3-0316-0000.sourceText: Tak for spørgsmålet. Det kan man løse, og det løser man allerede i dag, fordi man har, med de her parallelaftaler, fuldstændig adgang til alle de her oplysninger. Det er blevet nummerpladeregistrering, vi har samarbejdet med Europol, vi har selv et kontor dernede, vi kan få DNA-svar osv. Så jeg ved, at det her er muligt i Danmark, og jeg har selv gjort det utallige gange, og oplysningerne er kun et opkald væk. Og jeg kan supplere med, at Danmark sidste år har sendt 40 000 SIENA-anmodninger, som også er et samarbejde, man har. Så vores parallelaftaler gælder faktisk ikke kun Europa, men også uden for, og det gør, at vi står langt stærkere i efterforskning af kriminalitet i Danmark.
3-0316-0000.englishText: Thanks for the question. This can be solved, and it is already being solved today, because with these parallel agreements, you have complete access to all this information. It has become number plate registration, we have cooperated with Europol, we have an office down there ourselves, we can get DNA answers, etc. So I know that this is possible in Denmark, and I have done it countless times myself, and the information is only a phone call away. And I can add that Denmark sent 40,000 SIENA requests last year, which is also a collaboration that we have. So our parallel agreements actually apply not only to Europe, but also outside, and this means that we are in a much stronger position in the investigation of crime in Denmark.

3-0317-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Nie da się mówić o przestępczości zorganizowanej, która trudni się handlem narkotykami, bez tematu nielegalnej imigracji. Tak się składa, że akurat koalicja rządząca w Unii Europejskiej jest odpowiedzialna za wpuszczenie nielegalnych imigrantów. Więc jeżeli chcecie zwalczyć drogę dotyczącą narkotyków, to musicie też zająć się nielegalną imigracją. Temat, który dotyczy konsekwencji chociażby za pomoc związaną z nielegalnymi imigrantami pod przykrywką organizacji pozarządowych, leży i nie jest dalej procedowany, dlatego, że lewica to blokuje.

Może warto zwrócić uwagę na to, jakim doświadczeniem może podzielić się Polska. Tak się składa, że miałem przyjemność być w rządzie, który zatrzymał nielegalną migrację, który doprowadził do tego, że odsyłano nielegalnych migrantów.

Ale co się dzieje? Zaraz na drugi dzień przyjmujecie rozwiązania, które są związane z paktem migracyjnym. Chcecie, aby ci migranci, z których wielu trudni się działalnością przestępczą – wzrost przestępczości na różnym tle, w tym seksualnym, jest gigantyczny – zostali przerzuceni do innych krajów? Więc prosta odpowiedź jest taka: zero nielegalnych migrantów i zamkniemy również temat związany ze skalą problemu z narkotykami.
3-0317-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is impossible to talk about organized crime that deals in drug trafficking without the topic of illegal immigration. It so happens that the ruling coalition in the European Union is responsible for admitting illegal immigrants. So if you want to tackle drugs, you also have to tackle illegal immigration. The topic, which concerns the consequences of, for example, helping illegal immigrants under the guise of non-governmental organizations, remains and is not pursued further because the left is blocking it.

Perhaps it is worth paying attention to what experience Poland can share. It so happens that I had the pleasure of being in the government that stopped illegal migration, that led to illegal migrants being sent back.

But what's happening? The very next day you adopt solutions related to the migration pact. Do you want these migrants, many of whom are engaged in criminal activities - the increase in crime on various grounds, including sexual, is gigantic - to be transferred to other countries? So the simple answer is: no illegal migrants and we will also close the issue related to the scale of the drug problem.

3-0318-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, igual les parezco un poco dura, pero voy a decir algo.

La droga que mañana van a ofrecer a cualquiera de nuestros hijos, la cocaína en cualquier capital europea, probablemente venga de España, todo un país europeo.

España es la principal puerta del sur de Europa, y es una puerta que está completamente abierta. Es la puerta por la que se está colando buena parte de la droga que está envenenando nuestro continente.

Tranquilos, porque esta frontera tiene guardianes, guardias civiles valientes que cada noche salen a plantarle cara al narco con más vocación que recursos. Pero quiero decirle algo, comisario: les estamos mandando a la guerra sin armas. Mientras enfrente tienen semisumergibles y armamento bélico, detrás tienen un Estado cada vez más débil y un Gobierno enfermo de corrupción.

Ha muerto gente en Barbate, han muerto en Huelva y van a seguir muriendo. Porque los criminales los matan, sí. Pero por falta también de nuestra voluntad política. Así que, comisario, por favor, más recursos para Europa y para Frontex, más inteligencia compartida, penas más duras contra los criminales.

No esperemos al próximo funeral para reconocer el peligro. Son una profesión de riesgo.
3-0318-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, I may seem a little harsh to you, but I am going to say something.

The drug that tomorrow they are going to offer to any of our children, cocaine in any European capital, probably comes from Spain, an entire European country.

Spain is the main door to southern Europe, and it is a door that is completely open. It is the door through which a good part of the drugs that are poisoning our continent are slipping.

Don't worry, because this border has guards, brave civil guards who go out every night to stand up to the drug traffickers with more vocation than resources. But I want to tell you something, commissioner: we are sending them to war without weapons. While in front they have semi-submersibles and military weapons, behind them they have an increasingly weak State and a Government sick with corruption.

People have died in Barbate, they have died in Huelva and they will continue to die. Because criminals kill them, yes. But also due to lack of our political will. So, Commissioner, please, more resources for Europe and for Frontex, more shared intelligence, tougher penalties against criminals.

Let's not wait for the next funeral to recognize the danger. They are a risky profession.

3-0319-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Tylko w 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad półtora miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. Belgijska Antwerpia jest dla gangów narkotykowych bramą przemytu do Europy – przypadkiem, tuż pod nosem eurokratów, tych nauczycieli praworządności.

W latach 2018–2023 liczba pacjentów rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów związanych z kokainą wzrosła o 31%. Liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu uzależnienia od cracku wzrosła o 35%. Taka skala przemytu narkotyków to dzieło Komisji Europejskiej. To polityka otwartych granic. W czasie, gdy Europejczycy boją się gangów narkotykowych w swoich miastach, kartele narkotykowe traktują europejskie wybrzeża i porty jak swoje magazyny. Służby ochrony granic potrzebują realnego wsparcia, twardego prawa i wolnej ręki w działaniu, a nie ataku lewicowej agendy ze strony Komisji Europejskiej.

Powiem szczerze: brak waszej skuteczności w zwalczaniu przemytu narkotyków do Europy nasuwa pytanie, czy wy czasami nie współpracujecie z przemytnikami i nie czerpiecie jakichś korzyści finansowych z handlu narkotykami w Europie. Tak dla kolegi pytam.
3-0319-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In 2024 alone, European Union member states reported over one and a half million drug-related crimes. Antwerp, Belgium, is a smuggling gateway to Europe for drug gangs - coincidentally, right under the noses of Eurocrats, these teachers of the rule of law.

Between 2018 and 2023, the number of patients entering treatment for cocaine-related problems increased by 31%. The number of people entering treatment for crack addiction has increased by 35%. This scale of drug smuggling is the work of the European Commission. It's an open borders policy. At a time when Europeans fear drug gangs in their cities, drug cartels treat Europe's coastlines and ports as their warehouses. Border protection services need real support, tough law and a free hand in action, not an attack by the leftist agenda from the European Commission.

Let me be honest: your lack of effectiveness in combating drug smuggling into Europe raises the question whether you sometimes cooperate with smugglers and derive some financial benefits from drug trafficking in Europe. I'm asking for my friend's sake.

3-0321-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, a nova estratégia de combate às drogas da União Europeia não pode repetir dois erros: esquecer a emergência do combate às drogas sintéticas, ignorar que as suas fronteiras ocidentais começam no coração do Atlântico com os Açores e com a Madeira.

É pelo Atlântico que têm passado rotas cada vez mais exploradas por redes internacionais de tráfico de droga, com barcos, drones e até narcossubmarinos. É por isso que é urgente reforçar a vigilância marítima, a tecnologia, a partilha de informação, a cooperação para as agências europeias, mas também o reconhecimento da importância das nossas forças de segurança que tanto têm feito com tão pouco.

Precisamos também de reconhecer que as fronteiras externas da União Europeia começam pelos Açores e pela Madeira, e os Açores e a Madeira têm um papel fundamental na segurança da União Europeia. E é também por isso que precisamos de ter uma nova estratégia para o Atlântico, que enquadre as novas tensões geopolíticas, mas também o combate ao tráfico de droga e a segurança da União Europeia.
3-0321-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the European Union's new strategy to combat drugs cannot repeat two mistakes: forgetting the emergency of the fight against synthetic drugs, ignoring that its western borders begin in the heart of the Atlantic with the Azores and Madeira.

It is through the Atlantic that routes increasingly explored by international drug trafficking networks, with boats, drones and even narco-submarines, have passed. This is why it is urgent to reinforce maritime surveillance, technology, information sharing, cooperation for European agencies, but also recognition of the importance of our security forces who have done so much with so little.

We also need to recognize that the external borders of the European Union begin with the Azores and Madeira, and the Azores and Madeira play a fundamental role in the security of the European Union. And this is also why we need to have a new strategy for the Atlantic, which addresses the new geopolitical tensions, but also the fight against drug trafficking and the security of the European Union.

3-0322-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, i nostri confini sono un colabrodo e voi lo sapete.

Oggi parliamo di narcotraffico nel Mediterraneo, ma la droga è il sintomo: la malattia è che noi non difendiamo i nostri confini, perché ogni anno dai nostri porti arrivano tonnellate di droga – soprattutto dal Nord Africa – che stanno uccidendo migliaia di giovani europei.

Quella stessa rotta, che negli ultimi 15 anni ha portato clandestinamente, via mare, un milione e mezzo di immigrati in Italia e tre milioni in Europa, è stata sfruttata anche per trafficare droga e armi e alimentare profitti miliardari per le mafie.

Mentre voi predicavate porti aperti e mentre von der Leyen e le sinistre europee trasformavano Frontex in un bersaglio ideologico, scafisti e organizzazioni criminali facevano affari d'oro.

Difendere i confini non è uno slogan, è l'unico strumento serio e concreto per bloccare il narcotraffico.
3-0322-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, our borders are a sieve and you know it.

Today we talk about drug trafficking in the Mediterranean, but drugs are the symptom: the disease is that we do not defend our borders, because every year tons of drugs arrive from our ports - especially from North Africa - which are killing thousands of young Europeans.

That same route, which in the last 15 years has brought clandestinely, by sea, one and a half million immigrants to Italy and three million to Europe, has also been exploited to traffic drugs and weapons and fuel billions in profits for the mafias.

While you preached open ports and while von der Leyen and the European left transformed Frontex into an ideological target, smugglers and criminal organizations were doing brisk business.

Defending the borders is not a slogan, it is the only serious and concrete tool to stop drug trafficking.

3-0324-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário Costas Kadis, é preciso atuar em duas dimensões: por um lado, combater a toxicodependência, fazendo desaparecer o negócio lucrativo do narcotráfico; por outro lado, combater o tráfico de droga e as redes criminosas que nele florescem.

Em ambas as dimensões, o papel dos Estados é determinante. Para vencer este combate, precisamos de políticas eficazes de combate à toxicodependência, serviços públicos de saúde e inserção social robustos, de investimento público no tratamento e reabilitação dos consumidores.

Precisamos também de medidas de política criminal adequadas e de investimento nas forças e serviços de segurança nacionais, incluindo nas alfândegas, melhorando as condições de trabalho dos seus profissionais e reforçando a sua capacidade operacional.

Ao mesmo tempo, precisamos de nos libertar das imposições da UE sobre os orçamentos nacionais que condicionam o investimento público, que é essencial para todos estes objetivos.

E não podemos permitir que o combate ao narcotráfico seja o pretexto para a militarização, para justificar medidas de vigilância indiscriminada sobre os cidadãos, ou para propagandear suspeitas e preconceitos de natureza racista e xenófoba, como infelizmente acabámos de ouvir nas últimas intervenções feitas pela extrema‑direita.
3-0324-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner Costas Kadis, we need to act in two dimensions: on the one hand, combat drug addiction, making the lucrative business of drug trafficking disappear; on the other hand, combat drug trafficking and the criminal networks that flourish within it.

In both dimensions, the role of States is decisive. To win this fight, we need effective policies to combat drug addiction, robust public health and social insertion services, and public investment in the treatment and rehabilitation of consumers.

We also need appropriate criminal policy measures and investment in national security forces and services, including customs, improving the working conditions of their professionals and strengthening their operational capacity.

At the same time, we need to free ourselves from EU impositions on national budgets that condition public investment, which is essential for all these objectives.

And we cannot allow the fight against drug trafficking to be the pretext for militarization, to justify indiscriminate surveillance measures on citizens, or to propagate suspicions and prejudices of a racist and xenophobic nature, as we have unfortunately just heard in the latest interventions made by the extreme right.

3-0325-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le trafic de drogue obéit aux lois classiques de l’offre et de la demande. Aussi, tant qu’il y aura des consommateurs, il y aura des trafiquants de drogue, et le trafic de drogue continuera avec son cortège de morts, de destruction de la santé d’une partie de nos populations et de déstabilisation de nos sociétés.

Si nous voulons triompher dans cette lutte contre le trafic de drogue, alors nous devons travailler à dissuader la consommation de drogue. Cela passera par trois stratégies. Premièrement, le déploiement de sanctions dissuasives contre les consommateurs de drogue. Deuxièmement, la diffusion massive, dans tous les médias, de spots d’information sur les ravages de la drogue sur la santé, mais également sur les morts occasionnées, car les consommateurs doivent prendre conscience du fait qu’ils ont du sang sur les mains. Dernier point, la confiscation systématique de tous les biens acquis grâce au trafic de drogue. C’est ainsi que nous triompherons.
3-0325-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, drug trafficking obeys the classic laws of supply and demand. Also, as long as there are users, there will be drug traffickers, and drug trafficking will continue with its procession of deaths, destruction of the health of part of our populations and destabilization of our societies.

If we are to succeed in this fight against drug trafficking, then we must work to deter drug use. This will involve three strategies. First, the deployment of dissuasive sanctions against drug users. Secondly, the massive distribution, in all media, of information spots on the ravages of drugs on health, but also on the deaths caused, because consumers must be aware of the fact that they have blood on their hands. Last point, the systematic confiscation of all property acquired through drug trafficking. This is how we will triumph.

3-0326-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, «hay noches en que estamos solos mi compañero y yo contra quince narcolanchas». Desgraciadamente, no es el comienzo de una serie colombiana de Netflix: se trata del testimonio de un guardia civil español, denunciando la indefensión con la que nuestros agentes se ven obligados a combatir al narco.

Una indefensión que tiene un altísimo coste humano. En los últimos dos años, cuatro agentes han sido asesinados en España y, en las últimas semanas, uno en Portugal. Esta escalada de violencia más propia de otras latitudes es la nueva normalidad en las costas europeas, pero Europa no puede seguir tolerándolo.

No podemos seguir dependiendo del heroísmo de nuestros agentes. Los Gobiernos europeos tienen la obligación —política y moral— de dotarles de los mejores medios para combatir al narco. Ellos no quieren palmaditas en la espalda ni homenajes en los funerales, aunque algunos ni siquiera se atrevan a hacerlo, quieren simplemente los medios para poder cumplir con su deber en defensa de todos los europeos.
3-0326-0000.englishText:
Madam President, "There are nights when my partner and I are alone against fifteen drug boats." Unfortunately, it is not the beginning of a Colombian Netflix series: it is the testimony of a Spanish civil guard, denouncing the helplessness with which our agents are forced to fight drug traffickers.

A helplessness that has a very high human cost. In the last two years, four agents have been murdered in Spain and, in recent weeks, one in Portugal. This escalation of violence more typical of other latitudes is the new normal on European coasts, but Europe cannot continue to tolerate it.

We cannot continue to depend on the heroism of our agents. European governments have the obligation – political and moral – to provide them with the best means to combat drug trafficking. They do not want pats on the back or tributes at funerals, although some do not even dare to do so, they simply want the means to be able to fulfill their duty in defense of all Europeans.

3-0328-0000.sourceText:
La discussione è chiusa.

La votazione si svolgerà durante la prossima tornata.
3-0328-0000.englishText:
The discussion is closed.

The vote will take place during the next part-session.

3-0328-5000.sourceText:
Jeśli handel narkotykami kwitnie, to dlatego, że ochrona granic zewnętrznych pozostaje niewystarczająca. Państwa graniczne potrzebują większego wsparcia finansowego, nowoczesnych narzędzi i silniejszej współpracy z Frontexem, Europolem oraz Eurojustem. Zamiast mnożyć biurokrację i ograniczać wymianę informacji między służbami, Unia Europejska powinna zapewnić im skuteczne instrumenty działania. Nie ma również potrzeby tworzenia kolejnych instytucji, jeśli osłabią one kompetencje istniejących agencji.

W 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad 1,5 miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. W latach 2018–2023 liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów z kokainą wzrosła o 31%, a z powodu uzależnienia od cracku o 35%. To pokazuje, że Europa przegrywa walkę z przemytem narkotyków i zorganizowaną przestępczością.

Przestępcy nie mogą czuć się bezkarnie. Europejskie porty nie mogą być magazynami i punktami prze0ładunkowymi dla karteli narkotykowych. Wiele danych wskazuje na związek między przestępczością narkotykową a nielegalną migracją oraz nadużywaniem procedur azylowych. Osoby łamiące prawo powinny mieć pełną świadomość, że łamanie prawa będzie skutkowało szybkim powrotem do kraju pochodzenia.

Europa potrzebuje bezpiecznych granic zamiast ideologii, współpracujących służb zamiast przepisów, które uniemożliwiają im skuteczne działanie, realnej ochrony granic i zdecydowanych działań przeciwko międzynarodowym kartelom, aby przywrócić bezpieczeństwo swoim obywatelom.
3-0328-5000.englishText:
If the drug trade is booming, it is because the protection of external borders remains insufficient. Border states need more financial support, modern tools and stronger cooperation with Frontex, Europol and Eurojust. Instead of increasing bureaucracy and limiting the exchange of information between services, the European Union should provide them with effective instruments of action. There is also no need to create additional institutions if they weaken the competences of existing agencies.

In 2024, European Union member states reported over 1.5 million drug-related crimes. Between 2018 and 2023, the number of people entering treatment for cocaine problems increased by 31% and for crack addiction by 35%. This shows that Europe is losing the fight against drug smuggling and organized crime.

Criminals cannot feel impunity. European ports cannot be warehouses and transhipment points for drug cartels. Much data indicates a link between drug crime, illegal migration and abuse of asylum procedures. People breaking the law should be fully aware that breaking the law will result in a quick return to their country of origin.

Europe needs secure borders instead of ideology, cooperating services instead of regulations that prevent them from operating effectively, real border protection and decisive action against international cartels to restore the security of its citizens.

3-0334-0000.sourceText:
L'ordine del giorno reca la discussione sulla dichiarazione del Parlamento sul Futuro del sostegno dell'UE a favore delle forze democratiche, degli attori contrari alla guerra e della società civile repressa russi (2026/2794(RSP)).

Vorrei ricordare agli onorevoli deputati che per questa discussione si terrà un unico giro di interventi di oratori dei gruppi politici. Pertanto non è prevista la procedura "catch the eye" e non saranno accettati interventi cartellino blu.

Vorrei inoltre ricordare agli oratori che, date le misure di prova attualmente in vigore e l'orario fisso di conclusione della discussione, sarà necessario rispettare rigorosamente il tempo di parola.
3-0334-0000.englishText:
The next item is the debate on Parliament's statement on the Future of EU support for Russian democratic forces, anti-war actors and repressed civil society (2026/2794(RSP)).

I would like to remind honorable Members that for this debate there will be a single round of speeches by speakers from the political groups. Therefore the "catch the eye" procedure is not foreseen and blue card interventions will not be accepted.

I would also like to remind speakers that, given the testing measures currently in place and the fixed end time of the debate, speaking time will need to be strictly respected.

3-0335-0000.sourceText: Cienītā sēdes vadītāja! Kolēģi! Krievijas pilna mēroga uzbrukums Ukrainai, kas turpinās nu jau piekto gadu, nav tikai militārs konflikts. Krievijas neoimperiālistiskai agresijai ir un būs dziļa un ilgstoša ietekme uz starptautiskajām tiesībām, Eiropas drošību, demokrātiju un miljoniem cilvēku dzīvi. Visi Krievijas valsts instrumenti – valdība, ekonomika, finanšu sektors, propaganda, pareizticīgā baznīca – kalpo karam un militarizē sabiedrību. Tāpēc vienīgais ceļš uz Krievijas atdzimšanu un sabiedrības atveseļošanu ir Ukrainas uzvara karā. Krievijas neoimperiālisms ir jāaptur. Tikai caur sakāvi Krievija var kļūt par valsti, kurā attīstīsies demokrātija, valdīs likuma vara, būs nodrošinātas cilvēktiesības un pamatbrīvības. Tāpēc mūsu pienākums ir atbalstīt Ukrainas pašaizsardzību. Eiropas Parlaments ir demokrātijas mājvieta. Tāpēc mēs atbalstām Krievijas demokrātisko opozīciju, pilsonisko sabiedrību, cilvēktiesību aktīvistus, kuri nosoda agresiju pret Ukrainu. Viņi turpina pretestību Kremļa režīmam, neskatoties uz represijām, apcietināšanām un trimdu. Režīms nežēlīgi vēršas pret katru, kas neatbalsta agresiju. Ir ierosinātas vairāk nekā 5000 krimināllietas, cietumos smok vairāk nekā 4000 politieslodzīto. Politieslodzīto atbrīvošana ir prasība, kura ir jāiekļauj Ukrainas un Krievijas miera sarunās, kuras agrāk vai vēlāk notiks. Tomēr Krievijas demokrātiskie spēki ir sašķelti. Vēsture atkal un atkal ir pierādījusi, ka diktatūru uzvar tie, kas uzvaras vārdā atliek malā uzskatu un personāliju nesaskaņas un koncentrējas uz stratēģisko mērķi – demokrātiskas un likumpaklausīgas valsts un sabiedrības izveidošanu. Bez vienotības Krievijas demokrātisko spēku ietekme uz politisko procesu Krievijā būs maznozīmīga.
3-0335-0000.englishText: Dear chairman of the meeting! Colleagues! Russia's full-scale assault on Ukraine, now in its fifth year, is not just a military conflict. Russia's neo-imperialist aggression has and will have a profound and lasting impact on international law, European security, democracy and the lives of millions of people. All instruments of the Russian state - government, economy, financial sector, propaganda, Orthodox Church - serve war and militarize society. Therefore, the only way to the revival of Russia and the recovery of society is the victory of Ukraine in the war. Russian neo-imperialism must be stopped. Only through defeat can Russia become a country where democracy will develop, the rule of law will rule, and human rights and fundamental freedoms will be ensured. Therefore, it is our duty to support Ukraine's self-defense. The European Parliament is the home of democracy. Therefore, we support the Russian democratic opposition, civil society, human rights activists who condemn the aggression against Ukraine. They continue to resist the Kremlin regime despite repression, arrests and exile. The regime brutally targets anyone who does not support aggression. More than 5,000 criminal cases have been initiated, and more than 4,000 political prisoners are in jail. The release of political prisoners is a requirement that must be included in the Ukraine-Russia peace talks, which will take place sooner or later. However, Russia's democratic forces are divided. History has proven time and time again that dictatorships are won by those who, in the name of victory, put aside differences of opinion and personalities and focus on the strategic goal of creating a democratic and law-abiding state and society. Without unity, the influence of Russian democratic forces on the political process in Russia will be insignificant.

3-0336-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Russia non è Putin.

La Russia sono anche migliaia di donne e uomini che, in un clima asfissiante, continuano a difendere la democrazia, i diritti umani e le libertà fondamentali. Sono persone che si oppongono alla brutale guerra di aggressione della Russia contro l'Ucraina ed è proprio da loro che ogni giorno ci arrivano innumerevoli segnalazioni di cittadini repressi, detenuti, imprigionati e maltrattati solo perché si sono esposti, hanno alzato la testa e la voce dicendo la verità sulla guerra di Putin.

La propaganda del regime impedisce alle forze democratiche di esprimersi e quando qualcuno riesce a sfuggire alle maglie fittissime di questa rete, il sistema giudiziario prende la scena, confezionando sentenze ad hoc per punire attivisti, giornalisti e chiunque abbia il coraggio di alzare la voce.

L'Unione europea deve essere ferma e decisa nel suo incrollabile sostegno al popolo ucraino di fronte alla guerra di aggressione di Putin. Allo stesso tempo, l'Unione deve continuare a sostenere gli attivisti russi per i diritti umani, gli attori pro‑democrazia e gli attivisti contro la guerra, persone che spesso rischiano la propria incolumità e la propria vita per il loro impegno e per presentare un'altra Russia: la Russia libera, democratica, una Russia dello Stato di diritto. Una Russia così – ricordiamoci – è possibile.
3-0336-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Russia is not Putin.

Russia is also thousands of women and men who, in a suffocating climate, continue to defend democracy, human rights and fundamental freedoms. They are people who oppose Russia's brutal war of aggression against Ukraine and it is precisely from them that every day we receive countless reports of citizens repressed, detained, imprisoned and mistreated just because they exposed themselves, raised their heads and raised their voices telling the truth about Putin's war.

The regime's propaganda prevents democratic forces from expressing themselves and when someone manages to escape the very dense mesh of this network, the judicial system takes the stage, crafting ad hoc sentences to punish activists, journalists and anyone who has the courage to raise their voice.

The European Union must be firm and resolute in its unwavering support for the Ukrainian people in the face of Putin's war of aggression. At the same time, the Union must continue to support Russian human rights activists, pro-democracy actors and anti-war activists, people who often risk their safety and their lives for their efforts and for presenting another Russia: free, democratic Russia, a Russia of the rule of law. A Russia like this – let's remember – is possible.

3-0337-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Caros Colegas, meus caros amigos, façamos um pouco de História.

Erros europeus desde o fim da Guerra Fria, a queda do Muro de Berlim: muito pouco diálogo político com a Rússia e total dependência energética desse país. O resultado era previsível porque nos afastámos politicamente e abraçámos uma dependência económica e energética.
