Meus caros amigos, longe, muito longe de aceitar este regime na Rússia, pelo contrário, criticá-lo vivamente. Agora, nós não temos de nos imiscuir nos assuntos internos de outros países, de países terceiros, ainda por cima alheios à União Europeia.

A prioridade deve ser fixar e resolver os problemas da Europa, antes de arranjar agendas externas que nem sempre são claras nem honestas. Portanto, vamos tentar, mais uma vez, que a Europa se comporte à altura e que resolva os seus problemas em vez de andar a tentar resolver os dos outros.
3-0337-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Dear Colleagues, my dear friends, let's do a little History.

European mistakes since the end of the Cold War, the fall of the Berlin Wall: very little political dialogue with Russia and total energy dependence on that country. The result was predictable because we moved away politically and embraced economic and energy dependence.

My dear friends, far, far from accepting this regime in Russia, on the contrary, I strongly criticize it. Now, we do not have to meddle in the internal affairs of other countries, third countries, even outside the European Union.

The priority must be to fix and resolve Europe's problems, before arranging external agendas that are not always clear or honest. Therefore, let's try, once again, for Europe to behave up to the task and solve its problems instead of trying to solve others' problems.

3-0338-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Cieszę się, że rozmawiamy w Parlamencie Europejskim o innej Rosji, o Rosji, która nie będzie śmiertelnym zagrożeniem dla wolnego świata i która nie będzie ociekała krwią niewinnych ofiar. Czy taka Rosja jest możliwa? Kiedy spojrzymy na historię tego kraju, to trudno znaleźć podstawę do optymizmu. Zarówno carska Rosja, jak i czerwona Rosja były agresywnymi państwami imperialistycznymi. Putin czerpie z obu tych tradycji. Takie wartości jak demokracja, prawa człowieka, prawa obywatelskie w Rosji nigdy się nie zakorzeniły.

Ci, którzy marzą o tym, aby z Rosji uczynić państwo cywilizowane, są po prostu mordowani. Tak stało się z Anną Politkowską, Borysem Niemcowem, Aleksiejem Nawalnym. Dziś w Rosji nie ma żadnej zorganizowanej opozycji. Nie oznacza to, że nie należy wspierać tych, którzy, będąc w większości na emigracji, deklarują niechęć wobec dyktatury. Wsparcie to musi być jednak adekwatne do realnie podejmowanych działań oraz rzeczywiście wyznawanych wartości. Należy również pamiętać, że niemal 20% obywateli współczesnej Rosji to przedstawiciele mniejszości narodowych. Ich aspiracje narodowe zasługują na szczególną uwagę.
3-0338-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I am glad that we are talking in the European Parliament about a different Russia, a Russia that will not be a mortal threat to the free world and that will not be dripping with the blood of innocent victims. Is such a Russia possible? When we look at the history of this country, it is difficult to find grounds for optimism. Both Tsarist Russia and Red Russia were aggressive imperialist states. Putin draws on both of these traditions. Such values ​​as democracy, human rights and civil rights have never taken root in Russia.

Those who dream of turning Russia into a civilized state are simply murdered. This is what happened to Anna Politkovskaya, Boris Nemtsov, Alexei Navalny. Today there is no organized opposition in Russia. This does not mean that we should not support those who, most of them emigrating, declare their aversion to dictatorship. However, this support must be adequate to the actions actually undertaken and the values ​​actually professed. It should also be remembered that almost 20% of the citizens of modern Russia are representatives of national minorities. Their national aspirations deserve special attention.

3-0339-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, la géographie nous l’impose: parce que la Russie est européenne et que c’est avec elle que nous partageons ce continent, il nous faut trouver les voies et moyens de coexister dans une paix solide et durable.

Cela demande deux choses: la première est de toujours plus aider l’Ukraine à infliger à Vladimir Poutine la défaite qu’il mérite. La stabilité de notre continent exige que plus personne ne puisse croire, en Russie, que la force brutale puisse triompher du droit et que les missiles puissent reconstituer l’empire des tsars. Peut-être ce jour est-il plus proche qu’on ne le croit – on verra –, mais la certitude est que rien ne sourit plus à Vladimir Poutine, qu’aucune dictature ne survit à l’humiliation d’une déroute militaire, et qu’une page se tournera donc bientôt à Moscou, dans trois jours, trois mois ou trois ans.

Ce jour-là, nous devons le préparer, et c’est pour cela que nous avons entamé et que nous poursuivrons un dialogue avec l’opposition russe. Avant même que la victoire de l’Ukraine ne lève un vent de liberté à Moscou, il faut que les Russes – non pas le Kremlin, mais les Russes – nous entendent leur dire que nous ne voulons rien d’autre que vivre à leurs côtés, dans la sécurité et la coopération, et que, le jour venu, nous tendrons la main à une Russie libérée, enfin libre de choisir l’Europe et la démocratie.
3-0339-0000.englishText:
Madam President, geography imposes it on us: because Russia is European and it is with it that we share this continent, we must find the ways and means to coexist in a solid and lasting peace.

This requires two things: the first is to increasingly help Ukraine to inflict on Vladimir Putin the defeat he deserves. The stability of our continent requires that no one in Russia can any longer believe that brutal force can triumph over law and that missiles can reconstitute the empire of the tsars. Perhaps this day is closer than we think – we will see – but the certainty is that nothing smiles on Vladimir Putin anymore, that no dictatorship survives the humiliation of a military rout, and that a page will therefore soon be turned in Moscow, in three days, three months or three years.

We must prepare for that day, and that is why we have started and will continue a dialogue with the Russian opposition. Even before Ukraine's victory raises a wind of freedom in Moscow, the Russians – not the Kremlin, but the Russians – must hear us tell them that we want nothing more than to live alongside them, in security and cooperation, and that, when the day comes, we will extend our hand to a liberated Russia, finally free to choose Europe and democracy.

3-0342-0000.sourceText:
, от името на групата ESN. – Господин Председател, мечтата на колективния Запад винаги е била да види Майдан в Москва. В продължение на десетилетия Западът обучаваше и финансираше много хора и организации в Русия, надявайки се те да се превърнат в неговата пета колона и сами да съсипят страната си. Но въпреки милиардите долари и евро, дадени за тази цел, мнозинството от руските граждани отхвърли данайския дар на западните лицемери. Нормалните руски граждани отлично разбират, че тези хора, въпреки всичките си високопарни слова пет пари не дават за демокрацията, свободата и просперитета на Русия. Единственото, което искат, е тотален контрол върху Руската федерация и да я грабят безнаказано.

Западът много иска да се повтори ситуацията от 90-те години, когато техният любимец Елцин и приближените му олигарси изпълняваха безпрекословно желанията на чуждите властови центрове и разпродаваха страната си. Днешното ръководство на Русия отдавна отхвърли тази васална зависимост и затова Брюксел и Вашингтон правят всичко възможно, за да го свалят. Само че нито излетите колосални суми, нито истеричната пропаганда постигнаха тази цел. Чуждестранните агенти на влияние в Русия или избягаха при своите покровители, или замълчаха засрамени.

Тотално сбъркана е политиката на колективния Запад по отношение на Русия. Вместо да водят откровен диалог с Москва, западните ръководители решиха, че могат лесно да съсипят тази държава. Сметнаха, че на безценица ще си купят руския елит така, както са правели западните колонизатори с местното население в Африка и Америка. Повярваха, че днес тлъстите грантове и безплатните воаяжи до Брюксел и Вашингтон за руснаците ще бъдат това, което някога са били искрящите мъниста за американските и африканските племенни вождове.

Да, отделни НПО-та и политици се продадоха, но в крайна сметка се оказа, че огромният финансов ресурс, отделен за антируска пропаганда, не е довел до нищо. Продължаването на тази стратегия ще доведе до същия нулев резултат.
3-0342-0000.englishText:
, on behalf of the ESN Group. - Mr. Chairman, the dream of the collective West has always been to see Maidan in Moscow. 3-0344-0000.sourceText: L'ordine del giorno reca la discussione sulla dichiarazione della Commissione su Focolaio di Ebola nella Repubblica Democratica del Congo e in Uganda: solidarietà e preparazione dell'Unione europea in termini di salute globale (2026/2803(RSP)).
3-0344-0000.englishText: The next item is the debate on the Commission statement on Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda: European Union solidarity and global health preparedness (2026/2803(RSP)).

3-0346-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, izbijanje ebole u Demokratskoj Republici Kongu i Ugandi ponovno nas podsjeća da zarazne bolesti ne poznaju granice.

U današnjem međusobno povezanom svijetu, zdravstvena kriza u jednom dijelu svijeta može vrlo brzo postati sigurnosni izazov i za Europu. Zato odgovor na ovakve epidemije nije samo pitanje humanitarne pomoći, nego i pitanje zdravstvene sigurnosti, otpornosti naših sustava i odgovorne međunarodne suradnje. Svjetska zdravstvena organizacija ovu je epidemiju proglasila međunarodnom javnozdravstvenom krizom. Upravo zato brzina reakcije, međunarodna koordinacija i razmjena stručnog znanja mogu biti presudni za zaustavljanje širenja bolesti.

Europska unija već je pokazala solidarnost pružanjem financijske pomoći, slanjem stručne potpore te ulaganjem u istraživanje i razvoj novih cjepiva, dijagnostike i terapije. Istodobno, EU pomaže u jačanju epidemiološkog nadzora, laboratorijskih kapaciteta i pripravnosti susjednih država kako bi se spriječilo daljnje širenje zaraze. Europa mora nastaviti pažljivo pratiti razvoj situacije. Iako stručne procjene pokazuju da je rizik za građane Europske unije trenutačno vrlo nizak, iskustva iz proteklih godina pokazala su koliko se zdravstvene okolnosti mogu brzo promijeniti. Zato moramo nastaviti ulagati u pripravnost naših zdravstvenih sustava, jačati sustave ranog upozoravanja, razvijati zajedničke europske kapacitete za odgovor na zdravstvene krize te produbljivati suradnju sa Svjetskom zdravstvenom organizacijom.

Borba protiv zaraznih bolesti test je naše sposobnosti da djelujemo zajednički, pravodobno i solidarno. Samo suradnjom, ulaganjem u znanost i odgovornim međunarodnim djelovanjem možemo spriječiti da lokalna epidemija preraste u globalnu prijetnju.

Upravo zato europska solidarnost i pripravnost moraju ostati temelj našeg odgovora na ovakve zdravstvene izazove.
3-0346-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairperson, Commissioners, colleagues, the outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda reminds us once again that infectious diseases know no borders.

In today's interconnected world, a health crisis in one part of the world can very quickly become a security challenge for Europe as well. That is why the response to such epidemics is not only a question of humanitarian aid, but also a question of health security, the resilience of our systems and responsible international cooperation. The World Health Organization declared this epidemic an international public health crisis. This is precisely why the speed of reaction, international coordination and exchange of expert knowledge can be crucial for stopping the spread of the disease.

The European Union has already shown solidarity by providing financial aid, sending expert support and investing in research and development of new vaccines, diagnostics and therapy. At the same time, the EU is helping to strengthen the epidemiological surveillance, laboratory capacities and preparedness of neighboring countries in order to prevent further spread of the infection. Europe must continue to closely monitor the development of the situation. Although expert assessments show that the risk for citizens of the European Union is currently very low, the experiences of the past years have shown how quickly health circumstances can change. That is why we must continue to invest in the preparedness of our health systems, strengthen early warning systems, develop common European capacities for responding to health crises, and deepen cooperation with the World Health Organization.

The fight against infectious diseases is a test of our ability to act together, in a timely manner and in solidarity. Only through cooperation, investment in science and responsible international action can we prevent a local epidemic from growing into a global threat.

This is precisely why European solidarity and preparedness must remain the basis of our response to such health challenges.

3-0347-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, el brote que tiene origen en la República Democrática del Congo y en Uganda no es un asunto africano. Es un asunto global y también europeo.

Las enfermedades no se detienen en las fronteras. Un brote puede empezar muy lejos de Europa, pero tarda en llegar exactamente lo mismo que tarda en desplazarse una persona. Al principio, nos llegan noticias, cifras, unos cientos de casos y las primeras muertes —ya llevamos 500—. Entonces, podemos caer en el error de decir que, como es en África y no aquí, no es nuestro problema.

¿Alguien se acuerda de la pandemia? Porque es exactamente esto. Y yo sé que el ébola no es el COVID-19, pero deberíamos haber aprendido de la pandemia. Es absolutamente importante que nuestra respuesta sea doble. Por un lado, apoyo firme a los países afectados, prevención, preparación y respuesta desde la Unión Europea. Por otro lado, que nuestros mecanismos se compartan también en coordinación con los países del Sur Global.

Señora comisaria, yo le quiero dar las gracias por su compromiso, por ir al terreno, por su constante trabajo, por ser luz en un momento oscuro; porque necesitamos reforzar la vigilancia, la logística, la comunicación comunitaria, y la coordinación entre nuestros centros de vigilancia y los africanos. Y, sobre todo, porque la solidaridad no es caridad, es contener el brote en origen. Y es justicia. Pero es también la forma más inteligente de asegurar la seguridad de los europeos.
3-0347-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the outbreak originating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is not an African issue. It is a global and also a European issue.

Diseases do not stop at borders. An outbreak can start very far from Europe, but it takes exactly the same time to arrive as it takes a person to travel. At first, we receive news, figures, a few hundred cases and the first deaths—we are already at 500—. So, we can make the mistake of saying that since it is in Africa and not here, it is not our problem.

Does anyone remember the pandemic? Because it is exactly this. And I know that Ebola is not COVID-19, but we should have learned from the pandemic. It is absolutely important that our response be twofold. On the one hand, firm support for the affected countries, prevention, preparation and response from the European Union. On the other hand, that our mechanisms are also shared in coordination with the countries of the Global South.

Madam Commissioner, I want to thank you for your commitment, for going to the field, for your constant work, for being a light in a dark moment; because we need to strengthen surveillance, logistics, community communication, and coordination between our surveillance centers and the African ones. And, above all, because solidarity is not charity, it is containing the outbreak at its source. And it is justice. But it is also the smartest way to ensure the security of Europeans.

3-0348-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, en République démocratique du Congo, les populations subissent déjà les ravages de la guerre. Désormais, elles doivent affronter une nouvelle catastrophe: Ebola – plus de 1 500 cas, plus de 500 morts.

Mais il faut dire les choses: ce virus se propage aussi parce qu’il arrive dans des régions, l’Ituri et le Kivu, détruites par la guerre. Depuis 2021, l’est du Congo est à nouveau ravagé par les attaques du M23, soutenu par le régime de Paul Kagame. Des millions de personnes ont dû fuir, des infrastructures et des hôpitaux ont été incendiés.

Alors, comment arrêter Ebola? Comment arrêter quand il n’y a pas assez d’ambulances, quand les centres de soins sont détruits, quand les médecins ne peuvent même plus atteindre les malades? Oui, il faut envoyer de l’aide humanitaire, mais fermer les yeux sur les vrais responsables de ce chaos, c’est accepter que la situation continue; c’est nous rendre complices.

L’Union européenne doit enfin agir, comme le demande le Parlement depuis plusieurs années: sanctionner le Rwanda et M. Kagame et faire pression pour mettre fin à cette guerre. Pourquoi tant de complaisance pour le Rwanda? C’est le moment de montrer qu’on sait faire aussi une action politique, et pas uniquement une action humanitaire!
3-0348-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, people are already suffering the ravages of war. Now they face a new disaster: Ebola – more than 1,500 cases, more than 500 deaths.

But things must be said: this virus is also spreading because it arrives in regions, Ituri and Kivu, destroyed by war. Since 2021, eastern Congo has once again been ravaged by attacks by the M23, supported by the Paul Kagame regime. Millions of people had to flee, infrastructure and hospitals were burned.

So how do you stop Ebola? How can we stop when there are not enough ambulances, when health centers are destroyed, when doctors can no longer even reach the sick? Yes, we must send humanitarian aid, but turning a blind eye to those truly responsible for this chaos means accepting that the situation will continue; it makes us complicit.

The European Union must finally act, as Parliament has been asking for several years: sanction Rwanda and Mr. Kagame and put pressure to end this war. Why so much complacency for Rwanda? Now is the time to show that we also know how to take political action, and not just humanitarian action!

3-0349-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC est une des plus graves de l’histoire. De plus, le conflit armé dans l’est de la RDC rend la lutte presque impossible. Sans sécurité, il est impossible de stopper l’épidémie.

L’Afrique, chers collègues, est un partenaire essentiel. C’est notre voisin. Face à un virus qui menace toute une région, nous ne pouvons pas rester spectateurs: nous devons protéger les civils, protéger le personnel de santé et garantir un accès à l’aide humanitaire. Et nous devons renforcer notre soutien aux organisations locales, comme l’hôpital de Panzi du Dr Denis Mukwege, qui sont en première ligne dans la lutte contre Ebola.

Nous devons aussi rétablir la sécurité dans la région. Comme d’autres intervenants l’ont dit, nous devons commencer à sanctionner le Rwanda. La paix doit revenir là-bas pour permettre le combat contre Ebola. Notre devoir est clair: sauver les vies. Chaque jour compte.
3-0349-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, the Ebola epidemic in the DRC is one of the most serious in history. In addition, the armed conflict in eastern DRC makes the fight almost impossible. Without security, it is impossible to stop the epidemic.

Africa, dear colleagues, is an essential partner. He's our neighbor. Faced with a virus that threatens an entire region, we cannot remain spectators: we must protect civilians, protect health personnel and guarantee access to humanitarian aid. And we must step up our support for local organizations, like Dr. Denis Mukwege’s Panzi Hospital, who are on the front lines in the fight against Ebola.

We must also restore security to the region. As other speakers have said, we need to start sanctioning Rwanda. Peace must return there to allow the fight against Ebola. Our duty is clear: save lives. Every day counts.

3-0350-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, questo virus, che in molti abbiamo paragonato a quanto è accaduto qualche anno fa con il COVID, è un virus molto più letale, molto più pericoloso: non esistono cure, non esistono vaccini e non esiste nessun modo per fermare le emorragie all'interno del corpo e all'esterno del corpo di questi poveri pazienti.

Noi dobbiamo veramente sostituirci a quanto gli Stati Uniti hanno fatto con il loro passo indietro rispetto all'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità. Se non lo vogliamo fare perché crediamo che l'aiuto e la solidarietà siano importanti, dovremmo farlo per egoismo, perché, come tanti hanno detto, a partire anche dalla Commissaria, i virus non hanno bisogno di un passaporto per attraversare un confine.

Il fatto che ci siano già stati 1 500 contagi, 500 persone che hanno perso la vita e vedere quelle immagini – dove, signora Commissaria, è vero che è stato fatto uno sforzo, ma, di fatto, sul territorio, dove queste persone muoiono, non hanno neanche la possibilità di avere quegli strumenti di protezione per i medici e per gli infermieri, tant'è vero che ne sono morti quasi venti – e anche per le stesse persone che assistono o vanno a trovare i loro cari.

Dobbiamo fare di più e dobbiamo farlo adesso, perché questo virus è veramente pericoloso e mortale.
3-0350-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, this virus, which many of us have compared to what happened a few years ago with COVID, is a much more lethal, much more dangerous virus: there are no cures, there are no vaccines and there is no way to stop the bleeding inside the body and outside the body of these poor patients.

We really need to replace what the United States has done with its step back from the World Health Organization. If we don't want to do it because we believe that help and solidarity are important, we should do it out of selfishness, because, as many have said, including the Commissioner, viruses don't need a passport to cross a border.

The fact that there have already been 1,500 infections, 500 people who have lost their lives and seeing those images – where, Commissioner, it is true that an effort has been made, but, in fact, in the area, where these people die, they don't even have the possibility of having those protection tools for doctors and nurses, so much so that almost twenty of them have died – and also for the very people who assist or visit their loved ones.

We must do more and we must do it now, because this virus is truly dangerous and deadly.

3-0351-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, bem sei que supervisionou pessoalmente o embarque de paracetamol para o Congo para ajudar no combate ao surto de Ébola. Mas é poucochinho, não é?

Queria fazer-lhe duas perguntas sobre ações concretas da União Europeia.

Em primeiro lugar, estamos perante uma variante para a qual não há nenhuma vacina comercial, mas sabemos agora que há avanços científicos que entusiasmam. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai, então, investir nestes avanços científicos para termos a vacina.

A segunda questão é sobre os serviços de saúde locais. Os Médicos Sem Fronteiras têm dito, e muito bem, que é preciso investir diretamente lá. Têm, aliás, pedido investimento direto para que os serviços de saúde possam não só monitorizar como controlar, tratar a doença. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai aumentar o seu apoio, porque tem de o fazer. Os casos detetados em Paris e Berlim mostram, aliás, que é do seu próprio interesse fazê-lo.

E uma nota final: a União Europeia tem particulares responsabilidades, porque se nas zonas de conflito é mais difícil controlar o surto de Ébola, não esqueçamos que somos parceiros comerciais daqueles minerais do sangue que estão a provocar os conflitos nas zonas mais afetadas.
3-0351-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I know that you personally supervised the shipment of paracetamol to Congo to help combat the Ebola outbreak. But it's little, isn't it?

I would like to ask you two questions about concrete actions by the European Union.

Firstly, we are facing a variant for which there is no commercial vaccine, but we now know that there are scientific advances that are exciting. And my question is whether the European Union will then invest in these scientific advances to have a vaccine.

The second question is about local health services. Doctors Without Borders have rightly said that it is necessary to invest directly there. They have, in fact, asked for direct investment so that health services can not only monitor but also control and treat the disease. And my question is whether the European Union will increase its support, because it has to. The cases detected in Paris and Berlin show, in fact, that it is in your own interest to do so.

And a final note: the European Union has particular responsibilities, because if it is more difficult to control the Ebola outbreak in conflict zones, let us not forget that we are trading partners of those blood minerals that are causing conflicts in the most affected areas.

3-0355-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo et en Ouganda est avant tout une tragédie humanitaire. Plus de 1 700 personnes ont été infectées, et des centaines ont perdu la vie. Derrière ces chiffres se cachent des familles, des communautés et des professionnels de santé, qui luttent pour survivre dans ces circonstances difficiles.

Le contexte d’insécurité et de tensions régionales rend la situation bien plus complexe dans l’est de la RDC. Le conflit est en cours, et l’instabilité liée à la crise entre la RDC et le Rwanda complique l’accès des travailleurs humanitaires, perturbe fortement les services de santé et accentue les mouvements de population à travers les frontières.

J’appelle la Commission et le Conseil à compléter notre aide humanitaire par un engagement diplomatique renouvelé, en exhortant toutes les parties à mettre en œuvre un cessez-le-feu immédiat afin de garantir l’accès humanitaire et de protéger les civils. Car protéger des vies nécessite non seulement une aide médicale, mais aussi la paix et la stabilité, pour que les communautés puissent se rétablir.
3-0355-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is above all a humanitarian tragedy. More than 1,700 people have been infected, and hundreds have lost their lives. Behind these numbers are families, communities and healthcare professionals struggling to survive in these difficult circumstances.

The context of insecurity and regional tensions makes the situation much more complex in eastern DRC. The conflict is ongoing, and the instability linked to the crisis between the DRC and Rwanda complicates access for humanitarian workers, severely disrupts health services and increases population movements across borders.

I call on the Commission and the Council to complement our humanitarian assistance with renewed diplomatic engagement, urging all parties to implement an immediate ceasefire to ensure humanitarian access and protect civilians. Because protecting lives requires not only medical help, but also peace and stability, so communities can recover.

3-0356-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, les nouvelles sur Ebola sont horribles, évidemment. C’est une maladie qui tue, qui fait peur aussi – transmissible, très mortelle –, mais, en même temps, il faut aussi qu’on ose s’attaquer aux causes fondamentales du problème.

En République démocratique du Congo, qu’est-ce qu’il faudrait pour combattre de manière efficace Ebola? Il ne s’agit pas uniquement de recherche d’un vaccin; il s’agit aussi d’un système de santé publique performant, de prévention – la détection! –, de pouvoir aller chercher, de pouvoir avoir les pratiques au niveau des enterrements, aussi, travailler avec les communautés locales.

Mais, pour tout cela, il faut des moyens. Et ces moyens-là, ils manquent, ils font défaut. Pourquoi? D’un côté, effectivement, parce qu’il y a tout simplement la guerre avec des acteurs impliqués comme le Rwanda, que nous sponsorisons toujours. Mais, deuxièmement, aussi à cause du pillage des ressources naturelles, organisé par les États-Unis et les multinationales européennes.

La RDC perd des sous, perd de l’argent, perd de la richesse à l’Occident et n’a donc plus les moyens pour investir dans ce système de santé publique. Donc, c’est sur cela qu’il faut travailler: sur notre politique commerciale, contre les multinationales occidentales européennes qui pillent les richesses du Congo.
3-0356-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, the news on Ebola is horrible, of course. It is a disease that kills, which is also frightening – communicable, very deadly – ​​but, at the same time, we must also dare to tackle the fundamental causes of the problem.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, what would it take to effectively combat Ebola? It's not just about finding a vaccine; it is also about an efficient public health system, prevention – detection! –, to be able to fetch, to be able to have burial practices, also, to work with local communities.

But for all this, resources are needed. And these means are lacking, they are lacking. For what? On the one hand, indeed, because there is quite simply war with actors involved like Rwanda, which we still sponsor. But, secondly, also because of the plundering of natural resources, organized by the United States and European multinationals.

The DRC is losing money, losing money, losing wealth in the West and therefore no longer has the means to invest in this public health system. So, this is what we need to work on: on our trade policy, against the Western European multinationals who are plundering the wealth of the Congo.

3-0357-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, sinds 2019 weten we helaas meer dan ooit dat virussen geen grenzen kennen. Hoewel de risico's voor Europa momenteel zeer laag zijn, zien we dat de humanitaire tragedie in Congo en Oeganda vandaag nog niet volledig ingedekt is. Gelukkig kan er gerekend worden op een sterke interventie van de Wereldgezondheidsorganisatie, van de Europese Unie en van haar lidstaten, met lokale ondersteuning van de gezondheidszorg en investeringen en onderzoek naar vaccins en behandelingen, versterken we ook de globale en dus ook de eigen weerbaarheid hier bij ons tegen nieuwe varianten, zoals dat hier het geval is.

Door samen te werken, onze Afrikaanse partners te ondersteunen en te investeren in innovatie, redden we niet alleen levens ter plaatse, maar versterken we ook de gezondheid en de veiligheid van onze eigen burgers. En net dat toont aan dat er meer dan ooit nood is aan een sterke Europese gezondheidsunie. Iets waar ik ook binnen de biotechverordening naar streef. We kunnen niet wegkijken van dergelijke tragedies, dus blijft een sterke steun vanuit Europa meer dan ooit noodzakelijk. En daarvoor rekenen we op u.
3-0357-0000.englishText:
Mr President, since 2019 we have unfortunately known more than ever that viruses know no borders. Although the risks for Europe are currently very low, we see that the humanitarian tragedy in Congo and Uganda has not yet been fully contained. Fortunately, we can count on a strong intervention from the World Health Organization, the European Union and its Member States, with local support for healthcare and investments and research into vaccines and treatments, we also strengthen global and therefore our own resilience against new variants, as is the case here.

By working together, supporting our African partners and investing in innovation, we are not only saving lives on the ground, but also strengthening the health and safety of our own citizens. And that shows that there is more need than ever for a strong European health union. Something I also strive for within the biotech regulation. We cannot look away from such tragedies, so strong support from Europe remains more necessary than ever. And we count on you for that.

3-0358-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, er zijn meer dan 1 500 bevestigde gevallen van ebola in Congo en Oeganda; meer dan 500 doden. Een uitbraak die zich uitbreidt naar nieuwe gebieden. Wat zo pijnlijk is, is dat we dit hebben zien aankomen: mondiale bezuinigingen op ontwikkelingssamenwerking, het afbreken van USAID. We wisten dat de crises hierdoor zouden toenemen, juist in landen waar conflicten en rampen al groot zijn. Meer geld naar infrastructuur, meer geld naar de winning van kritieke grondstoffen en minder geld naar armoedebestrijding, gezondheidszorg, onderwijs, minder geld naar de weerbaarheid van gemeenschappen. En dit is het directe gevolg.

De consequenties zijn desastreus, niet alleen voor de mensen die nu ziek zijn en die risico's lopen. Ebola ondermijnt de weg naar stabiliteit en ontwikkeling voor hele gemeenschappen. Het is een voorkoombare ziekte. Het voorkomen kost geld, het kost aanwezigheid, het kost vertrouwen. Vertrouwen dat jarenlang is opgebouwd en nu in rap tempo wordt afgebroken. Dit kan en moet anders, niet alleen incidenteel, maar ook structureel.
3-0358-0000.englishText:
Mr President, there are more than 1 500 confirmed cases of Ebola in Congo and Uganda; more than 500 dead. An outbreak spreading to new areas. What is so painful is that we saw this coming: global cuts in development cooperation, the dismantling of USAID. We knew that this would increase crises, especially in countries where conflicts and disasters are already widespread. More money to infrastructure, more money to the extraction of critical raw materials and less money to poverty reduction, health care, education, less money to the resilience of communities. And this is the direct result.

The consequences are disastrous, not only for the people who are currently ill and who are at risk. Ebola is undermining the path to stability and development for entire communities. It is a preventable disease. Prevention costs money, it costs presence, it costs trust. Trust that has been built up for years and is now being rapidly destroyed. This can and must be done differently, not only incidentally, but also structurally.

3-0359-0000.sourceText:
Fru Formand! Det er jo fuldstændig rigtigt, som kommissæren siger, at før vi er sikre alle sammen, er ingen sikre. Men jeg har samtidig lyst til også at fejre og gøre opmærksom på, at vi her i Europa faktisk har lært af det, vi har været igennem.

Vi har nu myndigheder, som holder øje; HERA, ECDC, som faktisk hver dag sørger for at sikre, at vi kan sove trygt om natten.

Mens alt det her er sket – og det har flere kommenteret på – så har USA sænket deres investeringer. USA har trukket sig fra WHO, USA har trukket sig helt ud af USAID, og i samme tidsrum har vi selvfølgelig prøvet at kompensere så godt som muligt. Vi har oprustet, og kommissæren har gjort en kæmpe indsats.

Jeg vil gerne spørge kommissæren; Kan kommissæren fortælle os, helt konkret, hvad foregår der lige nu? Hvilke aktiviteter er der sat i gang for at holde situationen under kontrol? Og frem for alt, hvad gøres der for at afhjælpe i landene netop nu?
3-0359-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is absolutely true, as the Commissioner says, that until we are all safe, no one is safe. But at the same time, I also want to celebrate and draw attention to the fact that here in Europe we have actually learned from what we have been through.

We now have authorities who are watching; HERA, ECDC, who actually make sure every day that we can sleep safely at night.

While all this has been happening - and several people have commented on it - the US has lowered its investments. The US has withdrawn from the WHO, the US has withdrawn completely from USAID, and in the same period we have of course tried to compensate as best as possible. We have upgraded and the Commissioner has made a huge effort.

I would like to ask the Commissioner; Can the Commissioner tell us, quite specifically, what is going on right now? What activities have been initiated to keep the situation under control? And above all, what is being done to remedy this in the countries right now?

3-0361-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der Ebola-Ausbruch in Ostafrika erinnert uns daran: Gesundheit kennt keine Grenzen. Der globale Gesundheitsschutz schützt auch unsere Sicherheit.

Unsere erste Verantwortung gilt den Menschen vor Ort; sie brauchen schnelle medizinische Hilfe und starke Gesundheitssysteme. Gerade jetzt, da sich internationale Partner, insbesondere die USA, aus Teilen der Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und der globalen Gesundheitsfinanzierung zurückziehen, wächst Europas, wächst unsere Verantwortung.

Doch dieser Ausbruch ist auch eine Mahnung an Europa. Die Lehre aus Ebola lautet: Vorsorge statt Abschottung. Pandemien bekämpft man dort, wo sie entstehen, nicht erst an unseren Außengrenzen.

Aber Gesundheitspolitik ist längst auch Sicherheits‑ und Wirtschaftspolitik. Wer über resiliente Lieferketten und sichere Rohstoffpartnerschaften spricht, muss auch in globale Gesundheit investieren.

Ebola ist deshalb ein Prüfstein, ob wir globale Gesundheit als humanitäre Verantwortung und als Voraussetzung für Sicherheit und Wohlstand verstehen. Gerade jetzt, da sich andere Akteure zurückziehen, muss Europa Verantwortung übernehmen – aus Solidarität und aus kluger Vorsorge.
3-0361-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen! The Ebola outbreak in East Africa reminds us: health knows no borders. Global health protection also protects our security.

Our first responsibility is to the local people; they need rapid medical assistance and strong health systems. Especially now that international partners, especially the USA, are withdrawing from parts of development cooperation and global health financing, Europe is growing and our responsibility is growing.

But this outbreak is also a reminder to Europe. The lesson from Ebola is: precaution instead of isolation. Pandemics are fought where they arise, not just at our external borders.

But health policy has long also become security and economic policy. Anyone who talks about resilient supply chains and secure raw material partnerships must also invest in global health.

Ebola is therefore a test of whether we understand global health as a humanitarian responsibility and a prerequisite for security and prosperity. Especially now, when other actors are withdrawing, Europe must take responsibility - out of solidarity and wise precaution.

3-0362-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, l'epidemia di Ebola in Congo e in Uganda ci ricorda che le crisi sanitarie possono superare rapidamente i confini nazionali, come dimostra anche il caso confermato in Francia di un medico rientrato dal Congo, segnalato dall'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità.

La solidarietà europea non è soltanto un dovere umanitario, ma anche un investimento nella sicurezza sanitaria internazionale. Sostenendo i paesi colpiti, proteggiamo le comunità locali, riduciamo il rischio di diffusione oltre i confini e rafforziamo la capacità globale di prevenire future emergenze.

Per questo, l'Unione europea deve continuare a sostenere la sorveglianza sanitaria, la ricerca, la prevenzione e la risposta rapida alle crisi. Investire nella solidarietà, nel coordinamento e nella preparazione significa rafforzare la tutela della salute pubblica in Africa, ma anche in Europa, contribuendo al contempo a una maggiore capacità globale di prevenire future epidemie.
3-0362-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the Ebola epidemic in Congo and Uganda reminds us that health crises can quickly cross national borders, as demonstrated by the confirmed case in France of a doctor returning from Congo, reported by the World Health Organisation.

European solidarity is not only a humanitarian duty, but also an investment in international health security. By supporting affected countries, we protect local communities, reduce the risk of spread across borders, and strengthen global capacity to prevent future emergencies.

For this reason, the European Union must continue to support health surveillance, research, prevention and rapid response to crises. Investing in solidarity, coordination and preparedness means strengthening public health protection in Africa, but also in Europe, while contributing to greater global capacity to prevent future epidemics.

3-0375-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, farmaceutska i biotehnološka industrija strateški su sektori za Europsku uniju.

To ispravno prepoznaje Mario Draghi u svojem izvješću o konkurentnosti u kojem naglašava da će upravo inovacije u području biotehnologije i napredne proizvodnje biti ključne za budući gospodarski rast i stratešku autonomiju Europe. Europska unija danas ostvaruje trgovinski suficit od oko 220 milijardi eura u lijekovima i farmaceutskim proizvodima, što pokazuje da riječ o jednoj od naših najuspješnijih industrija. No, taj uspjeh ne smijemo uzimati zdravo za gotovo. Konkurencija je sve snažnija, Kina agresivno ulaže u proizvodnju i biotehnologiju, Indija jača svoju poziciju kao globalni proizvođač lijekova i aktivnih sastojaka, a Sjedinjene Američke Države kroz svoje industrijske politike i poticaje privlače investicije, istraživanje i razvoj iz Europe.

Ako želimo zadržati vodeću poziciju, Europa mora djelovati odlučno. Zakon o kritičnim lijekovima i predloženi Zakon o biotehnologiji važni su koraci u dobrom smjeru. Međutim, za očuvanje europske konkurentnosti potrebno je učiniti više: osigurati snažnu zaštitu intelektualnog vlasništva, ubrzati izdavanje dozvola za strateške projekte, olakšati pristup kapitalu te pomoći europskim inovativnim tvrtkama da prerastu iz uspješnih startupova u globalno konkurentne scale-up kompanije.

Upravo zato nova strategija za konkurentno i održivo gospodarstvo EU-a mora biti više od okolišne ili poljoprivredne strategije. Njezina primjena mora povezati znanost, održivu proizvodnju biomaterijala, biotehnologiju i farmaceutsku industriju. Time ćemo ojačati europsku otpornost, povećati dodatnu vrijednost naših prirodnih resursa i osigurati da inovacije nastale u Europi ostanu u Europi.

To je put prema istinski konkurentnoj, održivoj i strateški autonomnoj Europskoj uniji.
3-0375-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairman, Commissioners, colleagues, the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries are strategic sectors for the European Union.

This is correctly recognized by Mario Draghi in his report on competitiveness, in which he emphasizes that innovations in the field of biotechnology and advanced manufacturing will be key to future economic growth and strategic autonomy of Europe. Today, the European Union realizes a trade surplus of around 220 billion euros in medicines and pharmaceutical products, which shows that it is one of our most successful industries. However, we must not take that success for granted. Competition is getting stronger, China is aggressively investing in production and biotechnology, India is strengthening its position as a global producer of medicines and active ingredients, and the United States of America is attracting investments, research and development from Europe through its industrial policies and incentives.

If we want to maintain our leading position, Europe must act decisively. The Critical Medicines Act and the proposed Biotechnology Act are important steps in the right direction. However, more needs to be done to preserve European competitiveness: ensure strong protection of intellectual property, accelerate the issuance of licenses for strategic projects, facilitate access to capital and help European innovative companies to grow from successful startups to globally competitive scale-up companies.

This is precisely why the new strategy for a competitive and sustainable EU economy must be more than an environmental or agricultural strategy. Its application must connect science, sustainable production of biomaterials, biotechnology and the pharmaceutical industry. This will strengthen European resilience, increase the added value of our natural resources and ensure that innovations made in Europe stay in Europe.

It is the path towards a truly competitive, sustainable and strategically autonomous European Union.

3-0376-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, desde luego que la bioeconomía puede ser una gran oportunidad. Pero no podemos sustituir, comisaria, una economía basada en extraer petróleo por otra basada en extraer cada vez más recursos de la naturaleza.

Sería un error porque la biomasa no es infinita. Nuestros bosques, suelos, mares y ecosistemas tienen límites. Y respetarlos no es un freno al desarrollo, es la condición para que ese desarrollo sea duradero.

Por eso, necesitamos una bioeconomía verdaderamente circular, que aproveche mejor los residuos y los subproductos, que utilice los recursos con inteligencia y que genere más valor añadido con menos materias primas.

Tampoco podemos olvidar algo esencial: la alimentación y la biodiversidad tienen que seguir siendo prioridad. La bioeconomía nunca puede competir con la producción de alimentos ni poner más presión sobre unos ecosistemas que ya están muy tensionados.

Si queremos una Europa más fuerte y competitiva, nuestra ventaja no vendrá de producir más recursos biológicos, sino de consumir menos recursos y de crear más valor utilizando menos.
3-0376-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, of course the bioeconomy can be a great opportunity. But we cannot replace, Commissioner, an economy based on extracting oil with another based on extracting more and more resources from nature.

It would be a mistake because biomass is not infinite. Our forests, soils, seas and ecosystems have limits. And respecting them is not a brake on development, it is the condition for that development to be lasting.

Therefore, we need a truly circular bioeconomy, which makes better use of waste and by-products, which uses resources intelligently and which generates more added value with fewer raw materials.

Nor can we forget something essential: food and biodiversity must continue to be a priority. The bioeconomy can never compete with food production or put more pressure on already stressed ecosystems.

If we want a stronger and more competitive Europe, our advantage will not come from producing more biological resources, but from consuming fewer resources and creating more value using less.

3-0377-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, le Conseil a reconnu en mars dernier la bioéconomie comme un levier de souveraineté industrielle, de transition écologique et de compétitivité. Charge maintenant aux États de tirer parti de leurs abondantes ressources agricoles et forestières et des nouveaux instruments européens, notamment l’accélérateur industriel et le règlement sur les biotechnologies.

En France, la bioéconomie représente 2 millions d’emplois et 300 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires par an. Mais la lecture des conclusions du Conseil interroge. On y parle de neutralité carbone et de suppression des obstacles réglementaires sans abaisser les normes, de simplification tout en installant une nouvelle bureaucratie, de protection du marché intérieur tout en prônant l’économie ouverte. Enfin, on détourne les enjeux de ce plan pour faire avancer la financiarisation de la nature et transformer l’agriculteur en simple fournisseur de services écosystémiques.

Pour faire de la bioéconomie un instrument de puissance géopolitique, l’UE doit sortir de ses dépendances stratégiques, mais aussi sortir de son inertie.
3-0377-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, last March the Council recognized the bioeconomy as a lever for industrial sovereignty, ecological transition and competitiveness. It is now up to States to take advantage of their abundant agricultural and forestry resources and new European instruments, notably the industrial accelerator and the biotechnology regulation.

In France, the bioeconomy represents 2 million jobs and 300 billion euros in turnover per year. But reading the Council's conclusions raises questions. We talk about carbon neutrality and the removal of regulatory obstacles without lowering standards, simplification while installing a new bureaucracy, protection of the internal market while advocating the open economy. Finally, we divert the issues of this plan to advance the financialization of nature and transform the farmer into a simple provider of ecosystem services.

To make the bioeconomy an instrument of geopolitical power, the EU must move away from its strategic dependencies, but also move away from its inertia.

3-0378-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dobbiamo riconoscere che la strategia dell'economia, della bioeconomia, è tanto.

Il termine greco "bio" riguarda il ciclo della vita.

Io mi soffermerò sul tema dei carburanti e sul loro utilizzo.

Se declinata in un'ottica di neutralità tecnologica, deve mettere anche al centro il tema dei carburanti. E parliamo di biocarburanti prodotti in Europa con materie prime europee e lavoratori europei che tengono insieme la decarbonizzazione, la sicurezza e l'occupazione.

Gli scarti animali, gli scarti dell'agricoltura, ma anche il recupero di materie prime e seconde rappresentano un buon punto di partenza per avere autonomia. Anche questo è "bio", se si considera, appunto, il ciclo della vita.

Sui carburanti, però, c'è una contraddizione. Noi oggi chiediamo – in queste ore ad Ankara, questo si dice – maggiore sforzo per la difesa, maggiore sforzo per poter essere autosufficienti, ma aerei militari che vanno a batteria non ne conosco, né carri armati, né navi, né la logistica che porta in giro i nostri mezzi e i nostri beni prodotti.

Allora dobbiamo avere un approccio della circolarità economica, garantire questo con un approccio della bioeconomia, e difendere ciò che è realmente europeo.
3-0378-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, we must recognize that the strategy of the economy, of the bioeconomy, is a lot.

The Greek term "bio" refers to the cycle of life.

I will focus on the topic of fuels and their use.

If expressed from a technological neutrality perspective, it must also put the issue of fuels at the centre. And we are talking about biofuels produced in Europe with European raw materials and European workers that bring together decarbonisation, security and employment.

Animal waste, agricultural waste, but also the recovery of raw and secondary materials represent a good starting point for autonomy. This too is "organic", if we consider the cycle of life.

Regarding fuels, however, there is a contradiction. Today we are asking - in these hours in Ankara, this is what they say - greater effort for defense, greater effort to be self-sufficient, but I don't know of military planes that run on battery power, nor tanks, nor ships, nor the logistics that transport our vehicles and our produced goods around.

Then we must have an economic circularity approach, guarantee this with a bioeconomy approach, and defend what is truly European.

3-0380-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, parliamo di costruire una bioeconomia europea competitiva e poi ostacoliamo una delle sue filiere più promettenti, la canapa, dove, in pochi anni, solo nell'Unione europea, la superficie coltivata è cresciuta del 60 % e la produzione di oltre l'84 %.

Non è soltanto un settore molto versatile, che fornisce materie prime per l'edilizia, il tessile, l'alimentazione, i mangimi e molti altri prodotti "bio‑based", ma anche un settore che dà agli agricoltori nuove fonti di reddito, diversificazione e quindi più resilienza, capacità di resistere alla crisi.

La nuova strategia europea per la bioeconomia deve sostenere chi lavora in questa filiera, superando gli ostacoli politici che ancora oggi ne frenano lo sviluppo.

A loro dobbiamo dare regole chiare, criteri che incentivino l'uso di materiali "bio-based" negli appalti pubblici e nelle costruzioni, investimenti – soprattutto negli impianti di prima trasformazione della fibra – e innovazione senza preconcetti.

L'Europa dispone già delle competenze, delle imprese e degli agricoltori interessati: ora serve una strategia capace di rispondere a tutto questo.
3-0380-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, we talk about building a competitive European bioeconomy and then we hinder one of its most promising supply chains, hemp, where, in just a few years, in the European Union alone, the cultivated area has grown by 60 % and production by more than 84 %.

It is not only a very versatile sector, which provides raw materials for construction, textiles, food, feed and many other "bio-based" products, but also a sector that gives farmers new sources of income, diversification and therefore more resilience, the ability to resist the crisis.

The new European strategy for the bioeconomy must support those who work in this supply chain, overcoming the political obstacles that still hold back its development today.

We must give them clear rules, criteria that encourage the use of "bio-based" materials in public procurement and construction, investments - especially in the first fiber transformation plants - and innovation without preconceptions.

Europe already has the skills, businesses and farmers involved: now we need a strategy capable of responding to all this.

3-0381-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, la bioéconomie est souvent présentée comme un secteur d’avenir, mais encore faut-il savoir au service de qui elle est mise en œuvre.

La nouvelle stratégie européenne de la Commission n’est, comme à son habitude, pas à la hauteur de l’enjeu. Sous couvert de compétitivité et d’innovation, elle organise la prédation généralisée du vivant. La logique est toujours la même: transformer le vivant en marchandise, exploiter davantage les forêts, les terres agricoles et la biomasse en allongeant l’exploitation des brevets. Le tout, en réduisant au maximum les normes environnementales et en remettant en cause le principe de précaution.

En réalité, cette stratégie ne répond qu’à une seule urgence: celle des intérêts des industriels et des capitalistes, en facilitant la privatisation du vivant à leur seul profit. À La France insoumise, nous refusons cette fuite en avant. Seule une stratégie fondée sur le bien commun, répondant aux besoins réels des populations, garantissant la préservation des écosystèmes, pourra faire face à la crise du climat.

Stop à l’écoblanchiment, place à la planification écologique!
3-0381-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, the bioeconomy is often presented as a sector of the future, but we still need to know for whom it is being implemented.

The Commission's new European strategy is, as usual, not up to the challenge. Under the guise of competitiveness and innovation, it organizes widespread predation of living things. The logic is always the same: transform living things into commodities, further exploit forests, agricultural land and biomass by extending the exploitation of patents. All this by reducing environmental standards as much as possible and calling into question the precautionary principle.

In reality, this strategy responds to only one emergency: that of the interests of industrialists and capitalists, by facilitating the privatization of life for their sole benefit. At La France insoumise, we refuse this headlong rush. Only a strategy based on the common good, responding to the real needs of populations, guaranteeing the preservation of ecosystems, will be able to address the climate crisis.

Stop greenwashing, make way for ecological planning!

3-0383-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, tá áthas orm labhairt ar an ábhar tábhachtach seo.

Europe's bioeconomy represents one of our greatest untapped economic opportunities – by turning agricultural residues, forestry by-products, marine resources and organic waste into high-value products, we can reduce our dependence on fossil-based materials while creating new jobs, new industries, and new income streams for rural communities. We need to frame the bioeconomy as a critical element of Europe's industrial policy, innovation policy and competitiveness policy. It strengthens European strategic autonomy by producing more of the materials, chemicals, fuels and ingredients we need here in Europe from resources we already have.

I therefore welcome investments such as Ireland's new National Biorefinery Pilot Plant in County Monaghan, which helps researchers, SMEs and industry from across the country to transform promising ideas into commercially viable products, bridging the gap between laboratory research and market deployment. If Europe is serious about competitiveness, circularity and supporting our rural economy, then we must put the bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial strategy, invest in innovation and give Europe's entrepreneurs the tools they need to scale-up and succeed.

Mar a deirimid as Gaeilge: 'Tapaigh an deis'.
3-0383-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I am pleased to speak on this important matter.

Europe's bioeconomy represents one of our greatest untapped economic opportunities – by turning agricultural residues, forestry by-products, marine resources and organic waste into high-value products, we can reduce our dependence on fossil-based materials while creating new jobs, new industries, and new income streams for rural communities. We need to frame the bioeconomy as a critical element of Europe's industrial policy, innovation policy and competitiveness policy. It strengthens European strategic autonomy by producing more of the materials, chemicals, fuels and ingredients we need here in Europe from resources we already have.

I therefore welcome investments such as Ireland's new National Biorefinery Pilot Plant in County Monaghan, which helps researchers, SMEs and industry from across the country to transform promising ideas into commercially viable products, bridging the gap between laboratory research and market deployment. If Europe is serious about competitiveness, circularity and supporting our rural economy, then we must put the bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial strategy, invest in innovation and give Europe's entrepreneurs the tools they need to scale-up and succeed.

As we say in Irish: 'Take the opportunity'.

3-0386-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie kann oder wird ein wichtiger Baustein für eine wettbewerbsfähige und unabhängigere Europäische Union sein, aber mehr Unabhängigkeit bedeutet nicht, dass wir einfach Biomaterialien produzieren und fossile durch biobasierte Materialien ersetzen. Schon heute stehen unsere Ökosysteme unter enormem Druck; die Bioökonomie darf deshalb nicht einfach das alte lineare Wirtschaftsmodell mit einem grünen Etikett fortsetzen.

Unsere Antwort muss – die Kommissarin hat es auch schon gesagt – eine Kreislauf-Bioökonomie sein, weniger Ressourcenverbrauch und eine klare Orientierung an der Abfallhierarchie. Unsere Chance liegt nämlich darin, mit weniger Ressourcen mehr Wert zu schaffen. Das Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz, das zweite Biotech-Gesetz bieten dafür wichtige Möglichkeiten – durch eine stärkere Kaskadennutzung von Biomasse, durch klare Kriterien, wann biobasierte Materialien über ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus tatsächlich einen Vorteil bringen, durch Quoten für den Einsatz dieser Materialien aus europäischer Produktion und durch die Staffelung von Abfallgebühren entsprechend der tatsächlichen Umweltfreundlichkeit der eingesetzten Materialien.

Ich bin überzeugt, so schaffen wir eine Bioökonomie, die nachhaltiger ist, die Europas Wettbewerbsfähigkeit stärkt durch Innovation, durch Ressourceneffizienz und durch weniger Abhängigkeit von globalen Rohstoffmärkten.
3-0386-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! The bioeconomy can or will be an important building block for a more competitive and independent European Union, but more independence does not mean that we simply produce biomaterials and replace fossil-based materials with bio-based materials. Our ecosystems are already under enormous pressure; The bioeconomy must therefore not simply continue the old linear economic model with a green label.

Our answer must be - the Commissioner has already said it - a circular bioeconomy, less consumption of resources and a clear orientation towards the waste hierarchy. Our opportunity lies in creating more value with fewer resources. The circular economy law and the second biotech law offer important opportunities for this - through greater cascade use of biomass, through clear criteria as to when bio-based materials actually bring an advantage over their entire life cycle, through quotas for the use of these materials from European production and through the staggering of waste fees according to the actual environmental friendliness of the materials used.

I am convinced that this is how we can create a bioeconomy that is more sustainable, that strengthens Europe's competitiveness through innovation, through resource efficiency and through less dependence on global raw material markets.

3-0388-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, ogni giorno nelle nostre case, nelle mense, nei supermercati e nelle aziende agricole milioni di tonnellate di cibo finiscono nella spazzatura.

In quei materiali c'è già una parte del futuro dell'Europa: quello che oggi scartiamo può diventare energia pulita, fertilizzanti naturali, nuovi materiali compostabili, nuove imprese, nuovi posti di lavoro.

La bioeconomia è una grande politica industriale, non solo ambientale. È una scelta di libertà, perché significa dipendere meno dalle materie prime importate e valorizzare ciò che già produciamo.

L'Europa possiede competenze, ricerca e imprese capaci di guidare questa trasformazione, ma siamo lenti.

Gli scarti organici non sono un problema da eliminare, ma una risorsa da valorizzare. Dobbiamo rendere più efficienti i nostri sistemi di raccolta e di riciclo in tutta Europa e promuovere i materiali compostabili, che rappresentano davvero la soluzione migliore. Oggi troppe filiere "bio‑based" restano bloccate da ostacoli burocratici che frenano l'innovazione.

In un mondo in cui le materie prime sono sempre più rare e più contese, continuare a sprecare risorse è un lusso che l'Europa non si può più permettere.

La bioeconomia non è un sogno per il futuro, è un'opportunità concreta per costruire un'Europa più forte, più competitiva e più autonoma.
3-0388-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, every day in our homes, canteens, supermarkets and farms, millions of tonnes of food end up in the bin.

In those materials there is already a part of Europe's future: what we discard today can become clean energy, natural fertilizers, new compostable materials, new businesses, new jobs.

The bioeconomy is a great industrial policy, not just an environmental one. It is a choice of freedom, because it means depending less on imported raw materials and enhancing what we already produce.

Europe has the skills, research and businesses capable of leading this transformation, but we are slow.

Organic waste is not a problem to be eliminated, but a resource to be valorised. We need to make our collection and recycling systems more efficient across Europe and promote compostable materials, which truly represent the best solution. Today too many "bio-based" supply chains remain blocked by bureaucratic obstacles that slow down innovation.

In a world where raw materials are increasingly rare and contested, continuing to waste resources is a luxury that Europe can no longer afford.

The bioeconomy is not a dream for the future, it is a concrete opportunity to build a stronger, more competitive and more autonomous Europe.

3-0389-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η ευρωπαϊκή βιοοικονομία μπορεί να αποτελέσει φυσικά σημαντικό εργαλείο για την πράσινη μετάβαση, την καινοτομία, τη βιομηχανική ανταγωνιστικότητα και τη στρατηγική αυτονομία της Ευρώπης. Όμως πρέπει να είμαστε σε κάτι πολύ ξεκάθαροι: Η βιοοικονομία δεν μπορεί να γίνει μια νέα μορφή πίεσης πάνω στη γη, στα δάση, στο νερό και στη βιοποικιλότητα γενικότερα. Δεν αρκεί να αντικαταστήσουμε τα ορυκτά υλικά δηλαδή με βιολογικούς πόρους, αν αυτό οδηγεί σε υπερεκμετάλλευση οικοσυστημάτων ή σε ανταγωνισμό με την παραγωγή τροφίμων.

Χρειαζόμαστε μια βιοοικονομία κυκλική, προπαντός δίκαιη και πραγματικά βιώσιμη, με προτεραιότητα στην υψηλή προστιθέμενη αξία και στις τοπικές αλυσίδες παραγωγής. Οι αγρότες, οι δασοκόμοι, οι αλιείς και οι παράκτιες κοινότητες δεν πρέπει να είναι απλώς προμηθευτές πρώτων υλών, πρέπει να είναι συμμέτοχοι στην αξία που δημιουργείται —και ιδιαίτερα στη Μεσόγειο, όπου η ξηρασία, η λειψυδρία και η απώλεια εδαφών επιδεινώνονται. Η βιοοικονομία πρέπει να συνδεθεί με την ανθεκτικότητα, την προστασία των φυσικών πόρων και την κοινωνική δικαιοσύνη.

Στρατηγική αυτονομία λοιπόν; Ναι, αλλά μέσα στα όρια της φύσης.
3-0389-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the European bioeconomy can of course be an important tool for Europe's green transition, innovation, industrial competitiveness and strategic autonomy. But we must be very clear about something: The bioeconomy cannot become a new form of pressure on land, forests, water and biodiversity in general. It is not enough to replace mineral materials with biological resources if this leads to overexploitation of ecosystems or competition with food production.

We need a bioeconomy that is circular, above all fair and truly sustainable, prioritizing high added value and local production chains. Farmers, foresters, fishermen and coastal communities should not just be suppliers of raw materials, they should be participants in the value created — and especially in the Mediterranean, where drought, water scarcity and soil loss are worsening. The bioeconomy must be linked to resilience, natural resource protection and social justice.

So strategic autonomy? Yes, but within the limits of nature.

3-0393-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrter Herr Präsident, liebe Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie bietet die einmalige Chance für Europa, einen einzigartigen Wirtschaftszweig zu erschließen, der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und die Nachhaltigkeit miteinander verbindet. Fakt ist: Ohne unsere Land- und Forstwirte wird dieser Sektor keinen Erfolg haben; sie dürfen nicht nur Lieferanten von Rohstoffen sein, sondern müssen weiter an der Wertschöpfungskette beteiligt werden.

Die Innovation ist da. Schon heute gibt es eine unglaubliche Bandbreite an Produkten und Prozessen, von Baumaterialien bis hin zu biobasierten Textilien: All das gibt es heute schon in Europa.

Jetzt müssen wir in die Breite kommen. Wir brauchen Investitionen und weniger Bürokratie. Wer biobasierte Produkte entwickeln will, darf nicht an komplizierten Genehmigungen oder widersprüchlichen Vorschriften scheitern. Deshalb sollte die Bioökonomie-Strategie bestehende Hemmnisse identifizieren und den Weg vorwärts aufzeigen.

Der angekündigte Biotech Act II muss nun die Bioökonomie weiter voranbringen. Wir brauchen schnellere Genehmigungsverfahren, innovationsfreundliche Rahmenbedingungen und bessere Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten, mit Land- und Forstwirtschaft im Zentrum. Bei uns schlummert so viel Potenzial: Lassen Sie uns jetzt Europa als Standort für biobasierte Produkte entfesseln!
3-0393-0000.englishText:
Dear Mr. President, dear Commissioner, The bioeconomy offers a unique opportunity for Europe to develop a unique economic sector that combines competitiveness and sustainability. The fact is: without our farmers and foresters, this sector will not be successful; They must not only be suppliers of raw materials, but must also be involved in the value chain.

The innovation is here. There is already an incredible range of products and processes, from building materials to bio-based textiles: all of this already exists in Europe today.

Now we have to get broader. We need investment and less bureaucracy. Anyone who wants to develop bio-based products must not fail because of complicated approvals or contradictory regulations. The bioeconomy strategy should therefore identify existing obstacles and show the way forward.

The announced Biotech Act II must now further advance the bioeconomy. We need faster approval processes, innovation-friendly framework conditions and better financing options, with agriculture and forestry at the center. We have so much potential lying dormant: Let us now unleash Europe as a location for bio-based products!

3-0394-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie-Strategie bietet neue Chancen für die Europäische Union: die Chance, fossile Rohstoffe zu ersetzen; die Chance, auf diesem Gebiet die Technologieführerschaft zu übernehmen, und dadurch auch die Chance, Arbeitsplätze und Wohlstand in Europa abzusichern und auszubauen, vor allem durch mehr Unabhängigkeit.

Das alles sind unterstützenswerte Ziele, und genau deshalb darf es hier nicht bei schönen Überschriften bleiben. Für mich heißt das, dass wir die Kreislaufwirtschaft weiter vorantreiben müssen und mit klaren Vorgaben gegen die Verschwendung von Ressourcen angehen. Für mich heißt das, dass wir endlich die Gesundheit unserer Böden und Gewässer sicherstellen müssen. Für mich heißt das auch, dass wir klare Regeln brauchen, mit denen unsere hohen Lebensmittelstandards und der Schutz der Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher abgesichert werden.

Eine Bioökonomie-Strategie, die auf ein starkes Fundament fußt, werde ich gerne unterstützen.
3-0394-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! The bioeconomy strategy offers new opportunities for the European Union: the chance to replace fossil raw materials; the opportunity to take technological leadership in this area and thereby also the opportunity to secure and expand jobs and prosperity in Europe, especially through greater independence.

These are all goals worth supporting, and that's exactly why we can't just stick with nice headlines. For me, this means that we must continue to promote the circular economy and address the waste of resources with clear guidelines. For me this means that we finally have to ensure the health of our soil and water. For me, this also means that we need clear rules to ensure our high food standards and the protection of consumers.

I will be happy to support a bioeconomy strategy that is based on a strong foundation.

3-0395-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, la bioéconomie, ce sont des innovations concrètes: plastique fabriqué à partir de déchets agricoles, carburants durables, ou encore médicaments. Nous avons pour cela d’excellents chercheurs et des entreprises innovantes. Mais, trop souvent, les innovations naissent chez nous et sont industrialisées ailleurs, parce que nos entreprises ont toujours les mêmes obstacles, en Europe: des procédures trop longues, un accès au marché insuffisant et un marché européen trop fragmenté.

Nous devons changer d’échelle. Il faut pour cela davantage d’investissement, avec le soutien de la BEI et du prochain budget européen. Il faut aussi des règles qui créent de vrais débouchés pour nos produits biosourcés et qui accélèrent la construction de nouvelles usines.

La bioéconomie, c’est donc aussi une politique industrielle, une politique d’innovation et un levier essentiel pour renforcer notre autonomie stratégique. Transformons ce potentiel en emplois, en investissements et en production, ici, en Europe!
3-0395-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the bioeconomy involves concrete innovations: plastic made from agricultural waste, sustainable fuels, and even medicines. For this, we have excellent researchers and innovative companies. But, too often, innovations are born here and are industrialized elsewhere, because our companies always have the same obstacles in Europe: procedures that are too long, insufficient market access and a European market that is too fragmented.

We need to change scale. This requires more investment, with the support of the EIB and the next European budget. We also need rules that create real outlets for our biosourced products and accelerate the construction of new factories.

The bioeconomy is therefore also an industrial policy, an innovation policy and an essential lever to strengthen our strategic autonomy. Let's transform this potential into jobs, investments and production, here in Europe!

3-0397-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, arvoisa komission jäsen, riippumattomuus Venäjän tai Lähi-idän fossiilipolttoaineista ei synny siten, että rajoitamme voimakkaasti Euroopassa uusiutuvien luonnonvarojen käyttöä. Biotalous on yksi tärkeimmistä keinoistamme vahvistaa omavaraisuutta ja rakentaa vahvempaa, uusiutuviin luonnonvaroihin perustuvaa Eurooppaa. Samalla vähennämme tuontiriippuvuutta, luomme työpaikkoja ja nostamme tietysti jalostusarvoa sekä vahvistamme huoltovarmuuttamme.

Tarvitsemme johdonmukaista sääntelyä, ilmasto- ja energiatavoitteiden yhteensovittamista, teknologianeutraalisuutta ja investointien, myös tutkimuksen, määrätietoista tukemista. Esimerkiksi ennallistamisasetuksen toimeenpanoon liittyy edelleen merkittäviä epävarmuuksia, mitä tulee sen laajuuteen, hintaan ja vaikutuksiin. Jos emme luo yrityksille ennustettavaa toimintaympäristöä, investoinnit jäävät tekemättä ja riippumattomuus jää pelkäksi puheeksi. On hyvä, että EU:n biotalousstrategia tunnistaa myös biokiertotalouden valtavan potentiaalin. Nyt tarvitaan myös poliittista rohkeutta hyödyntää sitä.
3-0397-0000.englishText:
Honorable Speaker, Honorable Member of the Commission, independence from fossil fuels in Russia or the Middle East does not come about by strongly limiting the use of renewable natural resources in Europe. Bioeconomy is one of our most important ways to strengthen self-sufficiency and build a stronger Europe based on renewable natural resources. At the same time, we reduce import dependence, create jobs and, of course, increase the processing value and strengthen our security of supply.

We need consistent regulation, coordination of climate and energy goals, technology neutrality and purposeful support of investments, including research. For example, the implementation of the Restoration Regulation remains subject to significant uncertainties regarding its scope, cost and impact. If we do not create a predictable operating environment for companies, investments will not be made and independence will remain just talk. It is good that the EU's bioeconomy strategy also recognizes the enormous potential of the biocircular economy. Now we also need the political courage to take advantage of it.

3-0398-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Strategische Autonomie bedeutet nicht nur, Abhängigkeiten bei Chips, Energie oder kritischen Rohstoffen zu verringern; sie bedeutet auch, unsere eigenen biologischen Ressourcen besser zu nutzen. Die Bioökonomie kann Europa in zentralen Bereichen unabhängiger machen – bei der Lebensmittelversorgung, bei Energie, bei Gesundheit und überall dort, wo wir heute noch von fossilen Rohstoffen abhängig sind.

Das ist kein Nischenthema. Die europäische Bioökonomie steht bereits heute für mehr als 17 Millionen Arbeitsplätze und eine Wertschöpfung von 2,7 Billionen Euro. Arbeitsplätze in der Bioökonomieindustrie sind hochproduktiv und schaffen fast drei weitere indirekte Arbeitsplätze in Europa. Gerade für ländliche Räume und Küstenregionen ergeben sich hier neue Chancen.

Europa ist in der Bioökonomie nicht abgehängt – im Gegenteil, wir sind stark in Forschung und Innovation. Was uns noch fehlt, ist die industrielle Skalierung; dafür braucht es mehr Pioniergeist, mehr Investitionsbereitschaft, europaweite Harmonisierung und Leitmärkte für biobasierte Produkte.

Gut, dass die EU‑Kommission das Thema auf die Agenda gesetzt hat. Unsere Aufgabe ist es jetzt, dafür zu sorgen, dass Biotech-Cluster, Regulierung und Finanzierung besser ineinandergreifen, damit die Bioökonomie in Europa international wettbewerbsfähig wird und bleibt.
3-0398-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! Strategic autonomy doesn't just mean reducing dependencies on chips, energy or critical raw materials; it also means making better use of our own biological resources. The bioeconomy can make Europe more independent in key areas - food supply, energy, health and everywhere we are still dependent on fossil raw materials.

This is not a niche topic. The European bioeconomy already represents more than 17 million jobs and a value creation of 2.7 trillion euros. Jobs in the bioeconomy industry are highly productive and create almost three more indirect jobs in Europe. There are new opportunities here, especially for rural areas and coastal regions.

Europe is not left behind in the bioeconomy - on the contrary, we are strong in research and innovation. What we still lack is industrial scale; This requires more pioneering spirit, more willingness to invest, Europe-wide harmonization and lead markets for bio-based products.

It's good that the EU Commission has put the issue on the agenda. Our task now is to ensure that biotech clusters, regulation and financing are better integrated so that the bioeconomy in Europe becomes and remains internationally competitive.

3-0399-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Biofiber i kläder och tyg, starka limträbalkar, snygga byggmaterial, gröna kemikalier, rengöringsmedel, smörjmedel, biobaserad färg och lim, bioplast, hållbara förpackningar, biogas, biodrivmedel, el och värme. Ja, listan kan göras lång.

Jag står ofta i den här talarstolen och säger att vi i EU måste bryta vårt beroende av fossila energikällor, insatsråvaror och kemikalier. Jag får lika ofta frågan, inte minst från den här sidan i parlamentet – de som förnekar klimatförändringarna och vill fortsätta handla med diktaturer och skurkstater – om hur det här ska gå till. Här har ni svaret: i bioekonomin. Låt oss göra det fossila till historia med bioresurser från skog, lantbruk och hav. Kan vi göra slut med det fossila?

Då duger det inte med EU-regler som ställer sig i vägen. Nu måste EU leverera enklare regler som möjliggör och inte blockerar skogsbruk, som bättre finansierar och tar vara på möjligheter och potentialen i hela vår biobaserade sektor.
3-0399-0000.englishText:
Mr Speaker! Biofibre in clothing and fabric, strong glulam beams, attractive building materials, green chemicals, cleaning agents, lubricants, bio-based paint and glue, bioplastics, sustainable packaging, biogas, biofuels, electricity and heat. Yes, the list can be made long.

I often stand in this pulpit and say that we in the EU must break our dependence on fossil energy sources, input raw materials and chemicals. I am asked just as often, not least from this side of Parliament – ​​those who deny climate change and want to continue trading with dictatorships and rogue states – about how this is to be done.
