Here you have the answer: in the bioeconomy. Let's make fossils history with bioresources from forests, agriculture and oceans. Can we do away with fossil fuels?

Then EU rules that stand in the way will not do. Now the EU must deliver simpler rules that enable and not block forestry, that better finance and harness the opportunities and potential of our entire bio-based sector.

3-0401-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, ako želimo istinsku stratešku autonomiju Europske unije, moramo početi od onoga što je temelj svake ekonomije, naših prirodnih resursa i sposobnosti da ih održivo koristimo.

Upravo zato bioekonomija nije samo razvojna prilika, nego strateška nužnost. Ona Europi omogućuje manju ovisnost o uvozu, jača našu proizvodnju i istodobno daje odgovor na klimatske izazove. U tome poljoprivreda ima nezamjenjivu ulogu, no ova tranzicija mora biti pravedna. Hrvatska to najbolje pokazuje: naša Slavonija, Zagorje, Međimurje, Banija, Lika, Dalmatinska zagora, Gorski kotar i brojne druge ruralne regije imaju golemi potencijal da postanu europski centri proizvodnje biomaterijala, obnovljive energije, inovacija i kvalitetnih radnih mjesta. Ono što nam nedostaje nije potencijal, nego ulaganja, moderna infrastruktura i snažnija europska potpora.

Zato trebamo ambicioznu europsku strategiju koja će povezati bioekonomiju, poljoprivredu i regionalni razvoj te ulagati upravo ondje gdje Europa može biti najjača: u svojim regijama.
3-0401-0000.englishText:
Dear President, if we want true strategic autonomy of the European Union, we must start from what is the foundation of every economy, our natural resources and the ability to use them sustainably.

This is precisely why the bioeconomy is not only a development opportunity, but a strategic necessity. It enables Europe to be less dependent on imports, strengthens our production and at the same time responds to climate challenges. Agriculture has an irreplaceable role in this, but this transition must be fair. Croatia shows this best: our Slavonija, Zagorje, Međimurje, Banija, Lika, Dalmatinska zagora, Gorski kotar and numerous other rural regions have enormous potential to become European centers for the production of biomaterials, renewable energy, innovation and quality jobs. What we lack is not potential, but investments, modern infrastructure and stronger European support.

That is why we need an ambitious European strategy that will connect the bioeconomy, agriculture and regional development and invest exactly where Europe can be strongest: in its regions.

3-0403-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, sigur că Uniunea Europeană are nevoie de o strategie în domeniul bioeconomiei. Numai că, doamnă comisar, chiar dumneavoastră ați spus, că există capital, dar oare ce ne lipsește? Încrederea.

Pentru că de foarte multe ori, în această perioadă, în Uniunea Europeană s-au făcut reglementări care se obstrucționează unele pe altele. Și ca să vă dau un exemplu concret: se vorbea aici de biotehnologia farmaceutică și este foarte important să avem această independență într-o industrie de care depinde, de fapt, viața oamenilor. Dar avem o directivă - directiva privind apele uzate. Noi, Parlamentul, am votat o rezoluție să o schimbați pentru că este prost gândită și are un impact și închide pe rând fabricile de medicamente.

Vă mai pot da exemple în domeniul textil - unde am lucrat vreo 36 de ani - că ani de zile Uniunea Europeană a ars câmpul cu cânepă, considerând-o absolut neutilizabilă și dăunătoare. De fapt, este o plantă textilă ecologică, care poate fi folosită în toate domeniile și este cea mai eficientă - pentru că nu arunci nimic din ea, de la uleiuri până la reziduuri care se folosesc în domeniul construcțiilor.

Și atunci lipsa aceasta de încredere că există o continuitate a politicilor face ca investitorul să nu investească. Poate că veniți să eliminați acele bariere, pentru că mai avem o barieră, bariera tarifelor, pentru că puneți taxe vamale - și o spun mereu aici - la materii prime mai mici decât la produsele finite.
3-0403-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, I am sure that the European Union needs a strategy in the field of the bioeconomy. However, Madam Commissioner, you yourself said that there is capital, but what are we missing? Confidence.

Because very often, during this period, regulations were made in the European Union that obstruct each other. And to give you a concrete example: we were talking about pharmaceutical biotechnology here, and it is very important to have this independence in an industry on which, in fact, people's lives depend. But we have a directive - the waste water directive. We, the Parliament, voted a resolution to change it because it is ill-conceived and has an impact and closes the drug factories one by one.

I can also give you examples in the textile field - where I worked for about 36 years - that for years the European Union burned the field with hemp, considering it absolutely unusable and harmful. In fact, it is an ecological textile plant that can be used in all fields and is the most efficient - because you do not throw away anything from it, from oils to residues that are used in the field of construction.

And then this lack of confidence that there is a continuity of policies makes the investor not invest. Maybe you come to remove those barriers, because we have another barrier, the tariff barrier, because you put tariffs - and I always say it here - on raw materials lower than on finished products.

3-0418-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señorías, supongo que han visto ustedes imágenes de mujeres en Sudán con sus hijos encima llorando de desesperación.

Ante esto hay dos opciones. Una es explicar lo que sucede en Sudán recurriendo al viejo relato del colonialismo según el cual los conflictos en el Sur Global se deben a que son unos bárbaros, a que no saben convivir en paz, a que no saben autogobernarse. Bajo ese relato siempre se han justificado las invasiones extranjeras y se ha callado ante la violencia que suponen.

Y hay otra opción: decir la verdad. Decir la verdad en el caso de Sudán implica decir que los 60 000 muertos son consecuencia de la responsabilidad de Occidente y sus aliados; que los Emiratos Árabes Unidos introducen las armas que sirven para cometer un genocidio y que extraen el oro de Sudán; que —como todos y todas sabemos— el Gobierno de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos es un Gobierno títere de los Estados Unidos e Israel; que los planes expansionistas del sionismo están detrás del genocidio que se está cometiendo en Sudán; y, otra vez más, que los Estados Unidos e Israel son la principal amenaza para la humanidad.
3-0418-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, I suppose you have seen images of women in Sudan with their children on top of them crying in despair.

Given this there are two options. One is to explain what is happening in Sudan by resorting to the old narrative of colonialism according to which the conflicts in the Global South are due to the fact that they are barbarians, because they do not know how to live together in peace, because they do not know how to govern themselves. Under this narrative, foreign invasions have always been justified and silence has been given to the violence they entail.

And there is another option: tell the truth. Telling the truth in the case of Sudan means saying that the 60,000 deaths are a consequence of the responsibility of the West and its allies; that the United Arab Emirates introduce weapons used to commit genocide and extract gold from Sudan; that—as we all know—the Government of the United Arab Emirates is a puppet government of the United States and Israel; that the expansionist plans of Zionism are behind the genocide being committed in Sudan; and, once again, that the United States and Israel are the main threat to humanity.

3-0419-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la situazione nella città di El Obeid, 340 000 abitanti, sta precipitando.

Centinaia di migliaia di civili sono intrappolati nei combattimenti, mentre continuano gli attacchi contro la popolazione e l'infrastruttura civile. L'Alto Commissario delle Nazioni Unite per i diritti umani ha confermato che i civili vivono in questa città da 18 mesi sotto assedio permanente e che si rischia una nuova tragedia umanitaria.

Sia chiaro: in Sudan non esiste una soluzione militare. Entrambe le parti sono responsabili di gravissime violazioni del diritto internazionale umanitario. Per questo, chiediamo un cessate il fuoco immediato, il pieno rispetto della dichiarazione di Gedda, un accesso umanitario senza ostacoli e sanzioni più severe contro chi alimenta il conflitto e impedisce addirittura l'arrivo di aiuti umanitari.

Non ci sarà pace finché il futuro del Sudan resterà nelle mani di questi gruppi estremisti. I Fratelli mussulmani hanno alimentato per anni radicalizzazione, violenza e instabilità in Sudan e in tutta la regione.

L'Unione europea, insieme alle Nazioni Unite e all'Unione africana, deve sostenere un processo politico che escluda ogni influenza dei movimenti islamisti radicali.
3-0419-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, the situation in the city of El Obeid, 340 000 inhabitants, is worsening.

Hundreds of thousands of civilians are trapped in the fighting, as attacks against the population and civilian infrastructure continue. The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has confirmed that civilians have been living in this city for 18 months under permanent siege and that there is a risk of a new humanitarian tragedy.

Let's be clear: there is no military solution in Sudan. Both parties are responsible for very serious violations of international humanitarian law. For this reason, we call for an immediate ceasefire, full compliance with the Jeddah Declaration, unhindered humanitarian access and more severe sanctions against those who fuel the conflict and even prevent the arrival of humanitarian aid.

There will be no peace as long as Sudan's future remains in the hands of these extremist groups. The Muslim Brotherhood has fueled radicalization, violence and instability in Sudan and across the region for years.

The European Union, together with the United Nations and the African Union, must support a political process that excludes any influence of radical Islamist movements.

3-0420-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Der Sudan gleicht der Hölle auf Erden – über 150 000 Tote, 14 Millionen Vertriebene, 25 Millionen Hungernde, massenhaft Vergewaltigungen und systematische Verfolgungen von Christen und nicht-arabischen Minderheiten. Es drohen jetzt weitere Massaker – wir verurteilen das aufs Schärfste.

Natürlich befeuert dieser Konflikt auch Massenmigration nach Europa. Wer aber den halben Sudan aufnimmt, hilft nicht dem Sudan, sondern wird selbst zum Sudan. Wir müssen daher unsere Außengrenzen schützen, und wir sollten dort helfen, wo es sinnvoll ist, nämlich in der Region, gemeinsam mit den Nachbarstaaten; das ist Diplomatie.

Es geht darum, Realismus mit Humanität zu verbinden: klare Kante gegen Kriegsverbrechen, keine Waffenlieferungen, die den Konflikt nur verlängern, regionale Stabilität statt weiterer Anreize für Massenmigration und deshalb enge Kooperation mit den Staaten der Region statt Werteimperialismus. Denn eine tragfähige Friedenslösung ist nur dann möglich, wenn man die regionalen und kulturellen Kontexte berücksichtigt; wer diese ignoriert, verschlimmert nur das Chaos.

Das ist eine Politik der Verantwortung gegenüber den Menschen im Sudan und gegenüber den Menschen in Europa.
3-0420-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! Sudan is like hell on earth - over 150,000 dead, 14 million displaced, 25 million starving, mass rape and systematic persecution of Christians and non-Arab minorities. There is now a threat of further massacres – we condemn this in the strongest possible terms.

Of course, this conflict also fuels mass migration to Europe. But anyone who takes in half of Sudan is not helping Sudan, but is becoming Sudan himself. We must therefore protect our external borders and we should help where it makes sense, namely in the region, together with neighboring states; that is diplomacy.

It's about combining realism with humanity: a clear stance against war crimes, no arms deliveries that only prolong the conflict, regional stability instead of further incentives for mass migration and therefore close cooperation with the states in the region instead of value imperialism. A viable peace solution is only possible if the regional and cultural contexts are taken into account; Anyone who ignores this will only make the chaos worse.

This is a policy of responsibility towards the people of Sudan and towards the people of Europe.

3-0421-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Powiem tak: Sudan to nasza sprawa. Sudan to nasza sprawa, bo kiedy głód staje się bronią, pojawia się co? Migracja.

Usłyszałam dzisiaj dwie złe odpowiedzi na ten temat. Pierwsza to lewicowe marzenia, że wystarczy otworzyć drzwi i świat się sam ułoży. Otóż nie ułoży się. Mieliśmy już tego przykłady. Druga odpowiedź: migracja to ryzyko – kto temu zaprzecza, nie kocha Europy.

Ta druga odpowiedź to prawicowy kabotynizm. Wiecie co? Mamy na tej sali europosła, który biega po ulicy i nagrywa ludzi tylko dlatego, że mają inny kolor skóry. To po prostu świr. Musimy wybrać inną drogę. Korytarze humanitarne – natychmiast. Rozliczenie zbrodni wojennych – natychmiast. Musimy działać, nie czekać.
3-0421-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Let me put it this way: Sudan is our business. Sudan is our business, because when hunger becomes a weapon, what happens? Migration.

I heard two wrong answers about this today. The first is leftist dreams that all you have to do is open the door and the world will take care of itself. Well, it won't work out. We have already had examples of this. Second answer: migration is a risk - anyone who denies it does not love Europe.

The second answer is right-wing cabotinism. You know what? We have an MEP in this room who runs in the street and records people just because they have a different skin color. He's just crazy. We have to choose a different path. Humanitarian corridors – immediately. Settlement of war crimes – immediately. We must act, not wait.

3-0422-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, depois de Zamzam e El-Fasher, El-Obeid corre o risco de ser o epicentro de uma nova tragédia no Sudão.

El-Obeid, que alberga uma população de meio milhão de habitantes, mas também um número indeterminado de pessoas internamente deslocadas, e que está desde há meses cercada. El-Obeid onde, aos ataques contínuos de drones que destruíram infraestruturas essenciais, semeando a fome e a cólera, ameaça agora juntar-se a repetição do massacre de civis a que assistimos antes, quando as Forças Rápidas de Suporte e as Forças Armadas Sudanesas se confrontaram, alimentadas pelo exterior.

«Os países com influência têm o dever de a exercer agora para parar esta loucura», foram as palavras do Alto Representante das Nações Unidas para os Direitos Humanos. E é isso que, hoje, pedimos que a União Europeia, mas também os Estados Unidos, o Egito, os Emirados Árabes Unidos façam. Respeito pelo bloqueio na entrada de armas, sanções individuais e responsabilização, participação na construção de uma solução civil para o conflito.
3-0422-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, after Zamzam and El-Fasher, El-Obeid is at risk of being the epicenter of a new tragedy in Sudan.

El-Obeid, which is home to a population of half a million inhabitants, but also an undetermined number of internally displaced people, and which has been surrounded for months. El-Obeid where, the continuous drone attacks that have destroyed essential infrastructure, sowing hunger and cholera, now threatens to be joined by a repeat of the massacre of civilians that we saw before, when the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces clashed, fueled from the outside.

«Countries with influence have a duty to exercise it now to stop this madness», were the words of the United Nations High Representative for Human Rights. And that is what, today, we ask the European Union, but also the United States, Egypt and the United Arab Emirates to do. Respect for blocking the entry of weapons, individual sanctions and accountability, participation in the construction of a civil solution to the conflict.

3-0423-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, mes chers collègues, à El-Obeid, les populations subissent des bombardements, des exécutions, des viols, des déplacements forcés et des violations répétées du droit international humanitaire. Il semble que nous soyons tous d’accord aujourd’hui pour faire ce constat.

On notera cependant qu’étrangement, on entend peu les élus d’extrême gauche – et je veux parler particulièrement de La France insoumise – autour de ce sujet. Il faut dire qu’ici il n’y a d’opportunité ni d’attaquer les Juifs ni d’attaquer Israël.

Alors la réalité – certains l’ont dit –, c’est que nombre d’États sont complices de ce qui se passe au Soudan, puisque les Émirats arabes unis, qui soutiennent les forces de soutien rapides à l’origine des massacres, jouissent chez nous, c’est vrai, d’un passe-droit scandaleux acheté à coups de pétrodollars.

Oui, si nous voulons arrêter de regarder ailleurs ou sortir de l’incantation pour réellement stopper ces massacres et ces exactions, commençons par pointer les vrais responsables et prenons aussi les mesures qui sont à notre portée!
3-0423-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, my dear colleagues, in El-Obeid, the populations are suffering bombings, executions, rapes, forced displacements and repeated violations of international humanitarian law. It seems that today we all agree on this observation.

It should be noted, however, that strangely, we hear little from far-left elected officials – and I want to talk particularly about La France insoumise – on this subject. It must be said that here there is no opportunity either to attack the Jews or to attack Israel.

So the reality – some have said it – is that a number of States are complicit in what is happening in Sudan, since the United Arab Emirates, which supports the rapid support forces behind the massacres, enjoys here, it is true, a scandalous privilege purchased with petrodollars.

Yes, if we want to stop looking elsewhere or get away from the incantation to really stop these massacres and these abuses, let's start by pointing out the real people responsible and also take the measures that are within our reach!

3-0426-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, les confieso que asisto a este debate con dosis de frustración y de impotencia, porque traemos una y otra vez el debate sobre Sudán a esta Cámara mientras Sudán se desangra y El Obeid se convierte en un símbolo de una tragedia anunciada una y otra vez.

En apenas tres semanas ha habido quince ataques con drones en la ciudad, ejecuciones sumarias, secuestros, tortura y violencia sexual en la región. Hay más de 13 millones de personas desplazadas, más de 33 millones necesitan ayuda urgente y millones viven bajo la amenaza del hambre. Pero al mundo directamente no le importa.

Debemos exigir de una vez por todas el cese inmediato de los ataques a los civiles, a las escuelas, a los mercados. El Derecho humanitario internacional no puede ser una promesa vacía ni una norma selectiva, debe ser siempre nuestra brújula de forma coherente.

Es verdad que la Unión Europea ha estado a la altura en la necesidad de la ayuda humanitaria, pero no es suficiente. Tenemos que desplegar la diplomacia humanitaria, garantizar los corredores y, sobre todo, parar esta barbarie de una vez por todas. La respuesta humanitaria necesita 2 900 millones de dólares, el 0,1 % del gasto militar, para abordar 20 millones de personas y sus necesidades. A nadie le importa y no estamos a la altura.
3-0426-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Madam Commissioner, I confess that I attend this debate with a dose of frustration and helplessness, because we bring the debate on Sudan to this House again and again while Sudan is bleeding to death and El Obeid becomes a symbol of a tragedy announced again and again.

In just three weeks there have been fifteen drone attacks in the city, summary executions, kidnappings, torture and sexual violence in the region. More than 13 million people are displaced, more than 33 million need urgent help, and millions live under the threat of hunger. But the world doesn't really care.

We must demand once and for all the immediate cessation of attacks on civilians, on schools, on markets. International humanitarian law cannot be an empty promise or a selective norm, it must always be our compass in a coherent way.

It is true that the European Union has met the need for humanitarian aid, but it is not enough. We have to deploy humanitarian diplomacy, guarantee the corridors and, above all, stop this barbarity once and for all. The humanitarian response needs $2.9 billion, 0.1% of military spending, to address 20 million people and their needs. Nobody cares and we are not up to it.

3-0428-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, c’est la troisième fois en six mois qu’une discussion alarmante de la situation dramatique au Soudan est à l’ordre du jour de cette assemblée. À chaque fois, nous dénonçons les massacres, les conditions de vie, voire de survie, des populations déplacées, de millions d’enfants menacés par la famine, de femmes et de jeunes filles exposées aux violences sexuelles, sans oublier les dizaines de milliers de morts.

La dernière fois, il s’agissait également d’attirer l’attention sur l’ingérence extérieure, et notamment celle des Émirats arabes unis.

Aujourd’hui, c’est la situation d’El-Obeid qui nous préoccupe. Il est impératif que l’Union européenne mette en place des mesures de protection immédiates. Les populations d’El-Obeid doivent être protégées. L’Union européenne doit être à leurs côtés.
3-0428-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, this is the third time in six months that an alarming discussion of the dramatic situation in Sudan has been on the agenda of this assembly. Each time, we denounce the massacres, the living conditions, even survival, of displaced populations, of millions of children threatened by famine, of women and young girls exposed to sexual violence, without forgetting the tens of thousands of deaths.

Last time, it was also about drawing attention to external interference, particularly that of the United Arab Emirates.

Today, it is the situation of El-Obeid that concerns us. It is imperative that the European Union puts in place immediate protective measures. The populations of El-Obeid must be protected. The European Union must be at their side.

3-0430-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire Šuica, je vais essayer avec une grande retenue de vous exprimer la profondeur de ma colère par rapport à vos paroles, qui dégoulinent d’hypocrisie.

Vous avez parlé du massacre d’El-Facher – des milliers de Soudanais massacrés par les Forces rapides, soutenues par les Émirats arabes unis. Vous n’avez pas osé le dire, mais vous le savez. Qu’avez-vous fait? Un mois après ce massacre, vous avez été dans les Émirats leur offrir un partenariat stratégique avec l’Union européenne. Ça revient à les encourager à continuer leur soutien aux massacres au Soudan. Et encore aujourd’hui, vous n’arrivez pas à les condamner, à prononcer ces mots et à prendre des sanctions contre eux.

La même chose, vous l’avez faite avec les Palestiniens:: le jour où les Nations unies ont publié un rapport disant qu’Israël cible délibérément des enfants palestiniens, vous allez en Israël, sourire avec le président israélien: «J’ai hâte de développer de nouveaux partenariats.»

Prenez des sanctions, arrêtez vos larmes de crocodile et condamnez les Émirats et condamnez Israël!
3-0430-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner Šuica, I will try with great restraint to express to you the depth of my anger at your words, which are dripping with hypocrisy.

You spoke about the El-Facher massacre – thousands of Sudanese massacred by the Rapid Forces, supported by the United Arab Emirates. You didn't dare say it, but you know it. What did you do? A month after this massacre, you went to the Emirates to offer them a strategic partnership with the European Union. This amounts to encouraging them to continue their support for the massacres in Sudan. And even today, you cannot condemn them, pronounce these words and take sanctions against them.

The same thing you did with the Palestinians: the day the United Nations released a report saying Israel is deliberately targeting Palestinian children, you go to Israel, smile with the Israeli president: “I look forward to developing new partnerships.”

Take sanctions, stop your crocodile tears and condemn the Emirates and condemn Israel!

3-0432-5000.sourceText: The resolution on the El-Obeid humanitarian catastrophe has been used by the left-wing and progressive groups in the European Parliament to attack the United Arab Emirates, instead of focusing strictly on resolving the humanitarian crisis in Sudan. This approach is even more problematic as the resolution ignores the role of actual malign actors, like Russia, Iran, and others, whose actions have contributed to this conflict. EP should have remained focused on the humanitarian disaster in El-Obeid by prioritizing the protection of civilians, ensuring humanitarian access, and supporting accountability for all perpetrators on the basis of verified evidence. Instead, the resolution devotes particular attention to the UAE while failing to acknowledge the broad network of external actors that has fueled and prolonged this conflict. Numerous reports have documented the involvement of Russian-linked Wagner forces and their successor structures, alongside other foreign actors, in sustaining violence and instability in Sudan. Instead of being constructive, the resolution was weaponized by the left-wing and progressive groups to attack the UAE so they could score political points in their home countries. Humanitarian resolutions should remain impartial, evidence-based, and centered on the victims. Selectively and incorrectly attributing responsibility undermines the credibility of Parliament's message and its position as an effective actor in this conflict resolution.
3-0432-5000.englishText: The resolution on the El-Obeid humanitarian catastrophe has been used by the left-wing and progressive groups in the European Parliament to attack the United Arab Emirates, instead of focusing strictly on resolving the humanitarian crisis in Sudan. This approach is even more problematic as the resolution ignores the role of actual malign actors, like Russia, Iran, and others, whose actions have contributed to this conflict. EP should have remained focused on the humanitarian disaster in El-Obeid by prioritizing the protection of civilians, ensuring humanitarian access, and supporting accountability for all perpetrators on the basis of verified evidence. Instead, the resolution devotes particular attention to the UAE while failing to acknowledge the broad network of external actors that has fueled and prolonged this conflict. Numerous reports have documented the involvement of Russian-linked Wagner forces and their successor structures, alongside other foreign actors, in sustaining violence and instability in Sudan. Instead of being constructive, the resolution was weaponized by the left-wing and progressive groups to attack the UAE so they could score political points in their home countries. Humanitarian resolutions should remain impartial, evidence-based, and centered on the victims. Selectively and incorrectly attributing responsibility undermines the credibility of Parliament's message and its position as an effective actor in this conflict resolution.

3-0436-0000.sourceText:
Weer ging het afschuwelijk mis in Nigeria. Nu in het dorp Kawel, waar tientallen christenen het leven lieten bij een aanval door extremisten. Maar ik denk ook aan de tientallen scholieren die recent werden ontvoerd in de deelstaat Borno. De aanslagen en de ontvoeringen gaan maar door en nemen in intensiteit alleen maar toe.

Onze resolutie spreekt duidelijke taal. Wij roepen Nigeria op het probleem onder ogen te zien, de bevolking veel beter te beschermen en de daders te straffen.

Maar de vraag is ook vandaag: wat kunnen wij doen om het geweld in Nigeria te helpen stoppen? Welke mogelijkheden ziet u, commissaris? Ziet u bijvoorbeeld mogelijkheden om Nigeria te helpen bij het trainen van politiemensen? Natuurlijk is Nigeria primair zelf verantwoordelijk, maar als we kijken naar de escalatie van het geweld in de regio, mogen wij niet werkeloos toezien.
3-0436-0000.englishText:
Once again things went horribly wrong in Nigeria. Now in the village of Kawel, where dozens of Christians were killed in an attack by extremists. But I also think of the dozens of students who were recently kidnapped in Borno state. The attacks and kidnappings continue and are only increasing in intensity.

Our resolution speaks plainly. We call on Nigeria to face the problem, to protect the population much better and to punish the perpetrators.

But the question is also today: what can we do to help stop violence in Nigeria? What possibilities do you see, Commissioner? For example, do you see opportunities to help Nigeria train police officers? Of course, Nigeria itself is primarily responsible, but when we look at the escalation of violence in the region, we cannot stand idly by.

3-0438-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Am 22. Juni verüben bewaffnete Milizionäre im Dorf Kawel im nigerianischen Bundesstaat Plateau ein Massaker. Mindestens 22 unschuldige Menschen wurden in dieser christlichen Gemeinde, die nicht geschützt wurde, getötet.

Angriffe auf christliche Dorfgemeinschaften, auf Bäuerinnen und Bauern, auf Geistliche, Schulen und Gesundheitseinrichtungen nehmen zu, ebenso die Entführungen; Frauen und Mädchen sind massiv betroffen. Die katholische Bischofskonferenz Nigerias bekräftigt, dass Christen genauso wie Muslime Opfer des anhaltenden Terrorismus sind.

Gezielte Gewalt gegen Zivilisten wurzelt in Konflikten um politische Macht, Landstreitigkeiten, ethnische Zugehörigkeit, Sektenzugehörigkeit und Bandenkriminalität. Wir erwarten von den nigerianischen Behörden entschlossenes Handeln: eine umfassende Untersuchung des Massakers von Kawel, strafrechtliche Verfolgung der Täter und wirksamen Schutz gefährdeter Gemeinden und der Zivilbevölkerung sowie die entschiedene Bekämpfung bewaffneter Gruppen.

Wo Menschen aufgrund ihres Glaubens verfolgt werden, greift das die Religionsfreiheit an, und das ist ein fundamentales Menschenrecht, das wir schützen müssen.
3-0438-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! On June 22, armed militiamen carried out a massacre in the village of Kawel, Plateau State, Nigeria. At least 22 innocent people were killed in this unprotected Christian community.

Attacks on Christian village communities, farmers, clergy, schools and health facilities are increasing, as are kidnappings; Women and girls are massively affected. The Catholic Bishops' Conference of Nigeria reiterates that Christians, like Muslims, are victims of ongoing terrorism.

Targeted violence against civilians is rooted in conflicts over political power, land disputes, ethnicity, sect affiliation and gang violence. We expect decisive action from the Nigerian authorities: a comprehensive investigation into the Kawel massacre, prosecution of the perpetrators and effective protection of vulnerable communities and civilians, as well as the decisive fight against armed groups.

Where people are persecuted because of their faith, it attacks religious freedom, and that is a fundamental human right that we must protect.

3-0439-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, silenzio, il mondo tace mentre in Nigeria si consuma una strage: decine e decine di cristiani massacrati ancora, ogni settimana, nell'indifferenza generale.

Solo nel 2025 si parla di 3 500 cristiani uccisi da mani islamiste. Non sono numeri: sono famiglie intere sterminate, villaggi rasi al suolo, chiese bruciate con i fedeli dentro.

È una strategia precisa: terrorizzare, confiscare le loro terre, sradicare un'intera comunità. Non è più un'emergenza umanitaria, ormai le caratteristiche sono quelle di un genocidio.

I cristiani sono oggi il gruppo religioso più perseguitato al mondo, ma continuate a girarvi dall'altra parte o a parlare di un'inesistente islamofobia. L'Europa non riconosce né contrasta questa persecuzione islamista.

Non possiamo più aspettare. Ogni giorno di silenzio è complice di chi ammazza i cristiani.
3-0439-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, silence, the world is silent while a massacre takes place in Nigeria: dozens and dozens of Christians massacred again, every week, amid general indifference.

In 2025 alone, there is talk of 3,500 Christians killed by Islamist hands. They are not numbers: they are entire families exterminated, villages razed to the ground, churches burned with the faithful inside.

It is a precise strategy: terrorize, confiscate their lands, eradicate an entire community. It is no longer a humanitarian emergency, the characteristics are now those of a genocide.

Christians are the most persecuted religious group in the world today, but you continue to look the other way or talk about non-existent Islamophobia. L'Europa non riconosce né contrasta questa persecuzione islamista.

Non possiamo più aspettare. Every day of silence is an accomplice to those who kill Christians.

3-0440-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Weltweit werden rund 400 Millionen Christen verfolgt; Christen sind damit die am stärksten verfolgte Glaubensgemeinschaft weltweit. Besonders brutal ist diese Verfolgung in Nigeria; nirgendwo auf der Welt werden mehr Christen ermordet als dort – ermordet aus einem Grund: weil sie Christen sind. So geschehen auch vor zwei Wochen: Fulani-Milizen ermordeten mindestens 23 Christen im Dorf Kawel, darunter einen Pastor. Der US-Gesandte bei der UN, Mike Waltz, sagt, das ist keine zufällige Gewalt, das ist ein Genozid, ein Genozid an Christen.

All diese Fakten sind seit Langem bekannt, doch in Europa spricht man kaum darüber. Warum? Vielleicht, weil die Opfer Christen und die Täter Islamisten sind. Wir aber sollten die Täter beim Namen nennen: Boko Haram, der westafrikanische Ableger des „Islamischen Staates“, Fulani-Milizen – kurzum islamistische Terroristen. Sie morden, entführen, vergewaltigen, foltern.

Wir können das nicht länger hinnehmen; wir müssen Druck ausüben. Nigeria muss seine Christen schützen; Nigeria muss den islamistischen Terror bekämpfen. Dafür muss Nigeria seine Institutionen stärken – Polizei, Justiz, Sicherheitsapparat. Falls nicht, darf kein Cent mehr von uns nach Nigeria fließen.
3-0440-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner! Around 400 million Christians are persecuted worldwide; Christians are therefore the most persecuted religious community in the world. This persecution is particularly brutal in Nigeria; Nowhere in the world are more Christians murdered than there – murdered for one reason: because they are Christians. This is what happened two weeks ago: Fulani militias murdered at least 23 Christians in Kawel village, including a pastor. The US envoy to the UN, Mike Waltz, says this is not random violence, this is a genocide, a genocide against Christians.

All of these facts have been known for a long time, but they are rarely talked about in Europe. Why? Maybe because the victims are Christians and the perpetrators are Islamists. But we should name the perpetrators: Boko Haram, the West African branch of the “Islamic State”, Fulani militias – in short, Islamist terrorists. They murder, kidnap, rape, torture.

We can no longer accept this; we have to apply pressure. Nigeria must protect its Christians; Nigeria must fight Islamist terrorism. To achieve this, Nigeria must strengthen its institutions – police, judiciary, security apparatus. If not, not a single cent will be allowed to flow from us to Nigeria.

3-0441-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, no puede ser que la matanza de cristianos por motivos religiosos no nos despierte la misma indignación que nos provocan otras matanzas y persecuciones en el mundo.

Les doy unos datos: según datos de Open Doors, 388 millones de cristianos están perseguidos en el mundo y el año pasado hubo 4 849 asesinados. Especialmente grave es el caso de Nigeria, donde se da el 72 % de estos asesinatos, la mayoría ejecutados por grupos terroristas islamistas. No podemos caer en la trampa de pensar que aquí lo que está ocurriendo son guerras entre clanes por recursos naturales. Está habiendo una persecución real de cristianos y Europa no puede permanecer callada.

Desde la Unión Europea debemos tomar medidas, debemos endurecer nuestro régimen de sanciones así como la condicionalidad y el control de nuestras ayudas a terceros países para evitar financiar aquellos Estados, como el de Nigeria, que de una manera activa o pasiva permiten esta violencia contra los cristianos y este atentado contra los derechos humanos.
3-0441-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Madam Commissioner, it cannot be that the massacre of Christians for religious reasons does not arouse in us the same indignation that other massacres and persecutions in the world provoke in us.

I'll give you some data: according to data from Open Doors, 388 million Christians are persecuted in the world and last year there were 4,849 murdered. The case of Nigeria is especially serious, where 72% of these murders occur, the majority carried out by Islamist terrorist groups. We cannot fall into the trap of thinking that what is happening here are wars between clans over natural resources. There is a real persecution of Christians and Europe cannot remain silent.

From the European Union we must take measures, we must toughen our sanctions regime as well as the conditionality and control of our aid to third countries to avoid financing those States, such as Nigeria, that actively or passively allow this violence against Christians and this attack on human rights.

3-0442-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, parler de la situation au Nigeria dans cet hémicycle permet de mettre en lumière les persécutions et violences quotidiennes auxquelles doivent faire face les civils. Réduire le débat à la religion est cependant la preuve que beaucoup ici n’ont pas compris ce qui se passe dans ce pays, ou alors qu’ils ne veulent pas le comprendre. Ou simplement ils se servent de ces atrocités pour servir leur agenda politique.

Comment ne pas voir que les victimes des massacres ont un seul point commun: non pas leur religion, mais le fait d’être civil? Comment ne pas voir l’influence du changement climatique, de la pression démographique, de la raréfaction des terres dans ces conflits?

Il est de notre devoir d’élus de faire preuve d’honnêteté intellectuelle afin d’apporter un réel soutien à la population nigériane, sans quoi nous continuerons à compter les morts.
3-0442-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, talking about the situation in Nigeria in this Chamber helps to highlight the daily persecution and violence that civilians have to face. Reducing the debate to religion, however, is proof that many here have not understood what is happening in this country, or that they do not want to understand it. Or they simply use these atrocities to serve their political agenda.

How can we not see that the victims of the massacres have only one thing in common: not their religion, but the fact of being civil? How can we not see the influence of climate change, demographic pressure and land scarcity in these conflicts?

It is our duty as elected officials to demonstrate intellectual honesty in order to provide real support to the Nigerian population, otherwise we will continue to count the dead.

3-0443-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, quando denunciou a perseguição e o suplício de Jean Calas, Voltaire não estava apenas a fazer a defesa de um homem injustamente condenado: estava a lembrar a toda a Europa que toda a intolerância praticada em nome de Deus é, sempre, um pacto com o Diabo.

A intolerância desumaniza, simultaneamente, a sua vítima e o seu autor. Dessa denúncia nasceu um tratado sobre a tolerância que permanece uma das magnas cartas da Europa.

Por isso, quando me chegam relatos de comunidades cristãs ameaçadas na Nigéria, no Sudão, em Moçambique ou um pouco por todo o Médio Oriente, ouvimos mais do que notícias distantes. Reconhecemos os nossos demónios.

A Europa tem uma responsabilidade especial de proteger as comunidades cristãs, onde quer que elas sejam perseguidas, porque em cada Jean Calas silenciado - na Europa de ontem, ou na África e no Médio Oriente de hoje - ouvimos, de novo, a voz de Voltaire.
3-0443-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, when he denounced the persecution and torture of Jean Calas, Voltaire was not just defending a man unjustly condemned: he was reminding the whole of Europe that all intolerance practiced in the name of God is always a pact with the Devil.

Intolerance simultaneously dehumanizes its victim and its perpetrator. From this denunciation was born a treatise on tolerance that remains one of Europe's great charters.

Therefore, when reports come to me of threatened Christian communities in Nigeria, Sudan, Mozambique or throughout the Middle East, we hear more than distant news. We recognize our demons.

Europe has a special responsibility to protect Christian communities, wherever they are persecuted, because in every silenced Jean Calas - in Europe yesterday, or in Africa and the Middle East today - we hear, again, the voice of Voltaire.

3-0444-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! W czerwcu 2026 r. w wiosce Kawel w stanie Plateau w Nigerii doszło do brutalnego ataku na chrześcijańską społeczność. Dziesiątki osób zginęły, wiele zostało rannych, a cała wioska została zniszczona. To nie jest pojedynczy incydent, lecz element szerszego, powtarzającego się wzoru prześladowanych chrześcijan w regionie, ataków na rolników, kościoły, szkoły, duchownych. I mimo wielokrotnych ostrzeżeń władze nigeryjskie nie zapewniły ochrony, a sprawcy nadal cieszą się bezkarnością.

Potępiamy tę zbrodnię z całą stanowczością. Wyrażamy głębokie współczucie rodzinom ofiar. Wzywamy rząd Nigerii do natychmiastowego, transparentnego śledztwa, ukarania winnych i przerwania kultury bezkarności. Apelujemy o realne wzmocnienie ochrony ludności chrześcijańskiej i podjęcie konkretnych działań przeciwko fali przemocy.

Niestety, reakcja Unii Europejskiej pozostaje dalece niewystarczająca. Oficjalna linia Unii Europejskiej, w tym wypowiedzi wysokiej przedstawiciel Kai Kallas, unika jasnego określenia tych wydarzeń mianem prześladowania chrześcijan. Zamiast tego skupia się na złożonych czynnikach, konfliktach o ziemię między rolnikami a hodowcami, zmianami klimatu, działalności bandytów i terrorystów. Jednocześnie Unia z niezwykłą czujnością doszukuje się przejawów islamofobii w Europie, nawet tam, gdzie chodzi o uzasadnioną krytykę radykalnego islamu.

To wyraźny przejaw odchodzenia europejskich elit od chrześcijańskich korzeni Europy. Unia powstała w oparciu o chrześcijańskie wartości, godność osoby ludzkiej, sprawiedliwość, solidarność. Fundamenty Europy są chrześcijańskie. Nie możemy więc pozostawać obojętni na cierpienie milionów chrześcijan na świecie, od lat najbardziej prześladowanej grupy religijnej.

Takie selektywne podejście źle wróży przyszłości Europy. Osłabia naszą spójność kulturową. Ignoruje realia demograficzne i pozbawia nas zdolności do skutecznego przeciwstawienia się radykalnemu islamowi. Czas, by Europa wróciła do swoich korzeni, nie tylko słowami, ale także czynami.
3-0444-0000.englishText:
Mr President! In June 2026, a brutal attack on a Christian community took place in the village of Kawel in Plateau State, Nigeria. Dozens of people died, many were injured, and the entire village was destroyed. This is not a single incident, but part of a broader, recurring pattern of persecuted Christians in the region, attacks on farmers, churches, schools and clergy. And despite repeated warnings, the Nigerian authorities failed to provide protection, and the perpetrators continue to enjoy impunity.

We condemn this crime in the strongest possible terms. We express our deep sympathy to the families of the victims. We call on the Nigerian government to conduct an immediate, transparent investigation, punish those responsible and end the culture of impunity. We appeal for a real strengthening of the protection of the Christian population and for taking concrete actions against the wave of violence.

Unfortunately, the European Union's response remains far from sufficient. The official line of the European Union, including the statements of High Representative Kai Kallas, avoids clearly defining these events as persecution of Christians. Zamiast tego skupia się na złożonych czynnikach, konfliktach o ziemię między rolnikami a hodowcami, zmianami klimatu, działalności bandytów i terrorystów. At the same time, the EU is extremely vigilant in looking for manifestations of Islamophobia in Europe, even where it involves justified criticism of radical Islam.

This is a clear manifestation of the departure of European elites from the Christian roots of Europe. The Union was founded on Christian values, human dignity, justice and solidarity. The foundations of Europe are Christian. Therefore, we cannot remain indifferent to the suffering of millions of Christians around the world, the most persecuted religious group for years.

This selective approach bodes ill for Europe's future. It weakens our cultural cohesion. It ignores demographic realities and deprives us of our ability to effectively oppose radical Islam. It is time for Europe to return to its roots, not only in words but also in deeds.

3-0445-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Nigeria zajmuje siódme miejsce w światowym rankingu prześladowań chrześcijan Open Doors, a jednocześnie pozostaje krajem, w którym ginie ich najwięcej na świecie. Według raportu European Center for Law and Justice tylko w pierwszych 220 dniach w 2025 roku zamordowano ponad 7000 chrześcijan, a między styczniem a kwietniem tego roku kolejnych 1400. A my od lat słyszymy o konfliktach o ziemię. Ale jak konfliktem o ziemię wytłumaczyć palenie kościołów, ataki na chrześcijańskie wsie, mordowanie wiernych podczas nabożeństw czy okrzyki wzywające Allaha podczas masakr? Trzeba to powiedzieć jasno, że za tymi zbrodniami stoją ugrupowania islamistyczne. Dodatkowo w dwunastu północnych stanach Nigerii obowiązuje szariat, a wpływy radykalnych środowisk islamskich stale rosną.

Obecny prezydent, jak i wiceprezydent są muzułmanami, co łamie obowiązującą od lat zasadę, zgodnie z którą chrześcijanin i muzułmanin są zrównoważeni na najwyższych stanowiskach państwowych. A tymczasem Unia Europejska nadal pogłębia strategiczne partnerstwo z Nigerią w obszarze bezpieczeństwa, migracji, energii i rozwoju gospodarczego. Przeznaczyła ponad 700 milionów euro grantów na lata 2021–27 dla Nigerii, w której łamane są prawa człowieka.

Musimy upomnieć się o chrześcijan, gdziekolwiek oni żyją, gdziekolwiek mieszkają, dlatego, że Europa będzie chrześcijańska albo nie będzie jej wcale.
3-0445-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Nigeria ranks seventh in the Open Doors global ranking of persecution of Christians, and at the same time remains the country where the most Christians are killed in the world. According to a report by the European Center for Law and Justice, over 7,000 Christians were murdered in the first 220 days of 2025 alone, and another 1,400 between January and April this year. And we have been hearing about land conflicts for years. But how can the burning of churches, attacks on Christian villages, murders of believers during services or shouts invoking Allah during massacres be explained by the conflict over land? It must be said clearly that Islamist groups are behind these crimes. Additionally, sharia is in force in twelve northern states of Nigeria, and the influence of radical Islamic circles is constantly growing.

The current president and vice president are Muslims, which violates the long-standing rule according to which Christians and Muslims are balanced in the highest state positions. Meanwhile, the European Union continues to deepen its strategic partnership with Nigeria in the areas of security, migration, energy and economic development. It has allocated over €700 million in grants for 2021-27 to Nigeria, where human rights are violated.

We must stand up for Christians, wherever they live, wherever they live, because Europe will be Christian or it will not be Christian at all.

3-0446-0000.sourceText: Gerbiamas Pirmininke, komisare, kolegos. Žudynės, įvykdytos Nigerijoje, Kawel kaime, sukrėtė ne tik vietos bendruomenes, bet ir visą civilizuotą pasaulį. Ginkluotos islamistų grupuotės jau ne vienerius metus terorizuoja Nigerijos kaimus ir bendruomenes. Bendrai Afrika šiandien išlieka smurto prieš krikščionis epicentru, o Nigerijoje matome ne pavienius nusikaltimus, bet pasikartojančius, koordinuotus išpuolius net prieš dvasininkus ir bažnyčias. Tai sąmoningai toleruojamas smurtas ir valstybės pareigos ignoravimas, kurio nebeįmanoma paslėpti už atsargių diplomatinių formuluočių. Nigerijos valdžia privalo ginti savo piliečius, tirti nusikaltimus ir bausti vykdytojus. Europos Sąjunga privalo kalbėti griežtai: remti aukas, spausti valdžią ir taikyti priemones tiems, kurie kursto ir finansuoja ar dangsto šį terorą. Tikėjimo laisvė yra pamatinė žmogaus teisė ir ji turi būti ginama ne rytoj, o dabar ir be išlygų.
3-0446-0000.englishText: Dear President, Commissioner, colleagues. Žudynės, įvykdytos Nigerijoje, Kawel kaime, sukrėtė ne tik vietos bendruomenes, bet ir visą civilizuotą pasaulį. Armed Islamist groups have been terrorizing villages and communities in Nigeria for years. In general, Africa today remains the epicenter of violence against Christians, and in Nigeria we see not isolated crimes, but repeated, coordinated attacks, even against clergy and churches. This is a deliberate tolerance of violence and a disregard for the duty of the state, which can no longer be hidden behind careful diplomatic wording. The Nigerian government has a duty to protect its citizens, investigate crimes and punish the perpetrators. The European Union must speak tough: support the victims, pressure the authorities and apply measures to those who incite and finance or cover up this terror. Freedom of belief is a fundamental human right and must be protected not tomorrow, but now and without reservations.

3-0447-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, quello che sta accadendo in Nigeria non può essere liquidato come un semplice conflitto tribale: è una persecuzione folle contro i cristiani.

E i numeri sono terribili: 3 490 cristiani uccisi in un anno per motivi legati alla fede, significa che quasi tre cristiani su quattro uccisi nel mondo sono stati uccisi in Nigeria. Villaggi distrutti, chiese attaccate, famiglie massacrate, fedeli rapiti: ma dov'è l'indignazione in Europa?

Guardate questa parte dell'Aula, quella a sinistra, è vuota. Non c'è un parlamentare di sinistra che oggi si scaglia contro il massacro dei cristiani. Volevo vedere se era stato ucciso un musulmano: erano tutti qua, era tutto pieno, era tutta piena l'Aula, a sinistra, a dire "islamofobia".

In quest'Aula si sente parlare soltanto di islamofobia. E di cristianofobia, qualcuno vuole cominciare a parlarne? Qualcuno vuole cominciare a difendere i cristiani nel mondo?

Ecco, l'Unione europea deve condizionare aiuti e cooperazione alla protezione delle comunità cristiane e pretendere dal governo nigeriano sicurezza e giustizia.

(L'oratrice accetta di rispondere a una domanda "cartellino blu")
3-0447-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, what is happening in Nigeria cannot be dismissed as a simple tribal conflict: it is a mad persecution against Christians.

And the numbers are terrible: 3,490 Christians killed in one year for reasons related to faith, meaning that almost three out of four Christians killed in the world were killed in Nigeria. Villages destroyed, churches attacked, families massacred, faithful kidnapped: but where is the indignation in Europe?

Look at this part of the Chamber, the one on the left, it is empty. There is not a left-wing parliamentarian who today rails against the massacre of Christians. I wanted to see if a Muslim had been killed: they were all here, it was all full, the Chamber was full, on the left, saying "Islamophobia".

In this House we only hear about Islamophobia. And about Christianophobia, does anyone want to start talking about it? Does anyone want to start defending Christians around the world?

Here, the European Union must condition aid and cooperation on the protection of Christian communities and demand security and justice from the Nigerian government.

(The speaker agrees to answer a "blue card" question)

3-0449-0000.sourceText:
Guardi, La ringrazio perché è l'unico rappresentante di sinistra oggi in quest'Aula a seguire il dibattito – ah, no, siete due, scusate mi scuso tantissimo – due rappresentanti della sinistra a seguire questo dibattito e quindi questo vi fa molto onore. Ma Lei crede che questo sia sufficiente?

Cioè, io credo che ormai la cristianofobia non è più soltanto in Nigeria, cari miei. La cristianofobia si sta spargendo a macchia d'olio anche in Europa, perché è difficile oggi andare in giro in Europa con una croce al collo, in certi quartieri, a Bruxelles, a Strasburgo, a Parigi e a Roma. Pensiamo a questo.
3-0449-0000.englishText:
Look, I thank you because you are the only representative of the left in this Chamber today to follow the debate – ah, no, there are two of you, sorry, I apologize very much – two representatives of the left to follow this debate and therefore this does you a great honor. Ma Lei crede che questo sia sufficiente?

That is, I believe that Christianophobia is no longer just in Nigeria, my dears. Christianophobia is spreading like wildfire in Europe too, because it is difficult today to go around Europe with a cross around your neck, in certain neighborhoods, in Brussels, in Strasbourg, in Paris and in Rome. Let's think about this.

3-0450-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, a Kawel, in Nigeria, decine di cristiani sono stati massacrati.

Ancora. Ancora una volta, donne e uomini, famiglie intere, uccisi soltanto perché cristiani. E Open Doors ci dice che negli ultimi due anni 5 000 cristiani sono stati uccisi.

Dal cuore dell'Europa abbiamo il dovere di non tacere, ma non basta, non basta parlare, non basta denunciare, non basta dare il nostro cordoglio: dobbiamo agire.

Dobbiamo cominciare, perché l'Unione europea deve dimostrare che noi sappiamo utilizzare gli strumenti diplomatici e di cooperazione per pretendere che le comunità cristiane vengano difese, che i responsabili vengano perseguiti e che avvenga davvero lo smantellamento delle reti terroristiche.

Basta, quindi, esportare ideologia progressista in Africa. Dobbiamo invece legare i nostri accordi di partenariato e commerciali al rispetto della libertà religiosa.

Difendere i cristiani, infatti – i nostri fratelli – significa difendere la pace, la civiltà e anche difendere noi stessi, proprio laddove c'è più necessità.
3-0450-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, in Kawel, Nigeria, dozens of Christians were massacred.

Still. Once again, women and men, entire families, killed just because they were Christians. And Open Doors tells us that 5,000 Christians have been killed in the last two years.

From the heart of Europe we have the duty not to remain silent, but it is not enough, it is not enough to speak, it is not enough to denounce, it is not enough to give our condolences: we must act.

We must start, because the European Union must demonstrate that we know how to use diplomatic and cooperation tools to demand that Christian communities are defended, that those responsible are prosecuted and that the dismantling of terrorist networks actually takes place.

It is therefore enough to export progressive ideology to Africa. Instead, we must link our partnership and trade agreements to respect for religious freedom.

Defending Christians, in fact - our brothers - means defending peace, civilization and also defending ourselves, precisely where there is most need.

3-0452-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, πριν δύο εβδομάδες, στις 22 Ιουνίου, εισέβαλαν στο χωριό Kawel της Νιγηρίας ένοπλοι και εκτέλεσαν τουλάχιστον 20 χριστιανούς αμάχους. Ανάμεσά τους ο πάστορας Markus Nyam και μια έγκυος γυναίκα. Δυστυχώς, αυτό δεν είναι μεμονωμένο περιστατικό· είναι μοτίβο. Σύμφωνα με το πρόγραμμα Open Doors, η Νιγηρία καταγράφει τους περισσότερους δολοφονημένους για την πίστη τους χριστιανούς από κάθε άλλη χώρα στον πλανήτη. Είναι θλιβερό. Επανερχόμαστε ξανά και ξανά θέτοντας το ζήτημα της προστασίας των χριστιανικών πληθυσμών, αλλά η ευρωπαϊκή και η παγκόσμια κοινότητα κάνει πως δεν ακούει. Μένουμε απλοί παρατηρητές στα εγκλήματα που συντελούνται από μουσουλμάνους μετανάστες εναντίον γηγενών Ευρωπαίων μέσα στο σπίτι μας, σε χώρες της Ευρώπης, και κλείνουμε τα μάτια μας. Περιμένουμε απλά την καταστροφική εξέλιξη αυτών των γεγονότων.

Πρέπει να ξυπνήσουμε άμεσα. Εδώ, στο Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο, πρέπει να θέσουμε την προστασία αυτών των κοινοτήτων ως άμεση προτεραιότητα, με κυρώσεις και πίεση προς την Νιγηρία αλλά και προς όλες τις χώρες όπου διώκονται και δολοφονούνται συστηματικά χριστιανοί. Η Ευρώπη οφείλει να δράσει τώρα. Πρέπει να προστατεύσει τους γηγενείς πληθυσμούς της από την ανεξέλεγκτη μετανάστευση και την εξάπλωση του ισλαμιστικού εξτρεμισμού.
3-0452-0000.englishText:
Madam President, two weeks ago, on June 22, armed men invaded the village of Kawel in Nigeria and executed at least 20 Christian civilians. Among them Pastor Markus Nyam and a pregnant woman. Unfortunately, this is not an isolated incident; it is a pattern. According to the Open Doors program, Nigeria records the most Christians murdered for their faith than any other country on the planet. It's sad. We come back again and again raising the issue of the protection of Christian populations, but the European and world community pretends not to listen. We remain mere observers to the crimes committed by Muslim immigrants against native Europeans at home in European countries and close our eyes. We are simply waiting for the catastrophic development of these events.

We must wake up immediately. Here in the European Parliament, we must make the protection of these communities an immediate priority, with sanctions and pressure on Nigeria but also on all countries where Christians are systematically persecuted and murdered. Europe must act now. It must protect its native populations from uncontrolled immigration and the spread of Islamist extremism.

3-0453-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Ez most a harmadik alkalom, hogy ebben a ciklusban a nigériai keresztényüldözés kérdésével foglalkozunk. Sajnálatos, hogy dacára ennek, a Bizottság – és itt azért többen is – mindent elkövet, hogy a keresztényekkel szembeni támadásokat kizárólag etnikai konfliktusként próbálja beállítani. A keresztényüldözés tényének elismerésétől a von der Leyen–bizottság úgy tart, mint ördög a szenteltvíztől. Holott óvatos becslések szerint 2024 óta – hölgyeim és uraim, tisztelt képviselőtársaim – tízezer keresztény ember veszítette életét pusztán a hite miatt Nigériában.

A karácsonyra, húsvétra, pünkösdre időzített, templomok elleni támadásokat nem lehet félremagyarázni. Hány halott kell még ahhoz, hogy a keresztényüldözést ne akarják relativizálni? Hány halott kell még, hogy végre megfelelő forrásokat tegyenek az üldözött keresztények védelméért és a közösségek támogatásáért? És kérdés: mit tesz a Bizottság, a külügyi szolgálat a keresztények elleni erőszak megelőzéséhez? Nagyon megtisztelő lenne, ha végre érdemi választ kapnánk.
3-0453-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President! This is the third time in this cycle that we have addressed the issue of Christian persecution in Nigeria. It is unfortunate that, despite this, the Commission - and several others here - are doing everything they can to frame the attacks against Christians as an ethnic conflict. The von der Leyen committee is as afraid of acknowledging the fact of Christian persecution as the devil is of holy water. Although, according to conservative estimates, since 2024, ladies and gentlemen, dear fellow representatives, ten thousand Christians have lost their lives simply because of their faith in Nigeria.

Attacks on churches timed for Christmas, Easter, and Pentecost cannot be misinterpreted. How many more dead are needed so that they don't want to relativize the persecution of Christians? How many more dead are needed to finally make adequate resources for the protection of persecuted Christians and the support of communities? And a question: what does the Commission, the Foreign Service, do to prevent violence against Christians? It would be a great honor if we finally got a meaningful answer.

3-0454-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, kršćani su najprogonjenija vjerska skupina na svijetu.

Mediji ignoriraju tu činjenicu, ova plenarna dvorana je prazna. Danas stojimo pred užasnim masakrom u selu Kawel u Nigeriji, gdje su militanti 22. lipnja upali u to selo i ubili desetke nedužnih ljudi, svećenike, žene i djecu. Dok osuđujemo ovaj masakr kršćanske vrijednosti, kršćanstvo kao temelj europske civilizacije je na udaru. Dok ne progovorimo o tome, dok ne prestanu antikršćanski napadi, vandalizmi, vandalizam na crkvama, gotovo svaki tjedan nova crkva je u plamenu, stvari neće se promijeniti.

Moramo jasno i glasno progovoriti u ime ne samo nedužnih ljudi u svijetu koji trpe, nego kršćana u samoj Europi koji postaju danas meta raznoraznih skupina i napada.

(Govornik je pristao odgovoriti na pitanje postavljeno podizanjem plave kartice.)
3-0454-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairperson, colleagues, Christians are the most persecuted religious group in the world.

The media ignores this fact, this plenary hall is empty. Today, we are facing a terrible massacre in the village of Kawel in Nigeria, where militants invaded the village on June 22 and killed dozens of innocent people, priests, women and children. While we condemn this massacre of Christian values, Christianity as the foundation of European civilization is under attack. Until we talk about it, until the anti-Christian attacks, the vandalism, the vandalism of the churches, almost every week a new church is on fire, things will not change.

We must speak clearly and loudly on behalf of not only the innocent people in the world who are suffering, but Christians in Europe itself who are today becoming the target of various groups and attacks.

(The speaker agreed to answer the question posed by holding up the blue card.)

3-0455-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, postoje jasni podaci da su kršćani najprogonjenija vjerska zajednica na svijetu.

I što mislite zašto je nekima ovdje u Europskom parlamentu i Europi općenito tako teško priznati tu činjenicu?
3-0455-0000.englishText:
Honorable Chairperson, there is clear data that Christians are the most persecuted religious community in the world.

And why do you think it is so difficult for some here in the European Parliament and in Europe in general to admit that fact?

3-0456-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, hvala na pitanju kolega Sokol.

Nažalost, radi se o jednom velikom licemjerju u Europi, dakle Europa danas zapravo se srami vlastitog identiteta. Imamo ljude koji dižu glas u ime ljudskih prava. Čak rekao bih, ponekad imam dojam da životinje uživaju veću zaštitu kod nekih ljudi u ovom Parlamentu nego nedužni ljudi.

Dakle, moramo raščistiti neke stvari. Nema Europe bez kršćanstva, ljudska prava sama kao koncept je nastao u okrilju kršćanske civilizacije. Dakle, trebamo se ponositi time. Zapadna civilizacija je nešto čime se trebamo ponositi, a ne sramiti.

Nažalost, Europa je to izgubila iz vida. I dok se to ne promijeni, bojim se da ćemo ići dalje krivim smjerom.
3-0456-0000.englishText:
Dear Chairperson, thank you for your question, colleague Sokol.

Unfortunately, this is a big hypocrisy in Europe, so Europe today is actually ashamed of its own identity. We have people who raise their voices in the name of human rights. I would even say, sometimes I have the impression that animals enjoy more protection from some people in this Parliament than innocent people.

So we need to clear some things up. There is no Europe without Christianity, human rights itself as a concept was created under the auspices of Christian civilization. So we should be proud of that. Western civilization is something we should be proud of, not ashamed of.

Unfortunately, Europe has lost sight of this. And until that changes, I'm afraid we'll keep going in the wrong direction.

3-0458-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Jag kan stå här och säga att jag är kristen utan rädsla för att jag ska bli mördad eller att min familj ska utsättas för våld. Hade jag levt i Nigeria hade inte det här varit fallet.

Nigeria är ett av världens farligaste länder för kristna. Kyrkor bränns, familjer mördas och kvinnor och barn utsätts för sexuellt våld. När Mellanösternkonflikten dominerar nyhetssändningarna fylls våra gator med protester, men när kristna slaktas är tystnaden öronbedövande. Var är de blåhåriga feministerna? Var är människorättsorganisationerna? Var är Svenska kyrkan?

Hyckleriet om mänskliga rättigheter har nått en ny bottennivå. Antingen gäller mänskliga rättigheter alla eller så är det bara tomma ord. EU måste sluta blunda för att kristna är världens mest förföljda religiösa grupp.
3-0458-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker! I can stand here and say I am a Christian without fear that I will be murdered or that my family will be subjected to violence. Had I lived in Nigeria this would not have been the case.

Nigeria is one of the world's most dangerous countries for Christians. Churches are burned, families are murdered and women and children are subjected to sexual violence. When the Middle East conflict dominates the news, our streets are filled with protests, but when Christians are being slaughtered, the silence is deafening. Where are the blue-haired feminists? Where are the human rights organizations? Where is the Church of Sweden?

The hypocrisy of human rights has reached a new low. Either human rights apply to everyone or they are just empty words. The EU must stop turning a blind eye to the fact that Christians are the world's most persecuted religious group.

3-0459-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, nada deja más desprotegidos a nuestros hermanos cristianos que un Parlamento que se niega a llamar a las cosas por su nombre.

El 22 de junio, hombres armados irrumpieron de madrugada en la aldea cristiana de Kabul, dispararon contra los vecinos, quemaron sus casas, asesinaron a más de veinte personas, entre ellas a su párroco. Esto no es un conflicto tribal. Tampoco por la escasez de recursos como se trata de justificar hoy aquí. Es una persecución contra los cristianos por su fe, porque no es un caso aislado.

¿Cuántas iglesias tienen que arder? ¿Cuántos sacerdotes tienen que ser secuestrados? ¿Cuántas comunidades cristianas tienen que desaparecer para que esta Cámara reconozca la verdad?

Es incomprensible que decir esto sea un problema para una parte del Parlamento. Es incomprensible que algunos Grupos sigan negando el componente religioso de los ataques del terrorismo islámico. La acción internacional debe ser mucho más contundente. La Unión Europea no puede mirar hacia otro lado ni mucho menos criticar a quienes tienen la valentía de actuar, porque la verdad no se puede ocultar.

Se está cometiendo genocidio contra los cristianos.
3-0459-0000.englishText:
Madam President, nothing leaves our Christian brothers more unprotected than a Parliament that refuses to call a spade a spade.

On June 22, armed men broke into the Christian village of Kabul at dawn, shot at the neighbors, burned their houses, and murdered more than twenty people, including their parish priest. This is not a tribal conflict. Nor because of the scarcity of resources as they try to justify here today. It is a persecution against Christians for their faith, because it is not an isolated case.

How many churches have to burn? How many priests have to be kidnapped? How many Christian communities have to disappear before this House recognizes the truth?

It is incomprehensible that saying this is a problem for part of Parliament. It is incomprehensible that some Groups continue to deny the religious component of Islamic terrorist attacks. International action must be much more forceful. The European Union cannot look the other way, much less criticize those who have the courage to act, because the truth cannot be hidden.

Genocide is being committed against Christians.

3-0461-0000.sourceText: Mnie dziwi jedna rzecz: że jak się patrzy na lewą stronę, to jest zupełnie pusta. Ale ci, którzy przemawiali, twierdzą, że to jest taki konflikt symetryczny, że chrześcijanie i muzułmanie walczą i że to są jakby te same siły, które walczą, jakby był to symetryczny konflikt. Jak więc może pan wytłumaczyć, że w stosunku do populacji zostało zamordowanych prawie pięć razy tyle chrześcijan co muzułmanów?
3-0461-0000.englishText: One thing surprises me: when you look at the left side, it is completely empty. But those who spoke say that it is such a symmetrical conflict, that Christians and Muslims are fighting and that it is like the same forces that are fighting, as if it was a symmetrical conflict. So how can you explain that, relative to the population, almost five times as many Christians as Muslims were murdered?

(Renew), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Frau Präsidentin, kann ich trotzdem noch Catch-the-eye machen oder eines von beiden? Beides, okay.

3-0469-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, mes chers collègues, la persécution sanglante des chrétiens se propage en Afrique subsaharienne, et le Nigeria est particulièrement touché par ce drame. Ces deux dernières années, 3 490 chrétiens ont été tués – plus de 40 000 d’entre eux ont perdu la vie depuis le début de l’insurrection islamiste de Boko Haram en 2009.

Ces populations sont tuées, violées, déplacées et traitées dans des conditions atroces. Les églises sont incendiées, et les enlèvements massifs dans les écoles chrétiennes se multiplient. Les 13 et 14 juin encore, plus de 250 personnes ont été tuées par les milices islamistes. Un autre exemple de leur barbarie: Leah Sharibu, une jeune femme de 21 ans, est détenue depuis 2018 par un groupe islamiste car elle refuse d’abjurer sa foi chrétienne.

Le Nigeria est également touché par une grave crise humanitaire: des milliers de familles sont contraintes de fuir les violences; elles vivent dans des conditions indignes, privées d’aide humanitaire et de soins.

Pour ces familles et pour toutes les victimes de cette violence, notre devoir est clair: cesser les pudeurs diplomatiques, désigner les responsables, éradiquer les coupables de ces crimes, cibler et conditionner nos financements, soutenir les communautés menacées, porter haut et fort la voix des chrétiens persécutés.
3-0469-0000.englishText:
Madam President, my dear colleagues, the bloody persecution of Christians is spreading in sub-Saharan Africa, and Nigeria is particularly affected by this tragedy. In the past two years, 3,490 Christians have been killed – more than 40,000 of them have lost their lives since the Boko Haram Islamist insurgency began in 2009.

These populations are killed, raped, displaced and treated in atrocious conditions. Churches are being burned, and mass kidnappings from Christian schools are increasing. Again on June 13 and 14, more than 250 people were killed by Islamist militias. Another example of their barbarity: Leah Sharibu, a 21-year-old young woman, has been detained since 2018 by an Islamist group because she refuses to renounce her Christian faith.

Nigeria is also affected by a serious humanitarian crisis: thousands of families are forced to flee the violence; they live in undignified conditions, deprived of humanitarian aid and care.

For these families and for all the victims of this violence, our duty is clear: stop diplomatic modesty, name those responsible, eradicate those guilty of these crimes, target and condition our funding, support threatened communities, speak loudly and clearly the voice of persecuted Christians.
