3-0476-5000.sourceText:
Ponia Pirmininke,

Daugelyje pasaulio šalių vyksta masiniai krikščionių persekiojimai. Deja, vis dažniau pasirodo nerimą keliančių pranešimų apie krikščionių genocidą Nigerijoje ir Sudane.Nigerijos bažnyčia prašo pagalbos ir persekiojimo užbaigimo. Kaip Europos Parlamentas, atstovaujantis lotyniškajai civilizacijai, pagrįstai krikščioniškomis vertybėmis, negalime ignoruoti šio pagalbos šauksmo. Privalome pasitelkti visas įmanomas priemones, kad paveiktume Nigerijos valdžią ir kuo greičiau nutrauktume persekiojimą. Nigerijoje tikėjimas Kristumi kainuoja žmonių gyvybes. Deginami krikščionių kaimai, o vien per pastaruosius dvejus metus nužudytųjų skaičius viršijo 7000. Remiantis organizacijos „Open Doors“ duomenimis, per pastaruosius 16 metų Nigerijoje buvo nužudyta 125 000 krikščionių. Vietos bažnyčia perspėja, kad krikščionių padėtis, ypač centrinėje šalies dalyje, prilygsta genocidui. Didžiausi smurto židiniai yra šalies centrinėje dalyje, kur džihadistai žudo krikščionis. Dėl šios padėties kuriama daug pabėgėlių stovyklų, kuriose humanitarinė padėtis yra apgailėtina. Vien Maiduguri mieste yra daugiau nei 30 šalies viduje perkeltų asmenų stovyklų, kuriose gyvena šimtai tūkstančių perkeltųjų. Nigerijos krikščionių bendruomenė gali susidurti su egzistencine grėsme. Todėl būtina, kad tarptautinė bendruomenė nedelsdama imtųsi veiksmų ir padėtų persekiojamiesiems. Europos Sąjunga negali likti abejinga šiam klausimui.
3-0476-5000.englishText:
Madam President,

There are massive persecutions of Christians in many countries of the world. Unfortunately, disturbing reports about the genocide of Christians in Nigeria and Sudan are appearing more and more often. The Nigerian church is asking for help and an end to the persecution. As a European Parliament representing a Latin civilization based on Christian values, we cannot ignore this cry for help. We must use all means possible to influence the Nigerian authorities to end the persecution as soon as possible. Faith in Christ costs lives in Nigeria. Christian villages are being burned, and over 7,000 have been killed in the last two years alone. According to Open Doors, 125,000 Christians have been killed in Nigeria in the last 16 years. The local church warns that the situation of Christians, especially in the central part of the country, is tantamount to genocide. The biggest centers of violence are in the central part of the country, where jihadists are killing Christians. This situation has led to the creation of many refugee camps where the humanitarian situation is deplorable. There are more than 30 IDP camps in Maiduguri alone, housing hundreds of thousands of displaced people. The Christian community in Nigeria may be facing an existential threat. It is therefore imperative that the international community takes immediate action to help the persecuted. The European Union cannot remain indifferent to this issue.

3-0478-0000.sourceText: Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgt die Aussprache über sechs Entschließungsanträge zum Thema „Entführung, Zwangskonvertierung und Kinderehe von Maria Shahbaz und der Schutz von Mädchen in Pakistan” (2026/2801(RSP)).
3-0478-0000.englishText: The next item on the agenda is the debate on six motions for resolutions on “Abduction, forced conversion and child marriage of Maria Shahbaz and the protection of girls in Pakistan” (2026/2801(RSP)).

3-0479-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, kršćani su najprogonjenija vjerska skupina na svijetu.

Zato Europska unija mora iskoristiti sve instrumente svoje vanjske i razvojne politike kako bi zaštitila položaj kršćana gdje god su izloženi progonu, nasilju i sustavnoj diskriminaciji. U tom kontekstu posebno zabrinjavaju učestali slučajevi prisilne islamizacije kršćana u Pakistanu. Ondje se maloljetne kršćanske djevojčice otimaju, prisilno obraćaju na islam i prisiljavaju na brak sa svojim otmičarima. To nije samo teško kršenje ljudskih prava, nego i oblik vjerskog progona kojemu ne smijemo više okretati leđa. Slučaj trinaestogodišnje, naglašavam trinaestogodišnje Marije Shahbaz koja je nakon otmice prisilno obraćena na islam i udana za svojeg otmičara tragično potvrđuje razmjere ovog progona. Procjenjuje se da se svake godine u Pakistanu otme oko tisuću djevojčica, od kojih su mnoge kršćanke, kako bi bile prisilno obraćene i udane. To mora prestati.

Kolegice i kolege, Europska unija mora ovo pitanje dosljedno postavljati u svim svojim političkim i gospodarskim odnosima s Pakistanom i jasno dati do znanja da progon kršćana neće ostati bez odgovora.
3-0479-0000.englishText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, kršćani su najprogonjenija vjerska skupina na svijetu.

That is why the European Union must use all instruments of its foreign and development policy to protect the position of Christians wherever they are exposed to persecution, violence and systematic discrimination. In this context, frequent cases of forced Islamization of Christians in Pakistan are of particular concern. There, minor Christian girls are kidnapped, forcibly converted to Islam and forced to marry their captors. This is not only a serious violation of human rights, but also a form of religious persecution that we must no longer turn our backs on. The case of the thirteen-year-old, I emphasize the thirteen-year-old Marija Shahbaz, who after the kidnapping was forcibly converted to Islam and married to her captor, tragically confirms the extent of this persecution. It is estimated that around a thousand girls, many of whom are Christian, are abducted every year in Pakistan to be forcibly converted and married. This has to stop.

Colleagues, the European Union must raise this question consistently in all its political and economic relations with Pakistan and make it clear that the persecution of Christians will not go unanswered.

3-0480-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, in Pakistan sono 19 milioni le spose bambine a cui viene strappata l'infanzia e vengono negati l'istruzione e il futuro in nome di un patriarcato brutale, che considera la pubertà biologica come garanzia di maturità per il matrimonio.

Il dramma delle spose bambine, però, è solo la punta di un iceberg, di una violazione sistematica dei diritti. Alle donne sono vietati il lavoro e l'istruzione, ma anche votare e persino aprire un conto in banca, senza un uomo accanto: una vera e propria apartheid basata su una disuguaglianza di genere, ma anche su una discriminazione dovuta alla povertà e all'esclusione sociale, in particolare delle minoranze.

È più che mai urgente una legislazione che protegga le donne e le bambine, rispondendo alle denunce di matrimoni forzati, accertando le responsabilità e offrendo alle vittime un sostegno completo e inclusivo, compresi rifugi sicuri, assistenza legale e consulenza psicologica.
3-0480-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, in Pakistan there are 19 million child brides whose childhood is taken away from them and their education and future are denied in the name of a brutal patriarchy, which considers biological puberty as a guarantee of maturity for marriage.

The drama of child brides, however, is only the tip of the iceberg, of a systematic violation of rights. Women are prohibited from work and education, but also from voting and even opening a bank account, without a man by their side: a real apartheid based on gender inequality, but also on discrimination due to poverty and social exclusion, particularly of minorities.

More urgent than ever is legislation that protects women and girls by responding to reports of forced marriages, holding accountable and offering victims comprehensive and inclusive support, including safe havens, legal assistance and psychological counselling.

3-0481-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de zaak van Maria Shahbaz staat niet op zichzelf: ieder jaar worden in Pakistan honderden christelijke meisjes en hindoemeisjes ontvoerd, gedwongen zich te bekeren tot de islam en te trouwen met een vaak veel oudere moslimman.

Dat is een mensonterende praktijk die niet alleen strijdig is met de vrijheid van godsdienst, maar ook een ernstige aantasting vormt van de rechten van het kind, de rechten van de ouders en het recht op vrijheid en veiligheid.

Vandaag doen wij met onze breedgedragen resolutie een dringend appel op de Pakistaanse autoriteiten om een einde te maken aan deze gedwongen huwelijken, en Maria Shahbaz de vrijheid te geven om terug te keren naar haar ouders.

Pakistan wil graag aanspraak blijven maken op het stelsel van algemene tariefpreferenties plus. Daar valt over te praten, maar dan verwachten we wel het volledig respecteren van de rechten van minderheden.
3-0481-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Maria Shahbaz's case is not an isolated one: every year hundreds of Christian and Hindu girls are kidnapped in Pakistan, forced to convert to Islam and marry an often much older Muslim man.

This is a degrading practice that is not only contrary to freedom of religion, but also seriously undermines the rights of the child, the rights of parents and the right to freedom and security.

Today, our broad-based resolution urgently calls on the Pakistani authorities to put an end to these forced marriages and give Maria Shahbaz the freedom to return to her parents.

Pakistan would like to continue to benefit from the Generalized Tariff Preferences Plus scheme. That can be discussed, but we do expect full respect for the rights of minorities.

3-0482-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, notre résolution s’adresse aux autorités du Pakistan. L’enlèvement, la conversion religieuse forcée, le mariage forcé de Maria Shahbaz, 13 ans, et à travers elle de toutes les autres jeunes filles soumises au même régime, sont contraires à la convention des droits de l’enfant et à la convention internationale sur l’élimination de toutes les formes de discrimination à l’égard des femmes – conventions que le Pakistan a pourtant ratifiées il y a déjà trente ans. Ne pas les appliquer l’expose à un retrait de son accès privilégié au marché européen.

Je m’adresse aussi à l’Union européenne: nous avons la capacité d’améliorer la situation des droits de l’homme, des femmes, des minorités, des enfants, en tant que deuxième partenaire commercial du Pakistan.

Nous attendons le respect de l’état de droit et l’interdiction des mariages forcés et des mariages d’enfants, la mise en place de mécanismes de soutien aux victimes, et que l‘on s’attaque aussi aux racines de ces problèmes que sont les inégalités et discriminations fondées sur le genre, la religion, la caste, mais aussi la pauvreté et l’exclusion sociale.
3-0482-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, our resolution is addressed to the authorities of Pakistan. L’enlèvement, la conversion religieuse forcée, le mariage forcé de Maria Shahbaz, 13 ans, et à travers elle de toutes les autres jeunes filles soumises au même régime, sont contraires à la convention des droits de l’enfant et à la convention internationale sur l’élimination de toutes les formes de discrimination à l’égard des femmes – conventions que le Pakistan a pourtant ratifiées il y a déjà trente ans. Failure to apply them exposes it to a withdrawal of its privileged access to the European market.

I also address the European Union: we have the capacity to improve the situation of human rights, of women, of minorities, of children, as Pakistan's second trading partner.

We expect respect for the rule of law and the prohibition of forced marriages and child marriages, the establishment of support mechanisms for victims, and that we also attack the roots of these problems which are inequalities and discrimination based on gender, religion, caste, but also poverty and social exclusion.

3-0483-0000.sourceText:

Χάρη στις αριστερές και κεντροαριστερές πολιτικές σας φέρατε τη σαρία, την μπούρκα, τις κλειτοριδεκτομές και τους γάμους ανηλίκων εδώ, στην Ευρώπη. Οι φανατικοί ισλαμιστές δεν ενσωματώνονται, δεν αποδέχονται τις δυτικές αξίες και αποτελούν τεράστιο κίνδυνο για τις κοινωνίες μας. Δείτε τι συμβαίνει λίγο με τους βιασμούς, τις δολοφονίες, τις ληστείες και την εγκληματικότητα, που τα μέσα μαζικής ενημέρωσης φυσικά κρύβουν σε πολλές ευρωπαϊκές χώρες. Δείτε τι έχει γίνει στην Αγγλία.

Λυπάμαι πολύ για όσα συμβαίνουν στο Πακιστάν, αλλά περισσότερο λυπάμαι που τα βλέπουμε όλο και συχνότερα στην πατρίδα μου, την Ελλάδα, και στην Ευρώπη. Θέλετε λύση; Κόψτε κάθε οικονομική συναλλαγή με το Πακιστάν και απελάστε τους Πακιστανούς που βρίσκονται στην Ευρώπη παράνομα. Θα δείτε τότε πόσο γρήγορα θα υποχωρήσουν —αλλά δεν θέλετε λύσεις. 3-0483-0000.englishText:

Cut off all economic transactions with Pakistan and deport Pakistanis who are in Europe illegally. You will then see how quickly they will subside—but you don't want solutions. 3-0504-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable and distinguished Members, Commissioner Šuica, in today's world, we are faced with cyberattacks that wish to expose vulnerabilities in our cybersecurity. Such attacks need our full attention because cybersecurity is essential to protect economic activity and critical infrastructure in our Union. Cybersecurity is also about protecting our electronic devices, such as smartphones, where we keep much of our private and professional data.

Attempts to undermine the security of our private data undermine the right to privacy and data protection and freedom of expression. But let's be clear: the ultimate target of such attacks are our democracies and the rule of law. The use of commercial spyware to monitor the press, politicians and public institutions represents a massive challenge to democratic accountability. And while Member States and the European Union are constantly stepping up their efforts to increase cybersecurity, so do those who want to harm our values and our Union. That is why we need to focus on strengthening our democratic resilience.

L’une des facettes de la résilience démocratique est la protection de nos démocraties contre les attaques, notamment les menaces hybrides, la manipulation de l’information et les ingérences étrangères, ainsi que la désinformation.

L’autre facette de la résilience démocratique réside dans la protection de la liberté de nos citoyens et de nos médias, de la tenue d’élections libres et équitables et ainsi que de la solidité des institutions et des processus démocratiques.

Je tiens à vous assurer que le renforcement de la résilience démocratique constitue une priorité majeure pour nos États membres, non seulement à l’échelon national, mais aussi à travers le partage d’informations, la coopération opérationnelle et le renforcement conjoint des capacités.

Ce renforcement de la résilience démocratique est également l’objectif du bouclier européen de la démocratie, que nous sommes actuellement en train de mettre en œuvre.

As Irish Presidency, we are committed to supporting all these efforts in strengthening democratic resilience. During the next semester, we will be paying attention to the protection of citizens online, notably our children, and the safety of political candidates and elected representatives.

I know that these are important issues for the European Parliament as well and I am sure that we will have the occasion to exchange on such matters with you in the months to come. Thank you very much for your attention.
3-0504-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honorable and distinguished Members, Commissioner Šuica, in today's world, we are faced with cyberattacks that wish to expose vulnerabilities in our cybersecurity. Such attacks need our full attention because cybersecurity is essential to protect economic activity and critical infrastructure in our Union. Cybersecurity is also about protecting our electronic devices, such as smartphones, where we keep much of our private and professional data.

Attempts to undermine the security of our private data undermine the right to privacy and data protection and freedom of expression. But let's be clear: the ultimate target of such attacks are our democracies and the rule of law. The use of commercial spyware to monitor the press, politicians and public institutions represents a massive challenge to democratic accountability. And while Member States and the European Union are constantly stepping up their efforts to increase cybersecurity, so do those who want to harm our values ​​and our Union. That is why we need to focus on strengthening our democratic resilience.

One facet of democratic resilience is protecting our democracies from attacks, including hybrid threats, information manipulation and foreign interference, and disinformation.

The other facet of democratic resilience lies in protecting the freedom of our citizens and our media, the holding of free and fair elections and the strength of democratic institutions and processes.

I would like to assure you that strengthening democratic resilience is a major priority for our Member States, not only at the national level, but also through information sharing, operational cooperation and joint capacity building.

This strengthening of democratic resilience is also the objective of the European Democracy Shield, which we are currently implementing.

As Irish Presidency, we are committed to supporting all these efforts in strengthening democratic resilience. During the next semester, we will be paying attention to the protection of citizens online, notably our children, and the safety of political candidates and elected representatives.

I know that these are important issues for the European Parliament as well and I am sure that we will have the opportunity to exchange on such matters with you in the months to come. Thank you very much for your attention.
