Powstaje pytanie: kto kogo kontroluje? Bo gdyby ktoś chciał stworzyć narzędzie do niszczenia demokracji, to takim narzędziem z pewnością jest Pegasus. Bo to jest narzędzie, które od strony osobistej potrafi niszczyć prywatność, wnikać w osobowość człowieka. Z drugiej strony niszczy organizacje, niszczy ugrupowania, demokrację, niszczy dziennikarzy, wolne sądy i praworządność.

Widzieliśmy takie nadużycia w Polsce, na Węgrzech. I gdy historia pokazuje, że takie narzędzia trafiają w ręce ludzi patologicznych, ludzi demagogicznych, populistycznych, zdegenerowanych moralnie, to Pegasusem można niszczyć i prywatność, i demokrację, i wybory.

Przeżyłem to osobiście, gdy jako partia w 2019 roku staliśmy się ofiarą Pegasusa. Podsyłano nam fałszywe analizy wyborcze i wiem, że takim systemem można zniszczyć człowieka. Można ingerować w system, w proces wyborczy, a przecież wolne wybory są świętem demokracji i fundamentem zaufania obywateli do państwa.

Dlatego chciałbym też podziękować na koniec badaczom z Citizen Lab i organizacjom pozarządowym oraz powiedzieć, że należy wdrożyć wszystkie rekomendacje komisji PEGA. Szacunek dla Citizen Lab, dla tych ludzi, którzy realizują zadania, które powinny być realizowane przez instytucje państwa.
3-0508-0000.englishText:
Madam President! This debate is very important because Pegasus is not an ordinary tool. This is a system that strikes at the very heart of democracy, European values ​​and the basic freedoms of citizens.

This debate takes on particular importance at a time when we learn that MEP Kouloglou from Greece was attacked with Pegasus while investigating, as part of the work of the PEGA committee, abuses related to Pegasus. This is shocking information. When the target is a parliamentarian investigating abuses related to these cyber weapons, then not only the privacy of this person is at risk, but also the ability of the European Parliament to carry out control activities of a public institution.

The question arises: who controls whom? Because if someone wanted to create a tool to destroy democracy, Pegasus is certainly such a tool. Because it is a tool that can destroy privacy from a personal perspective and penetrate a person's personality. On the other hand, it destroys organizations, destroys groups, destroys democracy, destroys journalists, free courts and the rule of law.

We have seen such abuses in Poland and Hungary. And when history shows that such tools end up in the hands of pathological people, demagogic, populist and morally degenerate people, Pegasus can be used to destroy privacy, democracy and elections.

I experienced this personally when, as a party, we became a victim of Pegasus in 2019. We were sent false election analyzes and I know that such a system can destroy a person. You can interfere in the system, in the electoral process, but free elections are a celebration of democracy and the foundation of citizens' trust in the state.

Therefore, I would also like to finally thank the researchers from Citizen Lab and non-governmental organizations and say that all recommendations of the PEGA committee should be implemented. Respect for Citizen Lab, for those people who carry out tasks that should be carried out by state institutions.

3-0509-0000.sourceText:
Sinjura President,

Iċ-ċittadini Ewropej kollha għandhom dritt għall-privatezza u għandu jkollhom rashom mistrieħa li l-komunikazzjoni personali tagħhom tibqa' waħda privata.

Imma wieħed jistaqsi: dan għadu l-każ? Illum il-ġurnata nħoloq spyware li permezz tiegħu l-ismartphones jistgħu jiġu aċċessati mingħajr ma wieħed ikun jaf u mingħajr il-ħtieġa li l-vittma jagħfas link intiż għall-phishing. Dan l-iżvilupp jista' joqtol id-dritt tagħna għall-privatezza u, agħar minn hekk, huwa theddida għat-tħaddim tad-demokraziji tagħna.

L-ispyware ntuża fil-konfront ta' uffiċjali eletti, anke fil-konfront ta' Membri ta' dan il-Parlament, biex jinkiseb aċċess għat-telefown tagħhom. Wieħed mill-kollegi tagħna safa vittma tal-ispyware Pegasus, proprju waqt il-ħidma tiegħu fil-kumitat PEGA, intiż sabiex jistħarreġ dan l-istess spyware. Ħaġa assurda u inkwetanti.

Il-ħtieġa għall-iskrutinju forensiku regolari għat-telefowns kollha tagħna hija biss ġlieda kontra s-sintomi. Ċittadini ordinarji, ġurnalisti u politikanti huma lkoll f'riskju, iżda m'għandhomx il-mezzi sabiex jagħmlu l-iskrutinju forensiku tat-telefowns tagħhom. Neħtieġu soluzzjonijiet reali, aktar miżuri ta' sikurezza ċibernetika u forsi regoli ġodda għall-Unjoni Ewropea biex it-telefowns tagħna jinżammu privati.

Ħadd m'għandu jkollu dritt jindaħal fil-komunikazzjoni privata tagħna. Servizzi sigrieti barranin jużaw din il-vulnerabbiltà sabiex jippruvaw jisirqu informazzjoni sensittiva mingħand il-politiċi tagħna. L-ispyware jagħmilha possibbli li tinkiseb informazzjoni kunfidenzjali biex jiġu influwenzati dibattiti politiċi jew saħansitra l-perkors tal-elezzjonijiet.
3-0509-0000.englishText:
Madam President,

All European citizens have a right to privacy and should rest assured that their personal communications will remain private.

But one wonders: is this still the case? Nowadays spyware has been created through which smartphones can be accessed without anyone knowing and without the need for the victim to click on a phishing link. This development could kill our right to privacy and, worse than that, is a threat to the functioning of our democracies.

Spyware has been used against elected officials, even against Members of this Parliament, to gain access to their phones. One of our colleagues fell victim to the Pegasus spyware, precisely during his work in the PEGA committee, intended to investigate this same spyware. An absurd and disturbing thing.

The need for regular forensic scrutiny for all our phones is just a symptom fight. Ordinary citizens, journalists and politicians are all at risk, but they don't have the means to forensically scrutinize their phones. We need real solutions, more cyber security measures and maybe new rules for the European Union to keep our phones private.

No one should have the right to interfere in our private communication. Foreign secret services use this vulnerability to try to steal sensitive information from our politicians. Spyware makes it possible to obtain confidential information to influence political debates or even the course of elections.

3-0510-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! System Pegasus to system, którego nie można kupić w sklepie. Mogą go kupić tylko rządy albo służby podległe rządom, czyli jest pod kontrolą państwa. I mam do państwa parę pytań. Znam też parę odpowiedzi. Czy korupcja jest groźnym przestępstwem? Tak. Czy politycy dopuszczają się korupcji? Znamy wiele przykładów. Czy służby policyjne powinny ścigać korupcję? Tak. Czy politycy powinni być traktowani inaczej niż zwykli obywatele? Nie. Czy polityk dopuszczający się korupcji powinien być ścigany? Tak. Czy służby mogą stosować nowoczesne metody ścigania przestępców? Tak, jest to niezbędne dla skutecznego działania.

Kontrola operacyjna powinna być prowadzona za zgodą właściwych organów państwa i pod ich kontrolą. W Polsce są to sądy. Dlaczego zatem zajmujemy się tą sprawą? Bo nie ma wątpliwości, że jakiś organ państwa, prawdopodobnie w sposób legalny – nie mamy tutaj żadnej wiedzy, czy była zgoda, czy nie, ale domyślam się, że była to kwestia legalna – prowadził postępowanie.

Jestem przekonany, że zamiast paraliżować atakami służby walczące z przestępczością, należy zastanowić się, co zrobić, by Komisja Europejska była bardziej transparentna albo żeby majątki polityków były upublicznione. Nie macie wrażenia, że oświadczenia majątkowe składane przez europosłów są nieczytelne dla opinii publicznej? Więcej jawności! Jawność jest wrogiem korupcji. Politycy także dopuszczają się przestępstw.
3-0510-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The Pegasus system is a system that cannot be purchased in a store. It can only be purchased by governments or services subordinate to governments, i.e. it is under state control. And I have a few questions for you. I also know some answers. Is corruption a serious crime? Yes. Do politicians commit corruption? We know many examples. Should the police pursue corruption? Yes. Should politicians be treated differently from ordinary citizens? NO. Should a politician committing corruption be prosecuted? Yes. Can the services use modern methods of prosecuting criminals? Yes, it is necessary for effective operation.

Operational control should be carried out with the consent of the competent state authorities and under their control. In Poland these are the courts. So why are we dealing with this matter? Because there is no doubt that some state authority, probably legally - we have no knowledge here whether there was consent or not, but I assume it was a legal matter - conducted the proceedings.

I am convinced that instead of paralyzing services fighting crime with attacks, we should consider what to do to make the European Commission more transparent or to make politicians' assets public. Don't you have the impression that the asset declarations submitted by MEPs are illegible to the public? More transparency! Transparency is the enemy of corruption. Politicians also commit crimes.

3-0511-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Auch Jahre nach dem Untersuchungsausschuss ist bei der Frage Pegasus wenig passiert. Jetzt ist der nächste Kollege mit Überwachungssoftware überwacht worden, und die Kommission hat immer noch nicht gehandelt und noch nichts vorgelegt; hier muss endlich etwas passieren.

Aber ich muss ehrlich gestehen, ich finde diese Debatte schon etwas befremdlich. Wir sprechen hier über die Bedeutung und Wichtigkeit von privater und verschlüsselter Kommunikation, aber gleichzeitig werden wir morgen wahrscheinlich diese private, verschlüsselte Kommunikation von 450 Millionen Menschen angreifen mit der Chatkontrolle.

Wir haben jahrelang verhandelt. Wir hatten doch vor zwei Wochen schon fast eine finale Verhandlung zwischen Rat und Parlament – keine Massenüberwachung, Safety by Design, Kontrolle bei konkretem Verdacht. Aber das reicht einigen im Rat und auch hier im Parlament nicht; die wollen die anlasslose Kontrolle unserer Daten. Deswegen wird über die Chatkontrolle morgen wieder abgestimmt, obwohl wir sie schon zweimal hier im Parlament abgelehnt haben.

Man stimmt einfach so lange ab, bis das Ergebnis passt. Die privaten Chats von 450 Millionen EU‑Bürgern, die sind dann nicht mehr sicher; nicht einmal verschlüsselte Kommunikation wollen sie ausnehmen.

Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, ich appelliere wirklich an Sie! Morgen – stimmen Sie gegen diesen Wahnsinn, stimmen Sie gegen die Chatkontrolle, stimmen Sie für verschlüsselte und sichere Kommunikation und vor allem, stimmen Sie für das digitale Briefgeheimnis!
3-0511-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! Even years after the investigative committee, little has happened on the Pegasus issue. Now the next colleague has been monitored with surveillance software and the Commission has still not acted and has not yet produced anything; Something finally has to happen here.

But I have to honestly admit that I find this debate a bit strange. We're talking about the meaning and importance of private and encrypted communications, but at the same time, tomorrow we're probably going to attack those private, encrypted communications of 450 million people with chat control.

We have been negotiating for years. Two weeks ago we almost had a final negotiation between the Council and Parliament - no mass surveillance, safety by design, control in the event of concrete suspicion. But that is not enough for some in the Council and here in Parliament; They want our data to be controlled without cause. That's why the chat control will be voted on again tomorrow, even though we have already rejected it twice here in Parliament.

You simply vote until the result is correct. The private chats of 450 million EU citizens will no longer be safe; They don't even want to exclude encrypted communication.

Dear colleagues, I really appeal to you! Tomorrow – vote against this madness, vote against chat controls, vote for encrypted and secure communication and, above all, vote for digital privacy!

3-0512-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, juillet 2021: des journalistes d’investigation et des ONG révèlent que des milliers de personnes ont été illégalement espionnées à l’aide du logiciel espion Pegasus, qui accède sans clic à absolument toutes vos données sur votre téléphone. Juillet 2023: notre Parlement adopte un ensemble de recommandations afin que personne ne puisse être espionné illégalement, grâce à une réglementation stricte. Juillet 2026: alors qu’on ne compte plus les États membres où les scandales éclatent – Hongrie, Pologne, Espagne, Grèce, Slovaquie, Italie –, une nouvelle ligne rouge est franchie. Un ancien membre de ce Parlement a été espionné durant les travaux de la commission d’enquête.

Depuis cinq ans, les logiciels espions défraient la chronique; depuis cinq ans, c’est pourtant le silence radio. Je me tourne vers le Conseil; je me tourne aussi vers la Commission européenne: nada… Nada… Mme Virkkunen ne nous fait même pas l’honneur de sa présence, aujourd’hui! Face à ces attaques contre la démocratie et l’état de droit, contre l’intégrité du Parlement européen, avec l’espionnage de Stelios Kouloglou, on vous poursuivra jusqu’à ce qu’action s’ensuive.

Nous voulons une enquête concrète sur ces révélations. Qui a espionné Stelios? Pourquoi d’autres députés ont-ils été espionnés? Nous voulons que l’Europe se dote d’un «EU Tech Lab». Nous voulons aussi l’encadrement strict de l’utilisation des logiciels espions et, enfin, l’arrêt immédiat de tout affaiblissement du dispositif européen de protection des données personnelles et des droits fondamentaux.
3-0512-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, July 2021: Investigative journalists and NGOs reveal that thousands of people have been illegally spied on using Pegasus spyware, which accesses absolutely all your data on your phone without a click. July 2023: Our Parliament adopts a set of recommendations so that no one can be spied on illegally, thanks to strict regulations. July 2026: while we can no longer count the Member States where scandals are breaking out – Hungary, Poland, Spain, Greece, Slovakia, Italy – a new red line is crossed. A former member of this Parliament was spied on during the work of the commission of inquiry.

For five years, spyware has been in the news; for five years, however, there has been radio silence. I turn to the Council; I also turn to the European Commission: nada… Nada… Ms Virkkunen is not even honoring us with her presence today! Faced with these attacks against democracy and the rule of law, against the integrity of the European Parliament, with the espionage of Stelios Kouloglou, you will be pursued until action ensues.

We want a concrete investigation into these revelations. Who spied on Stelios? Why were other MPs spied on? We want Europe to have an “EU Tech Lab”. We also want strict supervision of the use of spyware and, finally, an immediate end to any weakening of the European system for the protection of personal data and fundamental rights.

3-0513-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, μετά από πρωτοβουλία του Αντιπροέδρου της Left Κώστα Αρβανίτη, συζητάμε σήμερα ένα πολύ σοβαρό ζήτημα κράτους δικαίου. Η επιβεβαιωμένη από το «Citizen Lab» παρακολούθηση του πρώην ευρωβουλευτή της Left Στέλιου Κούλογλου αποτελεί ευθεία επίθεση στην ανεξαρτησία του ίδιου του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου. Το θύμα ήταν μέλος της ειδικής εξεταστικής επιτροπής PEGA, που το Σώμα συγκρότησε για να διερευνήσει τη χρήση του Pegasus και άλλων παράνομων κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών στην Ευρώπη. Προφανώς, όταν παρακολουθείται ένα μέλος αυτής της επιτροπής, δεν τίθεται σε κίνδυνο μόνο η ιδιωτικότητά του· μέσα από την παρακολούθηση του πρώην συναδέλφου κάποιοι παρακολούθησαν και άλλους ευρωβουλευτές, όπως και το ερευνητικό έργο της επιτροπής PEGA.

Οι παρακολουθήσεις αυτές πλήττουν ευθέως τη δημοκρατία, το κράτος δικαίου και τη θεσμική ακεραιότητα των ευρωπαϊκών θεσμών, και μας υπενθυμίζουν ότι η ασφάλειά μας, η προστασία του κράτους δικαίου και η ανεξαρτησία των δημοκρατικών θεσμών παραμένει μία ευρωπαϊκή πρόκληση. Το πραγματικό ερώτημα είναι αν το ίδιο το Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο είναι διατεθειμένο να διερευνήσει ποιοι και για λογαριασμό ποιου παρακολούθησαν τον ευρωβουλευτή μέλος της εξεταστικής του επιτροπής. Αυτό είναι ένα ζήτημα θεσμικής αξιοπιστίας και προστασίας της εντολής των ευρωβουλευτών.

Ως Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο είχαμε ζητήσει από την Επιτροπή, όχι μόνο στο πόρισμα της επιτροπής PEGA αλλά και σε μεταγενέστερο ψήφισμά μας, να αναλάβει νομοθετική πρωτοβουλία απέναντι στις προκλήσεις που δημιουργούν τα κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά —και οι νέες αποκαλύψεις αποδεικνύουν με τον πιο δραματικό τρόπο ότι αυτό το αίτημα ήταν απολύτως δικαιολογημένο. Όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν τη στιγμή που στην Ελλάδα το σκάνδαλο των υποκλοπών όχι μόνο δεν έχει κλείσει, όπως επιχειρεί η σημερινή κυβέρνηση και η κυβερνητική πλειοψηφία, αλλά μπαίνει σε μια νέα, ιδιαίτερα κρίσιμη φάση. Μετά τον Νίκο Ανδρουλάκη, πρόεδρο του ΠΑΣΟΚ, τον πρώην υπουργό του ΣΥΡΙΖΑ Χρήστο Σπίρτζη, πλέον και ο πρώην πρωθυπουργός Αντώνης Σαμαράς ζήτησε επίσημα από τον Άρειο Πάγο να διερευνηθεί η παρακολούθησή του.

Σήμερα λοιπόν υπερασπιζόμαστε το δικαίωμα κάθε μέλους αυτού του Κοινοβουλίου να ασκεί ανεμπόδιστα τα καθήκοντά του. Υπερασπιζόμαστε την ανεξαρτησία των εξεταστικών επιτροπών μας. Υπερασπιζόμαστε την αξιοπιστία του ίδιου του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου, και γι' αυτό ζητούμε: πλήρη διερεύνηση της υπόθεσης από τις αρμόδιες αρχές της Ελλάδας, του Βελγίου και της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης· απόδοση ευθυνών και, επιτέλους, τη λήψη δεσμευτικών μέτρων για την απαγόρευση της χρήσης κακόβουλων κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών στην Ευρώπη.
3-0513-0000.englishText:
Madam President, following the initiative of Left Vice President Kostas Arvanitis, today we are discussing a very serious issue of the rule of law. The surveillance of former Left MEP Stelios Kouloglou, confirmed by Citizen Lab, is a direct attack on the independence of the European Parliament itself. The victim was a member of the PEGA special commission of inquiry, which the House established to investigate the use of Pegasus and other illegal spyware in Europe. Obviously, when a member of this committee is monitored, it is not only his privacy that is at risk; through the monitoring of the former colleague, some also monitored other MEPs, as did the PEGA committee's investigative work.

These surveillances directly affect democracy, the rule of law and the institutional integrity of European institutions, and remind us that our security, the protection of the rule of law and the independence of democratic institutions remain a European challenge. The real question is whether the European Parliament itself is willing to investigate who, and on whose behalf, monitored the MEP member of its investigative committee. This is a question of institutional credibility and protection of the MEPs' mandate.

As the European Parliament, we had asked the Commission, not only in the PEGA Committee's conclusion but also in our subsequent resolution, to take a legislative initiative in the face of the challenges posed by spyware — and the new revelations demonstrate in the most dramatic way that this request was fully justified. All this is happening at a time when in Greece the wiretapping scandal is not only not closed, as the current government and the ruling majority are trying to do, but is entering a new, particularly critical phase. After Nikos Androulakis, president of PASOK, the former SYRIZA minister Christos Spirtzis, now also the former prime minister Antonis Samaras has officially asked the Areopagus to investigate his surveillance.

So today we defend the right of every member of this Parliament to exercise their duties unimpeded. We defend the independence of our investigative committees. We defend the credibility of the European Parliament itself, which is why we demand: a full investigation of the case by the competent authorities of Greece, Belgium and the European Union; accountability and, finally, binding measures to ban the use of malicious spyware in Europe.

3-0514-0000.sourceText:
Vážená pani predsedajúca. Som presvedčený o tom, že ste stratili aj posledné zábrany. Klamete ľuďom od rána do večera. Pozrite sa, čo ste tam napísali! Vy ste túto tému nazvali Ochrana európskej demokracie.

Ja sa vás pýtam, kde je tá európska demokracia? V Európskej komisii, ktorej predsedníčka nechce zverejniť informácie o tom, ako nakupovala vakcíny? V tomto Parlamente, ktorý tu pretláča Chat Control, aby mohol špehovať telefón každého jedného obyvateľa Európskej únie? Alebo vtedy, keď ste osemkrát preukázateľne zasiahli do slobodných a demokratických volieb v jednotlivých členských štátoch.

Slovenská republika, z ktorej pochádzam, bola terčom vašich hybridných operácií, kedy Európska komisia výrazne s využitím Digital Services aktu obmedzovala dosahy politikov na sociálnych sieťach. Som jeden z tých, ktorým vaša Európska komisia prikázala sociálnych sietí, aby mu vypli dosah na sociálnych sieťach. Čo to má spoločné s demokraciou? Takejto demokracii by hádam tlieskal aj súdruh Stalin a Mao Ce-tung. Toto je vaša demokracia, ktorú chcete chrániť?

Samozrejme, že je obrovský problém, ak europoslancovi do telefónu nejaká tajná služba nainštaluje program Pegasus a špehujú ho. Je to obrovský problém, ktorý treba riešiť. Ale vy chcete predsa nainštalovať špehovací program do 450 miliónov telefónov obyvateľov Európskej únie. Chcete čítať každú šifrovanú komunikáciu, vidieť každú jednu fotografiu. Chcete čítať súkromné konverzácie medzi manželmi. Veď to je úchylné, choré a zvrátené.

Dvakrát toto plénum odmietlo Chat control a pretláčate ho zase. Tak nám nehovorte o ochrane súkromia, keď vy ste najväčší porušovatelia súkromia. Ako nám môžete hovoriť o ochrane demokracie a slobody slova, keď toto plénum odhlasovalo, že ide vyšetrovať našu politickú stranu Európa suverénnych národov za to, že otvorene hovoríme veci, ktoré neporušujú žiadne zákony, ale takzvané európske hodnoty? A vy ste tí, ktorí určia, čo sú tie európske hodnoty. Príde Európska komisia a povie Demokracia, sloboda slova. Ale odtiaľ potiaľ. My vám nastavíme, o čom môžete hovoriť. Chcete deportovať nelegálnych imigrantov? Hovoríte o reemigrácii – ako v mojom prípade: porušujete európske hodnoty! Lebo európskou hodnotou podľa tejto Európskej komisie je mať v Európe vrahov, teroristov a násilníkov, ktorí sem prišli nelegálne. A takto by som mohol pokračovať donekonečna. Neustále európsku demokraciu ničíte, potláčate, zakopali ste ju do hrobu. A dnes nám hovoríte, že my vám máme veriť, že vy budete chrániť súkromie, demokraciu a slobodu slova. Prv odíďte vy, prestaňte so všetkým, čo robíte, a potom môžeme veriť tomu, že sa demokracia bude v Európe dať obnoviť.
3-0514-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President. I am convinced that you have lost even the last inhibitions. You lie to people from morning to night. Look what you wrote there! You called this topic Protection of European Democracy.

I ask you, where is the European democracy? In the European Commission, whose president does not want to publish information about how she bought vaccines? In this Parliament pushing Chat Control to spy on the phone of every single resident of the European Union? Or when you have demonstrably interfered in free and democratic elections in individual member states eight times.

The Slovak Republic, where I come from, was the target of your hybrid operations, when the European Commission significantly limited the reach of politicians on social networks using the Digital Services Act. I am one of those whose social networks have been ordered by your European Commission to shut down his social media reach. What does this have to do with democracy? Comrade Stalin and Mao Zedong would probably applaud such a democracy. Is this your democracy you want to protect?

Of course, it is a huge problem if some secret service installs the Pegasus program on a MEP's phone and they spy on him. It's a huge problem that needs to be addressed. But you still want to install a spy program in 450 million phones of European Union residents. You want to read every encrypted communication, see every single photo. You want to read private conversations between spouses. After all, it is deviant, sick and perverted.

Twice this plenum rejected the Chat control and you push it again. So don't talk to us about privacy when you are the biggest privacy violators. How can you talk to us about protecting democracy and freedom of speech when this plenary voted to investigate our political party Europe of Sovereign Nations for openly saying things that do not violate any laws but so-called European values? And you are the ones who will determine what those European values ​​are. The European Commission will come and say Democracy, freedom of speech. But from there on. We will set up what you can talk about. Want to deport illegal immigrants? You talk about re-emigration - as in my case: you violate European values! Because the European value, according to this European Commission, is to have murderers, terrorists and rapists in Europe who came here illegally. And I could go on like this forever. You are constantly destroying European democracy, suppressing it, burying it in the grave. And today you tell us that we should trust you, that you will protect privacy, democracy and freedom of speech. First you leave, stop everything you are doing, and then we can believe that democracy can be restored in Europe.

3-0515-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Po raz kolejny wychodzi na jaw informacja przekazana przez Citizen Lab, instytut akademicki, która wykazuje, że system Pegasus był wykorzystywany w tak szeroki sposób, naruszając jedne z podstawowych wartości, jakie obowiązują w Unii Europejskiej, i wartości, które powinniśmy my, w Parlamencie Europejskim, chronić. Chodzi o prawo do prywatności.

Przypomnę, że sprawa Pegasusa wypłynęła w związku z naruszeniami, których dopuściła się ówczesna władza Prawa i Sprawiedliwości w Polsce. Na tej sali siedzi ówczesny senator Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej Krzysztof Brejza, ówczesny szef kampanii wyborczej partii opozycyjnej, a obecnie poseł do Parlamentu Europejskiego. To on i jego rodzina, a także wielu innych polityków, dziennikarzy, niezależnych prawników było inwigilowanych w Polsce systemem Pegasus zakupionym przez partię rządzącą. To oni chcieli wiedzieć, co się dzieje w ich domach. Chcieli wiedzieć, jakie są plany polityczne, i chcieli wiedzieć, jak walczyć z opozycją, z obywatelami i wszystkimi tymi, którzy nie stoją po stronie rządu.

Dlatego wówczas Parlament Europejski powołał komisję PEGA. I ta komisja w 2023 roku przygotowała raport liczący 145 stron, w którym Parlament Europejski wyraźnie stwierdził, że zarówno państwa członkowskie, jak i państwa spoza Unii wykorzystywały Pegasusa, a szczególnie w Polsce i szczególnie na Węgrzech. Drastycznie naruszano w związku z tym prawo Unii Europejskiej i nie zapewniano obywatelom żadnej ochrony. Te działania Pegasusa były wielopoziomowe, ponieważ ten system szpiegowski przechodził z jednego urządzenia na drugie. Tego dotyczą teraz, przypomnę Państwu, sprawy, które toczą się przed Europejskim Trybunałem Praw Człowieka i czekamy na wyroki właśnie w tej sprawie.
3-0515-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Po raz kolejny wychodzi na jaw informacja przekazana przez Citizen Lab, instytut akademicki, która wykazuje, że system Pegasus był wykorzystywany w tak szeroki sposób, naruszając jedne z podstawowych wartości, jakie obowiązują w Unii Europejskiej, i wartości, które powinniśmy my, w Parlamencie Europejskim, chronić. Chodzi o prawo do prywatności.

Let me remind you that the Pegasus case arose in connection with violations committed by the then authorities of Law and Justice in Poland. The then senator of the Republic of Poland, Krzysztof Brejza, then head of the opposition party's election campaign, and currently a member of the European Parliament, sits in this room. He and his family, as well as many other politicians, journalists and independent lawyers, were under surveillance in Poland using the Pegasus system purchased by the ruling party. They wanted to know what was happening in their homes. They wanted to know what the political plans were, and they wanted to know how to fight the opposition, the citizens and all those who were not on the government's side.

That is why the European Parliament established the PEGA committee. And this commission in 2023 prepared a 145-page report in which the European Parliament clearly stated that both member states and non-EU countries used Pegasus, especially in Poland and especially in Hungary. As a result, European Union law was drastically violated and no protection was provided to citizens. These Pegasus activities were multi-layered as this spy system passed from one device to another. Let me remind you, this is what the cases pending before the European Court of Human Rights concern and we are waiting for judgments in this case.

3-0516-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, ένας ακόμη συνάδελφός μας αποδεικνύεται ότι έπεσε θύμα παρακολούθησης με παράνομο κατασκοπευτικό λογισμικό: ο κύριος Κούλογλου, μέλος της εξεταστικής επιτροπής γι' αυτόν ακριβώς τον σκοπό, για τη διερεύνηση παρακολουθήσεων με παράνομο λογισμικό στην Ευρώπη. Είχε προηγηθεί η απόπειρα παρακολούθησης ενός ακόμη ευρωβουλευτή, του Νίκου Ανδρουλάκη, μέλους των Ευρωπαίων Σοσιαλιστών και Δημοκρατών, που καθόταν σε εκείνα τα έδρανα, προέδρου του ΠΑΣΟΚ και σήμερα αρχηγού της αξιωματικής αντιπολίτευσης στην Ελλάδα.

Ένα ζήτημα υψίστης σημασίας και για την πατρίδα μου και για την ευρωπαϊκή έννομη τάξη. Απαιτούμε πλήρη διαλεύκανση της υπόθεσης και όλων των υποθέσεων, τόσο από τις εθνικές αρχές όσο και από τους ευρωπαϊκούς θεσμούς. Είναι θέμα δημοκρατίας και κράτους δικαίου.
3-0516-0000.englishText:
Madam President, one more colleague of ours turns out to have been a victim of illegal spyware surveillance: Mr. Kouloglu, a member of the commission of inquiry for this very purpose, to investigate illegal software surveillance in Europe. It was preceded by the attempt to monitor another MEP, Nikos Androulakis, a member of the European Socialists and Democrats, who was sitting in those seats, president of PASOK and today the leader of the main opposition in Greece.

An issue of the utmost importance both for my country and for the European legal order. We demand a full clarification of the case and all cases, both from the national authorities and from the European institutions. It is a matter of democracy and the rule of law.

3-0517-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η δημοκρατία μας απειλείται. Παράνομα λογισμικά παρακολούθησης στρέφονται εναντίον των εκλεγμένων εκπροσώπων των πολιτών. Οι αποκαλύψεις για την παρακολούθηση ευρωβουλευτή με παράνομο λογισμικό μπορεί να εκπλήσσουν την Ευρώπη· δυστυχώς στην Ελλάδα η κοινή γνώμη μέσω του δημοσιογραφικού κατεστημένου έχει συμφιλιωθεί με αυτή την εικόνα. Βλέπουμε διαρκώς έναν μηχανισμό θαψίματος υποθέσεων από το κυβερνών παρακράτος. Το κυβερνητικό σύστημα έστησε μηχανισμό παρακολούθησης του συνόλου της αντιπολίτευσης και της κυβέρνησης.

Εμείς στεκόμαστε απέναντι. Δεν εφησυχάζουμε. Ζητάμε απόλυτη διαφάνεια. Όσοι διαθέτουν κρίσιμα στοιχεία για την προμήθεια και χρήση παράνομου λογισμικού από κρατικές αρχές, όπως ο Dilian, οφείλουν να κληθούν ενώπιον των αρμόδιων επιτροπών και να καταθέσουν όλα τα αποδεικτικά στοιχεία. Κάθε άρνηση διερεύνησης, κάθε καθυστέρηση ή απόκρυψη αποδεικνύει συνενοχή. Εμείς εδώ έχουμε μια αποστολή: να φωνάξουμε με κάθε τρόπο πως κανείς δεν βρίσκεται υπεράνω του νόμου και καμία κυβέρνηση, κανένας μηχανισμός εξουσίας δεν μπορεί να χρησιμοποιεί παράνομα μέσα παρακολούθησης χωρίς λογοδοσία. Η δημοκρατία προστατεύεται μόνο όταν η αλήθεια αποκαλύπτεται, όσο ισχυρό κι αν είναι το σύστημα της συγκάλυψης.
3-0517-0000.englishText:
Madam President, our democracy is under threat. Illegal surveillance software targets elected representatives of citizens. The revelations about MEP surveillance with illegal software may surprise Europe; unfortunately in Greece public opinion through the journalistic establishment has come to terms with this image. We constantly see a mechanism of burying cases by the ruling parastate. The government system set up a monitoring mechanism of the entire opposition and the government.

We stand opposite. We are not complacent. We demand absolute transparency. Those with critical evidence of the procurement and use of illegal software by government authorities, such as Dilian, must be called before the relevant committees and testify all the evidence. Every refusal to investigate, every delay or concealment proves complicity. We here have a mission: to shout in every way that no one is above the law and no government, no apparatus of power can use illegal means of surveillance without accountability. Democracy is only protected when the truth is revealed, no matter how powerful the system of cover-up.

3-0518-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Menschen Europas! Medien und Journalismus werden häufig als vierte Gewalt der Demokratie bezeichnet. Auch wenn dies vielleicht nicht der traditionellen Gewaltenteilung entspricht, wird die Aussage deutlich: Freier Journalismus und investigative Recherche sind unabdingbar für unsere Demokratie. Das gilt auch dann, wenn Menschen aus der Politik in den Journalismus wechseln.

Wir können und dürfen die Spionageattacken auf den Europaabgeordneten und Journalisten Stelios Kouloglou nicht unkommentiert stehen lassen. Dass Politiker sowie Journalistinnen und Journalisten solche Eingriffe in ihre Privatsphäre fürchten müssen, wenn sie ihrer Arbeit nachgehen, ist absolut inakzeptabel und schädlich für die europäische Demokratie.

Demokratie kann nur funktionieren, wenn Menschen ohne Angst ihre Meinung äußern, Missstände aufdecken und Verantwortung einfordern können. Einschüchterung und Überwachung von Politikerinnen und Politikern, von Journalistinnen und Journalisten gefährden nicht nur eine einzelne Person, sondern auch das Vertrauen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger in unsere europäischen Institutionen.

Dementsprechend muss die Kommission handeln; ich glaube, das wissen Sie, ich glaube, das haben Sie verstanden. Wir müssen den Schutz vor Spyware zu einer Priorität machen, weil uns diese Problemstellung in unserer jetzigen Welt immer und immer wieder entgegentreten wird.

Hier geht es nicht nur um einen Einzelfall, hier geht es um die demokratische Kontrolle an sich. Der Schutz der Freiheit der Abgeordneten, der Schutz der Pressefreiheit bedeutet den Schutz unserer gemeinsamen europäischen Werte.
3-0518-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear people of Europe! Media and journalism are often referred to as the fourth estate of democracy. Even though this may not correspond to the traditional separation of powers, the message is clear: Free journalism and investigative research are essential for our democracy. This also applies when people switch from politics to journalism.

We cannot and must not let the espionage attacks on the MEP and journalist Stelios Kouloglou go uncommented. The fact that politicians and journalists have to fear such invasions of their privacy when they go about their work is absolutely unacceptable and harmful to European democracy.

Democracy can only work if people can express their opinions without fear, expose grievances and demand responsibility. Intimidation and surveillance of politicians and journalists not only endanger a single person, but also the trust of citizens in our European institutions.

The Commission must act accordingly; I think you know that, I think you understand that. We need to make spyware protection a priority because we will face this issue over and over again in our current world.

This is not just about an individual case, this is about democratic control itself. Protecting the freedom of MPs, protecting the freedom of the press means protecting our common European values.

3-0523-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, Herr Minister! Wenn ein Mitglied eines Untersuchungsausschusses, der sich mit illegaler Verwendung von Spionagesoftware beschäftigt, während seiner Arbeit mit exakt jener Software, die Untersuchungsgegenstand ist, ausspioniert wird, dann ist das nichts anderes als ein massiver und unverfrorener Angriff auf Demokratie und Parlamentarismus. Und wenn tatsächlich dieselben Akteure dahinterstecken, die russische und belarussische Oppositionelle im Exil gezielt mit Spionagesoftware abgehört haben, ist das eine ungeheure Bedrohung unserer Souveränität und Auftrag, endlich entschieden zu handeln.

Europa wird von innen und außen angegriffen, und da kann nationale Sicherheit und darf nationale Sicherheit nicht das Aushebeln rechtsstaatlicher Prinzipien begründen. Bis heute wurde Predatorgate in Griechenland nicht lückenlos aufgeklärt: Wer hat den Auftrag zur Überwachung erteilt? Mit welchem Ziel? Alle Beteiligten sind zur Verantwortung zu ziehen.

Ein europäischer Rechtsakt mit klaren Mindeststandards für den Einsatz von Spyware ist überfällig, richterliche Kontrolle, strenge Aufsicht und wirksamer Schutz für Journalistinnen und Journalisten, Juristinnen, Juristen sowie Abgeordnete dringendst notwendig. Was muss noch passieren, damit die Kommission endlich handelt?
3-0523-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, Minister! If a member of an investigative committee that deals with the illegal use of spy software is spied on while working with the very software that is the subject of the investigation, then this is nothing other than a massive and blatant attack on democracy and parliamentarism. Und wenn tatsächlich dieselben Akteure dahinterstecken, die russische und belarussische Oppositionelle im Exil gezielt mit Spionagesoftware abgehört haben, ist das eine ungeheure Bedrohung unserer Souveränität und Auftrag, endlich entschieden zu handeln.

Europe is under attack from within and without, and national security cannot and should not justify the undermining of constitutional principles. To date, Predatorgate in Greece has not been completely solved: who gave the surveillance order? With what aim? Everyone involved must be held accountable.

A European legal act with clear minimum standards for the use of spyware is overdue; judicial control, strict supervision and effective protection for journalists, lawyers and members of parliament are urgently needed. What still needs to happen for the Commission to finally act?

3-0524-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, tuve el honor de ser miembro de la Comisión de Investigación de Pegasus la pasada legislatura y el sentido de la Comisión de Investigación es arrojar unas conclusiones que sean vinculantes para la Comisión, para que adopten iniciativas legislativas. Las recuerdo muy bien: un laboratorio europeo de referencia, y, sobre todo, declarar ilegal —por incompatible con la Carta de los Derechos Fundamentales de la Unión Europea— el uso de herramientas de espionaje masivo e indiscriminado; y no digamos el aspecto criminal que tiene su utilización contra periodistas, activistas, defensores de derechos humanos y nada menos que parlamentarios, porque Predator —que es la versión griega de Pegasus— ha sido utilizado contra Nikos Androulakis y contra Stelios Kouloglou, dos distinguidos miembros de este Parlamento Europeo, en su función parlamentaria, lo que es completamente inaceptable.

Por tanto, se tiene que declarar ilegal la utilización de un espionaje masivo y delictivo cuando se trata de espionaje contra activistas de derechos humanos, abogados o políticos y periodistas, porque solo puede ser utilizado con autorización judicial y contra criminalidad grave transnacional.

Por tanto, la Comisión está tardando en actuar y debe hacerlo.

(El orador acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0524-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, I had the honor of being a member of the Pegasus Commission of Inquiry last term and the purpose of the Commission of Inquiry is to draw conclusions that are binding on the Commission, so that they can adopt legislative initiatives. I remember them very well: a European reference laboratory, and, above all, declaring illegal – because it is incompatible with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union – the use of massive and indiscriminate espionage tools; and not to mention the criminal aspect of its use against journalists, activists, human rights defenders and no less than parliamentarians, because Predator - which is the Greek version of Pegasus - has been used against Nikos Androulakis and against Stelios Kouloglou, two distinguished members of this European Parliament, in their parliamentary function, which is completely unacceptable.

Therefore, the use of massive and criminal espionage must be declared illegal when it involves espionage against human rights activists, lawyers or politicians and journalists, because it can only be used with judicial authorization and against serious transnational crime.

The Commission is therefore slow to act and must do so.

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question asked under the "blue card" procedure)

3-0525-0000.sourceText: (Renew), Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank, Herr Kollege, dass Sie die blaue Karte akzeptieren. Was wäre in Ihren Augen eine Sanktion, die wir gegenüber Mitgliedstaaten, die sich in dieser Art illegal verhalten, vorbringen sollten?
3-0525-0000.englishText: (Renew), question about the “blue card” procedure. – Thank you, Mr. Colleague, for accepting the blue card. In your opinion, what would be a sanction that we should impose on Member States that behave illegally in this way?

3-0526-0000.sourceText: (S&D), Antwort auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“. – Es ist nicht nur illegal, es ist ein Verbrechen. Eine massive Spionage gegen Mitglieder des Europäischen Parlaments, mit den Rechtsanwälten, mit den Journalisten, das ist gegen die Charta der Grundrechte der Europäischen Union. Es sollte ein Verbrechen sein, und es sollte eine Strafe nach dem Strafgesetzbuch der Mitgliedstaaten der Europäischen Union nach sich ziehen.
3-0526-0000.englishText: (S&D), response to a question about the 'blue card' procedure. – It's not just illegal, it's a crime. Massive espionage against members of the European Parliament, with lawyers, with journalists, that is against the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. It should be a crime and it should attract punishment under the criminal code of the European Union Member States.

3-0529-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en Israel sus empresas de inteligencia militar nos pueden estar espiando a todos: a ciudadanos, a periodistas, pero también a diputados.

Hemos hablado de Stelios, un amigo, alguien que estaba investigando ese espionaje y resulta que estaba siendo a su vez espiado por el Gobierno griego con el software israelí Pegasus. Yo cené con él hace un par de semanas. ¿Estaba el Gobierno griego, o el de Israel, en esa cena? Es surrealista, es como encarcelar al bombero que intenta apagar un incendio.

En las distopías de Orwell, el Gran Hermano vigila a todo el mundo, pero aquí hemos ido un paso más allá: también se vigila a quien intenta demostrar que nos vigilan.

He oído al portavoz del Partido Popular de Polonia, que dice que es un gran peligro para la democracia. Pero, señorías del Partido Popular, han pasado tres años desde que el Parlamento aprobó sus recomendaciones y ustedes no han hecho absolutamente nada. ¿Por qué? ¿Quizás porque a ustedes no les espían, espían a sus adversarios políticos?
3-0529-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in Israel your military intelligence companies may be spying on all of us: citizens, journalists, but also deputies.

We have talked about Stelios, a friend, someone who was investigating this espionage and it turns out that he was in turn being spied on by the Greek Government with the Israeli Pegasus software. I had dinner with him a couple of weeks ago. Was the Greek government, or that of Israel, at that dinner? It's surreal, it's like imprisoning the firefighter who is trying to put out a fire.

In Orwell's dystopias, Big Brother watches over everyone, but here we have gone one step further: those who try to prove that they are watching us are also watched.

I heard the spokesperson of the Polish People's Party say that it is a great danger to democracy. But, ladies and gentlemen of the Popular Party, three years have passed since Parliament approved your recommendations and you have done absolutely nothing. Because? Maybe because they don't spy on you, they spy on your political adversaries?

3-0530-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, το σκάνδαλο υποκλοπών στην Ελλάδα, οι παρακολουθήσεις, και με κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά, ευρωβουλευτών, στρατιωτικών, δημοσιογράφων δεν είναι μεμονωμένα περιστατικά. Με ευρωενωσιακές οδηγίες και κανονισμούς, στην υλοποίησή τους από τις κυβερνήσεις, η παρακολούθηση των πάντων έγινε κανονικότητα. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση μάλιστα ζητά επειγόντως την έγκριση του επικίνδυνου κανονισμού μαζικής παρακολούθησης Chat Control. Από την υπόθεση Intellexa προκύπτει ότι τα κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά επιτρέπονται από τον κανονισμό ειδών διπλής χρήσης. Είναι νόμιμη η ανάπτυξή τους· η αγορά από κρατικές υπηρεσίες, όπως η ΕΥΠ στην Ελλάδα· η χρήση τους με επίκληση της έννοιας-λάστιχου «εθνική ασφάλεια». Το ευρωενωσιακό θεσμικό πλαίσιο «ουδείς εξαιρείται των παρακολουθήσεων» μετατρέπει τις υποκλοπές, παράνομες και νόμιμες, σε εργαλείο καταστολής, πρωτίστως ενάντια στο εργατικό λαϊκό κίνημα που αγωνίζεται για τις σύγχρονες ανάγκες του.

Αυτό είναι το κράτος δικαίου της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης που υπερασπίζονται τα άλλα κόμματα. Αυτά θέλει να κουκουλώσει και η κυβέρνηση της Νέας Δημοκρατίας. Η υπεράσπιση των λαϊκών δικαιωμάτων επιβάλλει τη ρήξη με την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, κατάργηση των αντιδραστικών κανονισμών, απαγόρευση εμπορίας και χρήσης κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών, αποκάλυψη και καταδίκη όλων των υπευθύνων.
3-0530-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the wiretapping scandal in Greece, the surveillance, including with spy software, of MEPs, soldiers, journalists are not isolated incidents. With EU directives and regulations, in their implementation by governments, tracking everything became normal. The European Union is even urgently calling for the approval of the dangerous Chat Control mass surveillance regulation. The Intellexa case shows that spyware is permitted under the dual-use regulation. It is legal to develop them; to purchase them from government agencies, such as the EYP in Greece; to use them invoking the rubber concept of "national security". The European Union institutional framework "no one is exempt from surveillance" turns wiretapping, illegal and legal, into a tool of repression, primarily against the labor popular movement that is fighting for its modern needs.

This is the rule of law of the European Union that the other parties are defending. This is what the New Democracy government wants to cover up. The defense of people's rights requires breaking with the European Union, repealing reactionary regulations, banning the sale and use of spyware, revealing and condemning all those responsible.

3-0531-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η Ευρώπη γεννήθηκε πάνω στα ερείπια ενός σκοτεινού παρελθόντος. Υποσχέθηκε στους πολίτες της ότι δεν θα φοβούνται ποτέ ξανά πως κάποιος ακούει πίσω από την πόρτα, διαβάζει τα γράμματά τους ή παρακολουθεί τις σκέψεις τους. Κι όμως, σήμερα ένας ακόμη ευρωβουλευτής —δεύτερος ευρωβουλευτής— αποκαλύπτεται ότι ήταν στόχος ισραηλινού κατασκοπευτικού λογισμικού. Όταν παρακολουθείται ένας ευρωβουλευτής, δεν κινδυνεύει μόνο ο ίδιος· κινδυνεύει η ελευθερία κάθε συνομιλίας, κάθε διαπραγμάτευσης, κάθε ψήφου μέσα σε αυτό το κοινοβούλιο. Υπάρχουν και άλλοι ευρωβουλευτές που παρακολουθήθηκαν; Μπορεί να είναι οποιοσδήποτε από μας. Το Κοινοβούλιο οφείλει να μας προστατεύσει. Η παρακολούθηση ενός ευρωβουλευτή είναι παραβίαση και προσβολή του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου.

Ζητώ από την Πρόεδρο να οργανώσει εθελοντικό έλεγχο ασφαλείας όλων των συσκευών των ευρωβουλευτών, να δούμε τι έκταση έχει πάρει αυτή η κατασκοπευτική απειλή, πόσοι παρακολουθούνται σήμερα. Ζητώ και από την Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή, τη Europol και τον Ευρωπαίο Επόπτη Προστασίας Δεδομένων να διερευνήσουν ανεξάρτητα αυτή την ευρωπαϊκή υπόθεση.
3-0531-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Europe was born on the ruins of a dark past. She promised her citizens that they would never again fear someone listening behind the door, reading their letters or watching their thoughts. And yet today another MEP — a second MEP — is revealed to have been targeted by Israeli spyware. When an MEP is monitored, it is not only him who is at risk; the freedom of every conversation, every negotiation, every vote in this parliament is at risk. Are there other MEPs who were monitored? It could be any of us. Parliament must protect us. Following an MEP is a violation and an insult to the European Parliament.

I ask the President to organize a voluntary security check of all MEPs' devices, to see how far this espionage threat has taken, how many are being monitored today. I also ask the European Commission, Europol and the European Data Protection Supervisor to independently investigate this European case.

3-0537-0000.sourceText: Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgen die Erklärungen zur Abstimmung.
3-0537-0000.englishText: The next item on the agenda is the explanations of vote.

3-0539-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über die Ukraine.
3-0539-0000.englishText: We now turn to the explanations of vote on the Commission's 2025 report on Ukraine.

3-0540-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea Raportului privind Ucraina pentru că, în primul rând, susțin Ucraina în a câștiga acest război pornit de către Rusia agresivă împotriva ei.

Mai mult decât atât, acest raport prevede pentru a doua oară următoarea situație: ia act de faptul că Parlamentul Ucrainei a adoptat o lege care permite parohiilor ortodoxe din Ucraina, aflate sub jurisdicția Patriarhiei Ortodoxe a Moscovei, să se dezafilieze de la Biserica Ortodoxă Rusă și să decidă cu privire la propria lor afiliere. În Ucraina există astăzi sute de parohii ortodoxe românești care doresc să iasă de sub jurisdicția Patriarhiei Moscovei și să își creeze propria structură ecleziastică bisericească în Ucraina.

Acest raport laudă, în acest sens, ia act de faptul că, în august 2024, parohiile ortodoxe românești din Ucraina au depus o cerere de recunoaștere a asociației religioase - Biserica Ortodoxă Română din Ucraina. Și raportul solicită Ucrainei, autorităților ucrainene să recunoască această asociație.
3-0540-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I voted in favor of the Ukraine Report because, first of all, I support Ukraine in winning this war waged by an aggressive Russia against it.

Moreover, this report provides for the second time the following situation: it notes that the Parliament of Ukraine has passed a law that allows Orthodox parishes in Ukraine, under the jurisdiction of the Orthodox Patriarchate of Moscow, to disaffiliate from the Russian Orthodox Church and decide on their own affiliation. In Ukraine today there are hundreds of Romanian Orthodox parishes that want to leave the jurisdiction of the Moscow Patriarchate and create their own ecclesiastical church structure in Ukraine.

This praise report, in this sense, takes note of the fact that, in August 2024, the Romanian Orthodox parishes in Ukraine submitted a request for recognition of the religious association - the Romanian Orthodox Church of Ukraine. And the report calls on Ukraine, the Ukrainian authorities to recognize this association.

3-0542-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über Moldau.
3-0542-0000.englishText: We now turn to the explanations of vote on the Commission's 2025 report on Moldova.

3-0544-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über Serbien.
3-0544-0000.englishText: We now turn to the explanations of vote on the Commission's 2025 report on Serbia.

3-0545-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea Raportului privind Serbia, în primul rând, pentru că susțin Serbia. Poți să ai o serie de critici la adresa Serbiei, la adresa Guvernului Serbiei, însă e important ca Serbia să fie susținută în acest proces de integrare europeană.

În plus de asta, la o serie de amendamente pe care le-am făcut, acest raport prevede, pentru prima dată în istoria Parlamentului European, ca autoritățile sârbești să nu mai facă distincție între comunitatea vlahă - sau etichetată ca vlahă - și comunitatea românească din Serbia. Cele două comunități etnice sunt aceeași comunitate românească. Că unii le spun vlahi, că alții le spun români, este irelevant. Ambele comunități sunt comunități românești și e important ca autoritățile sârbești să recunoască lucrul acesta.

Al doilea lucru pe care l-am cerut este ca Episcopiei Ortodoxe Române din Serbia să i se permită extinderea jurisdicției asupra întregului teritoriu al Serbiei - lucru care astăzi nu este permis. Sunt convins că acest raport va avea soluții benefice pentru comunitatea românească ortodoxă din Serbia și îi felicit pe colegii care l-au votat.
3-0545-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I voted in favor of the Report on Serbia, first of all, because I support Serbia. You can have a series of criticisms towards Serbia, towards the Government of Serbia, but it is important that Serbia be supported in this process of European integration.

In addition to that, to a series of amendments that we have made, this report provides, for the first time in the history of the European Parliament, that the Serbian authorities no longer distinguish between the Vlach community - or labeled as Vlach - and the Romanian community in Serbia. The two ethnic communities are the same Romanian community. That some call them Vlachs, that others call them Romanians, is irrelevant. Both communities are Romanian communities and it is important that the Serbian authorities recognize this.

The second thing I asked is that the Romanian Orthodox Episcopate in Serbia be allowed to extend its jurisdiction over the entire territory of Serbia - something that is not allowed today. I am convinced that this report will have beneficial solutions for the Romanian Orthodox community in Serbia, and I congratulate the colleagues who voted for it.

3-0546-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica, ljudje v Srbiji evropske vrednote branijo bolj pogumno kot marsikdo v tej dvorani. Podpore od Evropske unije, vsaj tiste na najvišji ravni, ne dobijo niti malo, kvečjemu nasprotno. Potem se pa čudite, zakaj v Srbiji ni zaupanja v Evropsko unijo. Od kdaj je stabilnost brez demokracije stabilnost in od kdaj se sporočila za nenapredek pošiljajo z idejami o odpiranju novih pristopnih poglavij? V tem poročilu, ki sem ga seveda podprla, smo upravičeno ostri - vsaj nekdo, kajne? Ker v Evropskem parlamentu si vsaj še upamo reči bobu bob.

Ni pa to poročilo ocena Srbije kot države, ni ocena ljudi, je ocena oblasti. Moja podpora gre ljudem v Srbiji tistim, ki se borijo proti korupciji, za svobodne medije in za državo, v kateri zakon velja za vse. Njihova prihodnost je evropska.

Pa če smo že pri času za odpiranje novih poglavij oziroma poglavja številka 3 – absolutno. Prvo poglavje: demokracija, drugo: odgovornost in tretje: institucije, ki delujejo. Dokler tega ni, pa pač ne morete odpirati nekih drugih poglavij, gospa von der Leyen, odprite raje oči.
3-0546-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the people of Serbia defend European values ​​more courageously than many people in this chamber. They do not receive any support from the European Union, at least at the highest level, on the contrary at best. Then you wonder why there is no trust in the European Union in Serbia. Since when is stability without democracy stability and since when are messages for non-progress sent with ideas about opening new accession chapters? In this report, which I of course supported, we are rightly harsh - at least someone, right? Because in the European Parliament, at least we still dare to say boba boba.

But this report is not an assessment of Serbia as a country, it is not an assessment of the people, it is an assessment of the authorities. My support goes to the people of Serbia, those who fight against corruption, for a free media and for a country where the law applies to everyone. Their future is European.

And if it's time to open new chapters or chapter number 3 - absolutely. Chapter One: Democracy, Second: Accountability and Third: Institutions That Work. Until that happens, you can't open any other chapters, Mrs. von der Leyen, better open your eyes.

3-0548-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu den Folgen der türkischen Invasion von 1974 für zyprische Frauen und Mädchen, den von den türkischen Streitkräften verübten Verbrechen und den Konsequenzen für die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter.
3-0548-0000.englishText: We now turn to the explanations of vote on the consequences of the 1974 Turkish invasion on Cypriot women and girls, the crimes committed by the Turkish armed forces and the consequences for gender equality.

3-0549-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, καταδικάζουμε την τουρκική εισβολή και κατοχή της Κύπρου, τα αποτρόπαια εγκλήματα που διέπραξε ο τουρκικός στρατός σε βάρος Κυπρίων, γυναικών και κοριτσιών, τον βίαιο εκτοπισμό, τη σεξουαλική κακοποίηση, τους βιασμούς, τον διαχωρισμό των οικογενειών, το τραύμα, τον στιγματισμό και τις ανυπολόγιστες μακροπρόθεσμες βαριές συνέπειές τους, στερούμενες και την παραμικρή στήριξη. Πέραν από την αυτονόητη αποζημίωση που υποχρεούται το τουρκικό κράτος να καταβάλει στα θύματά του, απαιτούμε να ανοίξουν τα κλειστά στρατιωτικά αρχεία, να γίνει αποτελεσματική έρευνα στα Κατεχόμενα με ταυτοποίηση και απόδοση των λειψάνων, αποζημίωση, στήριξη των οικογενειών των αγνοουμένων μέχρι να διακριβωθεί κάθε αγνοούμενος.

Και σήμερα, 52 χρόνια από την εισβολή, 32 από την ένταξη της Κύπρου στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, η απάντηση ενάντια στα διχοτομικά σχέδια και τη ΝΑΤΟποίηση του νησιού είναι: Κύπρος ανεξάρτητη, ένα και όχι δύο κράτη, μία και μόνη κυριαρχία, ιθαγένεια, διεθνής προσωπικότητα, με άμεση αποχώρηση των κατοχικών στρατευμάτων, χωρίς εγγυητές και προστάτες, χωρίς ξένα στρατεύματα και βάσεις, κοινή πατρίδα Ελληνοκυπρίων-Τουρκοκυπρίων με τον λαό της αφέντη στον τόπο του.
3-0549-0000.englishText:
Madam President, we condemn the Turkish invasion and occupation of Cyprus, the heinous crimes committed by the Turkish army against Cypriots, women and girls, forced displacement, sexual abuse, rape, family separation, trauma, stigmatization and their incalculable long-term heavy consequences, deprived of even the slightest support. In addition to the self-evident compensation that the Turkish state is obliged to pay to its victims, we demand that the closed military archives be opened, that an effective search be made in the Occupied Territories with the identification and return of the remains, compensation, support for the families of the missing until each missing person is identified.

And today, 52 years since the invasion, 32 since the accession of Cyprus to the European Union, the answer against the dichotomy plans and the NATOization of the island is: Cyprus independent, one and not two states, one and only sovereignty, citizenship, international personality, with the immediate withdrawal of the occupying troops, without guarantors and protectors, without foreign troops and bases, common homeland of Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots with master's people in his place.

3-0550-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, durante mis mandatos como presidente de la Comisión de Libertades, Justicia y Asuntos de Interior, tuve el honor de ser el ponente permanente para las personas desaparecidas en Chipre, cuya parte norte fue invadida por Turquía en 1974. Por tanto, me comprometí con esos miles de personas desaparecidas cuyas familias esperan todavía reparación y justicia.

Hemos votado sobre una propuesta de Resolución que incide sobre un aspecto sensible: la violación masiva de derechos humanos que supuso la violencia sexual perpetrada contra mujeres y niñas en la ocupación del norte de Chipre. Y, sin duda, la propuesta de Resolución incide en la igualdad de género, en los derechos humanos y en el Estado de Derecho.

Pero lo cierto es que hay una cuenta pendiente en la que esta Unión Europea se tiene que comprometer plenamente. Esa cuenta pendiente tiene una dimensión con Turquía, que todavía figura en la lista de los Estados candidatos a la adhesión, pero sobre todo con Chipre, cuya integridad territorial nacional continúa pendiente y en cuyo Parlamento nacional todavía hay asientos vacantes que esperan la representación de la comunidad turca de Chipre del Norte.
3-0550-0000.englishText:
Madam Speaker, during my terms as Chairman of the Committee on Freedoms, Justice and Home Affairs, I had the honor of being the permanent rapporteur for missing persons in Cyprus, the northern part of which was invaded by Turkey in 1974. I therefore committed myself to those thousands of missing persons whose families are still waiting for reparation and justice.

We have voted on a proposed resolution that affects a sensitive aspect: the massive violation of human rights caused by sexual violence perpetrated against women and girls in the occupation of northern Cyprus. And, without a doubt, the proposed Resolution affects gender equality, human rights and the rule of law.

But the truth is that there is a pending account in which this European Union has to fully commit itself. This pending account has a dimension with Turkey, which still appears on the list of candidate States for accession, but above all with Cyprus, whose national territorial integrity remains pending and in whose national Parliament there are still vacant seats awaiting representation of the Turkish community of Northern Cyprus.

3-0551-0000.englishText: This item on the agenda is now closed.

3-0555-0000.sourceText:
Die nächste Sitzung findet morgen, Donnerstag, den 9. Juli 2026, um 8.00 Uhr statt.

Die Tagesordnung wurde veröffentlicht und ist auf der Website des Europäischen Parlaments verfügbar.
3-0555-0000.englishText:
The next meeting will be tomorrow, Thursday, July 9, 2026, at 8:00 a.m.

The agenda has been published and is available on the European Parliament website.

3-0557-0000.sourceText:
Das Protokoll dieser Sitzung wird dem Parlament morgen zu Beginn der Nachmittagssitzung zur Genehmigung vorgelegt.

Die Sitzung ist hiermit geschlossen, und ich möchte mich bei den Dolmetschern für die Unterstützung während der heutigen Plenarsitzung bedanken.
3-0557-0000.englishText:
The minutes of this meeting will be submitted to Parliament for approval at the beginning of the afternoon sitting tomorrow.

The meeting is hereby closed and I would like to thank the interpreters for their assistance during today's plenary session.
